body.text: Śrāvakabhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s> (The Stage of the Disciple)

body.text: I. gotrabhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: I. <s>Gotrabhūmi</s> (The Level of Spiritual Lineage)

body.text: // [|] indriyairavikalatā, āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ, aparivṛttakarmāntatā [|]
body.translated_text: Non-deficiency of the sense-faculties, faith pertaining to the [proper] sphere, and non-reversal of the course of <s>karma</s> (action).

body.text: tatra manuṣyatvaṃ katamat | yathāpīhaikatyo manuṣyāṇāṃ sabhāgatāyāṃ pratyājāto bhavati | puruṣaśca puruṣendriyeṇa [samanvāgato bhavati | idamucyate manuṣyatvaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'being human' (<s>manuṣyatva</s>)? It is as follows: here a certain being is reborn in the community of humans, and is a male endowed with the male faculty. This is called 'being human.'

body.text: āryā[ya]tane pratyājātiḥ katamā [|] yathāpīhai] katyo madhyeṣu [ja]napadeṣu pratyājāto bhavati pūrvavadyāvadyatra gatiḥ satpuruṣāṇāmiyamucyate āryāyatane pratyājātiḥ [|]
body.translated_text: What is 'birth in a noble region' (<s>āryāyatane pratyājāti</s>)? It is as follows: here a certain being is reborn in the central countries, as before, up to where 'there is the way of noble persons.' This is called 'birth in a noble region.'

body.text: indriyairavikalatā katamā [|] yathāpīhaikatyaḥ ajāto bhavatyaneḍaka iti vistaraḥ [|] aṃgapratyaṃgāvikalo vā yadrūpeṇāṃpratyaṃgāvaikalyena śrotrāvaikalyādikena bhavyaḥ kuśalapakṣasamudāgamāya [|] idamucyate indriyā vaikalyaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: What is 'non-deficiency of the sense-faculties' (<s>indriyairavikalatā</s>)? It is as follows: here a certain being is not born deaf-mute, and so forth in detail; nor is he deficient in limbs and minor limbs — meaning that by virtue of non-deficiency of limbs, non-deficiency of hearing, and so on, he is capable of attaining the wholesome qualities. This is called 'non-deficiency of the sense-faculties.'

body.text: āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ katamaḥ [|] yathāpīhaikatyena tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhā pratilabdhā bhavati | cetasaḥ prasādaḥ [|] ayamucyate āyatanagataḥ prasādastadāyatanaṃ tathāgatapravedito dharmavinayaḥ sarveṣāṃ laukikalokottarāṇāṃ śukladharmāṇāmutpattaye [|] yā punaratra śraddhā, tena pūrvagamenādhipatyena sa āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: What is 'faith pertaining to the [proper] sphere' (<s>āyatanagataḥ prasādaḥ</s>)? It is as follows: here a certain person has obtained faith in the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline) proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> — that is, mental clarity (<s>cetasaḥ prasādaḥ</s>). This is called 'faith pertaining to the sphere.' That sphere is the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, for the arising of all mundane and supramundane wholesome qualities. And the faith that arises therein — by virtue of its being the forerunner and dominant factor — that is 'faith pertaining to the sphere.'

body.text: sarvakleśamalakāluṣyāpanayanā aparivṛttakarmāntatā yena paṃcānāmānantaryāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ, tadyathā mātṛvadhāt pitṛvadhādarhadvadhātsaṃghabhedāttathāgatasyāntike duṣṭacittarucirotpādādanyatamānyatamadānantaryaṃ karma dṛṣṭa eva dharme na kṛtaṃ bhavati nādhyācaritamiyamucyate | aparivṛttakarmāntatā | itīmāni pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi kṛtopacitāni [|] dṛṣṭa eva dharme parivartyābhavyo bhavati parinirvāṇāyāryamārgasyotpattaye tasmādetāni parivṛttakarmāntatetyucyate | svayamevānena sa ātmabhāva ebhiḥ pañcabhiraṅgaiḥ sampādito bhavati | tasmādātmasampadityucyate |
body.translated_text: What is 'non-reversal of the course of <s>karma</s>' (<s>aparivṛttakarmāntatā</s>), which removes the defilement and impurity of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)? It is when, in this very life, a person has not committed or undertaken any of the five <s>ānantarya</s> (immediately-retributive) actions, namely: matricide, patricide, the murder of an <s>Arhat</s>, causing schism in the <s>Saṅgha</s>, or maliciously causing blood to flow from the body of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. This is called 'non-reversal of the course of <s>karma</s>.' For these five immediately-retributive actions, when committed and accumulated, make one incapable in this very life of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> or of generating the Noble Path; therefore they are called 'reversal of the course of <s>karma</s>.' One's own person (<s>ātmabhāva</s>) is endowed with these five factors by oneself; therefore it is called <s>ātmasampad</s> (self-endowment).

body.text: parasampat katamā [|] tadyathā buddhānāmutpādaḥ, saddharmadeśanādeśitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ avasthānamavasthitānāṃ cānupravarttanaṃ | parataśca pratyanukampā [|]
body.translated_text: What is <s>parasampad</s> (endowment from others)? It consists of: the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>, the teaching of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the persistence of the teachings that have been taught, the continued transmission of the established teachings, and compassion from others.

body.text: tatraḥ buddhānāmutpādaḥ katamaḥ [|] yathāpīhaikatyaḥ sarvasarvasatve(ttve)ṣu kalyāṇaṃ hitādhyāśayamutpādya prabhūtairduṣkarasahasrairmahatā ca puṇyajñānasambhāreṇa [] ātmabhāvapratilambhe bodhimaṇḍe niṣadya, pañcanivaraṇāni prahāya, caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu sūpasthitacittaḥ, saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyān dharmān bhāvayitvā [a]nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhyate | ayamucyate buddhānā[mu]tpādaḥ | atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasu evamevā [kleśa ā yā] ta evaṃ buddhā bhagavanto loka utpadya tasyaiva ca śrāvakalokānukampāmupādāya catvāryāryasatyānyārabhya duḥkha sadbhirayañca dharmo niryāto, deśitaḥ, praśasto buddhaiśca buddhaśrāvakaiścā[yamucyate buddhānāmutpādaḥ] |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>'? It is as follows: here a certain being, having generated a wholesome and benevolent intention toward all beings, through immense thousands of difficult deeds and through a great accumulation of merit and knowledge, having attained a physical existence, sitting at the seat of <s>bodhi</s> (awakening), having abandoned the five <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances), with mind well-established in the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), having cultivated the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (qualities conducive to awakening), attains supreme perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). This is called 'the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>.' In the past, future, and present time-periods, just so do the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> arise in the world, and out of compassion for the disciple-world, beginning with the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāryāryasatyāni</s>) and the truth of suffering, this <s>Dharma</s> has gone forth, has been taught, and has been praised by the <s>Buddhas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Buddhas</s>. This is called 'the arising of <s>Buddhas</s>.'

body.text: deśitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ avasthānaṃ katamat | deśite saddharme, pravartite dharmacakre, yāvacca buddho bhagavāṃ(vān) (

children.text: ) jīvati, tiṣṭhati ca, parinirvṛte ca buddhe bhagavati, yāvatā kālena pratipattirna hīyate, saddharmaśca nāntardhīyate [|] idamucyate saddharmasyāvasthānaṃ yāva[vasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ] [|]
children.translated_text: lives and endures, and even after the blessed <s>Buddha</s> has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, as long as the practice does not decline and the true <s>Dharma</s> does not disappear — this is called 'the persistence of the true <s>Dharma</s>,' and should be understood as such.

body.translated_text: What is 'the persistence of the teachings that have been taught'? When the true <s>Dharma</s> has been taught and the wheel of <s>Dharma</s> has been set in motion, as long as the blessed <s>Buddha</s>

body.text: avasthitānāṃ dharmāṇāmanupravarttanaṃ katamat | yatta evādhigantāra[ḥ] saddharmasya, saddharmasākṣātkriyāyai bhavyāṃ pratibalatāṃ jānatāṃ viditvā yathādhigatāmevānulomikīmavavādānuśāsanīmanupravarttayantīdamucyate avasthitānāṃ dharmāṇāmanupravarttanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: What is 'the continued transmission of the established teachings'? When those who have realized the true <s>Dharma</s>, knowing and recognizing the capacity and readiness of those fit to witness the true <s>Dharma</s>, continue to transmit instruction and admonition in accordance with what they themselves have realized — this is called 'the continued transmission of the established teachings.'

body.text: parataḥ pratyanukampā katamā | parata ucyante dā yakadānapatayaḥ te yāni tasyānulomikāni jīvito padhāraṇāni taiḥ pratyanukampate (nte) yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārairiyamucyate parataḥ pratyanukampā ||
body.translated_text: What is 'compassion from others' (<s>parataḥ pratyanukampā</s>)? 'Others' refers to donors and patrons. They show compassion through provisions that sustain his life and are conducive [to practice], namely: robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines and requisites for the sick. This is called 'compassion from others.'

body.text: kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ katamaḥ [|] yathāpīhaikatyastathāgatasya vā, tathāgataśrāvakasya vā antikāddharmaṃ śrutvā śraddhāṃ pratilabhate | sa tāṃ pratilabhya idaṃ saṃśikṣate | saṃbādho gṛhāvāso rajasāmāvāsaḥ | abhyavakāśaṃ pravrajya yanva(yannva)haṃ sarvaṃ kaḍa(la)travargaṃ, dhanadhānyahiraṇyaṃ cotsṛjya svākhyāte dharmavinaye samyagevāgārādanāgārikāṃ pravrajeyam | pravrajitvā (

children.text: ) (pravrajya) ca pratipattyā sampādayeyamiti | ya evamutpannaśchandaḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣvayamucyate kuśalo dharmachandaḥ (cchandaḥ) ||
children.translated_text: let me accomplish [the goal] through practice.' The desire that thus arises for wholesome qualities — this is called 'wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.translated_text: What is 'wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>' (<s>kuśalo dharmacchandaḥ</s>)? It is as follows: here a certain person, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from the <s>Tathāgata</s> or from a disciple of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, obtains faith. Having obtained it, he trains thus: 'The household life is confined and a dusty path; going forth is the open air. Let me renounce all my possessions — the entire group of wives and children, gold, grain, and wealth — and go forth from the household life into homelessness in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. And having gone forth,

body.text: pravrajyā katamā [|] yā tameva kuśalaṃ dharmacchandamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā jñapticaturthena vākkarmaṇā upasampatkuśalairaśī(ḥśī)lasamādānaṃ vā [|] iyamucyate pravrajyā ||
body.translated_text: What is 'going forth' (<s>pravrajyā</s>)? It is when, making that very wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> the dominant factor, one undertakes the moral precepts through a formal act of ordination consisting of a motion and three proclamations (<s>jñapticaturtha vākkarman</s>), or through the undertaking of moral discipline. This is called 'going forth.'

body.text: śīlasambaraḥ katamaḥ [|] sa tathā pravrajitaḥ śīlavān viharati, prātimokṣasamvarasaṃvṛtaḥ | ācāragocarasampannaḥ | aṇumātreṣvavadye ṣu bhayadarśī, samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu [|] ayamucyate śīlasamvaraḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is 'moral restraint' (<s>śīlasamvara</s>)? Having thus gone forth, one lives virtuous, restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> restraint, endowed with proper conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults, and training by undertaking the rules of training. This is called 'moral restraint.'

body.text: indriyasamvaraḥ katamaḥ || sa tameva śīlasamvaraṃ niśrityārakṣitasmṛtirbhavati | nipakasmṛtiḥ | smṛtyārakṣitamānasaḥ samāvasthāvacārakaḥ [|] sa cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā | na nimittagrāhī bhavati, nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī yato [a]dhikaraṇama sya pāpakā, akuśalā dharmāścittamanusraveyusteṣāṃ samvarāya pratipadyate [|] sa śrotreṇa śabdāṃ (bdān), ghrāṇena gandhān, jihvayā rasān, kāyena spraṣṭavyāni (|), manasā dharmān vijñāya na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī yato [a]dhikaraṇamasya pāpakā (

children.text: ) akuśalā dharmāścittamanusraveyusteṣāṃ samvarā [ya pratipadyate, rakṣati] mana indriyaṃ mana indriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | ayamucyate indriyasamvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: and mental objects with the mind, one does not grasp at their signs nor at their secondary features, since by reason of which evil, unwholesome qualities might flow into the mind; one practices for their restraint, guards the mental faculty, and achieves restraint through the mental faculty. This is called 'sense-restraint.'

body.translated_text: What is 'sense-restraint' (<s>indriyasamvara</s>)? Relying on that very moral restraint, one becomes guarded in mindfulness, alert in mindfulness, with a mind protected by mindfulness, dwelling in balanced conduct. Having seen forms with the eye, one does not grasp at their signs nor at their secondary features, since by reason of which evil, unwholesome qualities might flow into the mind; one practices for their restraint. Having cognized sounds with the ear, odors with the nose, tastes with the tongue, tangibles with the body,

body.text: bhojane mātrajñatā katamā [|] sa tathā saṃvṛtendriyaḥ pratisaṃkhyāyāhāramāharati | na darpārthaṃ, na madārthaṃ, na maṇḍanārthaṃ, na vibhūṣaṇārthaṃ, yāvadevāsya kāyasya sthitaye, [yāpanāyai, brahmacaryānugrahāya] iti | paurāṇāṃ vedanāṃ prahāsyāmi, navāṃ ca notpādayiṣyāmi [|] yātrā ca me bhaviṣyati | balaṃca, sukhaṃ cānavadyatā ca, sparśavihāratā ceyamucyate bhojane mātrajñatā ||
body.translated_text: What is 'moderation in eating' (<s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s>)? With senses thus restrained, one partakes of food wisely reflecting — not for amusement, not for intoxication, not for beautification, not for adornment, but only for the maintenance and sustenance of this body, for supporting the holy life, thinking: 'I shall put an end to the old feeling and shall not generate a new one. There shall be for me subsistence, strength, well-being, blamelessness, and comfortable dwelling.' This is called 'moderation in eating.'

body.text: jāgarikānuyogaḥ katamaḥ | [sadivā caṃkramaniṣadyābhyāmāvaraṇīyebhyo (

children.text: ) dharmebhyaścittaṃ pari] śodhayati | sa divā caṃkramaniṣadyābhyāmāvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaścittaṃ pariśodhya, tato vihārānnirgamya, bahirvihārasya pādau prakṣālya, dakṣiṇena pārśvena siṃhaśayyāṃ kalpayatyālokasaṃjñī, smṛtaḥ, saṃprajānan, utthānasaṃjñāmeva manasi kurvan sa rātryāḥ paścime yāme [laghu laghveva prativibudhya, caṃkramaniṣadyābhyā] māvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaścittaṃ pariśodhayatīyamucyate pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktatā [|]
children.translated_text: one purifies the mind of obstructive qualities.] Having purified the mind during the day by walking and sitting from obstructive qualities, upon leaving the dwelling and washing the feet outside, one prepares the lion-posture on the right side, with the perception of light, mindful, clearly comprehending, keeping the thought of rising in mind. In the last watch of the night, rising lightly and swiftly, one purifies the mind of obstructive qualities by walking and sitting. This is called 'devotion to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night.'

body.translated_text: What is 'devotion to wakefulness' (<s>jāgarikānuyoga</s>)? [During the day, by walking and sitting,

body.text: saṃprajānadvihāritā katamā [|] sa tathā jāgarikānuyuktaḥ ati(bhi)kramapratikrame saṃprajānadvihārī bhavatyālokitavyavalokite, sāmmiñjitaprasārite, sāṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe, aśitapītakhāditasvādite (

children.text: ) nidrāklamavinodane, gate, sthite, niṣaṇṇe, śayite, jāgṛte, bhāṣite, tūṣṇīmbhāve samprajānadvihārī bhavati | iyamucyate samprajānadvihāritā ||
children.translated_text: in dispelling drowsiness and fatigue, in walking, standing, sitting, lying down, being awake, speaking, and being silent — one dwells with clear comprehension. This is called 'dwelling with clear comprehension.'

body.translated_text: What is 'dwelling with clear comprehension' (<s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s>)? Thus devoted to wakefulness, one dwells with clear comprehension in going forward and returning, in looking ahead and looking around, in bending and stretching, in wearing the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer robe), the inner robe, and carrying the bowl, in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting,

body.text: prāvivekyaṃ katamat [|] sa ebhirdharmaiḥ parikarmabhūmiṃ śodhayitvā viviktāni śayanāsanānyadhyāvasatyaraṇyāni, vṛkṣamūlāni, śūnyāgārāṇi, parvatakandaragiriguhāpalāla[puṃjā]bhyavakāśaśmaśānavanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanādīnīdamucyate prāvivekyam ||
body.translated_text: What is 'inclination toward seclusion' (<s>prāvivekya</s>)? Having purified the preparatory ground through these qualities, one resorts to secluded lodgings: forests, roots of trees, empty houses, mountain caves, grottoes, straw-heaps, open spaces, cremation grounds, forest clearings — remote lodgings and the like. This is called 'inclination toward seclusion.'

body.text: nivaraṇaviśuddhiḥ katamā [|] so [a]raṇyagato vā, vṛkṣamūlagato vā, śūnyāgāragato vā, paṃcabhyo nivaraṇebhyaścittaṃ viśodhayati | kāmacchandād vyāpādātstyānamiddhādauddhatyakaukṛtyādvicikitsāyāḥ [|] sa ebhyo nivaraṇebhyaścittaṃ viśodhya vinivaraṇaṃ samādhikalpatāyāmavasthāpayatīyamucyate nivaraṇa viśuddhiḥ |
body.translated_text: What is 'purification from hindrances' (<s>nivaraṇaviśuddhi</s>)? Having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty house, one purifies the mind from the five hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>): sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>), sloth and torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>), restlessness and remorse (<s>auddhatyakaukṛtya</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). Having purified the mind from these hindrances, one establishes it in a state free from hindrances and fit for <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). This is called 'purification from hindrances.'

body.text: samādhisanniśraya katamaḥ | sa pañcanivaraṇāni prahāya cetasopakleśa(cetasa upakleśa)karāṇi saṃkleśakarāṇi | viviktaṃ kāmairviviktampāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarka savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ prathamaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharati [|] savitarkasavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādāccetasa ekotībhāvādavitarkamavicāraṃ (

children.text: ) samādhijaṃ prītisukhaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati | sa prītervirāgādupekṣako viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajāna[n] sukhaṃ ca kāyena pratisamvedayate yat | tadāryā ācakṣate upekṣakaḥ smṛtimān sukhavihārī tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati sa sukhasya ca prahāṇāt pūrvameva saumanasyadaurmanasyayorastagamā(rastaṅgamā)daduḥkhāsukhamupekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhaṃ caturthaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati | ayamucyate samādhisanniśrayaḥ [|]
children.translated_text: born of <s>samādhi</s>, filled with rapture and happiness. With the fading away of rapture, one dwells equanimous, mindful and clearly comprehending, and experiences happiness with the body. As the Noble Ones declare: 'Equanimous, mindful, dwelling in happiness' — one enters and dwells in the third <s>dhyāna</s>. With the abandoning of happiness and the prior disappearance of joy and sorrow, one enters and dwells in the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> — neither painful nor pleasant, purified by equanimity and mindfulness. This is called 'the basis of <s>samādhi</s>.'

body.translated_text: What is 'the basis of <s>samādhi</s>' (<s>samādhisanniśraya</s>)? Having abandoned the five hindrances, which are defilements of the mind and sources of mental affliction, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome qualities, one enters and dwells in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption) — accompanied by <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), born of seclusion, filled with <s>prīti</s> (rapture) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness). With the subsiding of initial and sustained thought, through inner tranquility and unification of mind, one enters and dwells in the second <s>dhyāna</s> — free from initial and sustained thought,

body.text: so [a]nayānūpūrvyā uttarottarānviśiṣṭān viśiṣṭatarān viśiṣṭatamān pratyagrānātmasampatpūrvān samādhi] saṃniśrayaparyavasānān samudānayati | evaṃ pariśuddhe citte paryavadāte anaṃgaṇe vigatopakleśe ṛjubhūte karmaṇye sthite āniṃjyaprāpte sa ceccatvāryāryasatyānyārabhya teṣāṃ parijñāyai prahāṇāya sākṣātkriyāyai bhāvanāyai parato ghoṣamavavā dānuśāsanīṃ pratilabhate | evamasau bhavyo bhavati pratibalaśca yoganimittasya manaskārasyotpādanāya | ya (ta)tpūrvikāyāśca samyagdṛṣṭeryayā catvāryāryasatyānyabhisamāgacchati | vimuktiñca paripūrayati | nirupadhiśeṣe ca nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāti | tatra yā samyagdarśanamupādāya vimuktiparipūriḥ | (

children.text: ) nirupadhiśeṣaparinirvāṇaṃ cāyaṃ gotrasamudāgamo veditavyaḥ | tatrātmasampadamupādāya yāvatsamādhisanniśrayo [a]yaṃ | hīnaḥ samudāgamapratyayo veditavyaḥ | tatra yaḥ catuḥsatyadeśanāvavādādhipateyaḥ parato ghoṣaḥ, yaśca yoniśo manaskāraḥ | ayaṃ pradhānaḥ samudāgamapratyayo veditavyaḥ | idamucyate gotravyavasthānaṃ ||
children.translated_text: ) and the <s>nirupadhiśeṣaparinirvāṇa</s> (final nirvāṇa without remainder) — this should be understood as the full development of the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). Therein, beginning with the attainment of self-perfection up to the support of <s>samādhi</s> — this should be understood as the inferior condition for full development. Therein, the voice from another [i.e., teaching heard from others] that has the authority of instruction in the Four Noble Truths, and the proper mental attention (<s>yoniśo manaskāra</s>) — this should be understood as the principal condition for full development. This is called the determination of <s>gotra</s>.

body.translated_text: By this gradual progression, one develops increasingly superior, more superior, and most superior, fresh [attainments], beginning with self-endowment and culminating in the basis of <s>samādhi</s>. When the mind is thus purified, cleansed, unblemished, free from defilements, pliant, workable, stable, and has reached imperturbability — if, beginning with the Four Noble Truths, for their full understanding, abandonment, direct realization, and cultivation, one receives from another the instruction and admonition of the [<s>Dharma</s>]-proclamation, then one becomes capable and competent to generate the mental attention that serves as the basis for the practice, and the right view that precedes it, by which one fully comprehends the Four Noble Truths, fulfills liberation, and attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (element of <s>nirvāṇa</s>) without remainder. Therein, the fulfillment of liberation based upon right seeing —

body.text: gotrasthasya pudgalasya katamāni liṃgāni | āha | yānyaparinirvāṇadharmakasya liṃgāni | ( āha | yānyaparinirvāṇadharmakasya liṃgāni |) tadviparyayeṇa gotrasthasya pudgalasya liṃgāni veditavyāni |
body.translated_text: What are the signs of a person established in the <s>gotra</s>? He says: Those which are the signs of one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — (He says: Those which are the signs of one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> —) by the reverse of those, the signs of a person established in the <s>gotra</s> should be understood.

body.text: kāni punaraparinirvāṇadharmakaliṃgāni yaiḥ samanvāgataḥ aparinirvāṇadharmakaḥ | aparinirvāṇadharmako 'yamiti vijñeyaḥ | bahūnyaparinirvāṇadharmakaliṃgāni | (pradeśamātraṃ |) pradeśamātrantu nirdekṣyāmi | ihāparinirvāṇadharmasya pudgalasyādita evāla [] tṛṣṇā sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā ca sarvabuddhairāśrayasanniviṣṭā aprahāṇadharmiṇī bhavatyanutpādyā dūrāgatā pragāḍhasanniviṣṭā [idaṃ] | idaṃ prathama[ma]gotrakasthasya pudgalasya liṃgaṃ || punaraparamagotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ anekaparyāyeṇa saṃsāraguṇān vicitrān prabhūtāṃśca (

children.text: ) śrutvā nirvāṇaguṇāṃścānekaparyāyeṇa vicitrān | prabhūtāṃśca śrutvā parīttamapi prapaṃce saṃsāradoṣadarśanamādīnavadarśanaṃ | saṃvegamātraṃ notpāditavānatītamadhvānamupādāya notpādayiṣyatyānāgata[madhvāna]mupādāya notpādayati [varta]mānamadhvānamupādāya parīttakalpamātrakamavaramātrakaṃ nirvāṇe, tṛṣṇākṣaye, virāge, nirodhe guṇadarśanamuśansa (śaṃsa)darśanaṃ prasādamātrakamatītānāgatapratyutpannamadhvānamupādāya notpāditavānnotpādayiṣyati notpādayati | idaṃ dvitīyamagotrastha[sya pudgalasya] liṃgam | punaraparamagotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ [anekaparyā] [yeṇa..............] gāmīduḥ[khā] patrāpyeṇa samanvāgato bhavati | yenāyamaghṛṇacittaścāsaṃkucitacittaśca prahṛṣṭacittaśca sarvasyāyamadhyācarati | na ca kadācittani (nni)dānaṃ vipratisārī bhavati | nānyatra // [|] [idaṃ tṛtīyamagotrasthaṃ liṅgaṃ [|] puna]raparamagotrasthaḥ (
children.translated_text: ) and having heard in many ways the diverse and abundant merits of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — even a small vision of faults, a perception of danger, or a mere sense of urgency regarding the defects of <s>saṃsāra</s> in the realm of proliferation has not been generated in the past, will not be generated in the future, and is not being generated in the present; and even a minimal, merely slight vision of merits, perception of benefit, or mere faith regarding <s>nirvāṇa</s>, the destruction of craving, dispassion, and cessation has not been generated, will not be generated, and is not being generated with respect to the past, future, and present. This is the second sign of one not established in the <s>gotra</s>. Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s> [in many ways...] is endowed with shamelessness regarding the paths leading to suffering — whereby this one, being of a ruthless mind, an unshrinking mind, and a delighted mind, commits all evil deeds, and never feels remorse on that account, nor otherwise. [This is the third sign of one not established in the <s>gotra</s>. Further]more, one not established in the <s>gotra</s>

children.text: ) sarvākāraparipūrṇe [a]sya (|) do[ṣa]yukte citre (tte) gamake duḥkhaṃ vā ārabhya, samudayaṃ vā, nirodhamvā, mārgamvā, saddharme deśyamāne na labhate cetasa āvarjanamātre karmaṇi, muktimātre [yadutātītamadhvānamupādāyānāgatamadhvānamupādāya ya] duta pratyutpannamadhvānamupādāya | idaṃ caturthamagotrasthaṃ liṃgaṃ | punaraparamagotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ sa cet kadācit karha (rhi)cit svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajati | sa rājā bhinirṇīto vā, co (cau)rābhinirṇīto vā, ṛ[ṇā]rto vā, ajīvikāmayabhīto vā, mā[rabhayabhīto vā, aśramaṇaḥ śramaṇaprati] jñaḥ, abrahmacārī brahmacārī (ri-) pratijñaḥ, atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣvadhvasvagotrasthasya pudgalasyaivameva pravrajyā veditavyā | na vā śikṣākāmasya pudgalasya pravrajyopasampadbhikṣubhāvaḥ | tadanena paryāyeṇānenābhisandhinā arthato nai[ryāṇikato [a]gotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ pravrajita] iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | idaṃ pañcamamagotrasthasya pudgalasya liṃgam || punaraparamagotrasthaḥ pudgalo yatkiṃcit kuśalaṃ karma karoti | (
children.translated_text: ) when the true <s>Dharma</s> is being taught — complete in all aspects, connected with faults, varied and convincing — whether concerning suffering, or the origin, or cessation, or the path — does not obtain even a mere turning of the mind toward action, or a mere liberation, [whether with respect to the past, the future, or] the present. This is the fourth sign of one not established in the <s>gotra</s>. Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>, if at some time he goes forth in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> — he is either expelled as a criminal, or expelled as a thief, or distressed by debts, or frightened by the danger of losing his livelihood, [or frightened by the danger of death — a non-ascetic] claiming to be an ascetic, a non-celibate claiming to be celibate — in past, future, and present times, the going forth of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s> should be understood as being exactly thus. Nor does such a person who desires training obtain ordination, full ordination, or the state of a <s>bhikṣu</s>. By this manner and with this intention, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s> does not count as 'one who has gone forth' in terms of substance and in terms of leading to liberation. This is the fifth sign of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>. Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>, whatever wholesome <s>karma</s> he performs —

children.text: ) kāyena, vācā, manasā vā tatsarvaṃ bhavābhiprāyo vā, viśiṣṭamāyatipunarbhavamabhiprārthayamāno bhogābhiprāyo [vā bhavati | idaṃ ṣaṣṭhamagotrasthasya pudgalasya] liṃgaṃ | evaṃbhāgīyāni cāsya bahūni liṅgāni samvidyante yaiḥ samanvāgataḥ | aparinirvāṇadharmako [a]parinirvāṇadharmaka iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati ||
children.translated_text: ) whether by body, speech, or mind — all of it is either directed toward [continued] existence, or aspiring for a superior future rebirth, or directed toward enjoyments. [This is the sixth sign of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>.] Many such signs exist for him, possessing which one is reckoned as 'one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.'

body.translated_text: What then are the signs of one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, possessing which one is to be known as 'one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>'? The signs of one whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> are many. (In brief:) I shall indicate only a portion. Here, for a person whose nature is not to attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, from the very beginning, the craving [] — in every way and in all respects, implanted in the foundation by all <s>Buddhas</s> — is of a nature not to be abandoned, unarisen, come from afar, and deeply implanted. This is the first sign of a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>. Furthermore, a person not established in the <s>gotra</s>, having heard in many ways the diverse and abundant merits of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: tatra katame gotrasthāḥ pudgalāḥ | āha | asti gotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ | gotra eva sthito, nāvatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ [avatīrṇo na niṣkrāntaḥ, avatīrṇo niṣkrānto], mṛdvindriyo, madhyendriyaḥ, tīkṣṇendriyaḥ, rāgacarito, dveṣacarito, mohacaritaḥ | akṣaṇopapannaḥ | apramattaḥ, mithyāpratipannaḥ, amithyāpratipannaḥ, āvṛto [a]nāvṛtaḥ, dūre, antike [|] paripakvaścā [a]paripakvaśca, viśuddhaścāviśuddha[śca [|] ||
body.translated_text: Therein, which persons are established in the <s>gotra</s>? He says: There is a person established in the <s>gotra</s> — merely established in the <s>gotra</s>, neither descended nor emerged; [descended but not emerged; descended and emerged;] of soft faculties, of middling faculties, of sharp faculties; of passionate temperament, of hateful temperament, of deluded temperament; born in an unfavorable state; heedless; wrongly directed; not wrongly directed; obstructed; unobstructed; far; near; ripened and unripened; purified and unpurified.

body.text: tatra katamo gotrastha eva pudgalaḥ | āha |] yathāpīhaikatyaḥ pudgalo lokottaradharmabījamohāgato bhavati | na ca punaradyāpi labhate satpuruṣasaṃsevāṃ vāgamya, saddharmaśravaṇaṃ vā, tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhāṃ ca śīlaṃ ca samādadāti | na śrutamudgṛhaṇāti | na tyāgaṃ bṛṃhayati, na dṛṣṭimṛjūka[roti | ayamucyate gotrastha eva pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, which person is merely established in the <s>gotra</s>? He says:] Just as here a certain person possesses the seed of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>, yet has not yet obtained association with good persons, nor hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>; he does not take up faith and moral discipline in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>; he does not master what has been heard; he does not cultivate generosity; he does not straighten his views. This one is called a person merely established in the <s>gotra</s>.

body.text: a]sya viparyayeṇa śuklapakṣeṇa gotrasthaścāvatīrṇaśca (

children.text: ) veditavyaḥ | ayantu viśeṣo no tu lābhī bhavatyāryamārgasya | tatphalasya ca kleśa visaṃyogasya ||
children.translated_text: ) This is the distinction: however, he does not obtain the noble path, nor its fruit, nor the separation from afflictions.

body.translated_text: B]y the reverse of this, through the white [wholesome] side, one should be understood as both established in the <s>gotra</s> and having descended.

body.text: katamo gotrasthaścāvatīrṇaśca niṣkrāntaśca || etadevoktvā [a]yaṃ viśeṣaḥ [|] lābhī bhavatyāryamārgasya tatphalasya ca || [|]
body.translated_text: Which one is established in the <s>gotra</s>, having descended, and also emerged? Having stated just this, this is the distinction: he obtains the noble path and its fruit.

body.text: tatra mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yasya nātyarthaṃ jñeye vastunyālamba
body.translated_text: Therein, which person is of soft faculties? One whose faculties are extremely sluggish and slow with respect to the knowable object and

body.text: ne atyarthaṃ dhandhavāhīnīndriyāṇi bhavanti | mandavāhīni vā [|] śrutamayena vā, cintāmayena vā, bhāvanāmayena vā manasikāreṇa saṃprayuktāni | yaduta śraddhā, vīryaṃ, smṛtiḥ, samādhiḥ | prajñā vā [|] na samarthāni, na pratibalāni dharmasya vā prativedhāyārthasya vāśuca prativedhāya | ayamucyate mṛdvindriyaḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: support — conjoined with mental attention born of hearing, or born of reflection, or born of meditation — namely, faith, vigor, mindfulness, <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom — [which are] not capable, not powerful enough for the penetration of the <s>Dharma</s> or for the swift penetration of the meaning. This one is called a person of soft faculties.

body.text: madhyendriyaḥ katamaḥ [|] yasya nātyarthaṃ jñeye vastunyālambane dhandhavāhīnīndriyāṇi sarvaṃ pūrvavadvistareṇa vaktavyamayamucyate madhyendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Which one is of middling faculties? One whose faculties are not extremely sluggish and slow with respect to the knowable object and support — all this should be stated in detail as before — this one is called a person of middling faculties.

body.text: tīkṣṇe[ndriyaḥ pudgalaḥ] katamaḥ [|] yasya pudgalasya jñeye vastunyālambane [a]dhandhavāhīnīndriyāṇi bhavanti | amandavāhīni [|] śrutamayena [vā, (

children.text: ) cintāmayena vā, bhāvanāmayena vā manasikāreṇa saṃprayuktāni | yaduta śraddhā, vīryaṃ, smṛtiḥ,] samādhiḥ, prajñā vā [|] śaktāni bhavanti dharmasya prativedhāya, arthasya vā āśu ca prativedhāya | [tanu] vā [|] ayamucyate tīkṣṇendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ [|]
children.translated_text: ) born of reflection, or born of meditation — namely, faith, vigor, mindfulness,] <s>samādhi</s>, and wisdom — [which] are capable of the penetration of the <s>Dharma</s>, and of the swift penetration of the meaning — [or subtle.] This one is called a person of sharp faculties.

body.translated_text: Which person is of sharp faculties? One whose faculties with respect to the knowable object and support are not sluggish and slow, not feeble — conjoined with mental attention [born of hearing,

body.text: rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yo raṃjanīye ālambane tīvrarāgaśca bhavatyāyatarāgaśca, ayamucyate [rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Which person is of passionate temperament? One who, with respect to an attractive object, has intense passion and prolonged passion — this one is called [a person of passionate temperament.

body.text: dveṣacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yaḥ pra] tighasthānīye ālambane tīvradveṣaśca bhavatyāyatadveṣaścāyamucyate dveṣacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Which person is of hateful temperament? One who, with respect to an object that is a] basis for hostility, has intense hatred and prolonged hatred — this one is called a person of hateful temperament.

body.text: mohacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yo jñeye vastuni tīvramohaśca bhavatyāyatamohaścāyamucyate mohacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Which person is of deluded temperament? One who, with respect to a knowable object, has intense delusion and prolonged delusion — this one is called a person of deluded temperament.

body.text: akṣaṇopapannapramatta[mithyāpratipannāśca pudgalāḥ katame | akṣaṇo] papannāḥ pramattāmithyāpratipannānāvṛtā (pannā anāvṛtā) veditavyā[ḥ] ||
body.translated_text: [Which persons are born in an unfavorable state, heedless, and wrongly directed? Those born in an unfavorable state] should be understood as heedless, wrongly directed, and unobstructed.

body.text: dūre pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | asti pudgalaḥ kāladūratayā nirvāṇasya dūre | asti prayogadūratayā (|) tatra katamaḥ kāladūratayā dūre | anekairjātiśatairanekairjātiśatasahasraiḥ (

children.text: ) [anekajātiśatasahasraiḥ] tataḥ paścād bhavyo [bhavatyāśupratyayalābhāya | parinirvāṇāya | tatra | prayogadūratayā pu]dgalo gotra eva kevale sthito bhavati | nāvatīrṇaḥ | sa bhavyo bhavatyāśupratyayalābhāya | parinirvāṇāya [|] sa nirvāṇāyānārabdhaprayogadūratayā [dūratvāt prayoga] kāladūratayā ayamucyate dūre pudgalaḥ || āsanne pudgalaḥ | .............................
children.translated_text: ) [many hundreds of thousands of births,] only thereafter becomes capable of swiftly obtaining the conditions [for practice] and of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. [Therein, a person far by distance of practice] is one who remains established merely in the <s>gotra</s> alone, not having descended. He is capable of swiftly obtaining the conditions and of attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. [Yet] because of the distance of not having commenced practice toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and because of distance of time from practice — this one is called a person who is far. The person who is near .............................

body.translated_text: Which person is far [from <s>nirvāṇa</s>]? There is a person who is far from <s>nirvāṇa</s> by distance of time; there is one far by distance of practice. Therein, which one is far by distance of time? One who, after many hundreds of births, many thousands of births,

body.text: II. avatārabhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: II. The Stage of Descent (<s>Avatārabhūmi</s>)

body.text: ........... yaiḥ ṣaḍbhirbhavyo mṛdukuśalamūlasamanvāgato madhyakuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ | adhimātrakuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ | niṣṭhāprāyogiko, niṣṭhāgataśca |
body.translated_text: ........... by which six [conditions] one who is capable [becomes] endowed with soft wholesome roots, endowed with middling wholesome roots, endowed with superior wholesome roots, one engaged in the practice leading to the final goal, and one who has reached the final goal.

body.text: tatra katamo bhavya eva pudgalaḥ | yo gotrasthāna (naṃ) cā(bhi)dhyāyi(yī) tatprathamatastathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhāṃ pratilabhate | yā ca dṛṣṭimṛjūkaroti |
body.translated_text: Therein, which person is merely capable? One who, relying on the <s>gotra</s>, who aspires to the <s>gotra</s>, first obtains faith in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and who straightens his views.

body.text: tatra katamo mṛdukuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ | yo gotrasthastena vā tathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye tatprathamataḥ śraddhā pratilabdhā bhavati | yāvad dṛṣṭi ṛjūkṛtā [|] ayamucyate mṛdukuśalamūlasamanvāgataḥ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, which one is endowed with soft wholesome roots? One who is established in the <s>gotra</s> and who, in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, has first obtained faith and has straightened his views up to [the relevant point]. This one is called 'endowed with soft wholesome roots.'

body.text: madhyakuśalamūlasamanvāgato gotrasthaḥ pudgalastatprathamatastathāgatapravedite dharmavinaye śraddhāṃ pratilabhya, yāvaddṛṣṭimṛjuṃ kṛtvā ekamvā (kaṃ vā), dve vā, sambahulāni vā janmānyabhinirvarttayati | viśeṣāye(yai)ti |
body.translated_text: One established in the <s>gotra</s> who is endowed with middling wholesome roots — having first obtained faith in the <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> proclaimed by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, and having straightened his views, he undergoes one, or two, or many births, and progresses further.

body.text: ya[ḥ] paraiti | no caramamātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhate | yatra sthitaḥ parinirvātyayamucyate | adhimātrakuśalamū lasamanvāgataḥ pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: One who goes beyond but does not obtain the final bodily existence in which, being established, one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — this one is called a person endowed with superior wholesome roots.

body.text: tatra katamo niṣṭhāprāyogikaḥ pudgalaḥ | yaḥ pudgalaścaramamātmabhāvaṃ pratilabhyāsravakṣayāya samyagavavādānuśāsanīṃ, saddharmaśravaṇaṃ vā pratilabhya samyageva prayujyate | na cādhmāyi (yī?) sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā pratipadyate | āsravakṣayamanuprāpnoti | na niṣṭhāṃ gacchatyayamucyate niṣṭhāprāyogikaḥ pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, which person is engaged in the practice leading to the final goal? A person who, having obtained the final bodily existence and having received the proper instruction and teaching for the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> (defilements), or having received the hearing of the true <s>Dharma</s>, practices correctly. Yet he does not swell with pride; he practices in every way and in all respects; he attains the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s>; [but] does not reach the final goal — this one is called a person engaged in the practice leading to the final goal.

body.text: tatra niṣṭhāgataḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ [|] yaḥ samyagāveditaḥ samyaganuśiṣṭaḥ | yadutāsravakṣayāya tathā tathā pratipadyate | yat sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā āsravakṣayamanuprāpnoti | kṛtakṛtyo bhavati paramaśītībhāvaprāptaḥ [|] ayamucyate niṣṭhāgataḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, which person has reached the final goal? One who has been properly informed, properly instructed — namely, for the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s> — who practices accordingly, who in every way and in all respects attains the destruction of the <s>āśravas</s>, who has done what was to be done, who has attained the supreme state of coolness — this one is called a person who has reached the final goal.

body.text: tatra bhavyajātīyaḥ pudgalo gotraṃ niśritya, gotraṃ pratiṣṭhāya mṛdūni kuśalamūlāni pratilabhate | avatīrṇaśca (

children.text: ) bhavati | so [a]vatīrṇo mṛdūni kuśalamūlāni niśritya, pratiṣṭhāya, madhyāni kuśalamūlāni pratilabhatetaiścātmānamparipācayati | sa tathā paripacyamāno madhyāni kuśalamūlāni niśritya pratiṣṭhāyādhimātrāṇi kuśalamūlāni pratilabhate | paripakvaśca bhavati | so [a]dhimātrakuśalamūlahetusamudāgatenātmabhāvapratilambhena yadā sambhārañca samudānayati | cittaikāgratāñca spṛśati | samyaktvañca nyāmamavakrāmati | strota āpattiphalamvā, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vā [a]nāgāmiphalamvā sākṣātkaroti | no tvagraphalamarhatvaṃ(ttvaṃ) sākṣātkaroti | tadā niṣṭhāprāyogika ityucyate |
children.translated_text: He exists. Having entered, relying on and establishing himself in mild wholesome roots (<s>mṛdu kuśalamūla</s>), he obtains middling wholesome roots, and with those he matures himself. As he is thus maturing, relying on and establishing himself in middling wholesome roots, he obtains superior wholesome roots, and he becomes fully matured. When, by means of the acquisition of a personal existence (<s>ātmabhāvapratilambha</s>) produced from the cause of superior wholesome roots, he accumulates the provisions (<s>sambhāra</s>), attains one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>), enters the certainty of the right course (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>), and directly realizes either the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), or the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), or the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), but does not directly realize the final fruit of <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship) — then he is called 'one who is in the stage of approaching the final goal' (<s>niṣṭhāprāyogika</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, a person of the capable class, relying on and being grounded in the <s>gotra</s>, obtains soft wholesome roots. And having descended,

body.text: yadā tu sarvakleśaprahāṇamarhatvaṃ (ttvaṃ) sākṣātkaroti | tadā niṣṭhāgato bhavati ||
body.translated_text: But when he directly realizes <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship), the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), then he becomes 'one who has reached the final goal' (<s>niṣṭhāgata</s>).

body.text: saiṣā sādimadhyaparyavasānā sarvaśrāvakacaryā ṣaḍbhiḥ pudgalavyavasthānaiḥ sandarśitā bhavati | tatra gotreṇādi[ḥ] śrāvakacaryāyāḥ sandarśitaḥ | niṣṭhāyā (niṣṭhayā) paryavasānaṃ | tadanyena madhyaṃ saṃdarśitaṃ ||
body.translated_text: This entire course of all <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), having a beginning, middle, and end, has been shown through six classifications of persons (<s>pudgalavyavasthāna</s>). There, the beginning of the <s>śrāvaka</s>'s course has been shown by <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). The end [has been shown] by the final goal (<s>niṣṭhā</s>). The middle has been shown by the rest.

body.text: tatrāvatīrṇānāṃ pudgalānāṃ kiṃ parimāṇaniyatastulyaśca sarveṣāṃ kālo bhavati | parinirvāṇāyāhosvidaparimāṇaniyataḥ | (

children.text: ) atulyaniścayaḥ sarveṣāṃ kālo bhavati | na parinirvāṇāya āho naiṣāṃ parimāṇaniyataḥ kālo nāpi tulyaḥ sarveṣāmparinirvāṇāya [|] api tu yathāyogameṣāṃ yathāpratyayalābhaṃ parinirvāṇaṃ veditavyaṃ | keṣāṃciccireṇa, keṣāṃciccāticireṇa, keṣāṃcitpunaḥ kṣiprameva parinirvāṇaṃ bhavatyapi tu yo gotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ [sa] sarvakṣipraṃ parinirvāti | so [a]vaśyaṃ trīṇi janmānyabhi nirvarttayati | ekasminnavataratyekasmiṃ (smin) parimucyate | ekāsmiṃ(smin) janmani paripakvo bhavati | tatraiva ca parinirvāti | no cet parinirvāti | so [a]vaśyaṃ śaikṣakālaṃ karoti | parañca saptabhavānabhinirvarttayatīdamucyate avatāravyavasthānaṃ |
children.translated_text: of unequal certainty, and not the same duration for all for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? Indeed, the duration is neither fixed nor equal for all for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Rather, their <s>parinirvāṇa</s> should be understood as occurring according to the appropriateness of conditions obtained by each. For some it occurs after a long time, for some after a very long time, and for some <s>parinirvāṇa</s> occurs very quickly. However, a person who is in the <s>gotra</s>-stage attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> most quickly of all. He necessarily completes three births: in one he enters, in one he is liberated, and in one birth he becomes fully matured and there itself he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. If he does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> [then], he necessarily passes through the period of a learner (<s>śaikṣakāla</s>), and completes at most seven existences. This is called the classification of entry (<s>avatāravyavasthāna</s>).

body.translated_text: Among those persons who have entered, is the duration fixed and equal for all for the attainment of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation)? Or is it of unfixed duration,

body.text: avatīrṇasya pudgalasya katamāni liṃgāni | iha gotrasthaḥ pudgalaḥ avatīrṇamātra eva yadā janmāntaraparivarttenāpi smṛtisaṃpramoṣaṃ pratilabhate | āśāstari dharmavinaye vā sati samvidyamāne [a]pi durākhyāte dharmavinaye svākhyāte [a]pyanekaparyāyeṇa durākhyātasya dharmavinayasya varṇaṃ stutimānuśansaṃ(śaṃsaṃ) śrutvā nāvatarati | na pravrajati | pravrajito [a]pyavatīrṇo (

children.text: ) laghu laghveva pratyudāvarttakhe | prakṛtyaiva cāsya tatrārocakaḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | madhuni jātasyeva ca prāṇakasya śuktiprakṣiptasya kāmopabhogino vā karde(nde ?)ṇa, syandanikāyāmvā prakṣiptasya yathāpi tatpūrvakeṇaiva hetubalādhānena svākhyātasya vā punardharmavinayasya naiva varṇa[ṃ] stutimānuśansaṃ (śaṃsaṃ) śrṛṇoti vā kaṇḍati vā | alpamātramavaramātramvā śrutvā, aśrutvā vā laghu laghvevāvatarati pravrajati vā [|] tathā pravrajitaścāvatīrṇo na pratyudāvarttate | prakṛtyaiva cāsya tatra ruciḥ saṃtiṣṭhate | madhuprāṇakasya vā madhuni, kāmopabhogino vā praṇītāyāṃ kāmacaryāyāṃ | yathāpi tatpūrvakeṇāpi hetubalādhānena | idaṃ prathamamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam ||
children.translated_text: very quickly indeed he turns back. And by nature, a distaste for that [false teaching] remains in him — like a creature born in honey that is thrown into vinegar, or like one who enjoys sensual pleasures and is thrown into mud or a gutter. Just so, by the force of previously [accumulated] causes, when he hears the praise, eulogy, and commendation of the well-taught doctrine and discipline, or when it itches [i.e., stirs in him], having heard even a small amount or an inferior amount, or even without hearing, very quickly indeed he enters and goes forth. And having thus gone forth, having entered, he does not turn back. And by nature, a delight in that [true teaching] remains in him — like the creature of honey in honey, or like one who enjoys sensual pleasures in excellent sensual conduct. Just so, by the force of previously [accumulated] causes. This is the first mark of a person who has entered.

body.translated_text: What are the marks (<s>liṅga</s>) of a person who has entered? Here, a person in the <s>gotra</s>-stage, as soon as he has entered, even when he obtains loss of memory through the turning of another birth — even when there is a teacher or a <s>dharmavinaya</s> (doctrine and discipline) present, even when one that is well-taught is poorly expounded — upon hearing the praise, eulogy, and commendation of the poorly expounded doctrine and discipline in many ways, he does not enter [it], he does not go forth [into it]. Even if he has gone forth, having entered,

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ (lo) na tāvadvisaṃyukto bhavatyapāyakṣaṇagamanīyaiḥ kleśaiḥ | na ca punarakṣaṇepūpapadyate | avatīrṇaṃ ca pudgalaṃ sandhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is not yet freed from the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that lead to the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>) and unfavorable conditions (<s>akṣaṇa</s>). Yet he is not reborn in unfavorable conditions. And with reference to a person who has entered, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) has said:

body.text: samyagdṛṣṭiradhimātrā laukikī yasya vidyate | api jātisahasrāṇi nāsau gacchati durgatim ||
body.translated_text: 'One who possesses superior mundane right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), even through thousands of births, does not go to a lower realm.'

body.text: sa yadā adhimātreṣu kuśalamūleṣu pratiṣṭho bhavatyanupūrveṇa paripākagamanīyeṣu tathā nākṣaṇeṣūpapadyate [|] (

children.text: ) na tvanyeṣu | idaṃ dvitīyamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam |
children.translated_text: but not in other [favorable conditions either]. This is the second mark of a person who has entered.

body.translated_text: When he becomes established in superior wholesome roots that gradually lead to full maturation, he is likewise not reborn in unfavorable conditions,

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇa[ḥ] pudgalaḥ buddhasya vā, dharmasya vā, saṃghasya vā guṇāṃcchrutvā, anusmṛtya vā, labhate cetasaḥ prasādamudāraṃ, kuśalaṃ, naiṣkrabhyopasaṃhitaṃ, bhūyo bhūyastenālambanena, prasādadravacittatayā astraprapātādromāṃcā[dīni] pratilabhate idaṃ tṛtīyamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya (pudgalasya) liṅgam |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered, upon hearing or recollecting the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, or the <s>Saṃgha</s>, obtains a mental clarity (<s>cetasaḥ prasāda</s>) that is lofty, wholesome, and connected with renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>); again and again, through that object, with a mind flowing with faith, he experiences the shedding of tears, goosebumps, and the like. This is the third mark of a person who has entered.

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ prakṛtyaiva tīvreṇa hrīvyapatrāpyeṇa samanvāgato bhavati | yaduta sarvasāvaddyasthānasattā (mu)dācāreṣvidaṃ caturthamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is by nature endowed with intense moral shame (<s>hrī</s>) and moral dread (<s>vyapatrāpya</s>) — that is, regarding all conduct involving blameworthy situations. This is the fourth mark of a person who has entered.

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ chandiko bhavati | tīvracha (ccha)ndaḥ uddeśe, svādhyāye, paripṛcchāyāṃ, yoge, manasikāre, kiṃkuśalagaveṣī bhavati | idaṃ pañcamamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is zealous — he has intense zeal (<s>chanda</s>) for instruction, self-study, questioning, practice, and mental application; he is one who seeks what is wholesome. This is the fifth mark of a person who has entered.

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ sarvakarmānteṣvanavadyeṣu sa[rvasa]mādāneṣu kuśalapakṣaprayogeṣu dṛḍhārambhaśca bhavati sthirārambhaśca niścitārambhaśca yaduta samāgamāya [|] idaṃ ṣaṣṭhamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered, in all blameless activities, in all undertakings of the wholesome side, has firm endeavor, steady endeavor, and resolute endeavor — that is, for the purpose of attainment. This is the sixth mark of a person who has entered.

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ mandaraja[ska]jātīyo bhavati | mandamandaṃ kleśaparyavasthānamutpādayati | na ca punaḥ prabandhaṃ sthāpayatyaśaṭhaśca bhavatyamāyāvī nihatamadamānāhaṃkāraguṇābhiniviṣṭo doṣadveṣṭā [|] idaṃ saptamamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered is of the type having mild passion (<s>mandarajaska</s>). He produces afflictive mental states (<s>kleśaparyavasthāna</s>) only mildly and gently. He does not allow them to continue in a stream. He is without deceit (<s>aśaṭha</s>) and without guile (<s>amāyāvī</s>), one who has destroyed pride, conceit, and ego-attachment, devoted to qualities, and hating faults. This is the seventh mark of a person who has entered.

body.text: punaraparamavatīrṇaḥ pudgalo 'saṃlīnacitto bhavatyudareṣvadhigamyeṣu sthāneṣu nātmānamparibhavati | nāpratibalatāyāmavatarati | adhimuktibahulo bhavati | idamaṣṭamamavatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgam ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person who has entered has an unshrinking mind (<s>asaṃlīnacitta</s>) regarding the lofty and attainable stages; he does not despise himself, he does not sink into a sense of incapacity; he is rich in conviction (<s>adhimukti</s>). This is the eighth mark of a person who has entered.

body.text: imānyevaṃbhāgīyāni prabhūtānyavatīrṇānāṃ pudgalānāṃ liṅgāni veditavyāni || yeṣāmetat pradeśamātramākhyātaṃ ||
body.translated_text: These and marks of a similar kind should be understood as the abundant marks of persons who have entered, of which only a portion has been described here.

body.text: punaretāni liṅgāni mṛdukuśalamūlasthasyāvatīrṇasya mṛdūni bhavanti | sachi(cchi)drāṇyanirantarāṇi apariśuddhāni [|] madhyakuśalamūlasthitasya madhyāni, adhimātrakuśalamūlasthitasyādhimitrāṇi, nirantarāṇi, pariśuddhānīmānyucyante avatīrṇasya pudgalasya liṅgāni | yailiṃgaiḥ samanvāgata[ḥ] avatīrṇa iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | api punaretāni gotrasthānāmavatīrṇānāñca pudgalānāṃ ānumānikāni liṅgāni veditavyāni | buddhā eva tu bhagavantaḥ paramapārami[tā]prāptāśca śrāvakāstāyinaḥ | tatra pratyakṣadarśinaḥ | (

children.text: ) suviśuddhena jñānadarśanena pratyanubhavanti | yaduta gotraṃ cāvatārañca [||]
children.translated_text: They experience [it] with thoroughly purified knowledge and vision — namely, both the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) and the entry (<s>avatāra</s>).

body.translated_text: Furthermore, these marks, for one who has entered while established in mild wholesome roots, are mild — with gaps, without continuity, and impure. For one established in middling wholesome roots, they are middling. For one established in superior wholesome roots, they are superior — continuous and pure. These are called the marks of a person who has entered, by which marks one who is endowed is reckoned as 'entered.' Moreover, these marks should be understood as inferential marks (<s>ānumānika liṅga</s>) for both persons in the <s>gotra</s>-stage and persons who have entered. Only the blessed <s>Buddhas</s> and the <s>śrāvakas</s> who have reached the supreme perfection, being stable, are direct seers there.

body.text: avatīrṇāḥ pudgalāḥ katame [|] astyavatīrṇaḥ pudgalaḥ | avatīrṇa eva, na paripacyamāno, na paripakvo, na niṣkrāntaḥ || asti paripakvo na niṣkrāntaḥ | asti niṣkrānto na paripakva eṣāṃ ca pūrvavadvibhāgo veditavyaḥ || ye [a]pi tadanye mṛdvindriyā dayaḥ pudgalāḥ | gotrabhūmau nirdiṣṭāḥ | teṣāmihāpi yathāyogaṃ vibhāgo veditavyaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: What are the [types of] persons who have entered? There is a person who has entered — merely entered, not yet maturing, not yet matured, and not yet emerged. There is [a person who is] matured but not yet emerged. There is [a person who is] emerged but not matured. The classification of these should be understood as before. Those other persons of weak faculties who are described in the <s>gotra-bhūmi</s> (lineage stage) — their classification should also be understood here as appropriate.

body.text: tatra yaścāyamavatārasya svabhāvaḥ, yacca vyavasthānaṃ, yāni cemānyavatīrṇānāṃ liṅgāni | ye ceme avatīrṇāṃ pudgalāḥ tatsarvamabhisaṃkṣipyāvatārabhūmirityucyate ||
body.translated_text: Thus, that which is the nature of entry, the classification, and these marks of those who have entered, and these persons who have entered — all of this, summarized, is called the <s>avatāra-bhūmi</s> (stage of entry).

body.text: || uddānam ||
body.translated_text: || Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>) ||

children.text: svabhāvastad vyavasthānaṃ liṅgaṃ pudgala eva ca |
children.translated_text: The nature, the classification, the marks, and the persons themselves —
all this should be known as the <s>avatāra-bhūmi</s> (stage of entry) in brief.

body.text: ||śrāvakabhūmā[va]vatārabhūmiḥ samāptā ||
body.translated_text: || The <s>avatāra-bhūmi</s> (stage of entry) in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s> is completed. ||

body.text: naiṣkramyabhūmiḥ
body.translated_text: <s>Naiṣkramya-bhūmi</s> (Stage of Renunciation)

body.text: naiṣkramyabhūmiḥ katamā | āha [|] yacca laukikena mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ | yacca lokottareṇa mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ | yacca(yaśca) tayossambhāraḥ tadekatyamabhisaṃkṣipya naiṣkramyabhūmirityucyate |
body.translated_text: What is the <s>naiṣkramya-bhūmi</s> (stage of renunciation)? It is said: That which is the attainment of dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) through the mundane path (<s>laukika mārga</s>), and that which is the attainment of dispassion through the supramundane path (<s>lokottara mārga</s>), and the provisions (<s>sambhāra</s>) for both of these — all of this, summarized, is called the <s>naiṣkramya-bhūmi</s>.

body.text: laukikena mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanaṃ katamat | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ kāmadhātāvaudārikadarśī bhavati | prathama eva sa samāpattyupapattike dhyāne vivekaje prītisukhe śāntadarśī bhavati | sa tathādarśī tadbahulavihārī satkāyavairāgyamanuprāpnoti | prathamañca dhyānaṃ samāpadyate | evaṃ sarvadhyānādūrdhvaṃ sarvāsvadharimāsu bhūmiṣvaudārikadarśī bhavati | sarvāsu coparimāyu bhūmiṣu śāntadarśī, sa tathādarśī tadbahulavihārī samāno yāvadākiñcanyāyatanādvairāgyamanuprāpnoti | naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ ca samāpadyate [|] laukikena mārgeṇa (

children.translated_text: does not go beyond this, there is nothing further than this.

body.translated_text: What is the attainment of dispassion through the mundane path? Just as here some person sees the desire-realm (<s>kāmadhātu</s>) as coarse, and sees the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption) — which pertains to attainment and rebirth, born of seclusion, [endowed with] joy and happiness — as peaceful. Seeing thus, dwelling abundantly in that, he attains dispassion from the personal aggregate (<s>satkāya</s>) and enters the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Likewise, above all <s>dhyānas</s>, he sees all lower stages as coarse and all upper stages as peaceful. Seeing thus, dwelling abundantly in that, he attains dispassion up to the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) and enters the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>). The attainment of dispassion through the mundane path

body.text: lokottareṇa mārgeṇa vairāgya gamanaṃ katamat | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ satpuruṣāṇāṃ darśī āryadharmeṣu kovidaḥ duḥkhamvā duḥkhato yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | samudayamvā samadayataḥ | nirodhamvā nirodhataḥ | mārgamvā mārgataḥ | śaikṣeṇa jñānadarśanena samanvāgataḥ | tataścottari mārgaṃ bhāvayaṃstraidhātukebhyo darśanabhāvanāprahātavyebhyodharmebhya ātmānaṃ visaṃyojayati vimocayatyevaṃ cāsau traidhātukasamatikrānto bhavati | idamucyate lokottareṇa mārgeṇa vairāgyagamanam ||
body.translated_text: What is the attainment of dispassion through the supramundane path? Just as here some person, seeing virtuous people, skilled in the noble <s>dharmas</s> (teachings), truly understands suffering as suffering, origination as origination, cessation as cessation, and the path as the path. Endowed with the knowledge and vision of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), and furthermore, cultivating the path beyond that, he disjoins and liberates himself from the phenomena of the three realms (<s>traidhātuka</s>) that are to be abandoned through seeing and cultivation (<s>darśanabhāvanāprahātavya</s>). Thus he transcends the three realms. This is called the attainment of dispassion through the supramundane path.

body.text: tatra sambhāraḥ katamaḥ | tadyathā ātmasvaparasampat (ātmasampat) | parasampat, kuśalaḥ (lo)dharma[c]chandaḥ, śīlasamvaraḥ, bhojane mātrajñatā, pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktatā, saṃprajānadvihāritā, kalyāṇamitratā, (

children.text: ) saddharmaśravaṇacittaṃ (cintanā) a[na]ntarāyaḥ tyāgaḥ, śramaṇālaṃkāraśca itīme dharmā laukikalokottaravairāgya[gama]nāya sambhāra ityucyate | tatra yā cātmasampat, parasampat kuśalaśca dharmacha(ccha)nda eṣāṃ pūrvavadvibhāgo veditavyaḥ | yaduktaṃ nihīne bījasamudāgamapratyaye |
children.translated_text: hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> and reflection upon it, unobstructed renunciation (<s>tyāga</s>), and the ornaments of an ascetic (<s>śramaṇālaṃkāra</s>) — these factors are called the provisions for the mundane and supramundane attainment of dispassion. Among these, the perfection of self, the perfection of others, and wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> — the classification of these should be understood as before, as stated in [the section on] the deficient condition of seed-arising.

body.translated_text: What are the provisions (<s>sambhāra</s>) for these? They are: perfection of self (<s>ātmasampat</s>), perfection of others (<s>parasampat</s>), wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>kuśaladharmaśchanda</s>), moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>), moderation in food (<s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s>), vigilance during the first and last watches of the night (<s>pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktatā</s>), dwelling in full awareness (<s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s>), association with virtuous friends (<s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>),

body.text: tatra śīlasamvaraḥ katamaḥ [|] yathāpīhaikatyaḥ śīlavān viharati yāvat samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu [|] kathaṃ ca śīlavān viharati | yāvat samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu [|] (kathaṃ śīlavān viharati |) yathā samātteṣu śikṣāpadeṣu avipannakāyakarmāntaśca, bhavatyavipannakāyakarmāntaśca | akhaṇḍacārī, achi(cchi)dracārī evaṃ śīlavān bhavati ||
body.translated_text: What is moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>) among these? Just as here some person lives endowed with moral virtue, and trains himself having undertaken the training rules. And how does he live endowed with moral virtue, and train himself having undertaken the training rules? (How does he live endowed with moral virtue?) In that, having undertaken the training rules, he is one whose bodily conduct is unimpaired, and whose verbal conduct is unimpaired. He is one of unbroken conduct, one of conduct without gaps — thus he is morally virtuous.

body.text: kathaṃ prātimokṣasamvarasaṃvṛto bhavati | saptanairyāṇikaṃ śīlaṃ prātimokṣasamvara ityucyate | ta ete nikāyabhedena bahavaḥ samvarā bhavanti | asmiṃstvarthe (

children.translated_text: taking the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) restraint as the basis, it is said 'restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint.'

body.translated_text: How does one become restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> (individual liberation) restraint? The moral conduct of the seven classes of persons leading to liberation is called the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint. These, by differentiation of community, are many restraints. In this matter, however,

body.text: kathamācārasampanno bhavati | yathāpi tadīryāpathamitikaraṇīya(yaṃ) vā, kuśalapakṣaprayogamvā adhiṣṭhāya lokānuvarttinā, lokānutkrāntena, vinayānuvarttinā, vinayānutkrāntena cācāreṇa samanvāgato bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become endowed with proper conduct? One becomes endowed with conduct that is in conformity with the world, not transgressing worldly norms, in conformity with the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic discipline), and not transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s>, based upon the modes of deportment and what is to be done, or based upon the application to wholesome qualities.

body.text: tatra īryāpathādhiṣṭhāna ācāraḥ | kathaṃ na lokānu(ko)tkrānto [na] vina yotkrāntaḥ [|] yathāpi tadyatra caṃkramitavyaṃ | yathā caṃkramitavyaṃ [|] tatra yathā caṃkramyate (caṃkramate) yena na lokagarhito bhavati, na satāṃ, samyagratānāṃ, satpuruṣāṇāṃ, sahadhārmikāṇāṃ, vinayadharāṇāṃ, vinayaśikṣitānāmabadhyo bhavati | [a]garhyasthānīyaḥ | yathā caṃkrama evaṃ sthānaṃ, niṣadyā, śayyā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: Therein, conduct based on the modes of deportment: how is it not transgressing worldly norms and not transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s>? For example, wherever one should walk and however one should walk — one walks there in such a manner that one is not censured by the world, and does not become blameworthy and subject to reproach among the virtuous, among those rightly devoted, among good persons, among those who share the <s>Dharma</s>, among upholders of the <s>Vinaya</s>, and among those trained in the <s>Vinaya</s>. As with walking, so should standing, sitting, and lying down be understood.

body.text: tatra itikaraṇīya ācāraḥ | kathaṃ na lokotkrānto bhavati | na vinayotkrānta iti karaṇīyamucyate | cīvarācchādanaṃ | uccāravastrāvaṃ | udakadantakāṣṭhaṃ | grāmapraveśaḥ | piṇḍapātanirhāraparibhogaḥ | pātranirmārda (rja)naṃ sthāpanaṃ ca | pādaprakṣālanaṃ ca | śayanāsanaprajñaptiḥ | tasyaiva cābhisaṃkṣepaḥ pātrakarma cīvarakarma iti | yadvā punarevaṃbhāgīyaṃ kiṃcittaditikaraṇīyamityucyate | tacca yathāyogaṃ yatra kalpayitavyaṃ, yathā ca kalpayitavyaṃ tatra tathā kalpayati | (

children.text: ) yena laukikānāmanabha(bhi)yojyo bhavatyavigarhitaḥ | vinayadharāṇāṃ [vinayaśikṣitānā] manapavādyo bhavatyavigarhitaḥ | samyagratānāṃ sahadhārmikāṇāmevamitikaraṇīyādhiṣṭhāna ācāro lokānutkrānto bhavati | vinayānutkrāntaśca ||
children.translated_text: such that one is not reproachable by worldly people and is not censured, and is not open to criticism and is not blamed by upholders of the <s>Vinaya</s> and those trained in the <s>Vinaya</s>, by those rightly devoted and those who share the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, conduct based on what is to be done does not transgress worldly norms and does not transgress the <s>Vinaya</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, conduct based on what is to be done: how is it not transgressing worldly norms and not transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s>? What is to be done is stated: wearing the robe, defecation and urination, water and tooth-stick, entering a village, receiving and using alms-food, cleaning and storing the bowl, washing the feet, preparing the sleeping and sitting places, and the summary of these being bowl-duties and robe-duties. Or whatever else belongs to this category is called 'what is to be done.' And this, as appropriate, wherever it should be done and however it should be done, one does it accordingly,

body.text: tatra kuśalapakṣaprayogadhiṣṭhāna ācāraḥ [|] kathaṃ lokānutkrāntaśca bhavati, vinayānutkrāntaśca [|] kuśalapakṣaucyate [|] tadyathā svādhyāyagurūṇāṃ sāmīcīkarma, upasthā(pa)naṃ ca, tathā glānopasthānamanyo [a]nyamanukampācittamupasthāpya cchandadāna[sa]muprayogaḥ, paripṛcchā, dharmaśravaṇadakṣasyānalasasya vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kāyena caiyā(ceryā) kṛtyakriyā, pareṣāṃ ca kuśalapakṣasamudāpanā, dharmadeśanā | pratisaṃlayanapraveśaparyaṅkanibandhāniṣadyā iti ya evaṃ bhāgīyā apyanye dharmā ayamucyate | kuśalapakṣaprayogaḥ [|] sa evaṃ kuśalapakṣaprayogo (gaṃ) yathāyogaṃ yathāparikīrtitaṃ | yatra kalpayitavyaṃ tatra tathā kalpayati | yena nānuyojyo bhavati | garhito laukikānāṃ vinayadharāṇāṃ, vinayaśikṣitānāṃ, samyagratānāṃ, satpuruṣāṇāṃ, sahadhārmikāṇāmayamucyate kuśalapakṣa (

children.text: ) prayogādhiṣṭhāna ācāra(ro) lokānutkrānto, vinayānutkrāntaśca [|] ya ebhirākāraiḥ sampanna ācāra iyamucyate ācārasampat | evaṃ cācārasampanno bhavati |
children.translated_text: not transgressing worldly norms and not transgressing the <s>Vinaya</s>. One who is endowed with conduct in these ways — this is called perfection of conduct. Thus one becomes endowed with proper conduct.

body.translated_text: Therein, conduct based on the application to wholesome qualities: how does it not transgress worldly norms and not transgress the <s>Vinaya</s>? The wholesome qualities are stated: proper service to teachers and preceptors of recitation, attending upon them, likewise caring for the sick, establishing a mind of compassion toward one another, application to the giving of formal consent, inquiry, listening to the <s>Dharma</s> — for one who is skilled and diligent — performing bodily service and duties for wise fellow practitioners of the holy life, and also generating wholesome qualities in others, teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, entering into meditative retreat, binding the legs in cross-legged sitting — whatever other qualities belong to this category, this is called the application to wholesome qualities. One who applies himself to wholesome qualities, as appropriate and as has been described, wherever it should be done, does it accordingly — such that one is not reproachable or censured by worldly people, by upholders of the <s>Vinaya</s>, by those trained in the <s>Vinaya</s>, by those rightly devoted, by good persons, and by those who share the <s>Dharma</s>. This is called conduct based on the application to wholesome qualities,

body.text: kathañca gocarasampanno bhavati | pañca bhikṣoragocarāḥ (|) katame pañca [|] tadyathā ghoṣo, veṣaṃ (veśyā-)pānāgāraḥ, rājakulaṃ, caṇḍālakaṭhinameva pañcamamiti | ya etāṃstathāgatapratikṣiptānagocarān varjayitvā anyatra gocare caratyanavadye tatra kālenaivaṃ gocarasampanno bhavati ||
body.translated_text: And how does one become endowed with proper range of activity? There are five improper ranges of activity for a <s>bhikṣu</s>. What are the five? Namely: a place of entertainment, a brothel or tavern, the royal court, and a place of <s>caṇḍālas</s> (outcasts) as the fifth. Avoiding these improper ranges of activity prohibited by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, one who moves about in other blameless ranges of activity — at the appropriate time, thus one becomes endowed with proper range of activity.

body.text: kathamaṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati | aṇumātramavadyamucyate | kṣudrāṇu(nu)kṣudrāṇi śikṣāpadāni yeṣvadhyāpattirvyutthānaṃ ca prajñāyate | teṣāṃ yādhyāpattiridamavadyamaṇumātraṃ | punastathā hi tasyā adhyāpatteralpakṛccheṇa vyuttiṣṭhate yena tadaṇumātramityucyate |
body.translated_text: How does one become one who sees danger in the slightest faults? A slight fault is defined as the minor and secondary training rules in which transgression and restoration are recognized. The transgression of those rules — this is a slight fault. Moreover, since one recovers from such a transgression with little difficulty, it is called 'slight.'

body.text: tatra kathaṃ bhayadarśī bhavati | sā hai vāha(so 'ha)meṣāmadhyāpattihetorabhavyo vā syāmaprāptasya prāptaye, anadhi[gatasyādhi]gamāya, asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai, apāyago vā syāmapāyagāmī, ātmā vā me apavadet, śāstā vā, devatā vā, vijñā vā, sabrahmacāriṇo [a]dharmatayā vigarhayeyuḥ | digvidikṣu ca me pāpako varṇakīrttiśabdaśloko [a]bhyudgacchetsa ebhyo dṛṣṭadharmasāṃparāyikebhyastaddhetukebhyo vi[śi]ṣṭebhyo dharmebhyo bhayadarśī bhavati | yena tāni kṣudrāṇu(nu)kṣudrāṇi śikṣāpadāni jīvitahetorapi na saṃdhibhyo vyāpadyate | kadācit karha(rhi)cit smṛtisaṃpramoṣādadhyāpannaḥ laghu laghveva yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti vyuttiṣṭhate [|] evamaṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one see danger? He thinks: 'If I commit such transgressions, I might become incapable of attaining what has not been attained, of realizing what has not been realized, of directly experiencing what has not been directly experienced; or I might be destined for a bad rebirth; or my own self might reproach me, or the Teacher might, or the deities might, or the wise might, or my fellow practitioners of the holy life might censure me on grounds of unrighteousness; and in all directions and intermediate directions, an evil reputation and report of bad fame might arise concerning me.' Seeing danger in these things pertaining to the present life and the future, and from the causes thereof, he does not violate even the minor and secondary training rules, even at the cost of his life. If at any time, through a lapse of mindfulness, he commits a transgression, he quickly and readily makes amends and recovers according to the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus one sees danger in the slightest faults.

body.text: kathaṃ samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu | (

children.text: ) āha [|] pūrvamanena prātimokṣasamvarasamādānajñapticaturthena karmaṇā upasampadyamānena katipayānāṃ śikṣāpadānāṃ śarīraṃ śrutaṃ, sātirekaṃ ca tadanyaṃ divasaṃ śikṣāpadaśataṃ prātimokṣasūtroddiṣṭaṃ pratijñayevopagataṃ sarvatra la(bdhā)ṣyāmīti (lapsyāmīti) | ācāryopādhyāyānāmantikācchrutvā ālaptakasaṃlaptakasaṃstutakamapriyakānāṃ(ṇām) adhbaramāsaṃgaprātimokṣasūtroddeśataḥ | tataśca tena sarvaśikṣāsamādānāt prātimokṣasamvaraḥ pratilabdhastata uttarakālaṃ yeṣu śikṣāpadeṣu kuśalo bhavati | tāni tāvannādhyāpadyate | adhyāpannaśca yathādharmaṃ pratikaroti | yeṣu punaḥ śikṣāpadeṣu kuśalo bhavati | avyutpannabuddhiḥ | tāni pūrvaṃ pratijñāsamādānena samādattānyetarhi vyutpattikauśalyatayā samādadāti | tebhyaḥ pūrvaṃ yathāparikīrttitebhyaḥ sthānebhya ācāryasya vopādhyāyasya vā pūrvavat | vyutpattikauśalyatayā ca punaḥ samādāya, yathānuśiṣṭaḥ anyūnamadhikaṃ śikṣate | te[ṣu guru]sthānīyavyapadiṣṭeṣu śikṣāpadeṣu aviparītagrāhī ca bhavatyarthasya vyaṃjanasya ca | evaṃ samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣvayaṃ tāvadvibhaṃgaḥ śīlasamvarasya vistarakṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is said: previously, when this one was being fully ordained by the formal act with a motion and three announcements for the undertaking of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint, he heard the body of a certain number of training rules, and moreover on another day, more than a hundred training rules recited in the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> were accepted by him through his promise 'I shall obtain all of these.' Having heard from the teachers and preceptors, through conversation, dialogue, discussion, and friendly exchange, and from the fortnightly recitation of the <s>Prātimokṣa Sūtra</s> — and then, having thus undertaken all the training rules, the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint was obtained by him. Thereafter, those training rules in which he becomes skilled — those he does not transgress; and if he transgresses, he makes amends according to the <s>Dharma</s>. Those training rules in which he is not yet skilled, in which his understanding is undeveloped — those which were previously undertaken through the commitment of acceptance, he now undertakes through the skill of understanding. From those previously described sources, or from the teacher or preceptor as before, and having undertaken again through the skill of understanding, he trains neither deficiently nor excessively as instructed. In those training rules designated as major, he becomes one who grasps correctly both the meaning and the letter. Thus one undertakes and trains in the training rules. This is the detailed analysis of the <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) restraint.

body.translated_text: How does one undertake and train in the training rules?

body.text: tatra katamaḥ samāsārthaḥ | tathāyaṃ samāsārthastrilakṣaṇa eva | śīlaskandhaḥ paridīpito bhagavatā, tadyathā (

children.text: ) avipraṇāśalakṣaṇaḥ, svabhāvalakṣaṇaḥ, svabhāvaguṇalakṣaṇaśca | yathā kathamiti yattāvadāha śīlavān viharatītyanena tāvadavipraṇāśalakṣaṇaṃ śīlasamvarasyākhyātaṃ || yatpunarāha prāti mokṣasamvarasaṃvṛta iti | anena svabhāvalakṣaṇamākhyātaṃ | yatpunarāha | ācāragocarasampannaḥ | anena paramupanidhāya, tathā samādattasya prātimokṣasamvarasya guṇalakṣaṇamākhyātaṃ | tathāpi pare tāmācāragocarasampadamupalabhyāprasannāśca prasīdanti, prasannānāṃ ca bhavati bhūyobhāvaḥ | prasannāśca prasannādhikāraṃ kurvanti | na ca manānsi (manāṃsi) pradūṣayanti | nāvvarṇaṃ niścārayantyanyathā śīlasampannasyācāragocarasampannasyāyaṃ parādhipateyo guṇa ānuśansā (ānuśaṃsā) ca bhavedetadviparyayeṇa vā (cā)sya doṣa eva bhavet | yatpunarāha | aṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu [|] anenādhyātmādhipateyaguṇānuśansa(śaṃsa)lakṣaṇamākhyātaṃ | tatkasya hetoryadasyeda (ma)mācāragocarasampannaḥ parādhipateyaṃ guṇānuśansaṃ (śaṃsaṃ) pratilabheta | api ca | śīlaṃ vi pātayitvā (vipātya) taddhetustatpratyayamapāyeṣūpapadyate | abhavyatāmvā (tāṃvā) aprāptasya prāptaye pūrvat | yatpunaraṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī bhavati | prāgevādhi mātreṣvasamādāya ca śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣu tasmāttaddhetustatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt sugatāvupapadyate | bhavyo (
children.translated_text: the characteristic of non-loss, the characteristic of intrinsic nature, and the characteristic of intrinsic virtues. How so? What is stated as 'he dwells endowed with moral conduct' — by this, the characteristic of non-loss of the <s>śīla</s> restraint is declared. What is further stated as 'restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint' — by this, the characteristic of intrinsic nature is declared. What is further stated as 'endowed with proper conduct and range of activity' — by this, with reference to others, the characteristic of the virtues of the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint that has been undertaken is declared. For others too, perceiving that perfection of conduct and range of activity, those who were not faithful become faithful, and for those already faithful, there is increase of faith. And the faithful make faithful efforts; they do not defile their minds; they do not spread ill-repute. Otherwise, for one endowed with moral conduct but endowed with proper conduct and range of activity, this would be a virtue and benefit relating to others. In the reverse case, it would indeed be a fault. What is further stated as 'seeing danger in the slightest faults, he undertakes and trains in the training rules' — by this, the characteristic of the virtue and benefit relating to oneself is declared. For what reason? Because if this one is endowed with proper conduct and range of activity, he would obtain the virtue and benefit relating to others. But moreover, having damaged his moral conduct, he would be reborn in bad destinies on account of that cause and condition, or he might become incapable of attaining what has not been attained, as before. But because he sees danger in the slightest faults, still more so in the major ones, and undertakes and trains in the training rules, therefore, on account of that cause and condition, at the breaking up of the body, he is reborn in a good destiny. He becomes capable

children.text: ) vā bhavatyaprāptasya prāptasya prāptaye pūrva[va]danena kāraṇenā dhyātmādhipateyo (a)yaṃ śīlasamvarasya guṇānuśaṃsa ityucyate ||
children.translated_text: of attaining what has not been attained, as before. For this reason, this is called the virtue and benefit of the <s>śīla</s> restraint relating to oneself.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the summary meaning? The summary meaning also has three characteristics by which the aggregate of moral conduct has been illuminated by the <s>Bhagavat</s> (Blessed One), namely:
