body.text: aparaḥ punaḥ paryāyaḥ [|] samāsato bhagavatā samādattaśīlatā paridīpitā, nairyāṇikaśīlatā ca, śīlabhāvanā ca [|] tatra yattāvadāha | śīlavānviharatītyanena samādattaśīlatākhyātā | yat punarāha | prātimokṣasamvarasaṃvṛta ityanena nairyāṇikaśīlatā ākhyātā [|] tathā hi prātimokṣasamvarasaṃgṛhītaṃ śīlamadhiśīlaṃ śikṣetyucyate | adhiśīlaṃ ca śikṣāṃ niśritya, adhicittaṃ ca, adhiprajñaṃ ca śikṣāṃ bhāvayatyevamasau sarvaduḥkhakṣayāya | niryāto bhavati | yadutādhiśīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya pūvvaṃgamaṃ kṛtvā tasmāt prātimokṣasaṃvaro nairyāṇikaṃ śīlamityucyate | yatpunarāha | ācāragocarasampannaḥ aṇumātreṣvavadyeṣu bhayadarśī samādāya śikṣate śikṣāpadeṣvanena śīlabhāvanā ākhyātā | ebhirākāraistatprātimokṣasamvaraśīlambhāvayitavyaṃ | evaṃ ca bhāvitaṃ subhāvitaṃ bhavatīti sa eṣa ekaḥ śīlasamvaraḥ ṣaḍākāradeśanāpratyupasthāno veditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: There is yet another manner of explanation. In summary, the <s>Bhagavat</s> has illuminated the undertaking of moral conduct, the moral conduct leading to liberation, and the cultivation of moral conduct. Therein, what is stated as 'he dwells endowed with moral conduct' — by this, the undertaking of moral conduct is declared. What is further stated as 'restrained by the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint' — by this, the moral conduct leading to liberation is declared. For the moral conduct included in the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is called the training in higher moral conduct. Relying on the training in higher moral conduct, and the training in higher mind, and the training in higher wisdom, he cultivates them — thus he proceeds toward the cessation of all suffering. That is to say, having established and made primary the higher moral conduct, therefore the <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint is called the moral conduct leading to liberation. What is further stated as 'endowed with proper conduct and range of activity, seeing danger in the slightest faults, he undertakes and trains in the training rules' — by this, the cultivation of moral conduct is declared. By these methods, that <s>prātimokṣa</s> restraint moral conduct is to be cultivated. And thus cultivated, it becomes well cultivated. This single <s>śīla</s> restraint should be understood as presented through a teaching of six aspects.

body.text: sa caiṣa śīlasamvaro daśabhirākārairvipanno (

children.translated_text: and conversely, as perfected through ten aspects.

body.translated_text: And this <s>śīla</s> restraint is to be understood as deficient through ten aspects,

body.text: katamairdaśabhiḥ kāraṇairvipanno bhavati | ādita eva durgṛhīto bhavatyatilīno bhavatyanisṛto bhavati, pramādakausīdyaparigṛhīto bhavati | mithyā praṇihito bhavati | ācāravipattyā parigṛhīto bhavatyājīvavipattyā parigṛhīto bhavatyantadvayapatito bhavati || anairyāṇiko bhavati | samādānaparibhraṣṭaśca bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Through which ten aspects does it become deficient? It is badly grasped from the very beginning; it is excessively lax; it is not properly entered into; it is seized by heedlessness and laziness; it is wrongly directed; it is seized by deficiency of conduct; it is seized by deficiency of livelihood; it falls into one of the two extremes; it does not lead to liberation; and it has fallen away from the undertaking.

body.text: tatra kathamādito durgṛhītaṃ śīlaṃ bhavati | yathāpī haikatyo rājābhinirṇīto vā, pravrajitaścaurābhinirṇīto vā, ṛṇārttovā, bhayārtto vā, vā, a(ā)jīvikābhayabhīto (

children.text: ) vā, na śrāmaṇyāya, na brāhmaṇyāya, nātmaśamāya, nātmadamāya, nātmaparinirvāṇāyaivamādita[ḥ |] duḥgṛhīto (durgṛhītaṃ) bhavati |
children.translated_text: or terrified by the fear of loss of livelihood — not for the sake of the ascetic life, not for the sake of the holy life, not for the sake of inner tranquility, not for the sake of self-discipline, not for the sake of one's own <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). In this way, it is badly grasped from the beginning.

body.translated_text: Therein, how is moral conduct badly grasped from the beginning? For example, a certain person has gone forth having been banished by the king, or has gone forth having been banished as a thief, or being oppressed by debt, or afflicted by fear,

body.text: kathamatilīno (naṃ) bhavati | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ alajjī bhavati mandakaukṛtyaḥ | śaithilikaḥ śithilakārī śikṣopadiṣṭe [a]yamatilīno (naṃ) bhavati ||
body.translated_text: How does one become <s>atilīna</s> (excessively lax)? When a certain person is shameless, has little remorse, is slack and careless in matters prescribed by the training — this person is excessively lax.

body.text: kathamatisṛto (taṃ) bhavati | yathāpīhaikatyo durgṛhītagrāhī bhavatyasthānakaukṛtyaḥ | saukṛtyakaraṇīyeṣu sthāneṣu kaukṛtyāyamānaḥ [|] asthāne pareṣāmantike paribhavacittaṃ vā ākhyātaṃ votpādayati | pravedayatyevamatisṛtaṃ (bhavati) |
body.translated_text: How does one become <s>atisṛta</s> (excessively scrupulous)? When a certain person grasps wrongly, having remorse where it is not warranted, feeling remorse in matters where one should feel satisfaction, and inappropriately, in the presence of others, either generates or makes known a thought of contempt — thus one becomes excessively scrupulous.

body.text: kathaṃ pramādakausīdyaparigṛhītaṃ bhavati | yathāpīhaikatyo [a]tītamadhvānamupādāyāpattimāpannaḥ [|] sā cānena smṛtisaṃpramoṣādekatyā na yathādharmaṃ pratikṛtā bhavati | yathā atītamadhvānamupādāya evamanāgataṃ vartamānamadhvānamupādāya yāmāpattimāpanno bhavati | sā cānena smṛtisaṃpramoṣādekatyā na yathādharmapratikṛtā bhavati | na ca pūrvamevāpatterāyatyāmanadhyāpattaye tīvramautsukyamāpadyate | yannvahaṃ tathā tathā careyaṃ, yathā yathā caran viharaṃścāpattiṃ nādhyāpadyeya, tathā ca, tathā carati, viharati | yathāpattimadhyāpadyate | so [a]nena (

children.text: ) pūrvāntasahagatenāparāntasahagatena, madhyāntasahagatena, pūrvakālakaraṇīyena sahānucareṇa pramādena samanvāgato nidrāsukhaṃ, śayanasukhaṃ, pārśvasukhaṃ ca svīkaroti | adakṣaśca bhavatyalasaḥ, anutthānasaṃpannaḥ, na kartā bhavati vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kāyena vaiyāpṛtyamevaṃ (vyāpṛtyaivaṃ) pramādakausīdyaparigṛhītaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: endowed with this heedlessness associated with the past, associated with the future, associated with the present, and accompanied by the failure to perform what should be done in earlier times — embraces the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying down, and the pleasure of reclining on one's side. And one becomes unskillful, lazy, lacking in initiative, and does not render physical service to one's wise fellow practitioners in the holy life. Thus one becomes seized by heedlessness and laziness.

body.translated_text: How does one become seized by <s>pramāda</s> (heedlessness) and <s>kausīdya</s> (laziness)? When a certain person, with regard to the past, has fallen into an offense, and some of those [offenses], due to loss of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), have not been remedied in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>; just as with regard to the past, so too with regard to the future and the present — whatever offense one has committed, some of those, due to loss of mindfulness, have not been remedied in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>; and one does not generate intense zeal for the future non-commission of offenses, [thinking:] 'Let me conduct myself in such a way that, while so conducting myself and dwelling, I would not commit an offense' — and yet one conducts oneself and dwells in a way that one does commit offenses. That person,

body.text: kathaṃ mithyāpraṇihitaṃ bhavati | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ praṇidhāya brahmacaryaṃ carati | anenāhaṃ śīlena vā, bratena vā, tapasā vā, brahmacaryavāsena vā, devo vā syāṃ, devānyatamo vā, lābha satkārakāmo bhavati | parataḥ lābhasatkāraṃ prārthayate | lābhasatkārasya spṛhayati | evaṃ mithyāpraṇihitaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become <s>mithyāpraṇihita</s> (wrongly directed)? When a certain person practices the holy life with [wrong] aspirations, [thinking:] 'By this moral conduct, or by this vow, or by this austerity, or by this celibate life, may I become a god, or one among the gods.' One desires gain and honor, seeks gain and honor from others, and craves gain and honor. Thus one becomes wrongly directed.

body.text: kathamācāravipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati | yathāpīhaikatya īryāpathaṃ vādhiṣṭhāya itikaraṇīyambā kuśalapakṣaprayogaṃ vā lokotkrāntaśca bhavati | vinayotkrāntaśca pūrvavadevamācāravipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become seized by <s>ācāravipatti</s> (failure of conduct)? When a certain person, while maintaining a posture or engaging in what should be done or in the practice of wholesome qualities, transgresses worldly [norms] and transgresses the <s>Vinaya</s> (monastic discipline) — as before, thus one becomes seized by failure of conduct.

children.translated_text: has great desires and is not content, is hard to satisfy, of a difficult-to-please nature. That person seeks robes by unrighteous means, not by righteous means; seeks almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick by unrighteous means, not by righteous means. And for the sake of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick, on account of others' estimation of one's qualities, one contrives an extraordinary, contrived deportment and displays to others an appearance of non-agitated senses, non-restless senses, and calm senses, so that others, having formed an estimation of one's qualities, think that one should be given and served — namely, with robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. And one becomes a crow-like [person], garrulous, bold, a jester, one who [pointedly] addresses others by name and clan. One becomes learned, a retainer of the <s>Dharma</s>, yet expounds the <s>Dharma</s> to others solely for the sake of gain, whether the words of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> or one's own virtues — some real, some superimposed — one becomes a self-proclaimer, or causes others to proclaim them, or displays them in a superior way. Desiring robes or any of the ascetic requisites, whether abundant or superior, even when not deprived [of the ordinary kind], one displays [discontent with] the ordinary robe.

children.text: ) bhavati | asyecchan śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayaḥ cīvareṇa vighātaṃ saṃlakṣayitvā (saṃlakṣya) prabhūtaṃ praṇītaṃ cīvaraṃ dātavyaṃ kartavyaṃ maṃsyate(nte) | yathā cīvaramevamanyatamānyatamaṃ śrāmaṇakaṃ jīvitapariṣkāraṃ śrāddhānāñca brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāmantikādyathākāmaṃ vā alabhamānaḥ, asatsu vā [a]saṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣvalabhamāna evaṃcoparodhena yācate | niṣpiṣya niṣpiyāmi (pi)caināṃ paruṣayatyapi hīnamvā punarlabdhvā tathā saṃvidyamāneṣu bhogeṣu taṃ lābhaṃ mansa (maṃsa) yatyavasādayati | saṃmukhaṃ ca dātāraṃ dānapatiṃ, evaṃ cāha [|] haṃ bhoḥ, kulaputra, santyeke kulaputrāḥ kuladuhitaraśca ye tavāntikā nīcakulīnatarāśca [daridratarāśca] te punarevaṃ caivañca praṇītadāyino mana āpadāyinaśca | kasmāttvaṃ teṣāmantikāduccakulīnatarāścānyataraśca samāna eva samanāpa (mana āpa)dāyī, nāpraṇītaparīttadāyī ceti | ya ebhirākauraḥ kuhanāmbā niśritya, lapanāmvā, naimittikatāmvā, naiṣpeṣikatāmvā, lābhena lābhaṃ niścikīrṣatāṃ, cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān parataḥ paryeṣate | so [a]dharmeṇa [|] yaḥ punaradharmeṇa so [a]sya bhavati mithyājīvaḥ | evaṃ tacchīlamājīvavipattyā parigṛhītaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: Devout householders, perceiving the deprivation of robes for this person, will think that abundant and excellent robes should be given and provided. Just as with robes, so too with any of the ascetic requisites for livelihood — from devout householders, not obtaining as much as desired, or when there are no available resources, not obtaining [what one wants], one begs with importunity, pressing and pressing, and even speaks harshly. Or again, having received an inferior [gift], when resources are available, one disparages that gift and depreciates it. And face to face with the donor, the lord of giving, one speaks thus: 'Well, good sir! There are certain sons and daughters of good family who are of lower birth than you and poorer, yet they give generously and are mind-pleasing. Why are you, being of higher birth and otherwise equal, not generous with excellent and ample gifts, but give only inferior and small ones?' Whoever, relying on these modes — <s>kuhanā</s> (deception), <s>lapanā</s> (flattery), <s>naimittikatā</s> (hinting), <s>naiṣpeṣikatā</s> (pressuring), and the desire to gain through [previous] gains — seeks robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick from others by unrighteous means — that is one's <s>mithyājīva</s> (wrong livelihood). Thus that moral conduct becomes seized by failure of livelihood.

body.translated_text: How does one become seized by <s>ājīvavipatti</s> (failure of livelihood)? When a certain person

body.text: kathamantadvayapatitaṃ bhavati | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ (

children.text: ) kāmasukhallikānuyukto bhavatyadhyavasitatāṃparaḥ | pratilabdhāndharmeṇa vā adharmeṇa vā cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārān paribhuṅkte | ādīnavādarśī niḥsaraṇamaprajānannayamucyate eko [a]ntaḥ | punaraparamihaikatya ātmaklamathānuyukto bhavatyanekaparyāyeṇātmānamātāpayati, santāpayati | kaṣṭavratasamādāyī ca bhavati | tadyathā kaṇṭakāpāśrayo vā bhavati | bhasmādāyī musalāpāśrayaḥ | phalakāpāśrayo bhavati | utkuhakasthito bhavatyutkuhakaprahāṇayogamanuyuktaḥ [|] agniparicārako bhavati | yāvat trirapyagniṃ parica[rati] udakamadhyāhāro bhavati | yāvat trirapyudakamadhyāvai(va)hati | ekapādakaḥ sthitvā yataḥ sūryastataḥ parivartate | iti yo vā punarapyevaṃbhāgīya ātmakaklamathānuyogaḥ ayamucyate dvitīyo [a]ntaḥ | e[vamanta]dvayapatitaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: is devoted to the pursuit of sensual pleasure, intent upon indulgence, and enjoys robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick obtained by righteous or unrighteous means, not seeing the danger [in them], not understanding the escape — this is called the first extreme. Furthermore, here a certain person is devoted to self-mortification and torments and afflicts himself in many ways, and undertakes harsh vows. For example, one rests on thorns, or sits on ashes, or rests on a pestle, or rests on a plank; one stands in the squatting posture, engaged in the practice of abandoning the squatting posture; one tends the fire, and tends the fire up to three times; one takes food in the middle of water, and enters the water up to three times; standing on one foot, one turns toward wherever the sun is. Any such self-mortification practice of this kind — this is called the second extreme. Thus one becomes fallen into the two extremes.

body.translated_text: How does one become fallen into the two extremes (<s>antadvayapatita</s>)? When a certain person

body.translated_text: How does one become <s>anairyāṇika</s> (not conducive to liberation)? When a certain person grasps at moral conduct or vows with [wrong] views, [thinking:] 'By this very moral conduct, or by this very vow, there will be purification, there will be liberation, there will be deliverance'

body.text: kathaṃ samādānaparibhraṣṭaṃ bhavati | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ sarveṇa sarvamalajjī bha bhavati nirapekṣaḥ | śrāmaṇye sa ca bhavati | duḥśīlaḥ pāpadharmā antaḥ pūtiravasrutaḥ kaśambodakajātaḥ | śaṃkhasvarasamācāraḥ | aśramaṇa[ḥ] śramaṇapratijñaḥ abrahmacārī brahmacāripratijña evaṃ samādānaparibhraṣṭaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become <s>samādānaparibhraṣṭa</s> (fallen from one's undertaking)? When a certain person is completely shameless and without regard for the renunciant life, and becomes one of bad moral conduct, of evil qualities, inwardly rotten and oozing, of the nature of refuse-water, whose conduct is like the sound of a conch — not a renunciant though claiming to be a renunciant, not a celibate though claiming to be a celibate. Thus one becomes fallen from one's undertaking.

body.text: ebhirdaśabhiḥ kāraṇairvipanna (nnaṃ)śīlaṃ śīlavipattirityuktā bhagavatā [|]
body.translated_text: By these ten causes, moral conduct that is ruined constitutes <s>śīlavipatti</s> (moral failure) — so it was declared by the Blessed One.

children.translated_text: In some places, the Blessed One has spoken of <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) using the term 'root.' As it is said:

body.translated_text: Moreover, the practice of moral conduct was also taught by the Blessed One. And from among these causes, it should be understood through two causes: that which is not conducive to liberation and the falling away from one's undertaking — by these and the other causes, it should be understood as moral failure itself. And the bright counterparts of these very causes, which are established in the dark side, should be understood as <s>śīlasampattti</s> (moral accomplishment) through causes of the bright side, and as moral purification.

body.text: supratiṣṭhitamūla[ḥ] syāccittasyopaśame rataḥ |
body.translated_text: 'One should be well-established in the root, delighting in the calming of the mind,

And furthermore, it is said: 'One of moral conduct dwells restrained by the <s>Prātimokṣa</s> (monastic code) restraint' — and so forth in detail.

body.translated_text: In some places, it is spoken of using the term 'ornament.' As it is said: 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun) endowed with the ornament of moral conduct abandons the unwholesome and cultivates the wholesome.' In some places, it is spoken of using the term 'ointment.' Where it is said: 'A <s>bhikṣu</s> or <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> endowed with the ointment of moral conduct' — as before. In some places, it is spoken of using the term 'fragrance.' 'There is that gift which is of the nature of fragrance, whose scent wafts with the wind, against the wind, and with the wind.' In some places, it is spoken of using the term 'good conduct.' Where it is said: 'The result of good bodily conduct is desirable,

body.text: kena kāraṇena bhagavatā śīlaṃ mūlaśabdenoktam | pratiṣṭhārthaṃ ādhārārtho mūlārthaḥ | taccaitacchīlaṃ sarveṣāmeva laukikalokottarāṇāṃ [śuddhānā]manavadyānāmagryāṇāṃ pravarāṇāṃ sukhāhārāṇāṃ, pratiṣṭhāsthānīyaṃ cotpattaye, pratilaṃbhāya tasmānmūlaśabdenocyate | tadyathā pṛthivī pratiṣṭhā bhavatyādhāra[stṛṇagu]lmauṣadhivanaspatīnāmutpattaye evameva śīlambistareṇa pūrvavadvācyam |
body.translated_text: For what reason has the Blessed One spoken of <s>śīla</s> using the term 'root'? The meaning of 'root' is the meaning of foundation, of support. This moral conduct serves as the foundation for the arising and attainment of all worldly and supramundane [qualities that are] pure, blameless, supreme, excellent, and conducive to happiness. Therefore it is spoken of using the term 'root.' Just as the earth serves as the foundation and support for the arising of grasses, bushes, herbs, and forest trees — in exactly the same way, moral conduct [should be understood] — to be elaborated as before.

children.translated_text: endowed with fresh youthfulness — so long do those ornaments, when worn, produce a measure of beauty. But not so for one who is aged, old, advanced in years, eighty or ninety, with broken teeth and grey hair — on the contrary, wearing those ornaments, one appears as if ridiculed. And when calamity of health, or calamity of wealth, or calamity of kinsmen is present, they do not look beautiful. But moral conduct produces beauty for all persons, at all times. Therefore it is spoken of using the term 'ornament.'

body.translated_text: For what reason is <s>śīla</s> declared using the term 'ornament'? He says: Those other ornaments — necklaces, bracelets, armlets, rings, garlands of gold and silver — as long as a person is young, a youth, with black hair,

body.text: kena kāraṇenaśīlamanulepanaśabdenoktam | tatra bahukuśalamanavadyaṃ śīlasamādānaṃ sarvadauḥśīlyasamādānahetukaṃ kāyaparidāhaṃ cittaparidāhaṃ apanayati | gharmābhitaptasya uttamagrīṣmaparidāhe kāle pratyupasthite candanānulepanaṃ vā karpūrānulepanaṃ vā anena kāraṇena śīlamanulepanaśabdenocyate ||
body.translated_text: For what reason is <s>śīla</s> spoken of using the term 'ointment'? Therein, the undertaking of moral conduct that is abundantly wholesome and blameless removes the burning of body and the burning of mind caused by all [forms of] immorality. Just as, for one scorched by heat, when the time of the supreme summer heat has arrived, an ointment of sandalwood or an ointment of camphor [provides relief] — for this reason, moral conduct is spoken of using the term 'ointment.'

body.text: kena kāraṇena śīlaṃ gandhajātaśabdenocyate | śīlavataḥ khalu puruṣapudgalasya digvidikṣu kalyāṇaḥ (ṇaṃ) kīrttiyaśaḥ śabdaśloko niścarati | vividhānāmvā mūlagandhajātānāṃ, sāragandhajātānāmvā, puṣpagandhānāmvāteritānāṃ digvidikṣu mana āpo gandho niścarati | anena kāraṇena śīlaṃ gandhajātaśabdenocyate ||
body.translated_text: For what reason is <s>śīla</s> (moral conduct) designated by the word <s>gandhajāta</s> (fragrance)? Indeed, the good reputation, fame, glory, renown, and acclaim of a person endowed with <s>śīla</s> spread in all directions. Or, just as the fragrance of various root-fragrances, heartwood-fragrances, or flower-fragrances, when carried by the wind, spreads in all directions — for this reason <s>śīla</s> is designated by the word <s>gandhajāta</s>.

body.text: kena kāraṇena śīlaṃ sucaritaśabdenocyate | sukhagāminī eṣā caryā svargagāminī sugatigāminī / (
body.translated_text: For what reason is <s>śīla</s> designated by the word <s>sucarita</s> (good conduct)? This conduct leads to happiness, this conduct leads to heaven, leads to good destinations;

body.text: kena kāraṇena śīlaṃ samvaraśabdenocyate | nivṛttisvabhāva eṣa dharmo nivṛttilakṣaṇo viratisvabhāvaḥ | tasmāt samvaraśabdenocyate | asya khalu śīlasamvarasya trividhā pratyavekṣā pariśuddhinimittaṃ [|] katamā trividhā [|] yaduta kāyakarmapratyavekṣā, vākkarmapratyavekṣā, manaḥkarmapratyavekṣā |
body.translated_text: For what reason is <s>śīla</s> designated by the word <s>saṃvara</s> (restraint)? This <s>dharma</s> has the nature of cessation, has the characteristic of cessation, has the nature of abstention (<s>virati</s>). Therefore it is designated by the word <s>saṃvara</s>. Indeed, the examination of this <s>śīlasamvara</s> (moral restraint) for the sake of purification is threefold. What threefold? Namely: the examination of bodily action (<s>kāyakarma</s>), the examination of verbal action (<s>vākkarma</s>), and the examination of mental action (<s>manaḥkarma</s>).

body.text: tatra ca punaretāni
body.translated_text: And there, examining these actions, one purifies the <s>śīlasamvara</s>. Whatever action one has resolved to perform with the body, that very [action]

children.translated_text: one does not withdraw from; one pursues it. Whatever bodily action one has performed in the past — that too one frequently examines: 'Was this harmful to me?' as before. If, examining thus among the wise fellow practitioners in the spiritual life (<s>sabrahmacārin</s>), one knows 'this action of mine was harmful,' as before, one withdraws before the wise fellow practitioners; one does not pursue it. Whatever bodily action one has performed taking from the past — that too one frequently examines: 'Was this harmful to me?' as before. If, examining thus among the wise fellow practitioners, one knows 'this action of mine was harmful,' as before — one confesses (<s>pratideśayati</s>) before the wise fellow practitioners and makes amends according to the <s>Dharma</s>. But if, examining thus, one knows 'this bodily action of mine was not harmful,' as before — then with that very joy and gladness (<s>prītiprāmodya</s>), one dwells, training day and night, abiding abundantly. Thus one's bodily action is well-examined and well-purified — namely, in regard to past, future, and present time-periods. As with bodily action, so verbal action should be understood. The mind arises dependent on past formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>); the mind arises dependent on future and present formations. That mind too one frequently examines: 'Is this mind of mine harmful?' as before.

children.translated_text: Until one does not generate [the unwholesome mental action], one withdraws from it; one does not pursue it. But the wholesome mental action one generates, does not withdraw from, and pursues. Thus one's mental action is examined and well-purified — namely, in regard to past, future, and present time-periods. For what reason? Because in the past, future, and present, whatever <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) or <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (brahmins) have purified themselves by examining bodily, verbal, and mental action, and have abundantly dwelt [in purity] — all of them have done so by examining and purifying in this manner. As was stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) with reference to the venerable <s>Rāhula</s>:

One does not perform that action; one does not pursue it. But if one knows 'this bodily action of mine is not harmful, is wholesome,' as before, one performs it. That bodily action

children.text: ) pratyavekṣamāṇaḥ aviprati[sāraṃ pra]tilabhate | avipratisāriṇaḥ prāmodyaṃ pramuditacittasya prītirjāyate | prītamanasaḥ kāyaḥpraśrabhyate | praśrabdhakāyaḥ sukhaṃ vedayate | sukhitasya cittaṃ samādhīyate | samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | yathābhūtaṃ paśyati | yathābhūtaṃ jānan paśyannirvidyate [|] nirviṇṇo virajyate, virakto vimucyate, vimuktasya vimukti[ḥ] smṛtirjñā(vimuktijñā)nadarśanaṃ bhavati | yāvannirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāti | yacchīlavān puruṣapudgalaḥ śīlaviśuddhaydhiyateyamavipratisāraṃ pratilabhate | anupūrveṇa yāvannirvāṇagamanāyāyaṃ prathamaḥ śīlānuśansaḥ (śaṃsaḥ) | punaraparaṃ śīlavāṃ (vān) puruṣapudgalaḥ maraṇakālasamaye pratyupasthite, kṛtaṃ etanme sūktaṃ ta [......] (sucaritaṃ) kāyena vācā manasā na kṛtaṃ etanme duścaritaṃ kāyena pūrvavat | iti yā gatiḥ | kṛtapuṇyānāṃ kṛtakuśalānāṃ kṛtabhayabhīrūprāṇānāṃ tāṃ gatiṃ pretya gamiṣyāmīti dvitīyamavipratisāraṃ pratilabhate (|) sugatigamanāya, avipratisāriṇo hi puruṣapudgalasya bhadrakaṃ maraṇaṃ bhavati | bhadrikā kālakriyā bhadrako [a]bhisamparāyaḥ | ayaṃ dvitīyaḥ śīlānuśansaḥ (śaṃsaḥ) ||
children.translated_text: and obtains freedom from remorse (<s>avipratisāra</s>). For one free from remorse, gladness arises; for one whose mind is gladdened, joy (<s>prīti</s>) arises; for one whose mind is joyful, the body becomes tranquil (<s>praśrabdhi</s>); with a tranquil body, one experiences happiness (<s>sukha</s>); for one who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated (<s>samādhi</s>); with a concentrated mind, one knows things as they really are; one sees things as they really are; knowing and seeing things as they really are, one becomes disenchanted (<s>nirvid</s>); being disenchanted, one becomes dispassionate (<s>virakta</s>); being dispassionate, one is liberated (<s>vimukta</s>); for the liberated one, there arises the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s>); until one attains final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (realm of <s>nirvāṇa</s>) without remainder (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa</s>). That a person endowed with <s>śīla</s> rejoices in the purity of <s>śīla</s> and obtains freedom from remorse, progressing step by step up to the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> — this is the first benefit of <s>śīla</s>. Furthermore, a person endowed with <s>śīla</s>, when the time of death is at hand, [reflects:] 'I have done what is well-spoken, what is well-conducted with body, speech, and mind; I have not done what is ill-conducted with body,' as before. [Thinking:] 'The destination that those who have made merit, done what is wholesome, who are those for whom fear is [already] allayed, proceed to after death — to that destination I too shall go' — thus one obtains a second freedom from remorse, for going to a good destination. For a person free from remorse, death is auspicious, the passing away is auspicious, the future state is auspicious. This is the second benefit of <s>śīla</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, the ten benefits (<s>anuśaṃsa</s>) of the thus-purified <s>śīlasamvara</s>

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person endowed with <s>śīla</s>, even when asleep, is protected by the <s>devas</s> (gods). This is the fifth benefit of <s>śīla</s>.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person endowed with <s>śīla</s> is not suspicious of evil from others, nor is one fearful with a terrified mind. This is the sixth benefit of <s>śīla</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ śīlavāṃ(vān) puruṣapudgalaḥ badhakānāṃ pratyarthikānāmapi pra--trāṇāṃ chidraprāpto [a]pi rakṣyo bhavati | sarvadāyaṃ puruṣapudgala iti viditvā mitratāmvāpadyante (te) madhyamasthatāmvā[|]ayaṃ saptamaḥ śīlānuśansaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, a person endowed with <s>śīla</s>, even when vulnerable to enemies and adversaries, is protected. Having learned that 'this person is [virtuous],' they become friendly or at least neutral. This is the seventh benefit of <s>śīla</s>.

body.text: punaraparaṃ pūrvabahvāsthānānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ nivāsikānāmamanuṣyāṇāṃ chidraprāpto [a]pi rakṣyo bhavati | yaduta tadeva śīlamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā [|] ayamaṣṭamaḥ śīlānuśansaḥ (śaṃsaḥ) ||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, even when vulnerable to <s>yakṣas</s>, resident non-human beings of long standing, one is protected — namely, by making that very <s>śīla</s> one's ruler. This is the eighth benefit of <s>śīla</s>.

children.translated_text: and by being free from passion everywhere — this should be known as the tenth benefit of <s>śīla</s>.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, as before, all aspirations are fulfilled. If one aspires [to be reborn] in the families of <s>Kṣatriya</s> great householders, or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> great householders, or householder great householders in the desire realm, or among the gods of the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> heaven, or of the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s>, <s>Yāma</s>, <s>Tuṣita</s>, <s>Nirmāṇarati</s>, or <s>Paranirmitavaśavartin</s> gods — to be reborn in their company — because of the purity of one's moral observances, 'Having also attained the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions), may I dwell happily in this very life; and may I be reborn in the company of the gods of the form realm' — this aspiration of one endowed with <s>śīla</s> and free from passion is fulfilled. If one aspires: '... the liberations ... may I attain and dwell; or may I be reborn in the company of the gods of the formless realm,' as before. If one aspires: 'May I attain the ultimate final <s>nirvāṇa</s>' — one attains it. By the purity of one's moral conduct

body.text: nirdiṣṭaḥ śīlaskandho vibhāgaśaḥ, nirdiṣṭā vipattisampattiḥ | nirdiṣṭāni paryāyanāmāni | nirdiṣṭā pariśuddhipratyavekṣā, nirdiṣṭo [a]nuśaṃsaḥ ||
body.translated_text: The aggregate of moral conduct (<s>śīlaskandha</s>) has been set forth in its divisions; the failure and success have been set forth; the synonymous names have been set forth; the examination for purification has been set forth; the benefits have been set forth.

body.text: sa eṣa sarvākāraparipūrṇaḥ śīlasamvaraḥ saṃbhāraparigṛhīta ākhyātaḥ kathimo (to) vivṛtaḥ prakāśito yatrātmakāmaiḥ śrāmaṇyabrāhmaṇyakāmaiḥ kulaputraiḥ śikṣitavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: This <s>śīlasamvara</s>, complete in all aspects and accompanied by its provisions, has been declared, described, disclosed, and illuminated — wherein sons of good family who desire their own welfare and who desire the state of <s>śramaṇa</s> (asceticism) and <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (holiness) should train.

body.text: || uddānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: The analysis should be known as threefold; success is tenfold;
the synonyms are sixfold; purification is considered threefold;
the benefits are tenfold — this is the <s>śīlasamvara</s> (moral restraint).

Therein, how does one dwell with the doors of the sense faculties guarded, with mindfulness safeguarded, with alert mindfulness? — in detail, up to: one guards the mind faculty, the mind faculty. One so attains; thus one dwells with the doors of the sense faculties guarded.

body.translated_text: What is <s>indriyasamvara</s> (restraint of the sense faculties)? Just as here a certain person

body.text: tatra kathamārakṣitasmṛtirbhavati | yathāpīhaikatyenendriyaguptadvāratāmevādhipatiṃ kṛtvā śrutamudgṛhītaṃ bhavati | cintitamvā punarbhāvitamvā | tena ca śrutacintābhāvanādhipateyā smṛtiḥ pratilabdhā bhavati | (

children.text: ) sa tasyā eva smṛteḥ pratilabdhāyāḥ asaṃpramoṣārthamadhigamārthamavināśārthaṃ kālena kālaṃ tasminneva śrute yogaṃ karotyabhyāsaṃ karoti, cintāyāṃbhāvanāyāṃ yogamabhyāsaṃ karoti | na bhavati sa sta prayogā yi-kṛta prayoga evamanena tasyā[ḥ] śrutasamudāgamatā(gatā) yāścintā-samudāgatāyāḥ smṛteḥ kālena kālaṃ śrutacintābhāvanāyogakriyāyā ārakṣā kṛtā bhavati | evamārakṣitasmṛtirbhavati |
children.translated_text: He, for the purpose of not losing, of realizing, and of not destroying that very <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) once it has been obtained, from time to time applies himself and practices with respect to that very learned [teaching] — he applies himself and practices in reflection (<s>cintā</s>) and cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). He is not one whose effort has been [merely] commenced. In this way, the guard of the <s>smṛti</s> that has arisen from learning (<s>śruta</s>) and that has arisen from reflection (<s>cintā</s>) is maintained by him through the practice of learning, reflection, and cultivation from time to time. Thus he becomes one whose <s>smṛti</s> is guarded (<s>ārakṣitasmṛti</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, how does one have safeguarded mindfulness? Just as here, a certain person, making the guarding of the doors of the sense faculties the governing principle, has learned what has been heard, or reflected upon, or cultivated. And through that hearing, reflection, and meditation as the governing principle, mindfulness is obtained.

children.text: ) smṛtau balādhānaprāpto bhavati | yena śakto bhavati pratibalaśca rūpāṇāmabhibhavāya śabdānāṃ, gandhānāṃ, rasānāṃ, spraṣṭavyānāṃ, dharmāṇāmabhibhavāya |
children.translated_text: he reaches the point of empowerment (<s>balādhāna</s>), by which he becomes capable and strong enough to overcome forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: How does one become one of discerning <s>smṛti</s> (<s>nipakasmṛti</s>)? He is one who constantly applies himself to that very <s>smṛti</s>. [And he is one who applies himself to accomplishment.] Therein, constant application is called <s>sātatyakāritā</s> (continuity of practice). And therein, application to accomplishment is called <s>satkṛtyakāritā</s> (practice with earnestness). One who thus practices continuously and earnestly is called one of discerning <s>smṛti</s> (<s>nipakasmṛti</s>). He thus becomes one whose <s>smṛti</s> is guarded. Thus he does not lose that <s>smṛti</s>. He thus becomes one of discerning <s>smṛti</s>. And when that <s>smṛti</s> is thus unimpaired,

body.text: kathaṃ smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati | cakṣuḥ pratītya rūpāṇi cotpadyate | cakṣurvi[jñānaṃ, ca]-kṣurvijñānānantaramutpadyate | vikalpakaṃ manovijñānaṃ yena vikalpakena manovijñānena priyarūpeṣu rūpeṣu saṃrajyate | apriyarūpeṣu rūpeṣu vyāpadyate [|] sa bhā (tā)mevādhipatiṃ kṛtvā tasmādayoniśo vikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakāttasmāt saṃrakṣati | yathā saṃkleśo notpadyate | evaṃ śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ jihvāṃ kāyaṃ manaḥ pratītya dharmāścotpadyate manovijñānaṃ | tacca manovijñānamasyāyoniśevikalpasahagataṃ saṃkleśasamutthāpakaṃ | yena priyarūpeṣu dharmeṣu saṃrajyate | apriyarūpeṣu dharmeṣu vyāpadyate | sa tasmādayoniśovikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakāttanmānasaṃ rakṣatyevamasya saṃkleśo notpadyate | evaṃ smṛtyārakṣitamānasobhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become one whose mind is guarded by <s>smṛti</s> (<s>smṛtyārakṣitamānasa</s>)? Depending on the eye and forms, eye-consciousness arises. Immediately after the eye-consciousness, there arises a conceptualizing mind-consciousness (<s>vikalpakaṃ manovijñānam</s>), by which conceptualizing mind-consciousness one becomes attached to pleasant forms and develops aversion toward unpleasant forms. Making that [mind-consciousness] the governing [factor], he guards [himself] from that improper conceptualization (<s>ayoniśo vikalpa</s>) that gives rise to affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>), so that affliction does not arise. Likewise, depending on the ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind, and <s>dharmas</s>, mind-consciousness arises. And that mind-consciousness, accompanied by his improper conceptualization, gives rise to affliction, by which he becomes attached to pleasant <s>dharmas</s> and develops aversion toward unpleasant <s>dharmas</s>. He guards his mind from that improper conceptualization that gives rise to affliction — thus affliction does not arise for him. In this way, one becomes one whose mind is guarded by <s>smṛti</s>.

body.text: kathaṃ samāvasthāvacārako bhavati | samāvasthocyate | upekṣā kuśalā vā, avyākṛtā vā [|] sa tasmādayoniśo vikalpāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakāt tanmānasaṃ rakṣitvā kuśalāyāmvā upekṣāyāmavyākṛtāyāmvā avacārayati | (

children.translated_text: Therefore he is called one who conducts [oneself] in equanimity. Thus one becomes one who conducts [oneself] in equanimity.

body.translated_text: How does one become one who conducts [oneself] in equanimity (<s>samāvasthāvacāraka</s>)? Equanimity (<s>samāvasthā</s>) is said to be <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), whether wholesome or indeterminate. Having guarded his mind from that improper conceptualization that gives rise to affliction, he conducts [himself] in either wholesome or indeterminate equanimity.

body.text: kathaṃ punastasmādayoniśo vikalpasaṃkleśasamutthāpakān mānasaṃ rakṣati | na nimittagrāhī bhavati | teṣu rūpeṣu, śabdeṣu, gandheṣu, raseṣu, spraṣṭavyeṣu, dharmeṣu nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī bhavati yato [a]dhikaraṇamasya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāścittamanusraveyuḥ | sa cet punaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣāt kleśapracuratayā vā vivarjayato [a]pi nimittagrāhama(ho ')nuvyaṃjanagrāha[ḥ sa]mutpadyate eva | pāpakā akuśalāto duḥgṛhīto (pāpakādakuśalato durgṛhīto) bhavati ke (ye) dharmā anusarantyeva | cittaṃ teṣāṃ samvarāya pratipadyate | ābhyāṃ dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ tasmāt saṃkleśasamutthāpakādayoniśovikalpāttanmānasaṃ rakṣitaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: And how does one guard the mind from that improper conceptualization that gives rise to affliction? One does not grasp at the sign (<s>nimitta</s>). With respect to those forms, sounds, smells, tastes, tangibles, and <s>dharmas</s>, one does not grasp at the secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> would flow into the mind. If, however, through loss of <s>smṛti</s> or through the intensity of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), even while avoiding [them], grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics nevertheless arise, and [the mind] is badly grasped by evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that do flow [into it], one undertakes restraint (<s>saṃvara</s>) of the mind with respect to them. By these two modes, the mind is guarded from that improper conceptualization that gives rise to affliction.

body.text: kathaṃ ca punastanmānasamābhyāmākārābhyāṃ saraṃkṣya kuśalāyāmvā upekṣāyāmavadhārayatyavyā kṛtāyāmvā [|] dvābhyāmevākārābhyāṃ [|] katamābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ [|] yathāha rakṣati cakṣurindriyaṃ cakṣurindriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | yathā cakṣurindriyaṃ cakṣurindriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | me (e)vaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyāṃ (yān), rakṣati mana indriyaṃ mana indriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | ābhyāṃ dvābhyomākārābhyāṃ kuśalāyāmvā, avyākṛtāyāmvā upekṣāyāṃ tanmānasameva cārayati ||
body.translated_text: And how, having guarded the mind by these two modes, does one establish it in wholesome or indeterminate equanimity? By these same two modes. Which two? As it is said: 'One guards the eye-faculty and undertakes restraint by means of the eye-faculty.' Just as one guards the eye-faculty and undertakes restraint by means of the eye-faculty, so too [with] the ear, nose, tongue, and body [faculties]. 'One guards the mind-faculty and undertakes restraint by means of the mind-faculty.' By these two modes, one conducts the mind in either wholesome or indeterminate equanimity.

body.text: kathaṃ cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu na nimittagrāhī bhavati | nimittagrāha ucyate | yaccakṣurvijñānagocaro rūpe tasya gocarasya grāhī bhavati | cakṣurvijñānena [|] evaṃ nimittagrāhī bhavati | yaduta cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu śrotraghrāṇajih vākāyamanovijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu aparā jāti[r] nimittaṃ | sa cet punastaṃ gocaraṃ parivarjayati | cakṣurvijñānasyaivaṃ na (ca) na nimittagrāhī [bha]vati | cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣvevaṃ śrotra ghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu [|]
body.translated_text: How does one not grasp at the sign with respect to forms cognizable by the eye? Grasping at the sign (<s>nimittagrāha</s>) is said to be: when one grasps the object that is the domain of eye-consciousness with respect to form, through eye-consciousness — thus one grasps at the sign. Namely, with respect to forms cognizable by eye-consciousness, and with respect to forms cognizable by ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-consciousness, there is another kind of sign. If one avoids that domain of eye-consciousness, then one does not grasp at the sign. [This applies] with respect to forms cognizable by the eye, and similarly with respect to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind.

body.text: kathaṃ nānuvyaṃjanagrāhībhavati | cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu [|] anuvyaṃjanagrāha ucyate | yasteṣvevacakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu cakṣurvijñānasyaiva samanantarasahotpannasya vikalpakasya manovijñānasya yo gocaraḥ saṃrāgāya vā, saṃdveṣāya, vā saṃmohāya vā taṃ gocaraṃ parivarjayati | notpādayati tadālambanaṃ | tanmanovijñānamevaṃ nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī bhavati | yaduta cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu [|] evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajih vākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu aparā jātirnimittagrāhasyānuvyaṃjanagrāhasya ca | tatra nimittagrāho yaccakṣuṣā rupāṇyābhāsagatāni tajjaṃ manaskāraṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya paśyati [|] tatrānuvyaṃjanagrāhaḥ | tānyeva rūpāṇi cakṣuṣā ābhāsagatāni tajjaṃ manasikāraṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya paśyati | apitu parato [a]nusravapūrvakaṃ (

children.text: ) śrṛṇoti | santyevaṃ rūpāṇyevaṃ rūpāṇi cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇīti yāni tāni tadanugatāni nāmāni padāni vyaṃjanāni [yānya]dhipatiṃ kṛtvā, yāni niśritya pratiṣṭhāyāyaṃ puruṣapudgalaḥ yathāśrutāni cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi vikalpayatyayamucyate | anuvyaṃjanagrāhaḥ [|] yathā cakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu, evaṃ śrotraghrāṇajih vākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu veditavyaḥ | sa punarayaṃ nimittagrāho [a]nuvyaṃjanagrāhaśca asti yannidānamasya yadadhikaraṇaṃ yadadhipateyaṃ asya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāścittamanusravanti | asti yacca tannidānaṃ ca tadadhikaraṇaṃ ca tadadhipateyaṃ pāpakā akuśalā dharmā ścittamanusravanti | tatra yo [a]yaṃ nimittagrāho [a]nuvyaṃjanagrāho ayoniśogrāhaḥ yannidānaṃ yadadhikaraṇaṃ yadadhipateyamasya pāpakā akuśalā dharmāścittamanusravanti | tadrūpamasau nimittagrāhamanuvyaṃjanagrāhaṃ ca parivarjayati |
children.translated_text: one hears: 'There are such and such forms cognizable by the eye' — those names, words, and syllables that follow after them, making them the governing [factor], relying on which this person conceptualizes the forms cognizable by the eye as they have been heard — this is called grasping at the secondary characteristics. Just as with forms cognizable by the eye, so too it should be understood with respect to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. Furthermore, this grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics: there is that which is the cause, the basis, and the governing condition on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind; and there is that cause, basis, and governing condition on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind. Therein, this grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics is improper grasping — that which is the cause, the basis, the governing condition on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> flow into the mind. He avoids that form of grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics.

body.translated_text: How does one not grasp at the secondary characteristics with respect to forms cognizable by the eye? Grasping at the secondary characteristics (<s>anuvyañjanagrāha</s>) is said to be: with respect to those very forms cognizable by the eye, the domain of the conceptualizing mind-consciousness that arises immediately after and together with the eye-consciousness, [which domain serves] for attachment, aversion, or delusion — one avoids that domain. One does not generate [a cognition] with that as object. In this way, that mind-consciousness does not grasp at the secondary characteristics with respect to forms cognizable by the eye. Similarly with respect to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind. There is another distinction between grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics: grasping at the sign is when, with the eye, one sees forms that have come into appearance, directing attention born from that [perception]. Grasping at the secondary characteristics is when one sees those very forms that have come into appearance through the eye, directing attention born from that, and furthermore, preceded by hearing from others,

body.text: pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ katame [|] rāgaḥ, rāgasamutthāpitaṃ kāyaduścaritaṃ, vāgduścaritaṃ, manoduścaritaṃ | dveṣo, mohaḥ [|], mohasamutthāpitaṃ ca kāyaduścaritaṃ, vāgduścaritaṃ, manoduścaritamima ucyante pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ |
body.translated_text: What are evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>? <s>Rāga</s> (attachment), and bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct arising from <s>rāga</s>; <s>dveṣa</s> (aversion); <s>moha</s> (delusion), and bodily misconduct, verbal misconduct, and mental misconduct arising from <s>moha</s> — these are called evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.text: kathamete cittamanusravanti | yadālambanaṃ cittamanovijñānamutpadyate | gacchati pratisarati | tadālambanāstadālambanāstena cittamanovijñānena saṃprayuktāḥ [ḥ] kāyavāṅmanoduścaritasamutthāpakā[s] te rāgadveṣamohā utpadyante, gacchanti pratisaranti | tenocyante (te) cittamanupravanti ||
body.translated_text: How do these flow into the mind? When, with reference to an object, mind-consciousness arises, goes, and proceeds, then those [afflictions] — <s>rāga</s>, <s>dveṣa</s>, and <s>moha</s>, which give rise to bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct, and which are associated with and take the same object as that mind-consciousness — arise, go, and proceed. Therefore they are said to flow into the mind.

body.text: evaṃ tāvannimittagrāheṇānuvyaṃjanagrāheṇa ca ya utpadyate, saṃkleśaścakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu yāvanmanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu so [a]sya notpadyate nimittagrāhamanuvyaṃjanagrāhaṃ ca parivarjayataḥ [|] sa cet punaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣādvā, kleśapracuratayā vā, ekākino [a]pi viharataḥ pūrvadṛṣṭāni cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇyadhipatiṃ kṛtvā pūrvānubhūtāṃ (tān) śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñeyān dharmānadhipatiṃ kṛtvotpadyante pāpakā akuśalā dharmā[s] tānutpannānadhivāsayati, prajahāti, viśodhayati, vyantīkaroti | tenocyate teṣāṃ samvarāya pratipadyate |
body.translated_text: Thus, firstly, the affliction that arises through grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics with respect to forms cognizable by the eye, up to <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by the mind — that does not arise for one who avoids grasping at the sign and grasping at the secondary characteristics. If, however, through loss of <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) or through intensity of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), even while dwelling alone, evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> arise on the basis of previously seen forms cognizable by the eye, or on the basis of previously experienced <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind — he does not tolerate them [once] arisen, but abandons them, purifies them, and eliminates them. Therefore it is said: 'He undertakes restraint with respect to them.'

body.text: sa yeṣu rūpeṣu cakṣuḥ prerayitavyaṃ bhavati | yeṣu śrotraghrāṇajih vākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dharmeṣu manaḥ prerayitavyaṃ (

children.text: ) bhavati | teṣu tathā prerayati | yathā na saṃkliśyate | evamanena tasmāt saṃkleśānmana[indriyaṃ] rakṣitaṃ bhavati | tenocyate rakṣati mana indriyaṃ | yeṣu punaścakṣurvijñeyeṣu rūpeṣu cakśurindriyaṃ na prerayitavyaṃ bhavati | yeṣu śrotraghrāṇajih vākāyamanovijñeyeṣu dha[rmeṣu] mana indriyaṃ na prerayitavyaṃ bhavati | teṣu sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā na prerayati | tenocyatecakṣurindriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | tenocyate yāvanmana indriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | ayaṃ tāvadvibhaṃgo vistareṇendriyasamvarasya vijñeya[ḥ] |
children.translated_text: he directs [his faculties] toward them in such a way that he is not afflicted. In this way, the mind-faculty is guarded by him from that affliction. Therefore it is said: 'He guards the mind-faculty.' With respect to those forms cognizable by the eye toward which the eye-faculty should not be directed, and those <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind toward which the mind-faculty should not be directed — toward them he does not direct [his faculties] at all, in any way whatsoever. Therefore it is said: 'He undertakes restraint by means of the eye-faculty.' Therefore it is said: 'Up to — he undertakes restraint by means of the mind-faculty.' This, then, is the detailed analysis (<s>vibhaṅga</s>) of <s>indriyasaṃvara</s> (sense-faculty restraint) to be understood.

body.translated_text: With respect to those forms toward which the eye must be directed, and those <s>dharmas</s> cognizable by ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind toward which the mind must be directed,

body.text: samāsārthaḥ | yena ca saṃvṛṇoti, yataśca saṃvṛṇoti, yathā ca saṃvṛṇoti, yā cāsau saṃvṛtiḥ | tatsarvamekatyamabhisaṃkṣipyendriyasamvara ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Summary meaning: by what one restrains, from what one restrains, how one restrains, and what that restraint is — all of that, combined together, is called <s>indriyasaṃvara</s> (sense-faculty restraint).

body.text: tatra kena saṃvṛṇoti [|] yā ārakṣitā ca smṛtistayā saṃvṛṇoti [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, by what does one restrain? One restrains by means of guarded <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness).

body.text: kiṃ saṃvṛṇoti [|] cakṣurindriyaṃ saṃvṛṇoti | śrotraghrāṇajih vākāyamanaindriyaṃ saṃvṛṇoti | idaṃ saṃvṛṇoti |
body.translated_text: What does one restrain? One restrains the eye-faculty. One restrains the ear-, nose-, tongue-, body-, and mind-faculties. This is what one restrains.

body.text: kutaḥ saṃvṛṇoti | priyarūpāpriyarūpebhyo rūpebhyaḥ śabdebhyo yāvaddharmebhyo [a]taḥ saṃvṛṇoti (saṃvṛṇoti) |
body.translated_text: From what does one restrain? From forms of pleasant and unpleasant appearance, from sounds, up to <s>dharmas</s> — from these one restrains.

body.text: kathaṃ saṃvṛṇoti | na nimittagrāhī bhavati nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī (

children.text: ) yato [a]dhikaraṇameva pāpakā akuśalā dharmāścittamanusravanti | teṣāṃ samvarāya pratipadyate | rakṣatīndriyamindriyeṇa | samvaramāpadyate | ityevaṃ saṃvṛṇoti |
children.translated_text: on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> would flow into the mind. One undertakes restraint with respect to them. One guards the faculty by means of the faculty. One undertakes restraint. Thus one restrains.

body.translated_text: How does one restrain? One does not grasp at the sign and does not grasp at the secondary characteristics,

body.text: kā punaḥ saṃvṛtiḥ | yataḥ smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati | samāvasthāvacārakaḥ | iyamucyate saṃvṛtiḥ |
body.translated_text: And what is the restraint? That by which one becomes one whose mind is guarded by <s>smṛti</s>, and one who conducts [oneself] in equanimity — this is called restraint (<s>saṃvṛti</s>).

body.text: punaraparaḥ samāsārthaḥ [|] yaścasamvaropāyaḥ | yacca samvaraṇīyamvastu, yā ca saṃvṛtiḥ | tadekatyamabhisaṃkṣipyendriyasamvara ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Another summary meaning: the means of restraint, the thing to be restrained, and the restraint [itself] — combined together, these are called <s>indriyasaṃvara</s> (sense-faculty restraint).

body.text: tatra katamaḥ samvarovā (saṃvaropāyaḥ) [|] yadāha ārakṣitasmṛtirbhavati, nipakasmṛtiriti cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā na nimittagrāhī bhavati, nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī, yāvanmanasā dharmān vijñāya na nimittagrāhī bhavati, nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī | yato [a]dhikaraṇameva pāpakā akuśalā dharmāścittamanusravanti | teṣāṃ samvarāya pratipadyate | rakṣatīndriyamindriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | ayamucyate samvaropāyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the means of restraint (<s>saṃvaropāya</s>)? That which is stated: 'One has guarded <s>smṛti</s>, one has discerning <s>smṛti</s>'; 'Having seen forms with the eye, one does not grasp at the sign, does not grasp at the secondary characteristics; up to — having cognized <s>dharmas</s> with the mind, one does not grasp at the sign, does not grasp at the secondary characteristics, on account of which evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> would flow into the mind. One undertakes restraint with respect to them. One guards the faculty and undertakes restraint by means of the faculty.' This is called the means of restraint.

body.text: samvaraṇīyaṃ vastu katamat [|] cakṣūrūpaṃ caivaṃ yāvanmanodharmāścedamucyate samvaraṇīyaṃ vastu |
body.translated_text: What is the object requiring restraint? The eye and visible form, and so on up to the mind and mental objects — this is called the object requiring restraint.

body.text: tatra saṃvṛtiḥ katamā [|] yadāha | smṛtyārakṣitamānaso bhavati | samāvasthāvacāraka itīyamucyate saṃvṛtiḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the guarding? As it is said: 'One whose mind is protected by <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), who is established in [proper] conduct and comportment' — this is called the guarding.

body.text: sa khalvayamindriyasamvaraḥ samāsato dvividhaḥ | (

children.translated_text: That which is comprised in the power of analytical reflection (<s>pratisaṃkhyānabala</s>), and that which is comprised in the power of meditative cultivation (<s>bhāvanābala</s>).

body.translated_text: This <s>indriyasaṃvara</s> (sense-restraint) is, in brief, of two kinds:

body.text: tatra pratisaṃkhyānabala saṃgṛhīto yena viṣyeṣvādīnavaṃ paśyati | no tu tamādīnavaṃ vyapakarṣati | prajahāti | tatra [bhā]vanābalasaṃgṛhīto yena viṣyeṣvādīnavaṃ paśyati, taṃ ca punarādīnavaṃ vyapakarṣati | prajahāti | tatra pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhītenendriyasamvareṇa viṣayālambanaṃ kleśaparyavasthānaṃ notpādayati, na saṃmukhīkaroti | na caivāśa(śra)yasanniviṣṭamanuśayaṃ pra[jahā]ti, samudghātayati | tatra bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhīte[ne]ndriyasamvareṇa viṣayālambanaṃ ca kleśaparyavasthānaṃ notpādayati, na sammukhīkaroti | sarvadā sarvakālamāśrayasanniviṣṭaṃ cānuśayaṃ prajahāti | samudghātayati | ayamviśeṣaḥ, ayamabhiprāyaḥ | ida[ma]nākaraṇaṃ pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhītasya bhāvanābalasaṃgṛhītasya cendriyasamvarasya | tatra yo [a]yaṃ pratisaṃkhyānabalasaṃgṛhīta indriyasamvaro [a]yaṃ saṃbhāramārgasaṃgṛhītaḥ [|] yaḥ punarbhāvanābalasaṃgṛhīta indriyasamvaraḥ | sa vairāgyabhūmipatito veditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the sense-restraint comprised in the power of analytical reflection is that by which one sees the danger in sense-objects, but does not remove that danger nor abandon it. The sense-restraint comprised in the power of meditative cultivation is that by which one sees the danger in sense-objects and furthermore removes and abandons that danger. With the sense-restraint comprised in the power of analytical reflection, one does not produce nor bring face-to-face the <s>kleśa</s> (affliction) envelopment arising from sense-object apprehension, but one does not abandon nor uproot the latent tendency (<s>anuśaya</s>) lodged in the basis (<s>āśraya</s>). With the sense-restraint comprised in the power of meditative cultivation, one does not produce nor bring face-to-face the affliction-envelopment arising from sense-object apprehension, and one abandons and uproots at all times the latent tendency lodged in the basis. This is the distinction, this is the intended meaning. This is the differentiating factor between the sense-restraint comprised in the power of analytical reflection and that comprised in the power of meditative cultivation. The sense-restraint comprised in the power of analytical reflection is included in the <s>saṃbhāramārga</s> (path of accumulation). The sense-restraint comprised in the power of meditative cultivation should be understood as belonging to the stage of dispassion (<s>vairāgyabhūmi</s>).

children.translated_text: 'Not for the sake of amusement, not for the sake of adornment, not for the sake of embellishment' — and so on in detail as before.

body.translated_text: What is <s>bhojane mātrajñatā</s> (moderation in food)? Just as here someone partakes of food with analytical reflection:

body.text: kathaṃ pratisaṃkhyāyāhāramāharati | pratisaṃkhyocyate yayā prajñayā kabaḍaṃkārasyāhārasyādīnavaṃ samanupaśyatyādīnavadarśanena (
body.translated_text: How does one partake of food with analytical reflection? Analytical reflection is that wisdom by which one contemplates the danger of material food (<s>kabaḍaṃkāra āhāra</s>); having become disgusted through the perception of danger,

body.text: tatpunarādīnavadarśanaṃ katamat | yaduta yasyaiva kabaḍaṃkārasya paribhogānvayo vā, vipariṇāmānvayo vā, paryeṣaṇānvayo vā |
body.translated_text: What then is that perception of danger? It is the danger connected with the enjoyment (<s>paribhogānvaya</s>) of that very material food, or the danger connected with its transformation (<s>vipariṇāmānvaya</s>), or the danger connected with its pursuit (<s>paryeṣaṇānvaya</s>).

body.text: paribhogānvaya ādīnavaḥ (katamaḥ) [|] yathāpīhaikatyo yasmin samaye āhāramāharati varṇasampannamapi, gandhasampannamapi, rasasampannamapi, supraṇītamapi [|] tasya kabaḍaṃkāra āhāraḥ samanantarakṣipta eva āsye yadā dantayantracūrṇitaśca, lālāvisaraviklinnaśca bhavati | lālāpariveṣṭitaśca bhavati | sa tasmin samaye kaṇṭhanālīpraluṭhitaśca bhavati | sa yāsau pūrvikā, purāṇā manāpatā (na āpatā) tāṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ vijahāti | parāṃ ca vikṛtimāpadyate | yasyāṃ ca vikṛtau (

children.text: ) vartamānaśchanditakopamaḥ khyāti | tadavasthaṃ cainaṃ sa cedayaṃ bhoktā puruṣapudgalaḥ sa cedākārato manasi kuryāt samanusmarennāsya sarveṇa sarvamanyatrāpi tāvadavipariṇate, praṇīte bhojane bhogakāmatā santiṣṭheta | kaḥ punarvādastatra tadavastha iti ya ebhirākauraranekavidhairanayānupūrvyā bhojanaparibhogamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā yāsau śubhā varṇanibhā antarīyate, ādīnavaśca prādurbhavati aśū(śu)cisaṃgṛhītaḥ [|] ayamucyate paribhogānvayaḥ | ādīnavaḥ | yaduta āhāre |
children.translated_text: It becomes like vomit. If this eating person were to consider that condition of it attentively, were to recollect it in terms of its appearance, then in him there would not remain any desire to enjoy even food that has not yet been transformed, that is still refined — how much less so when it is in that [transformed] state! For through these and various other such disgusting stages, dependent upon the enjoyment of food, that attractive, beautiful color is concealed within, and danger consisting of impurity manifests. This is called the danger connected with the enjoyment of food.

body.translated_text: What is the danger connected with enjoyment of food? Just as here, when someone partakes of food that is excellent in color, excellent in fragrance, excellent in taste, and supremely refined — when that material food, immediately upon being placed in the mouth, is ground by the mill of the teeth, moistened and dissolved by the flow of saliva, and enveloped by saliva — at that time it rolls down through the throat passage, and at that moment it completely abandons all that former, original attractiveness, and undergoes an extreme transformation, in which state

body.text: tatra katamo vipariṇāmānvaya ādīnava āhāre | tasya tamāhāramāhṛtavatastu [ṣṭava] taḥ yadā vipariṇamati rātryā madhyame vā yāme, paścime vā yāme, tadā sa rudhiramānsa(māṃsa)snāyvasthitvagādīnyanekavidhāni bahunānāprakārāṇi | asmin kāye aśucindravyāṇi vivardhayati saṃjanayati |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the danger in food connected with transformation? When the food that one has consumed undergoes transformation during the middle or last watch of the night, then it increases and generates in this body many diverse kinds of impure substances such as blood, flesh, sinews, bones, skin, and the like.

body.text: arthataśca | atipariṇataścādhobhāgī (
