children.translated_text: the text further says: 'Having washed the feet outside the dwelling, entering the dwelling, one prepares the bed on the right side, placing foot upon foot' — by this, the second thing to be done correctly is declared, namely: one prepares the bed at the proper time, not at an improper time. The statement 'With the perception of light, mindful, clearly comprehending, keeping the thought of rising in mind, one prepares the bed' — by this, the third thing to be done correctly is declared, namely: one enters sleep with an undefiled mind, not with a defiled mind. The statement 'In the last watch of the night, rising lightly and swiftly, one purifies the mind from obstructive qualities' — by this, the fourth thing to be done correctly is declared, namely: one awakens at the proper time and does not let the time for rising pass. Therein, the statement 'With the perception of light, mindful, clearly comprehending, keeping the thought of rising in mind, one prepares the bed' — from these, for two reasons one enters sleep with an undefiled mind: namely, through mindfulness and through clear comprehension. And for two reasons one awakens at the proper time and does not let the time pass: namely, through the perception of light and through the perception of rising. And how does one sleep having grasped a wholesome object? Through clear comprehension, therefore, when the mind wavers from that wholesome object

children.text: ) saṃkliśyamānaṃ cittaṃ laghu laghveva samyakprajānāti | evamasyābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmasaṃkliṣṭacittasya śayyā bhavati | tatrālokasaṃjñayā, utthānasaṃjñayā ca | na gāḍhaṃ svapiti | nāsya dūrānugataṃ tanmiddhaparyavasthānaṃ bhavati | ityābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ kālena [prati]vibudhyate (ti) | notthānakālamativartate | ayaṃ jāgarikānuyogasya samāsārtho (rthaḥ) [|] yaśca pūrvako vistaravibhāgaḥ, yaścāyaṃ samāsārthaḥ | iyamucyate pūrvarātrāpararātraṃ jāgarikānuyuktā ||
children.translated_text: and becomes defiled, one correctly comprehends it lightly and swiftly. In this way, through these two reasons, the bed of one with an undefiled mind comes about. Therein, through the perception of light and the perception of rising, one does not sleep heavily, and the obstruction of sloth-and-torpor does not deeply pervade. Thus, through these two reasons, one awakens at the proper time and does not let the time for rising pass. This is the summarized meaning of devotion to wakefulness. Both the preceding detailed analysis and this summarized meaning — this is called 'devotion to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night.'

body.translated_text: And how was it taught? The statement 'During the day, by walking and sitting, one purifies the mind from obstructive qualities; so too in the first watch of the night' — by this, the first thing to be done correctly is declared, namely: as long as one is awake, one does not abandon the wholesome side, constantly cultivating wholesome qualities of the one [correct] side. Since

body.text: saṃprajānadvihāritā katamā | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ abhikramapratikrame saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati | ālokitavyavalokite, saṃmiṃjita (sāmmiñjita)prasārite, saṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe | aśite, pīte, khādite, svādite, niṣaṇṇe, śayite, jāgṛte, pra[la]pite, tūṣṇīṃbhāve, nidrāklamavinodane saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati |
body.translated_text: What is 'dwelling with clear comprehension' (<s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s>)? It is as follows: here a certain person dwells with clear comprehension in going forward and returning, in looking ahead and looking around, in bending and stretching, in [wearing] the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer robe), the inner robe, and carrying the bowl, in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, in sitting, lying down, being awake, speaking, being silent, and in dispelling drowsiness and fatigue — one dwells with clear comprehension.

body.text: tatra katamo [a]bhikramaḥ | pratikramaḥ katamaḥ | abhikramapratikrame samprajānadvihāritā [katamā] |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'going forward' (<s>abhikrama</s>)? What is 'returning' (<s>pratikrama</s>)? What is 'dwelling with clear comprehension in going forward and returning'?

body.text: tatrābhikramaḥ [|] yathāpīhaikatyo grāmamvā upakrāmati | grāmāntaramvā, kulamvā, [kulāntaramvā, vihāramvā], vihārāntaramvā [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, 'going forward' is as follows: here a certain person approaches a village, or another village, or a household, or another household, or a monastery, or another monastery.

body.text: tatra pratikramaḥ | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ grāmāntarāmvā (grāmādvā) pratinivarttate | grāmāntarādvā, kulādvā, kulāntarādvā, vihārādvā, vihārāntarādvā [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, 'returning' is as follows: here a certain person returns from a village, or from another village, from a household, or from another household, from a monastery, or from another monastery.

children.translated_text: while going forward, one comprehends 'I am going forward'; and where one should go forward, there one goes forward; and one goes forward at the proper time, not at an improper time; and in the manner in which one should go forward, with such deportment, such form, and such posture (<s>īryāpatha</s>), in that very way one goes forward. This is called 'dwelling with clear comprehension, namely in going forward and returning.'

body.translated_text: Therein, 'dwelling with clear comprehension' is as follows: while going forward, one correctly comprehends 'I am going forward.' 'Here I should go forward; here I should not go forward' — one correctly comprehends. 'This is the time for my going forward; this is not the time for going forward' — one correctly comprehends. This is called clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>). If one is endowed with that clear comprehension,

body.text: tatra katamadālokitaṃ, katamad vyavalokitaṃ | katamā ālokitavyavalokita saṃprajānādvihāritaḥ (tā) | tasyāsya pūrvaparikī[rttiteṣu dhamaṣu] abhikramataḥ, pratikramataśca yadabuddhipūrvakamacchandapūrvakaṃ | a[ntare]ṇa cakṣuṣā rūpadarśanamidamucyate ālokitaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'looking ahead' (<s>ālokita</s>)? What is 'looking around' (<s>vyavalokita</s>)? What is 'dwelling with clear comprehension in looking ahead and around'? For this person, while going forward and returning among the previously described activities, whatever unintentional, undesired, incidental seeing of forms with the eye occurs — this is called 'looking ahead.'

body.text: yatpunarupasaṃkrāntasya buddhipūrvakaṃ prayatnapūrvakaṃ, kṛtyapūrvakaṃ cakṣuṣā rūpadarśanaṃ, tadyathā rājñā(jñāṃ) rājyā(jā)mātrāṇāṃ, naigamānāṃ, jānapadānāmvā, brāhmaṇānāmvā, dhanināṃ, śreṣṭhināṃ, sārthavāhānāṃ, tadanyeṣāmbāhyakānāṃlayanānāṃ, mārutānāmavarakāṇāṃ, pra(prā)sādānāṃ, harmyatalānāmiti | yadvā punaranyeṣāṃ lokacitrāṇāṃ darśanamidamucyate | vyavalokitaṃ |
body.translated_text: But whatever intentional, deliberate, purposeful seeing of forms with the eye occurs for one who has arrived nearby — such as [seeing] kings, royal ministers, townspeople, countryfolk, <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, wealthy persons, guild-masters, caravan-leaders, and the dwellings of other outsiders, or [seeing] wind-shelters, enclosures, palaces, and terraces of upper stories — or whatever seeing of other worldly spectacles occurs — this is called 'looking around.'

body.text: yatpunarālokitaṃ ca vyavalokitaṃ ca svalakṣaṇataḥ (

children.text: ) samyageva prajānāti | yathā āloki(kayi)tavyaṃ, yathā vyavalokayitavyaṃ tadapisamyageva prajānāti | idamasyocyate saṃprajanyaṃ [|] sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ | sacedavalokayamāno jānātyavalokayāmīti | yaccāvalokayitavyaṃ vyavalokayitavyaṃ tadālokayati vyavalokayati | yadā ālokayitavyaṃ, vyavalokayitavyaṃ | tadā ālokayati, vyavalokayati [|] yathā ālokayitavyaṃ vyavalokayitavyaṃ tathā ālokayati, vyavalokayati | iyamasyocyate | saṃprajānadvihāritā | yadutālokitavyavalokite [|]
children.translated_text: ) — and also correctly understands how one should look ahead and how one should look around — this is called one's <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension). Endowed with that <s>saṃprajanya</s>, if while looking one knows 'I am looking,' and one looks ahead at and looks around at what should be looked ahead at and looked around at; when it should be looked ahead at and looked around at, then one looks ahead and looks around; and as it should be looked ahead at and looked around at, so one looks ahead and looks around — this is called one's <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension), namely, in looking ahead and looking around.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, one who correctly understands looking ahead and looking around in their specific characteristics (

body.text: tatra katamat saṃmiji(sammiñji)taṃ, katamat prasāritaṃ, katamā saṃmiji(sammiñji)taprasārite saṃprajānadvihāritā | sa tathā ālokayamāno, vyavalokayamānaśca | abhikramapūrvakaṃ, pratikramapūrvakañca, yatpādau vā sammiṃjayati, prasārayati | bāhū vā saṃmi(miṃ)jayati | prasārayati | hastau vā saṃmi(miṃ)jayati, prasārayati | ityanyatamānyatamamvā aṃgapratyaṃgaṃ sammiñjiyati | prasārayatīdamucyate | saṃmi(miṃ)jita prasāritaṃ [|] sacet saṃmi(miṃ)jitaprasāritaṃ svalakṣaṇataḥ prajānāti saṃmi(miṃ)jitavyaṃ | prasāritavyañca | samyageva prajānāti | yādi ca saṃmi(miṃ)ji(jayi)tavyaṃ, yadā prasāri(rayi)tavyaṃ tadapi samyageva prajānāti | yathā ca saṃmi(miṃ)ji(jayi)tavyaṃ, yathā (

children.text: ) prasāri(rayi)tavyaṃ, tadapi samyageva prajānāti, idamasyocyate saṃprajanyaṃ |
children.translated_text: ) to stretch — this is called one's <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'bending'? What is 'stretching'? What is the <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension) in bending and stretching? While thus looking ahead and looking around, preceded by stepping forward and stepping back, one either bends one's feet or stretches them; bends one's arms or stretches them; bends one's hands or stretches them — thus one bends or stretches one or another of one's major or minor limbs. This is called 'bending and stretching.' If one understands bending and stretching in their specific characteristics, correctly understands what should be bent and what should be stretched, correctly understands when to bend and when to stretch, and correctly understands how to bend and how (

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ | sa cet saṃmija(sammiñja)yamānaḥ(yan), prasārayamāṇaḥ(yan) | jānāti | saṃmi(miṃ)jayāmi | prasārayāmīti | yacca saṃmi(miṃ)jayitavyaṃ prasārayitavyaṃ saṃmi(miṃ)jayati, prasārayati | yadā ca saṃmi(miṃ)jayitavyaṃ, prasārayitavyaṃ tadā saṃmi(miṃ)jayati, prasārayati, iyamasyocyate | saṃprajānadvihāritā yaduta saṃmiṃji(sammiñji)ta prasārite ||
body.translated_text: Endowed with that <s>saṃprajanya</s>, if while bending and stretching one knows 'I am bending, I am stretching'; and one bends and stretches what should be bent and stretched; when it should be bent and stretched, then one bends and stretches — this is called one's <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension), namely, in bending and stretching.

body.text: tatra katamat saṃghāṭīdhāraṇaṃ | katamaccīvaradhāraṇaṃ, katamat, pātradhāraṇaṃ, katamā(mat)sāṃ(saṃ)ghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ (ṇe) | saṃprajānadvihāritā |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'wearing the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer robe)'? What is 'wearing the <s>cīvara</s> (inner robe)'? What is 'carrying the <s>pātra</s> (alms-bowl)'? What is the <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension) in wearing the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>cīvara</s>, and carrying the <s>pātra</s>?

body.text: yattāvadasya jyeṣṭhaṃ cīvaraṃ ṣaṣṭhikhannamvā (khaṇḍaṃ vā) navatikhannamvā(khaṇḍaṃ vā), dviguṇasīvitamvā, ekaguṇasīvitamvā iyamucyate sāṃghāṭī (saṃghāṭī) [|] tasya prāvaraṇaṃ paribhogaḥ | samyageva pariharaṇaṃ dhāraṇamityucyate |
body.translated_text: As for the principal robe — whether of sixty patches or ninety patches, whether double-stitched or single-stitched — this is called the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> (outer robe). Its proper wearing and use, and its correct maintenance, is called 'wearing' (<s>dhāraṇa</s>).

body.text: yatpunarasya madhyamvā, kanīyo vā, ādhiṣṭhānikamvā cī[varaṃ] atirekacīvaraṃ vā | ādhiṣṭhānikaṃ vā | cīvaraṃ atirekacīvaramvā vikalpanārhaṃ vikalpayati (

children.text: ) taccīvaramityucyate | tasya prāvaraṇaṃ paribhogaḥ | samyageva pariharaṇaṃ dhāraṇamityucyate | yatpunarasyādhiṣṭhānāni kamā(rmā)yasamvā, mṛnmayamvā bhaikṣabhojanamidamucyate | pātraṃ, tasya paribhogaḥ | samyageva pariharaṇaṃ dhāraṇamityucyate |
children.translated_text: ) — that is called the <s>cīvara</s> (robe). Its proper wearing, use, and correct maintenance is called 'wearing.' Furthermore, one's designated vessel, whether made of iron or of clay, for collecting almsfood — this is called the <s>pātra</s> (alms-bowl). Its use and correct maintenance is called 'carrying.'

body.translated_text: Furthermore, one's middle or lesser robe, whether a formally designated robe (<s>ādhiṣṭhānika</s>) or an extra robe, one who formally designates a robe fit for formal designation — whether a designated robe or an extra robe (

body.text: sa cetpunarayaṃ tāṃ sāṃ (saṃ)ghāṭīṃ, cīvaraṃ, pātraṃ, dhāraṇamvā svalakṣaṇataḥ samyageva prajānāti | yacca sāṃ (saṃ)ghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ | kalpikaṃ, akalpikaṃ vā, tadapi samyageva prajānati | yadā ca sāṃ (saṃ)ghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇaṃ dhārayitavyaṃ (karttavyaṃ) | tadā samyageva prajānāti | yathā ca dhārayitavyaṃ, tadapi samyageva prajānāti | idamasyocyate | saṃprajanyaṃ | sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ | sacet sāṃ (saṃ)ghāṭī(ṭīṃ), cīvaraṃ, pātraṃ dhārayamāṇo jānāti dhārayāmīti | yacca dhārayitavyaṃ taddhārayati | yadā ca dhārayitavyaṃ tadā dhārayati | yathā ca dhārayitavyaṃ tathā dhārayatīyamasyocyate saṃprajānadvihāritā | yaduta sāṃ (saṃ)ghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe |
body.translated_text: If one further correctly understands that <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>cīvara</s>, <s>pātra</s>, and their wearing in their specific characteristics; and correctly understands whether the wearing of the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>cīvara</s>, and <s>pātra</s> is proper (<s>kalpika</s>) or improper (<s>akalpika</s>); and correctly understands when the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>cīvara</s>, and <s>pātra</s> should be worn; and correctly understands how they should be worn — this is called one's <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension). Endowed with that <s>saṃprajanya</s>, if while wearing the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>cīvara</s>, and carrying the <s>pātra</s>, one knows 'I am wearing them'; and one wears what should be worn; and wears them when they should be worn; and wears them as they should be worn — this is called one's <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension), namely, in wearing the <s>saṃghāṭī</s>, <s>cīvara</s>, and carrying the <s>pātra</s>.

body.text: tatra katamadaśitaṃ | katamatpītaṃ | katamat khāditaṃ | katamatsvāditaṃ | katamā aśitapītakhāditāsvādite[ṣu] saṃprajānadvihāritā | yaḥ kaścit piṇḍapātaparibhogaḥ sarvaṃ tadaśitamityucyate | tasya punardvidhā bhedaḥ khāditaṃ; svāditaṃ ca | tatra khāditaṃ | manthā (

children.text: ) vā, [a]pūpā vā, odanakulmāṣamveti yadvā punaranyatamābhisaṃskārikamannaṃ vikṛtaṃ bhojyaṃ prāṇasaṃdhāraṇamidamucyate khāditamaśitamapītaṃ |
children.translated_text: ) cakes, rice, pulse, and whatever other prepared food — cooked food that sustains life — this is called 'chewed,' which is 'eaten' but not 'drunk.'

body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'eaten' (<s>aśita</s>)? What is 'drunk' (<s>pīta</s>)? What is 'chewed' (<s>khādita</s>)? What is 'tasted' (<s>svādita</s>)? What is the <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension) in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting? Whatever partaking of almsfood there is, all of that is called 'eaten' (<s>aśita</s>). This has a twofold division: 'chewed' and 'tasted.' Therein, 'chewed' includes: gruel,

body.text: svāditaṃ katamat | tadyathā kṣīraṃ, dadhi, navanītaṃ, sarpistailaṃ, madhu, śo(phā)ṇitaṃ, mānsaṃ (māṃsaṃ), matsyā, vallūrā, lavaṇaṃ, vanaphalamvā, bhakṣa(kṣya)prakāraṃ vā idamucyate svāditamaśitamapi (pī)taṃ ||
body.translated_text: What is 'tasted' (<s>svādita</s>)? Namely: milk, yogurt, butter, ghee, oil, honey, raw sugar, meat, fish, dried meat, salt, forest fruits, or various edible preparations — this is called 'tasted,' which is 'eaten' but also 'drunk.'

body.text: yatpunaḥ pīyate khaṇḍarasaṃ(so)vā, śarkarārasamvā (so vā), kāṃcikamvā, dadhimaṇḍamvā | śuktamvā, takramvā, antataḥ pānīyamapi [|] idamucyate pītaṃ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, what is drunk: sugar-cane juice, syrup, sour gruel (<s>kāñcika</s>), whey (<s>dadhimaṇḍa</s>), vinegar (<s>śukta</s>), buttermilk (<s>takra</s>), and even down to plain water — this is called 'drunk' (<s>pīta</s>).

body.text: sa cedaśitapītakhāditāsvāditaṃ svalakṣaṇataḥ samyageva prajānāti | yaccāśitavyaṃ, pātavyaṃ, khāditavyaṃ, svādi(dayi)tavyaṃ tadapi samyageva prajānāti | yadā cāśitavyaṃ, pātavyaṃ khāditavyaṃ, svādi(dayi)tavyaṃ tadeva (tadapi) samyageva prajānāti | yathā cāśitavyaṃ, pātavyaṃ, khāditavyaṃ | svādi(dayi)tavyaṃ | tadapi samyageva prajānāti | idamasyocyate saṃprajanyaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: If one correctly understands eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting in their specific characteristics; and correctly understands what should be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted; and correctly understands when it should be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted; and correctly understands how it should be eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted — this is called one's <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension).

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ aśamānaḥ (aśan), pibamānaḥ (piban), khādamānaḥ (khādan), svādayamānaḥ (svādayan) sa cejjānāti | aśnāmi, pibāmi, khādāmīti | yaccāśitavyaṃ, pātavyaṃ, khāditavyaṃ, (

children.text: ) tadaśnātiyāvatsvādayati | yadā cāśitavyaṃ (yāva)tsvādayitavyaṃ | tadā aśnāti, svādayati | yathā cāśitavyaṃyāvatsvādayitavyaṃ tathā [a]śnāti | yāvatsvādayitavyami (yāvatsvādayatī)yamasyocyate yāvat saṃprajānadvihāritā | yadutāśitapītakhāditāsvādite[ṣu] [||]
children.translated_text: ) and tastes [what should be tasted]; and eats when it should be eaten, up to tasting when it should be tasted; and eats as it should be eaten, up to tasting as it should be tasted — this is called one's <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension), namely, in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting.

body.translated_text: Endowed with that <s>saṃprajanya</s>, while eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, if one knows 'I am eating, I am drinking, I am chewing'; and eats what should be eaten, drinks what should be drunk, chews what should be chewed,

body.text: tatra katamadgataṃ, katamat sthitaṃ, katamanniṣaṇṇaṃ | katamacchayitaṃ | katamajjāgṛtaṃ | katamadbhāṣitaṃ, katamattū(mastū)ṣṇīmbhāvaḥ | katamā nidrāklamaprativinodanā | katamā gate, sthite, niṣaṇṇe śayite, jāgṛte, bhāṣite, tūṣṇīmbhāve, nidrāklamavinodanā[yāṃ] saṃprajānadvihāritā | yathāpīhaikatyaścaṃkrame caṃkramyate(mate), sahadharmikāṇāṃ copasaṃkrāmati | adhvānaṃ vā pratipadyate | idamasyocyate gataṃ | yathāpīhaikatyaścaṃkrame vā tiṣṭhati, sahadhārmikāṇāṃ vā puratastiṣṭhati | ācāryāṇāmupādhyāyānāṃ gurūṇāṃ gurusthānīyānāṃ idamucyate sthitaṃ | yathāpīhaikatyo maṃce, vā, pīṭhe vā, tṛṇasaṃstaraṇe vā, sanniviśati vā, sanniṣīdati vā | paryaṅkamābhujya, ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya, pratimukhāṃ (khīṃ) smṛtimupasthāpyedamucyate | niṣaṇṇaṃ | yathāpīhaikatyo (

children.text:
) bahirvihārasya pādau prakṣālya, vihāraṃ praviśya, dakṣiṇena pārśvena siṃhaśayyāṃ kalpayati | pāde pādamādhāya, mañce vā, pīṭhe vā, tṛṇasaṃstarake(ṇe) vā, araṇye, vṛkṣamūle vā, śūnyāgāre vā [|] idamucyate śayitaṃ |
yathāpīhaikatyo divā caṃkramaniṣadyābhyāmāvaraṇīyebhyo dharmebhyaścittaṃ pariśodhayatyevaṃ rātryāḥ prathame yāme, paścime yāme [|] idamucyate jāgṛtaṃ |
children.translated_text: ), having washed the feet outside the dwelling, enters the dwelling and arranges the lion-posture on the right side, placing foot upon foot, on a bed, a seat, or a grass-mat, in the forest, at the root of a tree, or in an empty house — this is called 'lying down.' Just as here a certain person, during the day, purifies the mind from obstructive qualities by walking and sitting — likewise in the first watch and the last watch of the night — this is called 'being awake.'

body.translated_text: Therein, what is 'going' (<s>gata</s>)? What is 'standing' (<s>sthita</s>)? What is 'sitting' (<s>niṣaṇṇa</s>)? What is 'lying down' (<s>śayita</s>)? What is 'being awake' (<s>jāgṛta</s>)? What is 'speaking' (<s>bhāṣita</s>)? What is 'silence' (<s>tūṣṇīmbhāva</s>)? What is 'dispelling drowsiness and fatigue' (<s>nidrāklamaprativinodana</s>)? What is the <s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> in going, standing, sitting, lying down, being awake, speaking, silence, and dispelling drowsiness and fatigue? Just as here a certain person walks on a walking path, or approaches fellow practitioners in the <s>Dharma</s>, or sets out on a journey — this is called 'going.' Just as here a certain person stands on a walking path, or stands before fellow practitioners in the <s>Dharma</s>, before <s>ācāryas</s> (teachers), <s>upādhyāyas</s> (preceptors), <s>gurus</s> (spiritual masters), and those in the position of <s>gurus</s> — this is called 'standing.' Just as here a certain person settles down or sits on a bed, a seat, or a grass-mat, sitting cross-legged, keeping the body upright, establishing mindfulness directed before oneself — this is called 'sitting.' Just as here a certain person (

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyastathā jāgarikānuyuktaḥ anuddiṣṭāṃśca dharmānuddiśati | paryavāpnoti | tadyathā sūtraṃ, geyaṃ, vyākaraṇamiti | vistareṇa pūrvavat | uddiṣṭeṣu ca dharmeṣu vacasā paricayaṃ karoti | yaduta vistareṇa svādhyāyakriyayā, pareṣāṃ vā vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati | kālena kālamālapati | pratisaṃmodaya[ti vi]jñaiḥ sabrahmacāribhissārddhaṃ, tadanyairvā gṛhasthairyāvadevodyojanaṃ pariṣkārārthamidamucyate | bhāṣitaṃ |
body.translated_text: Just as here a certain person, thus devoted to wakefulness, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> that has not been taught, and masters it — namely, <s>sūtra</s> (discourses), <s>geya</s> (verse portions), <s>vyākaraṇa</s> (expositions), and so forth in detail as before. And regarding the <s>Dharma</s> that has been taught, one engages in verbal familiarization — namely, extensively through the practice of <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-recitation), or explains to others in detail. From time to time one converses, exchanges greetings with wise fellow practitioners in the holy life, or with others — householders and so forth — only to the extent necessary for furnishing one's requisites. This is called 'speaking.'

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyo yathāśrutānāṃ, yathā parya[vā]taptānāndharmāṇāmmanasā parijitānāṃ, ekākī rahogato [a]rthaṃ ci[ntaya]ti, tulayatyupaparīkṣate | pratisaṃlīno vā punaḥ bhavatyadhyātmameva cittaṃ sthāpayati | damayati [|] śamayati | vyupaśamayati | ekotīkaroti | (

children.translated_text: ) concentrates it — or engages in the practice of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight meditation). This is called 'silence' (<s>tūṣṇīmbhāva</s>).

body.translated_text: Just as here a certain person, being alone and in seclusion, contemplates, weighs, and examines the meaning of the teachings that have been heard, mastered, and mentally absorbed. Or again, being in seclusion, one establishes the mind internally, restrains it, calms it, thoroughly pacifies it, unifies it,

body.text: yathāpīhaikatyaḥ grīṣmasamaye pratyupasthite, uttaptagrīṣmaparidāhe kāle vartamāne, uṣṇana vā bādhyate | śrānto vā bhavati | klāntasyotpadyate | akāle nidrāklamaḥ svapitukāmataḥ (tā) | ayamucyate nidrāklamaḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as here a certain person, when the summer season has arrived and the fierce heat of summer prevails, is oppressed by the heat, or becomes weary and fatigued — drowsiness and fatigue arise at an improper time, and the desire to sleep [comes]. This is called 'drowsiness and fatigue' (<s>nidrāklama</s>).

body.text: sa cet punarayaṃ gataṃ yāvannidrāklamavinodanaṃ | tatsvalakṣaṇataḥ samyageva prajānāti | yatra ca gantavyaṃ yāvannidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyaḥ | tadapi samyageva prajānāti | yadā ca gantavyaṃ | yāvadyathā nidrāklamaḥ | prativinodayitavyaḥ | tadapi samyageva prajānāti | yathā ca gantavyaṃ bhavati | yatra (yathā) ca yāvannidrāklamaḥ | prativinodayitavyaḥ tadapi samyageva prajānāti | idamasyocyate saṃprajanyaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: If one further correctly understands going, up to and including the dispelling of drowsiness and fatigue, in their specific characteristics; and correctly understands where one should go, up to and including how drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled; and correctly understands when one should go, up to and including when and how drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled; and correctly understands how one should go, and how drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled — this is called one's <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension).

body.text: sa tena saṃprajanyena samanvāgataḥ | gacchan yāvannidrāklamaḥ (maṃ) prativinodayan sa cejjānāti | (gacchāmi) gacchāmi yāvat (n) nidrāklamaṃ prativinodayāmi | yatra ca gantavyaṃ bhavati | yatra ca yāvannidrāklamaḥ prativinodayitavyo bhavati | tadā gacchati | tadā yāvannidrāklamaṃ prativinodayati | yathā ca gantavyaṃ bhavati | yathā yāvannidrāklamaḥ | prativinodayitavyo bhavati | tathā gacchati | tathā (

children.translated_text: ) up to and including dispelling drowsiness and fatigue — this is called one's [<s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s> (dwelling with clear comprehension)].

body.translated_text: Endowed with that <s>saṃprajanya</s>, while going, up to and including dispelling drowsiness and fatigue, if one knows 'I am going,' up to 'I am dispelling drowsiness and fatigue'; and one goes where one should go, and dispels drowsiness and fatigue where it should be dispelled; and when one should go, then one goes, and when drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled, then one dispels them; and as one should go, so one goes, and as drowsiness and fatigue should be dispelled, so one dispels them —

body.text: saṃprajānadvihāritāyā[ḥ] katamā ānupūrvo, katamā ca stutibhāvanā, yathāpīhaikatyo yaṃ yameva grāmaṃ vā nigamamvopa[ni]śritya viharati | tasyaivaṃ bhavati | mayā khalvayaṃ grāmo vā, nigamo vā piṇḍāyopa[saṃ]kramitavyaḥ | piṇḍāya caritvā, punareva vihāraṃ [prati]niṣkramitavyaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: What is the gradual sequence of dwelling in full awareness (<s>saṃprajānadvihāritā</s>), and what is the praise of its cultivation? Just as here some person dwells in dependence upon a village or a town. He thinks thus: 'I must surely go to this village or town for alms. Having gone for alms, I must again go forth to the monastery.'

body.text: santi(|) punaratra kulāni grāme vā, nagare vā, yāni mayā nopasaṃkramitavyāni | tāni punaḥ katamāni | tadyathā | ghoṣaṃ(ṣaḥ), pānāgāraṃ, veśyaṃ, rājakulaṃ, caṇḍālakaṭhinamiti | yāni vā punaḥ kulānyekāntena pratihatānyapratyudāvarttāni [|] santi ca punaḥ kulāni yāni mayopasaṃkramitavyāni | tadyathā kṣatriyamahāsālakulāni vā, brāhmaṇamahāsālakulāni vā, naigamakulāni vā, jānapadakulāni vā, dhanikulāni vā, śreṣṭhikulāni vā, sārthavāhakulāni vā mayopasaṃkramitavyāni, tāni nātisāyamupasaṃkramitavyāni | tānivikālaṃ, na ca kāryavyagreṣu dāyakadānapatiṣu, na (

children.text: ) krīḍāratimaṇḍanayogamanuyukteṣu, na grāmyadharmāya pravṛtteṣu, na kupiteṣu [|] tathā copasaṃkramitavyāni yathopasaṃkramannahanna bhrāntena hastinā sārdhaṃ samāgaccheyaṃ, na bhrāntena sthena, punaḥ caṇḍenāśvena, na caṇḍayā gavā, na caṇḍena kukkureṇa, na gahanaṃ, na kaṇṭakāvāṭaṃ vā mardeyaṃ | na śvabhre, palvale, prapāte prapateyaṃ | na syandikāyāṃ, na gūthakaṭhillacandropamaśca kulānyupasaṃkrameyaṃ | hrīmānapragalbhaḥ vyavakṛṣya kāyaṃ, vyavakṛṣya cittaṃ, na lābhakāmo na satkārakāmaḥ | yathā svena lābhena sucittaḥ, sumanāstathā parasyāvipralābhena sucittaḥ, sumanāḥ ananyotkarṣī, aparapaṃsakaḥ | anukampācitto, dayācittaḥ | evaṃ ca punarupasaṃkramitavyāni | tatkuta etallabhyaṃ pravrajitena parakuleṣu yaddadatu me pare, mā vā dadatu, yāvattvaritaṃ mā dhandhamiti vistareṇa [|] upasaṃkramya ca me [mayā] pratigrahe mātrā karaṇīyā | na ca lābhahetoḥ kuhanā karaṇīyā | lapanā, naimittikatā, naiṣpeṣikatā, lābhena lābhaniścikīrṣatā karaṇīyā(ḥ) | sa ca lābhaḥ araktena paribhoktavya[ḥ], asaktenāgṛddhenāgrathitenāmūḍhitena, anadhyavasitenādhyavasāyamāpannena [|] yāni ca rūpāṇi tatropasaṃkramatā upasaṃkrāntena vā draṣṭavyāni bhavanti | tānyekatyāni draṣṭavyāni | tatra yāni na draṣṭavyāni teṣu utkṣiptacakṣuṣā bhavitavyaṃ | susaṃhṛtendriyeṇa, yāni punardraṣṭavyāni (
children.translated_text: when they are engaged in sport, enjoyment, and adorning themselves, not when they are engaged in vulgar activities, not when they are angry. And I should approach in such a way that while approaching I would not encounter a raging elephant, nor a raging bull, nor a fierce horse, nor a fierce cow, nor a fierce dog; I should not trample through a thicket or a thorny ditch; I should not fall into a pit, a puddle, or a precipice; I should not [approach] through a gutter or through filth. And I should approach households like the moon — modest, without boldness, with body withdrawn, with mind withdrawn, not desiring gain, not desiring honor. Just as I am well-minded and well-disposed through my own gains, so I should be well-minded and well-disposed through the non-deprivation of others. Not exalting myself, not disparaging others. With a mind of sympathy and compassion. And I should approach in this manner. For what is obtainable by one who has gone forth, regarding others' households: 'Let others give to me or not give, as much as swift, not slow' — in detail. And having approached, I should exercise moderation in accepting. I should not engage in <s>kuhanā</s> (deceptive hinting) for the sake of gain, nor in <s>lapanā</s> (flattery), nor <s>naimittikatā</s> (hinting through signs), nor <s>naiṣpeṣikatā</s> (obtaining through pressure), nor in seeking gain through gain. And that gain should be consumed without attachment, without clinging, without greed, without binding, without delusion, without excessive investment, [while] having attained discernment. And whatever forms are to be seen while approaching or having approached, some of them should be seen. Among those that should not be seen, one should keep one's eyes averted, with the sense faculties well-restrained. But those that should be seen,
[one should see] having established well-placed <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) with regard to them.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, there are households in the village or town that I should not approach. Which are those? Namely: a cattle-pen, a tavern, a brothel, a royal household, or a caṇḍāla settlement. Or also those households that are completely hostile and will not turn [from hostility]. But there are households that I should approach — namely, households of great <s>Kṣatriya</s> householders, or great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders, or townsmen, or country-folk, or the wealthy, or guild-leaders, or caravan-leaders — these I should approach. I should not approach them too late in the day, not at an improper time, not when the donors and almgivers are busy with their tasks, not

body.text: kathaṃ rūpāṇi [punā] rūpāṇi nāvalokayitavyāni | tadyathā na narttako, na hāsako, na lāsaka iti [|] yadvā punaranyaccāvaraṇajātaṃ nṛtte vā, gīte vā, vādite vā pravṛttaṃ [|] tathā mātṛgrāmo viśeṣeṇa punaḥ śiśurudāravarṇo ra[ñjanī]ya iti yāni ca punā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭāni brahmacaryopaghātibhiḥ brahmacaryāntarāyāya, pāpakānāṃ cākuśalānāmvitarkāṇāṃ samudācārāya samvartteran | tadrūpāṇi rūpāṇi nāvalokayitavyāni, na vyavalokayitavyāni [|]
body.translated_text: And which forms should not be looked at? Namely: a dancer, a comedian, a performer; or anything else of an obstructing nature involved in dancing, singing, or music. Likewise, women especially — a young one, one of fine complexion, one who is charming. And whatever forms, when seen, would be destructive to the holy life, would be an obstacle to the holy life, and would lead to the arising of evil, unwholesome mental intentions — such forms should not be looked at, should not be examined.

Having returned to the monastery, having come back from those households, having gone forth [again], by day or by night, one should walk on one's individual walking-path for meditation (<s>caṃkrama</s>). Likewise, in one's own monastery, in one's own group, in one's own hut — the designated one, the individual one — not in another's section, not in an untrusted one, not in an uninvited one. Likewise, on a bed, a chair, a grass mat, in the forest, at the root of a tree, or in an empty dwelling — one should sit down, crossing the legs, setting the body upright, establishing <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) directed to the front. body.translated_text: And which forms should indeed be seen? Namely: one who is worn out, or old, or decrepit, whose body wheezes with rough labored breathing, whose body is bent forward, who leans on a stick with a trembling body; or one who is sick, suffering, severely ill — with swollen feet, swollen hands, swollen belly, swollen face, pallid and discolored; or one afflicted with skin disease, or with scabies, or with leprosy, with suffering-stricken limbs, with a body cooked [by fever], with impaired faculties; or one dead, who has passed away — dead for one day, or dead for two days, or dead for seven days, being eaten by crows and ospreys, by vultures, by dogs, by jackals, or by various animals of different species being devoured; or [a body] being placed upon a bier with a canopy spread over it, and behind it a great crowd of people weeping and wailing,

body.text: ālokasaṃjñinā smṛtena saṃprajā[nā]nena, utthānasaṃjñāmeva manasi kurvatā, rātryā[ḥ] paścime yāme laghuladhveva prativibudhya, bhāṣye vā, svādhyāyakriyāyāṃ vā yogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ | prahāṇe vā, pratisaṃlayane, dharmacintāyāṃ, lokāyatāśca maṃtrā vivarjayitavyāḥ (|) citrākṣaraścitrapadavyaṃjanā, anarthopasaṃhitā ye nābhijñāyai, na sambodhāya, na nirvāṇāya samvartante | ye vā punardharmāstathāgatabhāṣitā, gaṃbhīrā, gaṃbhīrābhāsā[ḥ], śūnyatāpratisaṃyuktā, idaṃpratyayā(yatā)pratītyasamutpādānulomāste satkṛtyodgṛ(dgra)hītavyāḥ | dṛḍhañca, sthirañca, sūdgṛhītāśca, na nāśayitavyāḥ | pratipattyā[ḥ] sampādanārthaṃ, na lābhasatkāra hetoḥ [|] te ca punardharmā vacasā suparijitāḥ kartavyāḥ | na ca saṃgaṇikayā atināmayitavyaṃ, na karmārāmatayā, na bhāṣyārāmatayā, kālena ca kālamupasthitayā smṛtyā vijñāsya(ssa)brahmacāriṇaḥ, ālapitavyāḥ, saṃlapitavyāḥ, pratisaṃbodhayitavyāḥ, paripṛcchana[jātī]yena ca bhavitavyaṃ, kiṃkuśalagaveṣiṇā || anupalaṃbhacittena, mitavādinā, yuktabhāṇinā, praśāntabhāṇinā ca || pareṣāṃ dhā(dha)rmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayitvā tvakāmena tūṣṇīṃbhāvena ca ye pāpakā akuśalā vitarkā nātitarkayitavyāḥ | na cāyoniśodharmacintāyuktena |
body.translated_text: with the perception of light, mindful, fully aware, keeping the perception of rising in mind. In the last watch of the night, having awoken quickly and lightly, one should apply oneself to recitation, or to the practice of self-study, or to abandonment, or to seclusion, or to reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>. And <s>lokāyata</s> (worldly materialist) <s>mantras</s> should be avoided — those with fancy letters and fancy words and expressions, connected with what is unprofitable, which do not conduce to higher knowledge, nor to awakening, nor to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. But those <s>dharmas</s> spoken by the <s>Tathāgata</s> (the Thus-Gone One) that are profound, that have the appearance of profundity, that are connected with emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), that accord with dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) and conditionality (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>) — those should be reverently learned, firmly, stably, and well-grasped; they should not be allowed to perish — for the purpose of accomplishing practice, not for the sake of gain and honor. And those <s>dharmas</s> should be well-mastered through verbal [recitation]. One should not pass time in socializing, nor in delight in work, nor in delight in talk. From time to time, with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) well-established, one should converse with, speak to, and instruct one's fellow practitioners in the holy life. One should be of an inquiring nature, seeking what is wholesome, with a mind free from grasping, speaking little, speaking what is fitting, speaking peacefully. Having spoken to others on a <s>Dharma</s> topic, being content, in silence — one should not excessively think evil, unwholesome thoughts. Nor should one be engaged in improper reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text:
How does one become an attainer (<s>adhigantā</s>)? One obtains the perception of impermanence (<s>anityasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of suffering in what is impermanent (<s>duḥkhasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of non-self in what is suffering (<s>anātmasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of repulsiveness in food (<s>āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of a blood-smeared [corpse] (<s>vilohitakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of a scattered [corpse] (<s>vikṣiptakasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of a skeleton (<s>asthisaṃjñā</s>), and the perception of contemplating emptiness (<s>śūnyatāpratyavekṣaṇasaṃjñā</s>). One obtains the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation absorption), the second, the third, the fourth, the sphere of infinite space (<s>ākāśānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of infinite consciousness (<s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s>), the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>), the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>karuṇā</s> (compassion), <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), <s>muditā</s> (sympathetic joy), the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), and the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) of two domains; the recollection of former lives (<s>pūrvenivāsa</s>), the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapāda</s>), the knowledge of others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>), <s>arhatva</s> (arhatship), and the mastery of the eight liberations (<s>aṣṭavimokṣa</s>). One becomes capable and powerful enough to instruct others through the three miraculous displays (<s>prātihārya</s>): the miraculous display of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>), the miraculous display of mind-reading (<s>ādeśanāprātihārya</s>), and the miraculous display of instruction (<s>anuśāsanāprātihārya</s>). Thus one becomes an attainer.
How does one become compassionate (<s>anukampaka</s>)? One is compassionate toward others — endowed with compassion (<s>kāruṇika</s>) and mercy (<s>dayāpanna</s>), desiring their welfare (<s>arthakāma</s>), desiring their benefit (<s>hitakāma</s>), desiring their happiness (<s>sukhakāma</s>), desiring their comfort (<s>sparśakāma</s>), desiring their safety and security (<s>yogakṣemakāma</s>). Thus one becomes compassionate.

body.translated_text: How is one patient (<s>kṣamāvān</s>)? When abused, one does not abuse in return; when provoked to anger, one does not provoke in return; when struck, one does not strike in return; when beaten, one does not beat in return. Even in the face of severe imprisonment, confinement, beating, threats, and mutilation, one considers oneself at fault. One traces it back to the ripening of <s>karma</s>. One does not become angry toward others, nor does one harbor resentment. Thus, even when disrespected, even when disparaged, even when reviled, one does not resort to retaliation and does not think of anything other than the purpose [of spiritual practice]. And one is patient with cold and heat, hunger and thirst, gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and serpents, with harsh words and hostile actions from others, with bodily sensations that are painful, intense, sharp, bitter, disagreeable, and life-threatening — one is patient, of the type that endures. Thus one is patient.

body.translated_text: Endowed with these eight qualities, one is an admonisher, a reminder, a reprover, an instructor, and a <s>Dharma</s>-teacher.

body.translated_text: How is one an admonisher (<s>codaka</s>)? One admonishes regarding higher moral conduct (<s>adhiśīla</s>) in case of failure in moral conduct, and regarding higher behavior (<s>adhyācāra</s>) in case of failure in behavior — on the basis of what is seen, heard, or suspected. One admonishes with what is true, not with what is false; at the right time, not at the wrong time; with what is connected to meaning, not disconnected from meaning; gently, not harshly; with the attitude of a friend, not out of hatred. Thus one is an admonisher.

body.translated_text: How does one remind of an offense? When a person falls into an offense, one remembers it and reminds that person: 'Venerable one, in such a place, regarding such a matter, at such a

body.text: kathaṃ dharmaṃ smārayati | yathāpi tacchrutānudgṛhītān dharmānekākī smarati | smartumicchati | tadyathā sūtraṃ, geyaṃ, vyākaraṇamiti vistareṇa pūrvavanna smarati | tamena (naṃ) smārayati | utsmāraṇikāmvāsyānuprayacchati | āpṛcchanaparipṛcchanikāṃ vā, evaṃ dharmāna smārayati |
body.translated_text: How does one remind of the <s>Dharma</s>? When someone alone remembers or wishes to remember the <s>Dharma</s> teachings that have been heard but not retained — such as <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, and so on in detail as before — but cannot remember, one reminds that person, or provides a memory aid, or questions and cross-questions [to help recall]. Thus one reminds of the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: kathaṃ dharma (arthaṃ) smārayati | yathāpi nathāṃ (cārthān) vismārayati (vismarati) | tamenaṃ smārayati | punarapi pratinavīkaroti | uttānī karoti | deśayati, saṃprakāśayati | yaccāpi kuśalamarthopasaṃhitaṃ, brahmacaryopasaṃhitaṃ | ciraka(kṛ)taṃ, cirabhāṣitamapyanusmārayitā bhavati | evaṃ smārako bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one remind of the meaning? When someone forgets the meanings, one reminds that person; one renews, clarifies, teaches, and illuminates [the meaning]. And whatever wholesome [teaching] is connected with meaning, connected with the holy life — even if long done, long spoken — one is a re-reminder of it. Thus one is a reminder.

body.text: kathamavavādako bhavati | prāvivekye pratisaṃlayane, yoge, manasikāra(re), śamathavipaśyanāyāṃ kālena kālamānulomikaṃ avavādaṃ pravarttayati | kālena ca kālaṃ tatpratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ karoti | tadyathā cetovinivaraṇasāṃpreyagāminīṃ śīlakathāmvā, prajñākathāmvā, vimuktikathāmvā, alpecchakathāmvā, vimuktijñānadarśanakathāmvā, saṃtuṣṭikathāmvā, prahāṇakathāṃ, virāgakathāṃ, nirodhakathāṃ, apacayakathāṃ, asaṃsargakathāṃ, idaṃpratyaya[tā (

children.translated_text: discourse in accordance with dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>). Thus one is an instructor.

body.translated_text: How is one an instructor (<s>avavādaka</s>)? Regarding seclusion (<s>prāvivekya</s>), meditative absorption (<s>pratisaṃlayana</s>), <s>yoga</s>, attention (<s>manasikāra</s>), and <s>śamatha</s>-<s>vipaśyanā</s> (calm abiding and insight), one gives timely instruction in accordance [with the practitioner's needs]. And from time to time one engages in discourse connected with those [practices] — such as discourse that removes the hindrances of the mind and leads to the higher good: discourse on moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), or on wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), or on liberation (<s>vimukti</s>), or on fewness of desires (<s>alpeccha</s>), or on the knowledge and vision of liberation (<s>vimuktijñānadarśana</s>), or on contentment (<s>saṃtuṣṭi</s>), discourse on abandonment (<s>prahāṇa</s>), on dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), on cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), on diminishing [defilements] (<s>apacaya</s>), on non-association (<s>asaṃsarga</s>), on conditionality (<s>idaṃpratyayatā</s>),

body.text: kathamanuśāsako bhavati | dharmeṇa, vinayena, samanuśāstuḥ śāsane ācāryo vā bhavati | upādhyāyo vā, sahadhārmiko vā, gururvā, gurusthānīyo vā, anyatamānyatamasminnadhikaraṇe atisṛtaṃ, vyatikrāntaṃ viditvā | kālena kālamavasādayati | daṇḍakarmama(rmā)nuprayacchati | praṇāmayati cainaṃ | punarapi ca dharmeṇa samayepratisaṃstarasāmīcīsaṃjñaptiṃ pratigṛhaṇāti | saṃrohakaśca bhavati | karaṇīye cākaraṇīye bhāvyācārānadhyācārān adhyācīrṇe (carite) anadhyācīrṇe (carite) ca śāstyanuśāstyevamanuśāsako bhavati |
body.translated_text: How is one a discipliner (<s>anuśāsaka</s>)? According to the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), in the teaching of the instructor — whether one is a teacher (<s>ācārya</s>), a preceptor (<s>upādhyāya</s>), a co-practitioner (<s>sahadhārmika</s>), an elder (<s>guru</s>), one in the position of an elder, [or another] — having learned of a transgression or violation in any matter whatsoever, one from time to time subdues [the offender], administers disciplinary action, and makes one bow down. And again, according to the <s>Dharma</s>, one accepts the proper acknowledgment of the <s>samaya</s> (agreement) and <s>sāmīcī</s> (formal amends). And one reconciles [the parties]. Regarding what is to be done and not to be done, proper conduct and improper conduct, what has been transgressed and what has not been transgressed — one disciplines and instructs. Thus one is a discipliner.

body.text: kathaṃ ca dharmadeśako bhavati | kālena kālaṃ pūrvakālakaraṇīyāṃ kathāṃ karoti | tadyathā dānakathāṃ, śīlakathāṃ, svargakathāṃ, kāmeṣvādīnava niḥsaraṇaṃ, vyavadānapakṣāndharmān vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati | kālena kālaṃ caturāryasatyapratisaṃyuktāṃ kathāṃ kathayati | duḥkhaṃ vā ārabhya, samudayamvā, nirodhamvā, phalamvā, saparipākāya (sattvasaṃkleśāya?) vā, satva(ttva) vyavadānāya vā, saddharmasya vā cirasthitaye, yuktaiḥ padavyaṃjanaiḥ, sahitairānulomikairānucchavikairaupāyikaiḥ, (

children.text: ) pratirūpaiḥ, pradakṣiṇairnipakasyāṃgasaṃbhāraistāṃ ca punaḥ kathāṃ kālena karoti | satkṛtyānusandhimanupatitāṃ | harṣayan, rocayannanu(yannu)tsāhayannanavasādayaṃśca yuktāṃ, sahitāṃ, avyavakīrṇāṃ, yathādhārmikīṃ, yathāparṣanmaitracitto, hitacittaḥ, anukampācittaḥ | aniśrito lābhasatkāraślokena cātmānamutkarṣayati | na parānpaṃsa(paṃsa)yatyevaṃ dharmadeśako bhavati |
children.translated_text: suitable, auspicious, and comprising the limbs of a discerning [teacher]. And that discourse one delivers at the right time, respectfully, maintaining continuity. Gladdening, inspiring, and encouraging, without causing despair; [delivering it] properly, harmoniously, without confusion, in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, in accordance with the assembly, with a mind of friendliness, a mind of benefit, a mind of compassion; not relying on gain, honor, and fame. And one does not exalt oneself nor disparage others. Thus one is a <s>Dharma</s>-teacher.

body.translated_text: How is one a <s>Dharma</s>-teacher? From time to time one gives preliminary discourse — such as discourse on generosity (<s>dāna</s>), discourse on moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), discourse on heaven (<s>svarga</s>), the danger in sense-pleasures, renunciation, and the factors on the side of purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>) — illuminating [them] in detail. And from time to time one gives discourse connected with the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>) — beginning with suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), or its origin (<s>samudaya</s>), or cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), or the path (<s>phala</s>), or for the maturation [of beings], or for the purification of beings, or for the long endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s> — with proper phrases and syllables, that are harmonious, consistent, appropriate,

body.text: yaścaibhiraṣṭābhi(ḥ) (samanvāgato) raṃgaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati | evaṃ ca kālena kālaṃ codako bhavati, smārakaḥ | avavādānuśāsakastasmāt kalyāṇamitra[m]ityucyate | ayaṃ tāvat kalyāṇamitratāyā vistaravibhāgaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: One who is endowed with these eight qualities — and who from time to time is an admonisher, a reminder, an instructor and discipliner — is therefore called a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend). This is the detailed analysis of <s>kalyāṇamitratā</s> (spiritual friendship).

body.text: samāsārthaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ [|] sa cedayaṃ mitrasuhṛdanukampakaḥ ādita eva hitakāmo bhavati | sukhakāmaśca [|] tacca punarhitasukhaṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | aviparyasto bhavatyaviparītadṛṣṭiḥ, pratibalaśca bhavatyupāyakuśalaḥ | yadutāsyaiva hitasukhasya samudāgamāyosaṃhārāya dakṣaśca bhavatyanalasa, utthānasampanna, ārabdhavīryajātīyaḥ | yaduta tameva hitasukhopasaṃhāramārabhya [|] (

children.text: ) ebhiścaturbhiḥ kāraṇaiḥ sarvākāraparipūrṇaḥ (ṃ) | samāsataḥ kalyāṇamitro (traṃ) veditavyaḥ (vyam) | ayaṃ ca punaḥ kalyāṇamitratāyāḥ samāsārthaḥ || yaśca pūrvo vistaravibhāgaḥ, yaścāyaṃ samāsārtha iyamucyate kalyāṇamitratā ||
children.translated_text: by these four qualities, in summary, one should be known as a <s>kalyāṇamitra</s> (spiritual friend) complete in all aspects. This is the summary meaning of <s>kalyāṇamitratā</s>. Both the previous detailed analysis and this summary meaning — this is called <s>kalyāṇamitratā</s> (spiritual friendship).

body.translated_text: What then is the summary meaning? If such a friend, companion, and sympathizer is from the very beginning one who desires benefit and desires happiness [for the other], and moreover understands that benefit and happiness as it really is, is not in error, has correct views, and has the capacity and skill in methods — namely, for the accomplishment and gathering of that very benefit and happiness — and is skilled, not lazy, endowed with initiative, of the type that has aroused vigor — namely, undertaking that very gathering of benefit and happiness;

body.text: saddharmaśravaṇacintanā katamā | saddharma ucyate buddhaiśca buddhaśrāvakaiśca sadbhiḥ samyaggataiḥ satpuruṣairākhyātaḥ | deśita uttāno vivṛtaḥ | saṃprakāśitaḥ | sa punaḥ katamaḥ | tadyathā sūtraṃ, geyaṃ, vyākaraṇamiti vistareṇa pūrvavat | dvādaśāṃgavacogataṃ saddharma ityucyate |
body.translated_text: What is <s>saddharmaśravaṇacintanā</s> (hearing and reflecting on the true <s>Dharma</s>)? The true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharma</s>) is said to be that which has been declared, taught, explained, disclosed, and illuminated by the <s>Buddhas</s> and the <s>Buddha</s>'s disciples — the good, the rightly gone, the true persons. What then is that? Namely, <s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, and so forth in detail as before. That which pertains to the twelve branches of the word [of the <s>Buddha</s>] (<s>dvādaśāṅgavacana</s>) is called the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: tatra sūtraṃ katamat | yattatra tatra bhagavatā tāṃstān (tāni tāni) vineyācaritāni cārabhya skandhapratisaṃyuktā vā kathā kṛtā, dhātupratisaṃyuktāvā kathā kṛtā, dhātusaṃgaṇasaṃyuktā vā, āyatanapratisaṃyuktā vā | pratītyasamutpādapratisaṃyuktā vā, āhārasatyasthiti [prati]saṃyuktā vā, śrāvakapratyekabuddhatathāgatapratisaṃyuktā vā | smṛtyupasthānasamyakprahāṇadhi(rdhi)pādendriyabalabodhyaṃgamārgāṃgapratisaṃyuktā | aśubhā, ānāpānasmṛtiśikṣāvetyaprasādapratisaṃyuktā kathā kṛtā [|] sā ca kathā saṃgītikāraiḥ parigṛhya śāsanacirasthitaye, yathā yogamanupūrveṇa racitā, anupūrveṇa samāyuktā | pratirūpairnāmakāyapadavyaṃjanakāyairyaduta teṣāṃ teṣāmarthānāṃ sūcanāyai (

children.translated_text: wholesome, connected with meaning, connected with the <s>Buddha</s>'s practice — this is called <s>sūtra</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>sūtra</s>? Whatever discourses the <s>Bhagavān</s> has given, here and there, beginning with the various deeds of those to be disciplined — discourse connected with the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), or discourse connected with the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), or connected with the classification of <s>dhātus</s>, or connected with the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense bases), or connected with <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), or connected with food, truth, and abiding, or connected with <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Tathāgatas</s>, or connected with the foundations of mindfulness (<s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>), right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>), bases of supernormal power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), faculties (<s>indriya</s>), powers (<s>bala</s>), factors of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and path-factors (<s>mārgāṅga</s>), or discourse connected with the contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>), mindfulness of breathing (<s>ānāpānasmṛti</s>), training, <s>vaiyāprasādya</s> (clarity/faith). That discourse, having been collected by the compilers of the council for the long endurance of the teaching, was arranged in due order according to method, properly combined — with appropriate name-bodies, phrase-bodies, and syllable-bodies — namely, for the indication of those various meanings,

body.text: geyaṃ katamat | yasyānte paryavasāne gāthā abhigītā, yacca sūtraṃ neyārthamidamucyate [geyaṃ] |
body.translated_text: What is <s>geya</s>? That at whose end or conclusion verses are sung, and whatever <s>sūtra</s> is of indirect meaning (<s>neyārtha</s>) — this is called <s>geya</s>.

body.text: vyākaraṇaṃ katamat | yasmiṃchrāvake (yasmiñchrāvake)bhyo [a]bhyatītakālagato (tau)upapattau vyākriyate | yacca sūtraṃ nītārthamidamucyate | vyākaraṇaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: What is <s>vyākaraṇa</s>? That in which <s>Śrāvakas</s> are given predictions regarding their past and future births. And whatever <s>sūtra</s> is of definitive meaning (<s>nītārtha</s>) — this is called <s>vyākaraṇa</s>.

body.text: gāthā katamā | yā na gadyena bhāṣitā | apitu pādopanibandhena dvipadā vā, tripadā vā, catuṣpadā vā, paṃcapadā vā, ṣaṭpadā vā iyamucyate gāthā ||
body.translated_text: What is <s>gāthā</s>? That which is not spoken in prose, but is arranged in metrical feet — two-footed, three-footed, four-footed, five-footed, or six-footed — this is called <s>gāthā</s>.

body.text: udānā katamā | yatpudgalasya nāma gotramaparikīrtayitvā (kīrttya), uddiśya bhāṣitamāyatyāmvā saddharmasthitaye, (

children.translated_text: and for the endurance of the teaching — this is called <s>udāna</s>.

body.translated_text: What is <s>udāna</s>? That which is spoken without announcing the name and lineage of the individual, directed [to a general audience], for the future endurance of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

body.text: nidānaṃ katamat | yatpudgalasya nāmagotramparikīrtayitvā (kīrttya) uddiśya bhāṣitam | yacca vinayapratisaṃyuktaṃ sotpattikaṃ sanidānaṃ prātimokṣasūtramidamucyate [nidānaṃ] [|]
body.translated_text: What is <s>nidāna</s>? That which is spoken having announced the name and lineage of the individual, directed [to that person]. And whatever is connected with the <s>Vinaya</s> (discipline), having an origin and a cause — the <s>Prātimokṣa</s>-sūtra — this is called <s>nidāna</s>.

body.text: avadānaṃ katamat | yatsadṛṣṭāntakamudāhataṃ | yena dṛṣṭāntena yasya prakṛtasyārthasya vyavadānaṃ bhavatīdamucyate | avadānaṃ |
body.translated_text: What is <s>avadāna</s>? That which is set forth with an analogy, by which analogy the purification of the subject matter takes place — this is called <s>avadāna</s>.

body.text: vṛttaṃ katamat | yatkiṃcitpūrvayogapratisaṃyuktamidamucyate vṛttakaṃ ||
body.translated_text: What is <s>vṛtta</s> (narrative)? Whatever is connected with a former connection (<s>pūrvayoga</s>) — this is called <s>vṛttaka</s>.

body.text: jātakaṃ katamat | yadatītamadhvānamupādāya tatra tatra bhagavataḥ cyutyupapādeṣu bodhisattvacaryā duṣkaracaryā | ākhyātā [|] idamucyate jātakaṃ ||
body.translated_text: What is <s>jātaka</s> (birth story)? That which, taking from the past, narrates the <s>Bodhisattva</s> conduct and difficult practices of the <s>Bhagavān</s> in his various deaths and rebirths — this is called <s>jātaka</s>.

body.text: vaipulyaṃ katamat | yatra bodhisattvānāṃ mārgo deśyate | anuttarāyai samyak saṃbodhaye | daśabalānāvaraṇajñānasamudāgamāya [|] idamucyate vaipulyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: What is <s>vaipulya</s> (extensive teaching)? That in which the path of the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is taught — for the unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), for the attainment of the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) and unobstructed knowledge — this is called <s>vaipulya</s>.

body.text: adbhutādharmāḥ katame | yatra buddhānāñca, buddhaśrāvakāṇāṃ ca, bhikṣūṇāñca, bhikṣuṇīnāñca, śikṣamāṇānāṃ, śrāmaṇekī(rī)ṇāmupāsikānāṃ, sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇāśca tadanyaprativiśiṣṭāścāścaryādbhutasammatā guṇaviśeṣā ākhyātā ime ucyante adbhutā dharmāḥ ||
body.translated_text: What are the <s>adbhutadharmāḥ</s> (marvels)? Where the uncommon and common extraordinary and marvelous qualities — esteemed as wonderful and astonishing — of <s>Buddhas</s>, disciples of <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇīs</s>, <s>śikṣamāṇās</s> (probationary nuns), <s>śrāmaṇerīs</s> (novice nuns), and <s>upāsikās</s> (female lay followers), as well as those surpassing others, are declared — these are called <s>adbhutadharmāḥ</s> (marvels).

body.text: upadeśāḥ katame [|] sarvamātṛkā abhidharmaḥ sūtrāntaniṣkarṣaḥ | sūtrāntavyākhyānamupadeśa ityucyate |
body.translated_text: What are the <s>upadeśāḥ</s> (instructions)? The entire <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrix); the <s>Abhidharma</s>; the extraction from the <s>sūtrāntas</s>. The explanation of the <s>sūtrāntas</s> is called <s>upadeśa</s> (instruction).

body.text: taccaitad dvādaśāṃgavacogatamasti sūtramasti vinayaḥ, astyabhidharmaḥ | tatra yattāvadāha | sūtraṃ geyaṃ vyākaraṇaṃ gāthodānāvadānavṛttakajātakavaipulyādbhutadharmā iti | idaṃ tāvatsūtraṃ | yatpunarāha | nidānamityayamucyate | vinayaḥ | yatpunarāha | upadeśā iti | ayamucyate | abhidharmaḥ |
body.translated_text: And this twelve-limbed word [of the <s>Buddha</s>] consists of <s>sūtra</s>, <s>vinaya</s>, and <s>abhidharma</s>. Therein, what is stated as: "<s>sūtra</s>, <s>geya</s>, <s>vyākaraṇa</s>, <s>gāthā</s>, <s>udāna</s>, <s>avadāna</s>, <s>vṛttaka</s>, <s>jātaka</s>, <s>vaipulya</s>, <s>adbhutadharma</s>" — this is the <s>sūtra</s> [basket]. What is further stated as "<s>nidāna</s>" — this is called <s>vinaya</s>. What is further stated as "<s>upadeśāḥ</s>" — this is called <s>abhidharma</s>.

body.text: taccaitad dvādaśāṃ[gaṃ śru]taṃ piṭakatrayasaṃgṛhītaṃ | sadbhiḥ samyaggatairdeśitaṃ | saddharma ityucyate | tasya śravaṇaṃ | saddharmaśravaṇaṃ [|] tatpunaḥ katamat | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ (

children.text: ) sūtradharo vā bhavati | vinayadharo vā | mātṛkādharo vā, sūtravinayadharo vā, sūtrābhidharmadharo vā, vinayamātṛkādharo vā | idamucyate saddharmaśravaṇaṃ | tatpunaḥ | śravaṇaṃ dvividhaṃ | vyaṃjanaśrama(va)ṇamarthaśravaṇaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: is a bearer of <s>sūtras</s>, or a bearer of <s>vinaya</s>, or a bearer of <s>mātṛkā</s>, or a bearer of <s>sūtra</s> and <s>vinaya</s>, or a bearer of <s>sūtra</s> and <s>abhidharma</s>, or a bearer of <s>vinaya</s> and <s>mātṛkā</s> — this is called hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>. And furthermore, hearing is twofold: hearing the letter (<s>vyañjanaśravaṇa</s>) and hearing the meaning (<s>arthaśravaṇa</s>).

body.translated_text: And this twelve-limbed <s>śruta</s> (teaching) is encompassed by the <s>tripiṭaka</s> (three baskets). Taught by those who are good and have gone the right way, it is called the <s>saddharma</s> (true Dharma). The hearing of it is <s>saddharmaśravaṇa</s> (hearing the true Dharma). What then is that? Just as here, someone

body.text: cintanā katamā | yathāpīhaikatyastāneva yathāśrutāndharmānekākī rahogataḥ | ṣaḍacintyāni sthānānitadyathā, ātmacintāṃ, sattvacintāṃ, lokacintāṃ, satvā(ttvā)nāṃ karmavipākacintāṃ, dhyāyināṃ dhyāyiviṣayaṃ, buddhānāṃ buddhaviṣayaṃ varjayitvā svalakṣaṇataḥ | sāmānyalakṣaṇataśca cintayati |
body.translated_text: What is <s>cintanā</s> (reflection)? Just as here, someone, alone and in seclusion, [reflects on] those very <s>dharmas</s> as heard — setting aside the six things that are inconceivable, namely: reflection on the self, reflection on beings, reflection on the world, reflection on the karmic ripening of beings, the domain of meditators, and the domain of <s>Buddhas</s> — and reflects upon them in terms of their particular characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇa</s>) and general characteristics (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.text: sā punaḥ cintā dvividhā gaṇanākārāsaha gaṇanāyogena dharmeṇa | tulanākārama(rā), yuktyā guṇadoṣaparīkṣaṇākārā [ca] [|] sa cetskandhapratisaṃyuktāṃ deśanāṃ cintayati | sa cedanyatamānyatamānyatamāṃ pūrvaniviṣṭāṃ deśanāṃ cintayatyābhyāṃ cintayati | yathā punaḥ kathami tirūpamucyate | daśa rūpīṇyāyatanānīti | yacca dharmāyatanaparyāpannaṃ rūpaṃ sa ca rūpaskandhaḥ, tisro (

children.text: ) vedanā vedanāskandhaḥ | ṣaṭ saṃjñākāyāḥ saṃjñāskandhaḥ | ṣaṭ cetanākāyāḥ cetanāskandhaḥ | ṣaḍ vijñānakāyā vijñānaskandha ityevaṃ gaṇanāsaṃkhyākārāṃ skandha[gaṇanāṃ] cintayatyuttarottaraprabhedena yena vā punarasyāḥ saṃkhyāgaṇanā kārāyāścintāyā apramāṇaḥ praveśanayo veditavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>vedanās</s> (feelings) constitute the <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling); the six groups of <s>saṃjñā</s> (perception) constitute the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of perception); the six groups of <s>cetanā</s> (volition) constitute the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations); the six groups of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) constitute the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness). Thus, he reflects on the enumeration and counting of the <s>skandhas</s> by way of successive subdivisions. And it should be understood that the mode of entry into this enumeration and counting form of reflection is immeasurable.

body.translated_text: And that reflection is twofold: by the mode of enumeration (<s>gaṇanākāra</s>), that is, by the method of counting; and by the mode of comparison (<s>tulanākāra</s>), that is, by reasoning and examination of merits and faults. If he reflects on a teaching related to the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), or if he reflects on some or another previously established teaching, he reflects by these two [modes]. How, then, is form spoken of thus? "There are ten <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) that are material" — and whatever form is included in the <s>dharmāyatana</s>, that too is the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form); the three

body.text: kathaṃ yuktyupaparīkṣākārayā cintayā skandhadeśanāṃ cintayati | catasṛbhiryuktibhirupaparīkṣate | katamābhiścatasṛbhiryadutāpekṣāyuktyā, kāryakāraṇayuktyā, upapattisādhanayuktyā | dharmatāyuktyā ||
body.translated_text: How does one reflect on the teaching concerning the <s>skandhas</s> by the mode of reasoned examination? One examines by means of four types of reasoning (<s>yukti</s>). Which four? Namely: the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>), the reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>), the reasoning of proof by evidence (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>), and the reasoning of the nature of things (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>).

body.text: apekṣāyuktiḥ katamā | dvividhā apekṣā utpatyapekṣā prajñaptyapekṣā ca | tatrotpattyapekṣā yairhetupratyayaiḥ skandhānāṃ prādurbhāvo bhavati | tasyāṃ skandhotpattau te hetavaste, pratyayā apekṣyante | yairnāmakāyapadakāyavyaṃjanakāyaiḥ skandhānāṃ prajñaptirbhavati | tasyāṃ skandhaprajñaptau te nāmapadakāyavyaṃjanakāyā apekṣyante | iyamucyate skandheṣūtpattyapekṣā | prajñaptyapekṣatā (kṣā) ca | yā cotpattyapekṣā | yā ca prajñaptyapekṣā sā yuktiryoga (

children.translated_text: that means — is for the arising of the <s>skandhas</s> and for the designation of the <s>skandhas</s>; therefore it is called the reasoning of dependence.

body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>)? Dependence is twofold: dependence with respect to arising (<s>utpattyapekṣā</s>) and dependence with respect to designation (<s>prajñaptyapekṣā</s>). Therein, dependence with respect to arising: those causes and conditions by which the <s>skandhas</s> come into manifestation — in that arising of the <s>skandhas</s>, those causes and conditions are what is depended upon. Those groups of names, phrases, and syllables (<s>nāmakāya</s>, <s>padakāya</s>, <s>vyañjanakāya</s>) by which the <s>skandhas</s> are designated — in that designation of the <s>skandhas</s>, those groups of names, phrases, and syllables are what is depended upon. This is called the dependence with respect to arising and dependence with respect to designation in the <s>skandhas</s>. And whatever is the dependence with respect to arising and whatever is the dependence with respect to designation — that reasoning, that logical method,

body.text: kāryakāraṇayuktiryā [ta]dutpannānāṃ skandhānāṃ svena hetunā svena pratyaryena tasmiṃstasmin svakāryakaraṇe viniyogastadyathā | cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi draṣṭavyāni | śrotreṇa śabdā[ḥ] śrotavyāḥ | yāvanmanasā dharmā vijñeyā iti | rūpeṇa cakṣuṣo gocare avasthātavyaṃ | śabdena śrotrasya, evaṃ yāddharmairmanasa iti | yadvā punaranyadapyevaṃbhāgīyaṃ | tatra tatra dharmāṇāmanyo [a]nyaṃ kāryakāraṇe pratiyuktiryoga upāya iyamucyate | kāryakāraṇayuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>)? The employment of the arisen <s>skandhas</s>, each by its own cause and its own condition, in its own particular function — for example: "Forms are to be seen by the eye; sounds are to be heard by the ear; up to — <s>dharmas</s> are to be cognized by the mind." And: "Form is to remain in the domain of the eye; sound in that of the ear; and so on up to — <s>dharmas</s> in that of the mind." Or whatever else is of the same kind. The mutual dependence of <s>dharmas</s> upon one another in their respective cause-and-effect [relations], in their respective [domains] — that reasoning, that logical method, that means — this is called the reasoning of cause and effect.

body.text: upapattisādhanayuktiḥ katamā [|] anityā[ḥ] skandhā iti, pratītyasamutpannā, duḥkhā[ḥ], śūnyā, anātmāna iti tribhiḥ pramāṇairupaparīkṣate yadu(ta)tāptāgamena, pratyakṣeṇānumānena ca [|] ebhistribhiḥ pramāṇairūpapattiyuktaiḥ satāṃ hṛdayagrāhakairvyavasthāpanā (

children.text: ) sādhanā kriyate | yaduta skandhānityatāyā vā, pratītyasamutpannatāyā vā, duḥkhatāyā[ḥ], śūnyatāyā, iyamucyate upapattisādhanayuktiḥ |
children.translated_text: establishment and proof are made of the impermanence of the <s>skandhas</s>, their dependent origination, their nature as suffering, and their emptiness. This is called the reasoning of proof by evidence.

body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of proof by evidence (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>)? [The propositions that] the <s>skandhas</s> are impermanent, dependently arisen, suffering, empty, and without self — these are examined by means of three <s>pramāṇas</s> (valid means of knowledge), namely: the testimony of the trustworthy (<s>āptāgama</s>), direct perception (<s>pratyakṣa</s>), and inference (<s>anumāna</s>). By these three valid means of knowledge — which are logically established and convincing to the hearts of the good —

body.text: dharmatāyuktiḥ katamā | kena kāraṇena tathābhūtā ete skandhā[ḥ], tathābhūto lokasanniveśaḥ kena kāraṇena kharalakṣaṇā pṛthivī, dravalakṣaṇā āpaḥ, uṣṇalakṣaṇaṃ tejaḥ[ḥ], samudīraṇalakṣaṇo vāyuḥ, (|) anityāḥ, skandhā[ḥ], kena kāraṇena śāntaṃ nirvāṇamiti | tathā rūpaṇalakṣaṇaṃ rūpaṃ | anubhavalakṣaṇā vedanā, saṃjānanalakṣaṇā saṃjñā, abhisaṃskaraṇalakṣaṇāḥ saṃskārāḥ, vijānanālakṣaṇaṃ vijñānamiti | prakṛtireṣāṃ dharmāṇāmiyaṃ svabhāva eṣa īdṛśaḥ | dharmataiṣā caiva cāsau dharmatā | saivātra yuktiryoga upāyaḥ [|] evaṃ vā etat syāt | anyathā vā, naiva vā syāt, sarvatraiva ca dharmataiva pratiprasaraṇadharmataiva yuktiḥ | cittanidhyāyanāya, cittasaṃjñāpanāya iyamucyate dharmatāyuktiḥ |
body.translated_text: What is the reasoning of the nature of things (<s>dharmatāyukti</s>)? For what reason are these <s>skandhas</s> of such a nature? For what reason is the arrangement of the world thus? For what reason does earth have the characteristic of hardness, water the characteristic of fluidity, fire the characteristic of heat, wind the characteristic of agitation? [For what reason] are the <s>skandhas</s> impermanent? For what reason is <s>nirvāṇa</s> peaceful? And [why does] form have the characteristic of being affected (<s>rūpaṇa</s>), <s>vedanā</s> the characteristic of experiencing, <s>saṃjñā</s> the characteristic of discerning, <s>saṃskāras</s> the characteristic of conditioning, and <s>vijñāna</s> the characteristic of cognizing? Such is their nature, such is their essence, such is this <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of things). That very <s>dharmatā</s> is here the reasoning, the logical method, the means. Whether it is thus or otherwise or not at all — in every case, <s>dharmatā</s> alone is the recourse, <s>dharmatā</s> alone is the reasoning — for the purpose of mental reflection and mental conviction. This is called the reasoning of the nature of things.

body.text: evaṃ catasṛbhiryuktabhiḥ skandhadeśanā upaparīkṣyata iti | yāvatpunaranyā kāciddeśanā iti yā evamābhyāṃ dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ gaṇanāsaṃkhyākārā ca yuktyupaparīkṣaṇākārā ca samyagupanidhyāyanā tasyāstasyā deśanāyāiyamucyate | saddharmaśravaṇacinta[n]ā ||
body.translated_text: Thus, the teaching on the <s>skandhas</s> is examined by these four types of reasoning. And with respect to whatever other teaching — by these very two modes, the mode of enumeration and counting and the mode of reasoned examination — [constitutes] proper mental contemplation of that teaching. This is called the reflection (<s>cintanā</s>) on hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: anantarāyaḥ katamaḥ [|] anantarāyo dvividhaḥ | adhyātmamupādāya bahirdhā ca [|] tatrādhyātmaṃ bahirdhā copādāyāntarāya(yaṃ) vakṣyati | tadviparyayeṇa [|] nantarāyo veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is the absence of obstacles (<s>anantarāya</s>)? The absence of obstacles is twofold: with reference to the internal (<s>adhyātma</s>) and with reference to the external (<s>bahirdhā</s>). Therein, the obstacles with reference to the internal and external will be stated; by their opposite, the absence of obstacles should be understood.

body.text: adhyātmamupādāyāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ pūrvameva kṛtapuṇyo bhavati | saukṛtatvāt puṇyānāṃ ca lābhī bhavati | kālena kālamānulomikāṃ (kānāṃ, keṣu) jīvitapariṣkārāṇāṃ (reṣu) | yaduta cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ (reṣu) tīvrarāgo bhavatyāyata (na)rāgaḥ | tīvradveṣaḥ āyata(na)dveṣaḥ | tīvramoha āyata(na)mohaḥ | pūrvaṃ vānenābādhasaṃvarttanīyāni karmāṇi kṛtāni bhavanti | yaddhetorābādhabahulo bhavati | dṛṣṭa eva dharme viṣamacārī bhavati | yo (ye)nāsyābhīkṣṇaṃ vāto vā kupyati, pittamvā, śleṣmamvā, viṣūcikā vā kāye santiṣṭhate | bhojanaguruko bhavati | bahvartho, bahukṛtyo, gaṇasannipātabahulo bhavati | karmārāmo vā, bhāṣyārāmo vā, nidrārāgaḥ (maḥ), saṃgaṇikārāmaḥ | ātmasaṃpragrāhakaścapalaḥ, pramattaḥ kudeśavāsī vā | ityevaṃbhāgīyā antarāyā adhyātmamupādāya veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: What is the obstacle with reference to the internal? Just as here, someone has previously performed merit. Due to [past] good deeds, he obtains requisites of livelihood in due course — namely, robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick. [Yet] he has intense craving, persistent craving; intense aversion, persistent aversion; intense delusion, persistent delusion. Or he has previously performed actions that bring about affliction, on account of which he is much afflicted. In this very life, he engages in unwholesome conduct, whereby wind frequently disorders him, or bile, or phlegm, or cholera (<s>viṣūcikā</s>) establishes itself in the body. He is heavy with food, has many concerns, many duties, and is often in group assemblies. He delights in work, delights in talk, is fond of sleep, delights in socializing, is self-promoting, fickle, heedless, or dwells in an unfavorable place. Obstacles of this and similar kinds, with reference to the internal, should be understood.

body.text: bahirdhopādāyāntarāyāḥ katame [|] tathāpi tadasatpuruṣāpāśrayaḥ | yato na labhate kālena kālamānulomikīmavavādānuśāsanīṃ [|] (

children.text: ) kudeśe vā vasati | yatrāsya vāsa(saṃ)kalpayato divā vāgraviloko (vogro raverāloko) bhavati | prabhūtaḥ, rātrau vā [|] uccaśabdo, mahāśabdomahājanakāyasya nirghoṣaḥ | tīvrakaṭukaśca vātātapasaṃsparśo, manuṣyādapi bhayamayamevaṃbhāgīyo bahirdhāpāyā(rdhopādāyā)ntarāyo veditavyaḥ | ayaṃ tāvadvistaravibhāgasyā(gaḥ) ||
children.translated_text: Or he dwells in an unfavorable place where, when he intends to settle, during the day the sunlight is intense and abundant, or at night there are loud sounds, great sounds, the roar of a great crowd of people, and the contact of wind and heat is sharp and harsh, and there is fear even from humans. Obstacles of this and similar kinds, with reference to the external, should be understood. This, then, is the detailed analysis.

body.translated_text: What are the obstacles with reference to the external? Likewise, he relies on bad persons, from whom he does not obtain timely and appropriate admonishment and instruction.

body.text: samāsārthaḥ punaḥ katamaḥ | samāsatastrividho [a]ntarāyaḥ | prayogāntarāya[ḥ], prāvivekyāntarāya[ḥ] | pratisaṃlayanā ntarāyaśca |
body.translated_text: What is the summary meaning? In brief, the obstacles are threefold: the obstacle to practice (<s>prayogāntarāya</s>), the obstacle to seclusion (<s>prāvivekyāntarāya</s>), and the obstacle to meditative absorption (<s>pratisaṃlayanāntarāya</s>).

body.text: tatra prayogāntarāyo yenāntarāyeṇa samava[hitena] saṃmukhībhūtenāśakto bhavatyapratibalaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ kuśalapakṣaprayoge [|] sa punaḥ katamaḥ | yadābādhako bhavati, bāḍhaglānaḥ, abhīkṣṇamasya vāto vā kupyate, pittamvā, śleṣmamvā (ṣma vā), viṣūcikā vāsya kāye santiṣṭhate [|] api tvasya daśati vṛściko vā, śatapadī vā, manuṣyo vainaṃ viheṭhayatyamanuṣyo vā [|] na ca lābhī bhavati cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāmayamevaṃbhāgīyaḥ prayogāntarāyo veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the obstacle to practice is that obstacle which, when encountered and come face-to-face with, renders one incapable and powerless in all practice of the wholesome. What is that? When one is afflicted, severely ill, when wind frequently disorders him, or bile, or phlegm, or cholera establishes itself in the body; or when a scorpion, a centipede, or a human being torments him, or a non-human being; and when he does not obtain robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicines for the sick. Obstacles of this and similar kinds should be understood as obstacles to practice.

body.text: prāvivekyāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ [|] yadbhojanaguruko bhavati, bahvartho, bahukṛtyo, bahukaraṇīyaḥ, karmārāmaratiṃ (

children.text: ) rato bhavati | teṣu teṣvitikaraṇīyeṣu prasṛtamānasaḥ | bhāṣyārāmo bhavati | śaktaḥ pratibalaḥ san | prāvivekyaprahāṇe, pratisaṃlayane, bhāvanāyāmuddeśamvādhyāyamātrakena(ṇa) saṃtuṣṭo nidrārāmo bhavati | styānamiddhaparyavasthitaḥ, kusīdajātīyo nidrāsukhaṃ, pārśvasukhaṃ, śayanasukhaṃ ca svīkaroti | saṃgaṇikārāmo bhavati sārdhaṃ gṛhasthapravrajitaiḥ | rājakathāmvā karoti | corakathāṃ vā, annakathāṃ vā, pānakathāṃ vā, vastukathāṃ vā, veśyākathāṃ vā, vīthīkathāmvā janapadamahāmātrākhyānakathāmvā, samudrākhyānakathāmvā [|] ityevaṃ bhāgīyayā anarthopasaṃhitayā kathayā kālamatināmayati | tatra cābhira(ma)to bhavatyabhīkṣṇeṇa(na) gaṇasannipātabahulo bhavati | teṣu teṣvadhikaraṇeṣu vyākṣiptamānaso bhavati | vyākulamānasaḥ | saṃsargārāmo bhavati | gṛhasthapravrajitānāmasamavahitānāṃ ca viyogaṃ gacchati | prapaṃcārāmo bhavati | prapaṃcarataḥ avakramaṇīyeṣu pūrvaṃgamaḥ, prāvivekyeṣu nikṣiptadhuraḥ | idamevaṃbhāgīyo (ima evaṃ bhāgīyā) dharmāḥ pravivekāntarāyo veditavyaḥ | yaiḥ samavahitaiḥ saṃmukhībhūtairna sukaraṃ bhavatyaraṇyavanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanānyadhyāvasituṃ | araṇyāni vā vṛkṣamūlāni (
children.translated_text: delight in work, with the mind engaged in all those various tasks; when one delights in talk — though capable and able for the abandonment of seclusion, for meditative absorption, and for cultivation — one is satisfied merely with study and recitation. One delights in sleep, is overcome by sloth and torpor, is of a lazy disposition, and cherishes the pleasure of sleeping, the pleasure of reclining, and the pleasure of lying down. One delights in socializing, with householders and renunciants alike. One engages in talk about kings, talk about thieves, talk about food, talk about drink, talk about goods, talk about courtesans, talk about streets, talk about stories of provincial officials, talk about stories of the ocean — and with such talk connected with purposelessness, one wastes time. And being delighted therein, one is frequently occupied with group assemblies, with the mind distracted and agitated in all those various matters. One delights in association, goes to the company of householders and renunciants who are inattentive. One delights in elaboration (<s>prapañca</s>), being fond of conceptual proliferation, foremost in what should be approached, and negligent in seclusion. These and similar <s>dharmas</s> should be understood as obstacles to seclusion — on account of which, when encountered and come face-to-face with, it is not easy to settle in remote forest and wilderness dwellings, in secluded lodgings, in forests, or at the roots of trees.

children.text:
