pratisaṃlayanāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ [|] tadyathā pratisaṃlayanamucyate śamatho vipaśyanā ca | tatrāsti śamathāntarāyaḥ | asti vipaśyanāntarāyaḥ | tatra śamathāntarāyaḥ pra[bhinnaḥ] adeśavāsaśca | yathāsya pramattasya styānamiddhaṃ vā cittaṃ paryavanahati | śamathamātramvā āsvādayati | līnatvāya vā cittamupanāmayati | andhakārāyitatvaṃ vā cetaso bhavati | yadrūpeṇa cādeśavāsena | manuṣyakṛto vā parataḥ saṃghaṭṭo bhavati | yenāsya cittambahirdhā vikṣipyate [|] ayaṃ śamathāntarāyaḥ | pratisaṃlayanāntarāyo veditavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: or empty dwellings. What is the obstacle to meditative retreat (<s>pratisaṃlayanāntarāya</s>)? Meditative retreat is said to comprise <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Therein, there is an obstacle to <s>śamatha</s> and an obstacle to <s>vipaśyanā</s>. The obstacle to <s>śamatha</s> consists of heedlessness and [improper] dwelling conditions. For one who is heedless, <s>styānamiddha</s> (dullness and drowsiness) either envelops the mind, or one savors mere <s>śamatha</s>, or inclines the mind toward laxity, or there arises a state of darkness in the mind. And through such improper dwelling conditions, there arises disturbance caused by other people from outside, by which the mind is scattered outward. This is the obstacle to <s>śamatha</s>, which should be understood as the obstacle to meditative retreat.

body.translated_text: What is the obstacle to seclusion (<s>prāvivekyāntarāya</s>)? When one is heavy with food, has many concerns, many duties, many things to be done, and is devoted to

body.text: vipaśyanāntarāyaḥ katamaḥ | yadutātmasaṃgrāhaścāpalyañca |
body.translated_text: What is the obstacle to <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight)? Namely, self-aggrandizement (<s>ātmasaṃgrāha</s>) and restlessness (<s>cāpalya</s>).

body.text: tatrātmasaṃgraho yathāpi tadahamasmyuccakulaḥ pravrajitaḥ | alīnaḥ | anye ca na tathetyātmānamutkarṣayati | saṃgṛhṇāti | parāṃśca pansa(paṃsa)yati | evamāḍhyakulapravrajitaḥ, adīnaḥ, evamabhirūpo darśanīyaḥ, prāsādika, evaṃ bahuśrutaḥ, sannicayaḥ | evamahamasmin kalyāṇavākyo vākkaraṇenopetaḥ, anye ca bhikṣavo na tatheti | ātmānamutkarṣayati | saṃpragṛhṇāti | parāṃśca pansa(paṃsa)yati | sa ātmānaṃ saṃpragṛhṇātyete bhavanti | bhikṣavaḥ, sthavirā, ratijñā, abhyavatīrṇabrahmacaryāḥ, (

children.text: ) tānna kālena kālaṃ paripṛcchati | paripraśnīkaroti | te cāsya na kālena kālamavivṛtāni ca sthānāni vivṛṇvanti | vivṛtāni ca sthānāni vivṛṇvanti | na ca gambhīramarthapadaṃ | sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca prajñayā pratividhya saṃprakāśayanti yāvadeva jñānadarśanasya viśuddhaye | evamasya sa ātmasaṃgrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: yet he does not from time to time question them, inquire of them. And they do not from time to time disclose to him what is undisclosed, open up what is closed, nor do they clearly illuminate the profound meaning and wording well and thoroughly with wisdom, for the sake of purifying his knowledge and vision. Such is his self-aggrandizement,

body.translated_text: Therein, self-aggrandizement is as follows: 'I am one who has gone forth from a high family; I am vigorous — while others are not thus' — and so he exalts himself, aggrandizes himself, and disparages others. Similarly: 'I have gone forth from a wealthy family; I am not wretched; I am handsome, attractive, inspiring confidence; I am learned, with stores [of knowledge]; I am eloquent, endowed with fine speech — while other <s>bhikṣus</s> are not thus' — he exalts himself, aggrandizes himself, and disparages others. His self-aggrandizement is such that there are <s>bhikṣus</s>, elders, who know what is enjoyable, who have completed the holy life,

body.text: āntarāyiko bhavati | yaduta vipaśyanāyāḥ [|] punaraparamalpamātrakasyāvaramātrakasya jñānadarśanamātrakasya sparśavihāramātrakasya lābhī bhavati | sa tena jñānamātrakeṇa | darśanamātrakeṇātmānamutkarṣayati | saṃpragṛhṇāti | sa ātmānaṃ saṃpragṛhṇaṃstāvatā saṃtuṣṭo bhavati nottari vyāyacchate | evamasyāntarāyaḥ kṛto bhavati | ātmasaṃpragraheṇa yaduta vipaśyanāyāḥ (nayā) [|] capalo vā punaḥ anupaśāntendriyo bhavati | uddhatendriyaḥ, unnatendriyaḥ | sa dūṣitacittī bhavati | subhāṣitabhāṣī, duṣkṛtakarmakārī, na sthiraṃ dharmāṃścintayati | na dṛḍhaṃ cintayati | yena vipaśyanāṃ na pūrayati na viśodhayatyevamasya cāpalyaṃ | antarāyo bhavati | yaduta vipaśyanāyā iti |
body.translated_text: which is an obstacle, namely to <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Furthermore, he obtains only a trifling, inferior measure of knowledge, vision, and experiential attainment. By that mere measure of knowledge, that mere measure of vision, he exalts himself, aggrandizes himself. Aggrandizing himself, he becomes satisfied with just that much and does not exert himself further. Thus the obstacle is created by self-aggrandizement, namely to <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Or again, [the practitioner] is restless (<s>capala</s>), with unquiet faculties, agitated faculties, elated faculties. He is one of corrupted mind, speaking well but acting badly; he does not reflect on <s>dharmas</s> steadily, does not reflect firmly — whereby he does not fulfill or purify <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Thus his restlessness is an obstacle, namely to <s>vipaśyanā</s>.

body.text: dvau dharmau śamathāntarāyau | yaduta pramādaḥ, ādeśavāsaśca [|] dvau dharmau vipaśyanāntarāyau yadutātmasaṃpragrahaścāpalyañca | iti yaśca śamathāntarāyaḥ | yaśca vipaśyanāntarāyaḥ | ayamucyate (
body.translated_text: Two <s>dharmas</s> are obstacles to <s>śamatha</s>: namely heedlessness and [improper] dwelling conditions. Two <s>dharmas</s> are obstacles to <s>vipaśyanā</s>: namely self-aggrandizement and restlessness. Both the obstacle to <s>śamatha</s> and the obstacle to <s>vipaśyanā</s> — this is called

body.text: ayaṃ ca punarantarāyasya samāsārtha iti | yaścāyaṃ samāsārthaḥ | yaśca pūrvako vistaravibhāgaḥ | tadekatyamabhisaṃkṣipyāntarāya ityucyate | asya cāntarāyasya viparyayeṇā[na]ntarāyo veditavya iti | ya eṣāmantarā[yā]ṇāmabhāvo vigamaḥ asaṃgatirasamavadhāra(cara)[ṇa]mayamucyate [ana]ntarāyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: And this is the summary meaning of the obstacle. Both this summary meaning and the preceding detailed analysis — combined together, these are called 'obstacle' (<s>antarāya</s>). And the opposite of this obstacle should be understood as 'non-obstacle' (<s>anantarāya</s>). The absence, disappearance, non-contact, and non-engagement with these obstacles — this is called non-obstacle.

body.text: tyāgaḥ katamaḥ | yaddānamanavadyaṃ cittālaṃkārārthaṃ, (

children.translated_text: for the purpose of purifying the mind, for the purpose of accumulating the requisites of <s>yoga</s> (spiritual practice), and for attaining the supreme goal — he gives.

body.translated_text: What is <s>tyāga</s> (relinquishment / generosity)? That giving (<s>dāna</s>) which is blameless, for the purpose of adorning the mind,

body.text: tatra ko dadāti [kasmai dadāti kutra dadāti]kena ca dadāti | kathaṃ dadāti | kasmāddadāti | yenāsya (

children.text: ) dānama[na]vadyaṃ bhavati || āha | dātā, dānapatirdadāti | ayamucyate dātā | yasya svakaṃ dīyate | tacca dātukāmasya, nādātukāmasya, ayamucyate dānapatiḥ |
children.translated_text: It is said: The giver, the donor (<s>dānapati</s>) gives. He is called the giver. The one whose own [property] is given — [this applies to] one who wishes to give, not to one who does not wish to give — he is called the donor (<s>dānapati</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, who gives? [To whom does he give? Where does he give?] By what means does he give? How does he give? Why does he give? — such that his giving is blameless.

body.text: tatra kutra dadāti | āha | caturṣu dadāti | duḥkhitāyoga(pa)kāriṇe | iṣṭāya, viśiṣṭāya ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, to whom does one give? It is said: One gives to four [kinds of recipients]: to the suffering, to benefactors, to the beloved, and to the distinguished.

body.text: tatra duḥkhitāyeti | kṛpaṇā vā, adhvagā vā, yācanakā vā, andhā vā, badhirā vā, anāthā vā, apratisaraṇā vā, upakaraṇavikalā iti | ye vā punaranye [a]pyevaṃbhāgīyā[ḥ |]
body.translated_text: Therein, 'to the suffering' means: the wretched, travelers, beggars, the blind, the deaf, the unprotected, those without refuge, those lacking requisites — and whoever else is of the same kind.

body.text: upakāriṇaḥ katame tadyathā mātāpitaraṃ (rau) āpāyakapoṣakaṃ (kau), samvardhakami(kāvi)ti | ye vā punaraṭavīkāntārāduttārayanti, durbhikṣādvā, paracakrabhayādvā, bandhanādvā | ābādhakādvā hitopadeśakāścāsya bhavanti | sukhopadeśakā, hitasukhopasaṃhārakā, utpannotpanneṣu cādhikaraṇeṣu sahāyakāḥ, sahanandinaḥ, sahaśokā, āpatsu caivaṃ na parityajanti iti ye vā punaranye [a]pyevaṃbhāgīyā ima upakāriṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Who are the benefactors? Namely, mother and father, nurses and providers, those who have raised [one]; and those who rescue [one] from forest-wilderness, from famine, from fear of foreign armies, from imprisonment; and those who give beneficial advice, pleasant advice, who bring about benefit and happiness, who are helpers in the various arising difficulties, who rejoice together and grieve together, and who do not abandon [one] in misfortune — and whoever else is of the same kind. These are the benefactors.

body.text: iṣṭāḥ katame [|] ye saṃstutā[ḥ] | yeṣāmasyāntike bhavati | prema vā, gauravamvā, bhaktivādo vā, ālaptakāḥ, saṃstutakāḥ sapriyakāśca bhavanti | iti vā punaranye [a]pyevaṃbhāgīyā ima ucyate iṣṭāḥ ||
body.translated_text: Who are the beloved? Those who are acquainted, toward whom one has affection, respect, or devotion, who are conversational, familiar, and dear — and whoever else is of the same kind. These are called the beloved.

body.text: viśiṣṭāḥ katame [|] te śrava(ma)ṇabrāhmaṇā[ḥ] (

children.text: ) sādhurūpasammatāḥ | avyābādhyāḥ avyābādhyaratāḥ, vigatarāgāḥ, rāgavinayāya pratipannāḥ, vigatadveṣā dveṣavinayāya pratipannāḥ | vigatamohā, mohavinayāya pratipannā iti | ye vā punaranye [a]pyevaṃ bhāgīyā ima ucyante viśiṣṭāḥ ||
children.translated_text: who are considered to be of good character, who are non-harmful, who delight in non-harming, who are free from attachment or who have entered upon the discipline of attachment, who are free from aversion or who have entered upon the discipline of aversion, who are free from delusion or who have entered upon the discipline of delusion — and whoever else is of the same kind. These are called the distinguished.

body.translated_text: Who are the distinguished? Those <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>

body.text: tatra kiṃ dadātītyāha | samāsataḥ sattvasaṃkhyātamasatva (ttva) saṃkhyātaṃ ca | vastu dadāti |
body.translated_text: Therein, what does one give? It is said: In summary, one gives a thing (<s>vastu</s>) that is either classified as a sentient being or classified as a non-sentient being.

body.text: tatra sattvasaṃkhyātamvastu katamat | tadyathā putradānaṃ dāsīdāsakarmakarapau[ruṣe]yahastyaśvagaveḍakakukkuṭastrīpuruṣadārakadārikamiti | yadvā punaranyadapyevaṃ bhāgīyaṃ vastu | adhyātmamvā punarupādāya karacaraṇaśiromānsa(māṃsa)rudhiravasādīnyanuprayacchati | idamapi puruṣasaṃkhyātaṃ dānaṃ yatra bodhisattvabodhāḥ saṃdṛśyante | asmiṃtvarthe nedaṃ dānamabhipretaṃ | yeṣu tu sarveṣvasyaiśvaryaṃ bhavati | vaśitā ca prabhaviṣṇutā ca | arhati ca tānsatvā (ttvā)n pareṣāṃ pratipādayituṃ | pratipādayaṃścātmānamanavadyaṃ karoti | na taddhetostatpratyayaṃ pare manānsi (nāṃsi) pradūṣayanti | ye ca satvā (ttvāḥ) pareṣu pratipāditā(ḥ)stena vyāpāditā bhavantīdamucyate anavadyaṃ satva(ttva)vastudānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is a thing classified as a sentient being? Namely: the gift of a son, the gift of a female slave, a male slave, a laborer, a servant, an elephant, a horse, a cow, a sheep, a rooster, a woman, a man, a boy, or a girl — or whatever other thing is of the same kind. Or, with reference to one's own person, one gives hands, feet, head, flesh, blood, marrow, and the like. This too is a gift classified as a person — [a practice] found among <s>Bodhisattvas</s> [striving for] awakening. But in this [present] context, this [kind of] giving is not intended. Rather, [it applies to] all those over whom one has authority, control, and power, and whom one is entitled to hand over to others. In handing them over, one renders oneself blameless — [provided that] others do not thereby defile their minds on that account, and the beings handed over to others are not killed by them. This is called blameless giving of a sentient-being-thing.

body.text: asattvasaṃkhyātamvastu katamat | tadyathā dhanavastu, (
body.translated_text: What is a thing classified as a non-sentient being? Namely: wealth-things,

body.text: tatra dhanavastu tadyathā maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravāḍā(lā)śmagarttapusāragaṇvajātarūparajatalohitikādakṣiṇāvartamiti | yadvā punaranyadapyevaṃ bhāgīyaṃ ratnamvā, hiraṇyamvā, rūpyamvā, vastramvā, bhāṇḍopaskaraṃ vā, gandhajātaṃ vā, mālyajātamvā, idamucyate dhanaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, wealth-things are: gems, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), conch-shell, crystal, coral, <s>aśmagarbha</s> (a precious stone), <s>musāragalva</s> (a precious stone), gold, silver, <s>lohitikā</s> (red gold or copper), and <s>dakṣiṇāvarta</s> (right-spiraling conch) — or whatever other thing is of the same kind: precious stones, gold bullion, silver, cloth, household utensils, varieties of perfume, varieties of garlands. This is called wealth.

body.text: dhānyaṃ katamat | yatkiṃñcid bhojyaṃ vā, peyamvā, tadyathā yavā vā, śālirvā, godhūmā vā, kolā vā, kulatthā vā, tilā vā, māṣā vā, ikṣurasamvā (so vā), mṛdvīkārasamvā (so vā), iti yadvā punarapyevaṃbhāgīyamidamucyate dhānyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: What is grain? Whatever is food or drink, namely: barley, rice, wheat, <s>kola</s> (jujube), <s>kulattha</s> (horse-gram), sesame, <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), sugarcane juice, grape juice — and whatever else is of the same kind. This is called grain.

body.text: deśavastu katamat | tadyathā kṣetravastu gṛhavastvāpaṇavastu, puṇyaśālāvihārapratiṣṭhāpanamiti | yadvā punaranyadapyevaṃbhāgīyamidamucyate deśavastu |
body.translated_text: What is a land-thing? Namely: field-property, house-property, shop-property, the establishment of rest-houses (<s>puṇyaśālā</s>) and monasteries (<s>vihāra</s>) — or whatever other thing is of the same kind. This is called a land-thing.

body.text: tatra yacca satva (sattva) saṃkhyātamvastu idaṃ dadātīti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, whether the thing is classified as a sentient being or [as a non-sentient being] — this is what one gives.

body.text: kena dadatīti | yā ca alobhasahagatā cetanā, cittābhisaṃskāro manaskarma | yacca tatsamutthāpitaṃ kāyakarma | vākkarma de[śa]vastuparityāgāya, svasaṃtāne vā [|] anena dadāti |
body.translated_text: By what means does one give? The volition (<s>cetanā</s>) accompanied by non-greed, which is the mental formation of the mind, the mental action — and the bodily action and verbal action generated by it, [directed] toward relinquishing the land-thing [etc.] or [from] one's own continuum — by this one gives.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ dadātīti | śraddhayā dadāti | āgamadṛṣṭiḥ, phaladarśī, satkṛtya dadāti | praṇatacittaḥ svahastaṃ (hastābhyāṃ) dadāti | anapaviddha[ḥ] kālena dadāti | yadaitatpareṣāmupayogyaṃ syātparānanupahatya dadāti | dharmeṇa, samayena, asāhasena, samudānayitvā (samudānīya) śuci dadāti | praṇītaṃ kalpikaṃ dadāti | yena na pare sāvadyā bhavanti | nātmā [|] abhīkṣṇaṃ dadāti | vinīya sātma[yanmalaṃ] sannidhimalaṃ ca dānaṃ dadāti | pūrvameva dānātsumanā dadacci(daṃści)ttaṃ prasādayati | datvā vā vipratisārī bhavati | evaṃ dadāti |
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one give? One gives with faith — looking to the scripture, foreseeing the fruit. One gives with respect — with a mind of devotion. One gives with one's own hands. One gives what is unblemished. One gives at the proper time — when it is useful to others. One gives without harming others. One gives what is pure — obtained by <s>dharma</s>, by agreement, without violence, having collected [it properly]. One gives what is refined and allowable — that by which neither others nor oneself incurs fault. One gives frequently. One gives having removed the stain of selfishness and the stain of hoarding. Before giving, one is already glad-minded, and one gladdens the mind [further]; having given, one does not feel regret. Thus one gives.

body.text: kasmāddadāti | āha | kāruṇyādvā dadāti | yaduta duḥkhiteṣu kṛtajñatāyā (tayā) dadāti | yaduta upakāriṣu premṇā, gauraveṇa, bhaktyā dadāti | yaduta iṣṭeṣu laukikalokāntaraviśeṣaprārthanayā dadāti | yaduta viśiṣṭeṣu [|] tasmāt | dadātītyucyate |
body.translated_text: Why does one give? It is said: One gives out of compassion — namely toward the suffering. One gives out of gratitude — namely toward benefactors. One gives out of affection, respect, and devotion — namely toward the beloved. One gives out of aspiration for worldly and supramundane distinction — namely toward the distinguished. For these reasons, one gives.

body.text: ebhirākārairato 'sya gṛhiṇo vā, pravrajitasya vā cittālaṃkārārthaṃ, cittapariṣkārārthaṃ | yogasaṃbhārārthamuttamārthasya prāptaye taddānamanavadyaṃ bhavati | ayamucyate tyāgaḥ ||
body.translated_text: By these modes, the giving of a householder or a renunciant, for the purpose of adorning the mind, for the purpose of purifying the mind, for the purpose of accumulating the requisites of <s>yoga</s>, and for attaining the supreme goal — that giving is blameless. This is called <s>tyāga</s> (relinquishment / generosity).

body.text: śramaṇālaṃkāraḥ katamaḥ [|] tadyathaikatyaḥ śrāddho bhavati | aśaṭhaḥ | alpābādhaḥ, ārabdha[vīrya]jātīyaḥ prājño [a]lpecchaḥ, saṃtuṣṭaḥ | supoṣaḥ, suka(bha)raḥ, dhutaguṇasamanvāgataḥ prāsādiko, mātrajñaḥ | satpuruṣadharmasamanvāgataḥ | paṇḍitadharmasamanvāgataḥ | paṇḍitaliṃgasamanvāgataḥ | kṣamaḥ, sū(su)rataḥ, peśalaśca bhavati ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>śramaṇālaṃkāra</s> (ornament of the renunciant)? As follows: a certain one has faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), is without deceit (<s>aśaṭha</s>), has few illnesses (<s>alpābādha</s>), is of vigorous disposition (<s>ārabdhavīryajātīya</s>), is wise (<s>prājña</s>), has few desires (<s>alpeccha</s>), is contented (<s>saṃtuṣṭa</s>), easy to support (<s>supoṣa</s>), easy to sustain (<s>subhara</s>), endowed with the <s>dhūtaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities), inspiring confidence (<s>prāsādika</s>), knowing the proper measure (<s>mātrajña</s>), endowed with the <s>dharmas</s> of a good person (<s>satpuruṣadharma</s>), endowed with the <s>dharmas</s> of a wise person (<s>paṇḍitadharma</s>), endowed with the marks of a wise person (<s>paṇḍitaliṅga</s>), is patient (<s>kṣama</s>), gentle (<s>sūrata</s>), and agreeable (<s>peśala</s>).

body.text: kathaṃ śrāddho bhavati | prasādabahulo bhavati | arthakalpanābahulaḥ | vimuktibahulaḥ chandikaśca kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu [|] sa śāstari prasīdati | na kāṃkṣati | na vicikitsati | śāstāraṃ satkaroti | gurukaroti | mānayati | pūjayati | satkṛtya, gurukṛtya, mānayitvā, pūjayitvā, niśritya, viharati | yathā śāstaryevaṃ dharme | sabrahmacāriṣu, śikṣāyāmavavādānuśāsanyāṃ, pratisaṃstare apramāde, samādhāvevaṃ śrāddho bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one have faith? One is abundantly endowed with serene confidence (<s>prasāda</s>), abundant in discerning meaning, abundant in [aspiration for] liberation, and is one who delights in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. He is serene toward the Teacher; he does not doubt, does not waver. He honors the Teacher, reveres him, respects him, worships him; having honored, revered, respected, and worshipped him, he dwells relying [on him]. As toward the Teacher, so too toward the <s>Dharma</s>, toward fellow practitioners of the holy life, toward the training, toward instruction and admonition, toward the practice of [proper] bedding, toward heedfulness, and toward <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). Thus one has faith.

body.text: kathamaśaṭho bhavati | rujako bhavati rujakajātīyaḥ | yathābhūtamātmānamāviṣkarttā bhavati | (

children.translated_text: in the presence of the Teacher, of the discerning, and of fellow practitioners of the holy life. Thus one is without deceit.

body.translated_text: How is one without deceit (<s>aśaṭha</s>)? One is straightforward, of a straightforward disposition. One is one who reveals oneself as one truly is,

body.text: kathamalpābādho bhavati | arogajātīyaḥ | samayāsādhinyā grahaṇyā samanvāgato bhavati | nātyuṣṇayā, nātiśītayā, avyābādhā(dha)yā, jātusukhayā yayāsyāśitapītakhāditāsvāditā[ni] samyakyukhena paripākaṃ gacchantyevamalpābādho bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one have few illnesses? One is of a healthy disposition, endowed with a digestion that is adequate for the occasion — neither too hot nor too cold, free from disorder, naturally comfortable — by which food eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is properly digested with even [digestive] heat. Thus one has few illnesses.

body.text: kathamārabdhavīryajātīyo bhavati | sthāmavānviharati | vīryavānutsāhī dṛḍhaparākramaḥ | nikṣiptadhuraḥ kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu dakṣaśca bhavatyanalasa utthānasampannaḥ [|] karttā bhavati | vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kāyena vaiyāpṛtyamevamārabdhavīryo bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become a person of aroused vigor? One dwells with strength, vigor, enthusiasm, and firm exertion. One has taken up the burden in wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and one becomes skillful, not lazy, endowed with initiative. One renders physical service to wise fellow practitioners in the holy life. Thus one becomes a person of aroused vigor.

body.text: kathaṃ prājño bhavati | dvidhā smṛtibuddhisampanno bhavati | adhandhe[ndriyaḥ], amūḍhendriyaḥ, aneḍakaḥ, pratibalaḥ, subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ arthamājñātumiti | sahajayāpi buddhyā samanvāgato bhavati | prāyogikayāpi buddhyā samanvāgato bhavati | evaṃ prājño bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become wise? One is endowed with <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) and <s>buddhi</s> (intelligence) in two ways. One has undulled faculties, unconfused faculties, is not dull-witted, and is capable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken <s>dharmas</s>. One is also endowed with innate intelligence and with intelligence acquired through practice. Thus one becomes wise.

body.text: kathamalpeccho bhavati | yāvadbhirguṇaiḥ samanvāgato bhavatyalpecchatāmādiṃ kṛtvā taiḥ parato jñātuṃ na samanveṣate | kaści(cci)nme(nmāṃ) pare na jānīyuḥ, alpeccha[ṃ] iti vā evaṃ guṇayukta ityevamalpecho bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become one of few desires (<s>alpeccha</s>)? Whatever qualities one is endowed with, beginning with fewness of desires, one does not seek to make those known to others, [thinking:] 'May others not know me as one of few desires, or as one endowed with such qualities.' Thus one becomes one of few desires.

body.text: kathaṃ saṃtuṣṭo bhavati | itaretareṣu cīvarapiṇḍapātena, śayanāsanena tuṣṭo bhavati, saṃtuṣṭaḥ, sa labdhvā cīvaraṃ lūhaṃ vā, praṇītamvā notkaṇṭhati | na paritasyati | labdhvā ca punaḥ araktaḥ paribhuṃkte | asakta iti vistareṇa pūrvavat | yathā cīvaramevaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ (taḥ), śayanāsanamevaṃ tuṣṭo bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become content (<s>saṃtuṣṭa</s>)? One is satisfied, content with whatever robes, almsfood, and lodging one receives. Having received a robe, whether coarse or excellent, one does not feel distress or anxiety. And having received it, one uses it without attachment, without clinging — in detail as before. As with robes, so too with almsfood and lodging — thus one becomes content.

body.text: kathaṃ supoṣo bhavati | ātmā asyaikaḥ poṣyo bhavati | na tu pare tadyathā dārakā vā, manuṣyā veti | ye vā punaranye [a]pi kecidyeṣāmarthāya yā (yā ya)mparyeṣṭimāpadyate | pare caivaṃ dāyakadānapatayo duṣpoṣyamiti paśye (śyeyuḥ) (n | ra) evaṃ supoṣyo bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become easy to maintain (<s>supoṣa</s>)? One has only oneself to maintain, and not others — such as children, servants, or whoever else on whose account one would undertake seeking. And the donors and lords of giving should see one as easy to maintain. Thus one becomes easy to maintain.

body.text: kathaṃ subharo bhavati | alpenāpi yāpayati | lūhenāpi yāpayatyevaṃ subharo bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become easy to support (<s>subhara</s>)? One sustains oneself even with little, even with what is coarse. Thus one becomes easy to support.

body.text: kathaṃ dhutaguṇasamanvāgato bhavati | piṇḍapātiko bhavati | sāvadānapiṇḍapātikaḥ | ekāsanikaḥ, khalu paścādbhaktikaḥ | traicīvariko, nāmatikaḥ, pānsu (pāṃsu)kūlikaḥ | (

children.text: ) āraṇyako, vṛkṣamūlikaḥ ābhyavakāśikaḥ | śmāśāniko, naiṣadyikaḥ | yāthāsaṃstarikaḥ [|] ta ete piṇḍapātacīvaraśayanāsanamārabhya dvādaśakā[dhuta]guṇā bhavanti | trayodaśā (śa) vā [|]
children.translated_text: a forest-dweller (<s>āraṇyaka</s>), a tree-root dweller (<s>vṛkṣamūlika</s>), an open-air dweller (<s>ābhyavakāśika</s>), a cemetery-dweller (<s>śmāśānika</s>), one who [only] sits (<s>naiṣadyika</s>), and one who uses whatever bedding is spread (<s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>). These, relating to almsfood, robes, and lodging, are the twelve <s>dhutaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities) — or thirteen.

body.translated_text: How does one become endowed with the <s>dhutaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities)? One becomes a <s>piṇḍapātika</s> (one who lives on alms-round), a <s>sāvadānapiṇḍapātika</s> (one who eats with care from alms), an <s>ekāsanika</s> (one-seater), a <s>khalupaścādbhaktika</s> (one who does not eat after the [allotted] meal), a <s>traicīvarika</s> (wearer of three robes), a <s>nāmatika</s> (wearer of woolen cloth), a <s>pāṃsukūlika</s> (wearer of refuse-rags),

body.text: tatra piṇḍapātikatvaṃ bhidyamānaṃ dvidhā bhavati | prāptapiṇḍapātikaśca, sāvadānapiṇḍapātika[ta]yā veśyānuveśyakulāni bhikṣitvā, paryaṭitvā (paryaṭya), yathālabdhaṃ yathopasampannaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ paribhuṃkte, no tu uccaiḥ śuṇḍāṃ praṇidhāya kulāni upasaṃkrāmati | ato [a]haṃ lapsye, praṇītaṃ khādanīyaṃ, bhojanīyaṃ, yāvadāptaṃ [|] tatra piṇḍapātikatvamaviśeṣeṇārabhya dvādaśa bhavanti | prabhedaṃ punaḥ ārabhya trayodaśa(ḥ) [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, the practice of alms-round, when differentiated, is of two kinds: being a <s>prāptapiṇḍapātika</s> (one who accepts whatever alms are received) and a <s>sāvadānapiṇḍapātika</s> (one who takes alms with care). Having begged from houses and neighborhoods, having wandered about, one consumes the almsfood as received, as obtained — but one does not approach houses with high expectations, [thinking:] 'From here I shall obtain excellent, choice food and provisions.' Therein, the alms-round practice, taken without distinction, constitutes twelve; but taking into account the subdivision, there are thirteen.

body.text: tatraikāsanikatvaṃ kathamat | ekasminnāsane niṣaṇṇoyāvatparibhoktavyaṃ | tāvatparibhuṃkte | vyutthitaśca punastasmādāsanānna paribhuṃkte | idamucyate | ekāsanikatvaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the practice of the one-seater (<s>ekāsanikatva</s>)? Having sat down on one seat, one consumes as much as is to be consumed. And having risen from that seat, one does not eat again. This is called the practice of the one-seater.

body.text: khalu paścādbhaktikatvaṃ katamat | bhojanārthaṃ niṣaṇṇastāvat(n) na paribhuṃkte | yāvatsarvabhojanaṃ pratīcchati | yāvatā jānāti śakṣyāmi yāpayituṃ | yataśca punarjānīte na me ata uttari bhojanena kṛtyaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | tataḥ sarvaṃ parihṛtyārabhate | (

children.translated_text: to eat. Thus one becomes a <s>khalupaścādbhaktika</s>.

body.translated_text: What is the practice of the <s>khalupaścādbhaktika</s> (one who does not eat after the meal)? Having sat down for the purpose of eating, one does not yet consume; one first accepts all the food, and as much as one knows one will be able to sustain oneself with, and when one further knows 'I shall have no need for more food than this,' then, having gathered it all, one begins

body.text: kathaṃ traicīvariko bhavati | tribhiśca cīvarairyāpayati, sāṃghāṭinā vā, uttarāsaṃgena, aṃtarvāsena ca | trayāṇāṃ cīvarāṇāmatirekamuttaraṃ na dhārayatyevaṃ trai[cīva]riko bhavati ||
body.translated_text: How does one become a wearer of three robes (<s>traicīvarika</s>)? One sustains oneself with three robes: the <s>sāṃghāṭī</s> (double outer robe), the <s>uttarāsaṅga</s> (upper robe), and the <s>antarvāsa</s> (inner robe). One does not keep any additional upper garment beyond the three robes. Thus one becomes a wearer of three robes.

body.text: kathaṃ nāmatiko bhavati || yatkiṃciccīvaraṃ dhārayati | tricīvaramvā, atirekacīvaramvā sarva tadaurṇikaṃ dhārayati | na tvanyaṃ (nyat) [|] evaṃ nāmatikaṃ dhārayati |
body.translated_text: How does one become a <s>nāmatika</s> (wearer of woolen cloth)? Whatever robe one wears — whether the three robes or any additional robe — one wears it entirely of wool, and not of any other [material]. Thus one wears the <s>nāmatika</s> garment.

body.text: kathaṃ pānsu (pāṃsu)kūliko bhavati | yaccīvaraṃ parairmuktaṃ bhavati | ucchiṣṭaṃ, rathyāyāmvā, vīthyāmvā, catvare vā, śrṛṃgāṭake vā, pathi vā, utpathevā, uccārasaṃsṛṣṭamvā, prasrāvasaṃsṛṣṭamvā, uccāraprasrāvapūyarudhirakheṭāprakṣitaṃ vā [|] tato yadaśuci tadapīnaya, sāramādāya, śodhayitvā, sīvitvā, vivarṇīkṛtya dhārayatyevaṃ pānsu(pāṃsu)kūliko bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become a wearer of refuse-rags (<s>pāṃsukūlika</s>)? A robe that has been discarded by others, cast off, [found] on a highway, in a lane, at a crossroads, at an intersection, on a road, off the road, mixed with excrement, mixed with urine, stained with excrement, urine, pus, blood, or spit — from that, removing what is impure, taking what is usable, washing, sewing, and dyeing it, one wears it. Thus one becomes a wearer of refuse-rags.

body.text: kathamāraṇyako bhavati | araṇye vanaprasthāni prāntāni śayanāsanāni adhyāvasati | yāni vyavakṛṣṭāni grāmanigamānāmevamāraṇyako bhavati ||
body.translated_text: How does one become a forest-dweller (<s>āraṇyaka</s>)? One dwells in remote lodgings in the forest, in the wilds, which are secluded, far removed from villages and towns. Thus one becomes a forest-dweller.

body.text: kathaṃ vṛkṣamūliko bhavati | vṛkṣamūle vāsaṃ (

children.translated_text: depending on the root of a tree. Thus one becomes a tree-root dweller.

body.translated_text: How does one become a tree-root dweller (<s>vṛkṣamūlika</s>)? One makes one's dwelling at the root of a tree,

body.text: kathamābhyavakāśiko bhavati | abhyavakāśe vāsaṃ kalpayati | anavakāśe vivṛte da (de)śe [|] evamābhyavakāśiko bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become an open-air dweller (<s>ābhyavakāśika</s>)? One makes one's dwelling in the open air, in an uncovered, exposed place. Thus one becomes an open-air dweller.

body.text: kathaṃ śmāśāniko bhavati | śmaśāne vāsaṃ kalpayati yatra mṛtamṛto janakāyaḥ | abhinirhriyata evaṃ śmāśāniko bhavati ||
body.translated_text: How does one become a cemetery-dweller (<s>śmāśānika</s>)? One makes one's dwelling in a cemetery, where the dead bodies of the deceased are brought out. Thus one becomes a cemetery-dweller.

body.text: kathaṃ naiṣadyiko bhavati | maṃce vā, pīṭhe vā, tṛṇasaṃstare vā niṣadyayā kālamatināmayati | no tu maṃcā (ma caṃ)vā, pīṭhaṃ vā, kuḍyamvā, (vṛkṣamūlaṃ) vṛkṣamūlamvā, tṛṇasaṃstaramvā,parṇasaṃstaramvā, niśritya pṛṣṭha vā (pṛṣṭhaṃ vā), pārśvamvā dadātyevaṃ naiṣadyiko bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become one who only sits (<s>naiṣadyika</s>)? On a bed, or a seat, or a grass mat, one passes the time only in a sitting posture. One does not give one's back or side to a bed, a seat, a wall, a tree-root, a grass mat, or a leaf mat. Thus one becomes one who only sits.

body.text: kathaṃ yāthāsaṃstariko bhavati | yasmin tṛṇasaṃstare vā, parṇasaṃstare vā śayyāṃ kalpayati | tṛṇasaṃstaramvā, parṇasaṃstaramvā sakṛtyañcaiva saṃskṛtaṃ bhavati | tathaiva śayyāṃ kalpayati | no tu punarvikopayati | abhisaṃskaroti caivaṃ ya(yā)thāsaṃstariko bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become one who uses whatever bedding is spread (<s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>)? Whatever grass mat or leaf mat on which one makes one's bed — a grass mat or leaf mat, once arranged and prepared, on that one makes one's bed, and one does not rearrange it or prepare it afresh. Thus one becomes a <s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>.

body.text: kenaite dhutaguṇā ucyante tadyathā ūrṇā vā, karpāsaṃ vā, dhutaṃ bhavatyasaṃvṛttamiti | ta[cca ta]smin (

children.text: ) samaye mṛdu ca bhavati | laghu ca, karmaṇyaṃ ca, yaduta sūtrābhinirhāre vā, tūlāvahade (te?) (tūlābhinirhāre) vā [|] evameva ihaikatyasya piṇḍapātarāgeṇa piṇḍapāte cittaṃ saktaṃ bhavati | saṃsaktaṃ cīvararāgeṇa śayanāsanarā[geṇa] śayanāsane cittaṃ saktaṃ bhavati | saṃsaktaṃ | sa ebhirdhutaguṇairviśodhayati ṛjūkaroti | mṛdukarmaṇyamārjavamāsravamvidheyaṃ yaduta brahmacaryavāsāya tenocyante dhutaguṇā iti ||
children.translated_text: time it becomes soft, light, and workable for the production of thread or for the removal of stuffing — in exactly the same way, here, when a certain person's mind is attached and entangled with attachment to almsfood, with attachment to robes, with attachment to lodging — that person, by means of these <s>dhutaguṇas</s>, purifies, straightens, and makes soft, workable, pliant, and compliant [the mind], that is, for the dwelling in the holy life. Therefore they are called <s>dhutaguṇas</s>.

body.translated_text: Why are these called <s>dhutaguṇas</s> (ascetic qualities)? Just as wool or cotton, when shaken (<s>dhuta</s>), becomes untangled — and at that

body.text: tatra piṇḍapātaprahīṇabhojanarāgasya prahāṇāya ekāsaniko bhavati | prabhūtabhojanarāgasya prahāṇāya nāmatiko bhavati | praṇītacīvararāgasya prahāṇāya nāmatiko bhavati | praṇītacīvararāgasya prahāṇāya traicīvariko bhavati | cīvare mṛdusaṃsparśarāgasya prahāṇāya pānsu(pāṃsu)kūliko bhavati | śayanāsanarāgaścaturvidhaḥ | tadyathā saṃsparśarāgaḥ | pratiśrayarāgaḥ | pārśvasukhaśayanasukharāgaḥ | āstaraṇapratyāstaraṇopacchādanarāgaḥ | tatra saṃsargarāgasya prahāṇāya āraṇyako bhavati | pratiśrayarāgasya prahāṇāya vṛkṣamūlikaḥ (

children.text: ) āmyavakāśikaḥ | śmāśāniko bhavati | api ca śmāśānikatvaṃ middhena rāgasya prahāṇāya bhavati | pārśvasukhaśayanāsanasukharāgasya prahāṇāya naiṣadyiko bhavati | āstaraṇapratyāstaraṇopacchāda[na]rāgasya prahāṇāya yāthāsāṃstariko bhavatyevaṃ dhutaguṇa samanvāgato bhavati |
children.translated_text: an open-air dweller (<s>ābhyavakāśika</s>), or a cemetery-dweller (<s>śmāśānika</s>). Moreover, the cemetery-dwelling practice is for the abandonment of attachment to torpor (<s>middha</s>). For the abandonment of attachment to the pleasure of lying on one's side and the pleasure of one's bed, one becomes one who only sits (<s>naiṣadyika</s>). For the abandonment of attachment to bedding, mattresses, and coverlets, one becomes a <s>yāthāsaṃstarika</s>. Thus one becomes endowed with the <s>dhutaguṇas</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, for the abandonment of attachment to food already received through alms, one becomes an <s>ekāsanika</s> (one-seater). For the abandonment of attachment to abundant food, one becomes a <s>nāmatika</s>. For the abandonment of attachment to excellent robes, one becomes a <s>traicīvarika</s> (wearer of three robes). For the abandonment of attachment to the soft touch of robes, one becomes a <s>pāṃsukūlika</s> (wearer of refuse-rags). Attachment to lodging is of four kinds: attachment to company, attachment to shelter, attachment to the pleasure of lying on one's side and the pleasure of one's bed, and attachment to bedding, mattresses, and coverlets. Therein, for the abandonment of attachment to company, one becomes a forest-dweller (<s>āraṇyaka</s>). For the abandonment of attachment to shelter, one becomes a tree-root dweller (<s>vṛkṣamūlika</s>),

body.text: kathaṃ prāsādiko bhavati | prāsādikenāti(bhi)kramapratikrameṇa samanvāgato bhavatyālokitavyalokitena saṃjimita (sāṃmiṃjita)prasāritena sāṃghāṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇenaivaṃ prāsādiko bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become inspiring (<s>prāsādika</s>)? One is endowed with an inspiring manner of going forth and returning, with looking ahead and looking around, with bending and stretching, and with the wearing of the <s>sāṃghāṭī</s> robe and carrying of the bowl. Thus one becomes inspiring.

body.text: kathaṃ mātrajño bhavati | iha śrāddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo vyarthaṃ pracārayati | yaduta cīvara piṇḍapāta śayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraistatra pratigra[heṇa] mātrāṃ jānāti | evaṃ mātrajño bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become one who knows the right measure (<s>mātrajña</s>)? Here, devout householders make offerings — namely, of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick — and in receiving these, one knows the proper measure. Thus one becomes one who knows the right measure.

body.text: kathaṃ satpuruṣadharmasamanvāgato bhavati | uccakulapravrajito vā sannāḍhyakulapravrajito vā, abhirūpo vā, darśanīyaḥ, prāsādiko, bahuśrutopakaraṇenopetaḥ | anyatamānyatamasya vā jñānamātrasya darśanamātrakasparśavihāra sārthakasya lābhī sannetenātmānamutkarṣayati | parāṃśca pansa (paṃsa)yati | dharmānudharmapratipanno bhavatyevaṃ satpuruṣadharmasamanvāgato bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become endowed with the qualities of a good person (<s>satpuruṣadharma</s>)? Whether one has gone forth from a high family, or from a wealthy family, or is handsome, good-looking, inspiring, or learned and well-equipped with resources, or is a recipient of any kind of knowledge, vision, or direct experience [in meditation] — one does not thereby exalt oneself or disparage others, but one practices in conformity with the <s>Dharma</s>. Thus one becomes endowed with the qualities of a good person.

body.text: kathaṃ paṇḍitaliṃgasamanvāgato bhavati | karmalakṣaṇo (

children.text: ) bālaḥ, karmalakṣaṇaḥ paṇḍitaḥ | yathākathamiti bālo duścintitacintī bhavati | durbhāṣitabhāṣī, duṣkṛtakarmakārī, paṇḍitaḥ punaḥ sucintitacintī bhavati | subhāṣitabhāṣī, sukṛtakarmakārī [|] evaṃ paṇḍitaliṃgasamanvāgato bhavati |
children.translated_text: and a wise person is characterized by his actions. In what way? A fool thinks ill-considered thoughts, speaks ill-spoken words, and performs ill-done deeds. A wise person, however, thinks well-considered thoughts, speaks well-spoken words, and performs well-done deeds. Thus one becomes endowed with the mark of a wise person.

body.translated_text: How does one become endowed with the mark of a wise person (<s>paṇḍitaliṅga</s>)? A fool is characterized by his actions,

body.text: kathaṃ kṣamo bhavati | ākruṣṭo na pratyākrośati | roṣito na pratiroṣayati | vādito na prativādayati | bhaṇḍito na pratibhaṇḍayati | sa cāyuṣmān kṣamo bhavati | śītasyoṣṇasya jighatsāyā[ḥ], pipāsāyāḥ, daṃśakamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasaṃsparśānāṃ(ṇāṃ), parato duruktānāṃ, durāgatānāṃ, vacanapathānāṃ | śārīrikāṇāṃ vedanānāṃ, duḥkhānāṃ, tīvrāṇāṃ, kharāṇāṃ, kaṭukānāṃ, amana āpānāṃ prāṇahāriṇīnāṃ kṣamo bhavatyadhivāsanajātīyaḥ | evaṃ kṣamo bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become patient (<s>kṣama</s>)? When reviled, one does not revile in return; when provoked to anger, one does not provoke in return; when scolded, one does not scold in return; when challenged, one does not challenge in return. And that venerable one is patient with cold and heat, hunger and thirst, the contact of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping creatures, harsh and unwelcome words from others, and bodily sensations that are painful, sharp, severe, bitter, disagreeable, and life-threatening — one is patient, of an enduring nature. Thus one becomes patient.

body.text: kathaṃ (sū) surato bhavati | yathāpi tanmaitreṇa kāya karmaṇā samanvāgato bhavati | maitreṇa vākkarmaṇā, maitreṇa manaskarmaṇā, śāsturantike vijñānāṃ ca, sabrahmacāriṇāṃ, sādhāraṇaparibhogī ca bhavatyaparibhogī ca | bhavatyapratiguptabhojī | lābhairdhārmikairdharmapratilabdhaiḥ, pātragataiḥ, pātraparyāpannaiḥ śīlasāmānyagataśca bhavati | dṛṣṭisāmānyagataśca | sa ebhiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ saṃrajanīyairdharmaiḥ (saṃraṃjanīyairdharmaiḥ) samanvāgataḥ priyakaraṇairgurukaraṇairsthavādakaraṇaiḥ sukhasaṃvāsyo bhavati | aviheṭhanajātīyaḥ | (

children.text: ) abhinandanti cainaṃ vijñāḥ | sabrahmacāriṇaḥ | ekavyavasāyaḥ | evaṃ sū (su)rato bhavati |
children.translated_text: And the wise fellow practitioners in the holy life rejoice in such a person, who is of one purpose. Thus one becomes one of good disposition.

body.translated_text: How does one become one of good disposition (<s>surata</s>)? One is endowed with bodily action that is friendly, verbal action that is friendly, and mental action that is friendly, toward the Teacher, toward wise fellow practitioners in the holy life. And one shares one's possessions in common and does not eat in concealment. With righteous gains, lawfully obtained, received in one's bowl and contained in one's bowl, one is united in moral conduct with others and united in views with others. Endowed with these six <s>saṃrajanīyadharmas</s> (qualities that produce harmony), which make one dear, which make one revered, which make one an elder — one becomes pleasant to live with, of a non-harassing nature.

body.text: kathaṃ peśalo bhavati | vigatabhṛkuṭirbhavatyuttānamukhavarṇaḥ, smitasārddhaṃgamaḥpūrvābhibhāṣī | priyavādī | saṃgrahaśīlaḥ | āttasantānaḥ [ḥ |] evaṃ peśalo bhavati |
body.translated_text: How does one become amiable? One is free from frowning, with a bright countenance, preceded by a smile in greeting; one speaks first; one speaks kindly; one is inclined toward being helpful; one is of a connected disposition. Thus one becomes amiable.

children.translated_text: removes them, and eliminates them, thinking: 'From that cause arises suffering, whether in this life or in the next.' And one does not let fall the arising of faith. One is of unbroken moral conduct, of unblemished vows. One partakes of what is given in faith, and does not reject what is given in faith. One does not renounce the training. One is a searcher for one's own inner faults and lapses; one conceals one's virtues and reveals one's faults. In the inner faults and lapses of others, there is no inclination [to look]. One does not commit an offense, even at the cost of one's life. And if one has committed an offense, one quickly and readily makes amends according to the <s>Dharma</s>. In what is to be done, one is skilled and diligent, acting by oneself, not seeking bodily service from others. One has faith in the inconceivable power of the <s>Buddhas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Buddhas</s>, and in the profound teaching, and does not reject it, thinking: 'The <s>Tathāgatas</s> alone are the seers and knowers, not I.' Having seen this, one does not become one who clings to one's own views, who grasps inconsistently, or who holds tenaciously to opinions. One endowed with these virtues, dwelling thus, training thus, adorned with the ornament of the ascetic, shines — just as a certain young man, of noble birth, an enjoyer of pleasures, bathed and anointed, clad in festive garments, adorned with various ornaments, shines — such as necklaces, armlets, finger-rings, or garlands of gold and silver.

children.translated_text: Even so, one adorned with the various virtues that are the ornaments of the ascetic blazes, shines, and radiates. Therefore it is called the ornament of the ascetic. This is what is called the ornament of the ascetic.

body.translated_text: One endowed with these qualities becomes a lover of the <s>Dharma</s>, a lover of virtues, and not a lover of gain, honor, fame, and renown. One is not possessed of the wrong view that is attributed to <s>Māra</s>, nor of the wrong view that denies. One does not superimpose a non-existent quality, and one does not deny an existent quality. Whatever is mere talk and chatter, idle syllables, signs and words, connected with <s>Lokāyata</s> (materialist philosophy) — knowing that to be purposeless, one avoids it from afar. One does not delight in it, one is not pleased by it, and on account of it one does not wear the mark of self or the robe. One avoids association with householders, which increases the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). One associates with the noble ones, which purifies knowledge. One does not make friendships with families or accept [gifts from them], thinking: 'From that, in many ways, there will arise distraction or involvement, and from changes and alterations in them will arise sorrow, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and despair.' And the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and secondary afflictions that arise, one does not tolerate them but abandons them,

body.translated_text: Therein, how many types of persons emerge on this ground of renunciation as taught and described? And how is the classification of persons established? What is the object of meditation? What is the instruction? What is the training? What are the qualities conforming to the training? What is the loss of the practice? What are the practices? What is the mental attention? How many practitioners of yoga are there? What is the task of yoga? What is the cultivation of yoga? What is the fruit of cultivation? How many types of persons are there? How many <s>Māras</s> are there? How many actions of <s>Māra</s> are there? How does effort become fruitless?

children.translated_text: one devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, one who has attained the view, one who is a body-witness, one who has at most one more birth, one who goes from family to family, one who is a single-intervener, one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state, one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> upon rebirth, one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with effort, one who goes upstream, one liberated by occasion, one of unshakeable qualities, one liberated by wisdom, and one liberated in both ways. Therein, what is a person of soft faculties? A person whose faculties are soft, slow-moving, sluggish with respect to the object to be known — and so forth as before. That person should be understood as twofold: one whose lineage is of soft faculties from the very beginning, and one whose faculties have not been developed.

body.translated_text: Therein, the types of persons are twenty-eight. What are the twenty-eight? Namely: one of soft faculties, one of sharp faculties, one excessively affected by passion, one excessively affected by hatred, one excessively affected by delusion, one excessively affected by pride, one excessively affected by discursive thought, one of equal endowment, one of the type with slight defilements, one on the path, one established in the fruit, a faith-follower, a <s>Dharma</s>-follower,

body.text: tīkṣṇendriyaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yasya pudgalasyendriyāṇi adhandhavāhīni bhavanti | amandavāhīni | jñeye vastunīti pūrvavat | sa punardvividho veditavyaḥ | ādita eva tīkṣṇendriyagotraḥ | paribhāvitendriyaśca ||
body.translated_text: What is a person of sharp faculties? A person whose faculties are not slow-moving, not sluggish with respect to the object to be known — and so forth as before. That person should be understood as twofold: one whose lineage is of sharp faculties from the very beginning, and one whose faculties have been developed.

body.text: rāgonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yena pudgalena pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu rāga āsevito, bhāvito, bahulīkṛtaḥ sa tena hetunā tena pratyayainaitarhi raṃjanīye vastuni tīvrarāgaśca, bhavatyāyata(na)rāgaśca | ayamucyate rāgonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is a person excessively affected by passion? A person who in previous births has cultivated, developed, and made much of passion — on account of that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object that arouses passion, experiences intense passion and sustained passion. This is called a person excessively affected by passion.

body.text: dveṣonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yena pudgalena dveṣaḥ pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu āsevito, bhāvito, bahulīkṛtaḥ | tena hetunā tena pratyayenaitarhi dveṣaṇīye vastuni tīvradveṣaśca bhavatyāyatadveṣaśca | ayamucyate | dveṣonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is a person excessively affected by hatred? A person who in previous births has cultivated, developed, and made much of hatred — on account of that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object that arouses hatred, experiences intense hatred and sustained hatred. This is called a person excessively affected by hatred.

body.text: mohonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yena pudgalena pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu moha āsevito, bhāvito, bahulīkṛtaḥ | tena ca hetunā tena pratyayena [|] etarhi mohanīye vastuni tīvramohaśca bhavatyāyata mohaścāyamucyate mohonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is a person excessively affected by delusion? A person who in previous births has cultivated, developed, and made much of delusion — on account of that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object that arouses delusion, experiences intense delusion and sustained delusion. This is called a person excessively affected by delusion.

body.text: mānonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yena pudgalena pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu māna āsevito, bhāvito, bahulīkṛtastena hetunā tena pratyayena [|] etarhi manyanīye(mānanīye)vastuni tīvramānaśca bhavatyāyatamānaśca || ayamucyate mānonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is a person excessively affected by pride? A person who in previous births has cultivated, developed, and made much of pride — on account of that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object that arouses pride, experiences intense pride and sustained pride. This is called a person excessively affected by pride.

body.text: vitarkonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yena pudgalena pūrvamanyāsu jātiṣu vitarka āsevito, bhāvito, bahulīkṛtastena ca hetunā tena ca pratyayena etarhi vitarka sthānīye vastuni tīvravitarkaśca bhavatyāyatavitarkaśca [|] ayamucyate vitarkonmadaḥ | pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is a person excessively affected by discursive thought? A person who in previous births has cultivated, developed, and made much of discursive thought — on account of that cause and that condition, now, with respect to an object that occasions discursive thought, experiences intense discursive thought and sustained discursive thought. This is called a person excessively affected by discursive thought.

As with passion, so too with hatred, delusion, pride, and discursive thought. This is called a person of equal endowment.

body.translated_text: What is a person of equal endowment? A person who in previous births has not cultivated, developed, or made much of passion, hatred, delusion, pride, or discursive thought, and these qualities have not been

body.translated_text: What is a person with slight defilements? A person who in previous births has not cultivated or made much of passion, and has frequently seen it as disadvantageous, has condemned and investigated it. On account of that cause and that condition, now, when an object arousing passion is present, encountered, intense, abundant, and overwhelming, one generates the defilement of passion; but when it is moderate or slight, one does not generate it. As with passion, so too should hatred, delusion, pride, and discursive thought be understood. This is called a person with slight defilements.

body.text: śraddhānusārī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yaḥ pudgalaḥ parata ava(to 'va)vādānuśāsanīṃ paryeṣate | tadvalena ca pratipadyate | yaduta phalasyādhigamāya | no tūdgṛhīteṣu dharmeṣu | paryavāpteṣu, cintiteṣu, tuliteṣūpaparīkṣiteṣu svayamevaśakto bhavati | pratibalaḥ | tān dharmān bhāvanākāreṇānusarttuṃ | nānyatra pudgalānusāriṇyā prajñayā pratipadyate | tasmācchraddhānusārītyucyate ||
body.translated_text: What is a faith-follower? A person who seeks instruction and guidance from others, and practices by the strength of that — namely, for the attainment of the fruit — but who, with respect to the <s>dharmas</s> that have been grasped, understood, reflected upon, weighed, and examined, is not by oneself capable or able to follow those <s>dharmas</s> in the mode of cultivation, but practices only through wisdom that follows persons [i.e., through trust in others]. Therefore one is called a faith-follower.

body.text: dharmānusārī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yatpu(yaḥ pu)dgalo yathāśruteṣu dharmeṣu, paryavāpteṣu, cintiteṣu | tuliteṣūpaparīkṣiteṣu, svayameva śakto bhavati | pratibalastāndharmānbhāvanākāreṇānusarttam || no tu parato 'vavādānuśāsanīmparyeṣate | yaduta phalasyādhigamāyāyamucyate dharmānusārī pudgalaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is a <s>Dharma</s>-follower? A person who, with respect to the <s>dharmas</s> as heard, understood, reflected upon, weighed, and examined, is by oneself capable and able to follow those <s>dharmas</s> in the mode of cultivation, and does not seek instruction and guidance from others for the attainment of the fruit. This is called a <s>Dharma</s>-follower.

body.text: kāyasākṣī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ [|] yoyaṃ pudgalaḥ | anulomapratilomamaṣṭau vimokṣānsamāpadyate | vyuttiṣṭhate ca, kāyena ca sākṣātkṛtya [bahulaṃ] viharati, na ca sarveṇa sarvamāsravakṣayamanuprāpnotyayamucyate kāyasākṣī pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>kāyasākṣin pudgala</s> (body-witness person)? children.translated_text: Passing through [the cycle], he makes an end of suffering. Both should be understood as <s>srotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer) persons.

body.translated_text: What is the <s>saptakṛdbhavaparama pudgala</s> (person of at most seven existences)? That person who, through the abandonment of the three <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters) — <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the self-collection), <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (grasping at rules and vows), and <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt) — becomes a <s>srotāpanna</s> (stream-enterer), one who by nature does not fall [into lower realms], who is determined, who is destined for <s>saṃbodhi</s> (awakening), who has at most seven existences — traversing seven times through the realms of gods and humans,

body.text: tatraikavīcikaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yasya sakṛdāgāminaḥ pudgalasya anāgāmiphalapratipannakasya kāmāvacarāṇāṃ kleśānāmadhimātramadhyadeśāḥ prahīṇā bhavanti | mṛdukāścaikāvaśiṣṭā (caikā avaśiṣṭā) bhavanti | sakṛcca kāmāvacarameva bhavamabhinirvṛtya tatraiva parinirvāti | sa punaḥ sakṛdāgacchatīmaṃ lokamayamucyate ekavīcikaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>ekavīcika pudgala</s> (one-interval person)? That person who is a <s>sakṛdāgāmin</s> (once-returner), who has entered upon the attainment of the fruit of <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner), whose intense and middling afflictions of the desire-realm (<s>kāmāvacara</s>) have been abandoned, and only mild ones remain — having been reborn once more in the desire-realm, he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> there itself. He returns once more to this world. This is called the one-interval [person].

body.text: antarāparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | āha | (

children.text: ) antarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ pudgalāstrayaḥ | ekontarāparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ | cyutamātra evāntarābhavābhinirvṛttikāle antarābhavamabhinirvatayatyabhinirvṛtte[ḥ] samakālameva parinirvāti | tadyathā parīttaḥ śakalikāgnirutpannaiva(nna eva) parinirvāti | dvitīyontarāparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ | antarābhavamabhinirvarttayatyabhinirvṛtteḥ (
children.translated_text: There are three kinds of persons who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state. The first person who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state: immediately upon death, at the very time of producing the intermediate existence (<s>antarābhava</s>), he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> simultaneously with its production — just as a small spark-fire is extinguished the very moment it arises. The second person who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state: he produces the intermediate existence, and after

children.text: ) samakālā(kālama)ntarā bhavettatrastha eva kālāntareṇa parinirvāti | no tu yenopapattibhavastenāsyāpyuparato bhavati | tadyathā aśubhānāmvā ayaḥsthālānāmvā, dīptāgnisaṃprataptānāmayoghanairhanyamānānāmayaḥprapāṭikā utpatatyeva(vaṃ) parinirvāti | tṛtīyontarāparinirvāyi (yī) pudgalaḥ antarābhavamabhinirvarttya yenopapatti bhavastenopanamati | upanataśca punaranupapanna eva parinirvāti | tadyathā | ayasprapāṭikā utpatya pṛthivyām | apatitaivamabhinirvāti | ta ime trayo 'ntarābhavaparinirvāyiṇaḥ pudgalāḥ ekatyamabhi saṃkṣipya antarāparinirvāyī pudgala ityucyate |
children.translated_text: Some time, while still in that [intermediate state], he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> after an interval of time, but does not cease by [reaching] the existence into which he would be reborn — just as when impure or iron vessels, heated in blazing fire, are struck with iron hammers, iron filings fly up and are extinguished. The third person who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state: having produced the intermediate existence, he approaches the existence into which he would be reborn, but attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> while approaching, before actually being reborn — just as iron filings, having flown up, are extinguished before falling to the ground. These are the three persons who attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state; collectively compressing them into one, [such a person] is called one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state.

body.translated_text: What is the <s>antarāparinirvāyin pudgala</s> (person who attains parinirvāṇa in the intermediate state)? It is said:

body.text: upapadyaparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | ya upapannamātra eva parinirvāti ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>upapadyaparinirvāyin pudgala</s> (person who attains parinirvāṇa upon rebirth)? One who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> immediately upon being reborn.

body.text: anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yonabhisaṃskāreṇāprayatnenākhedena mārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya (

children.translated_text: Having been reborn there, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — this is called the person who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without exertion.

body.translated_text: What is the <s>anabhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin pudgala</s> (person who attains parinirvāṇa without exertion)? One who, without volitional effort, without striving, and without fatigue, having come face to face with the path,

body.text: sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yobhisaṃskāreṇa prayatnena khedamārgaṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya tatropapannaḥ parinirvātyayamucyate sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyī pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>sābhisaṃskāraparinirvāyin pudgala</s> (person who attains parinirvāṇa with exertion)? One who, with volitional effort, with striving, and with the path of fatigue, having come face to face [with the path], having been reborn there, attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — this is called the person who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> with exertion.

body.text: ūrdhvasrotāḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yaḥ pudgalo 'nāgāmī | (

children.text: ) prathame dhyāne upapannaḥ sa na tatrastha eva parinirvāti | api tu tasmāccyavitvā uttarottaramabhinirvarttayabhya(nyā)vadakaniṣṭhānvā devāngacchati | naiva saṃjñā | (|) nāsaṃjñāyatanādvā | ayamucyate urdhvasrotāḥ pudgalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having been reborn in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), he does not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> while remaining there; rather, having departed from there, he proceeds to ever higher [realms], up to the <s>Akaniṣṭha</s> gods, or to the sphere of <s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s> (neither-perception-nor-non-perception). This is called the upward-streaming person.

body.translated_text: What is the <s>ūrdhvasrotas pudgala</s> (upward-streaming person)? That person who is an <s>anāgāmin</s> (non-returner),

body.text: samayavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | yo mṛdvindviyagātraḥ (gotraḥ) pudgalaḥ laukikebhyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihīyate | cetayati vā maraṇāya | anurakṣate vā vimuktimatyarthapramādabhayāpannayukto bhavati | yaduta etāmeva parihāṇimadhipatiṃ kṛtvā tanmātro vāsya kuśalapakṣo bhavati | no tu teṣāṃ teṣāṃ rātriṃdivasānāṃ kṣaṇalavamuhūrttānā (ṇā)matyayādatyarthaṃ viśeṣāya paraiti | yāvanna tīvramabhiyogaṃ karoti | ayamucyate samayavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>samayavimukta pudgala</s> (person liberated on occasion)? A person of mild faculties and [mild] lineage (<s>gotra</s>) who falls away from the worldly attainments of pleasant abiding in the present life (<s>dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihāra</s>). He either resolves upon death, or guards his liberation, being stricken with the fear of extreme heedlessness. Because of this very falling away, his wholesome quality is of that degree only, and during those days and nights, with the passing of moments, instants, and hours, he does not progress exceptionally toward distinction — not until he makes an intense effort. This is called the person liberated on occasion.

body.text: akopyadharmā pudgalaḥ katamaḥ | etadviparyayeṇā [ko] 'pyadharmā pudgalo veditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>akopyadharman pudgala</s> (person of unshakeable nature)? He should be understood as the opposite of the foregoing.

body.text: prajñāvimuktaḥ pudgala katamaḥ | yaḥ pudgalaḥ sarveṇa sarvamāsravakṣayamanuprāpnoti | no tvaṣṭau vimokṣān kāyena sākṣātkṛtyopasampadya viharati | ayamucyate prajñāvimukti (ktaḥ) pudgalaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: What is the <s>prajñāvimukta pudgala</s> (person liberated by wisdom)? That person who attains the complete destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) in every respect, but does not dwell having directly realized with the body the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) and having entered upon them. This is called the person liberated by wisdom.

body.text: ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ
body.translated_text: What is the <s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta pudgala</s> (person liberated in both ways)? That person who attains the complete destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> in every respect and dwells having entered upon the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> with the body. His mind is liberated from the <s>kleśāvaraṇa</s> (affliction-obstruction), and from the <s>vimokṣāvaraṇa</s> (liberation-obstruction). This is called the person liberated in both ways.

body.text: katamaḥ | yaḥ pudgala sarveṇa sarvamāsravakṣayamanu prāpnoti | aṣṭau vimokṣānkāyenopasampadya viharati | tasya kleśāvaraṇācca cittaṃ muktaṃ bhavati | vimokṣāvaraṇāccā[yamucya]te ubhayatobhāgavimuktaḥ pudgalaḥ ||

pudgalavyavasthānaṃ katamat | ekādaśabhiḥ prabhedaiḥ pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam | katamairekādaśabhistadyathā indriyaprabhedena, nikāyaprabhedena, caritaprabhedena [praṇidhānaprabhedena prapripatprabhedena mārgaphala prabhedena] prayogaprabhedena | samāpattiprabhedena upapattiprabhedena parihāṇi prabhedenā varaṇaprabhedena ca ||
body.translated_text: What is the classification of persons (<s>pudgalavyavasthāna</s>)? The classification of persons should be understood through eleven distinctions. Which eleven? Namely: by distinction of faculties (<s>indriya</s>), by distinction of group (<s>nikāya</s>), by distinction of conduct (<s>carita</s>), [by distinction of aspiration, by distinction of entering, by distinction of path and fruit,] by distinction of practice (<s>prayoga</s>), by distinction of attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>), by distinction of rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>), by distinction of decline (<s>parihāṇi</s>), and by distinction of obstruction (<s>āvaraṇa</s>).

body.text: indriyaprabhedena tāvat | mṛdvindriyastī (yatī) kṣṇendriyapudgalayorvyavasthānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: By distinction of faculties, first: the classification of persons of mild faculties and of keen faculties.

body.text: nikāyaprabhedena saptavidhapudgalavyavasthānaṃ | bhikṣu[r]bhikṣuṇī, śikṣamāṇā [śrāmaṇeraḥ] śrāmaṇerī upāsaka upāsikā ca ||
body.translated_text: By distinction of group, the classification of seven kinds of persons: <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), <s>bhikṣuṇī</s> (nun), <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> (probationary nun), <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (male novice), <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice), <s>upāsaka</s> (male lay follower), and <s>upāsikā</s> (female lay follower).

body.text: tatra caritaprabhedena saptānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ | yoyaṃ rāgonmadaḥ pudgalaḥ sa rāgacaritaḥ [|] yo dveṣonmadaḥ sa dveṣacaritaḥ | yo mohonmadaḥ sa mohacaritaḥ | yo mānonmadaḥ sa mānacaritaḥ | yo vitarkonmadaḥ sa vitarkacaritaḥ | yaḥ samaprāptaḥ samabhāgacaritaḥ | yo mandarajaskaḥ so [mandacarito] veditavyaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, by distinction of conduct, the classification of seven persons: the person intoxicated by <s>rāga</s> (passion) is of passionate conduct; one intoxicated by <s>dveṣa</s> (hatred) is of hateful conduct; one intoxicated by <s>moha</s> (delusion) is of deluded conduct; one intoxicated by <s>māna</s> (pride) is of proud conduct; one intoxicated by <s>vitarka</s> (discursive thought) is of discursive conduct; one who has equally arrived is of balanced conduct; one who has little dust [on the eyes] should be understood as of mild [affliction] conduct.

body.text: tatra rāgacaritasya pudgalasya katamāni liṃgāni | iha rāgacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ parītte sarvanihīne raṃjanīye vastuni ghanamadhimātraṃ rāgaparyavasthānamutpādayati | kaḥ punarvādo madhyapraṇīte [|] tacca punārāgaparyavasthānaṃ saṃtatyā cirakālamavasthāpayati | dīrghakālamanubaddho bhavati (|) tena paryavasthānena, raṃjanīyairdharmairabhibhūyate | no tu śakto [a]tiraṃjanīyāndharmānabhibhavituṃ [|] snigdhendriyaśca bhavatyakharendriyaḥ | karkaśendriyaḥ, aparuddhendriyaḥ | nātyarthaṃ pareṣāṃ viheṭhanajātīyo yaduta kāyena, vācā durvivejyaśca bhavati, duḥsaṃvejyaśca | hīnādhimuktikaśca bhavati | dṛḍhakarmāntaḥ | sthirakarmāntaḥ | dṛḍhavrataḥ | sthiravrataḥ | mahiṣṭhaśca bhavatyupakaraṇeṣu pariṣkāreṣu lolupajātīyastadgurukaśca, saumanasyabahulaśca bhavatyānandībahulo vigatabhṛkuṭiruttānamukhavarṇaḥ, smitapūrvaṃgama ityevaṃbhāgīyāni rāgacāritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni veditavyāni |
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the marks of a person of passionate conduct? Here, a person of passionate conduct, even in a small, wholly inferior, attractive object, produces a dense, excessive envelopment of passion (<s>rāgaparyavasthāna</s>) — how much more in a middling or excellent one! And he sustains the continuity of that passion-envelopment for a long time; he is pursued by that envelopment for a long duration. He is overpowered by attractive objects, yet is unable to overpower attractive objects. He is of smooth faculties, not of rough faculties, of gentle faculties, of unobstructed faculties. He is not excessively of a nature to harm others, whether by body or speech. He is hard to disgust and hard to alarm. He is of low aspiration. He is firm in his undertakings, steady in his undertakings, firm in his vows, steady in his vows. He is possessive and covetous regarding requisites and furnishings, attached to them. He is generally of pleasant temperament, generally joyful, without a frown, with an open countenance, approaching others with a smile first — such and similar should be understood as the marks of a person of passionate conduct.

body.text: dveṣacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni katamāni | iha dveṣacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ | dveṣaṇīye vastuni parīttena pratighavastunimittena ghanaṃ,prabhūtaṃ pratighaparyavasthānamutpādayati | kaḥ punarvādo madhyādhimātre(ṇa) [|] tasya ca pratighaparyavasthānasya dīrghakālaṃ santatimavasthāpayati | cirakālamanubaddho bhavati | pratighaparyavasthānena | sa dveṣaṇīyairdharmairabhibhūyate | no tu dveṣaṇīyāndharmānchakno (ñchakno)ti (

children.text: ) abhibhavituṃ | rukṣendriyaśca bhavati | kharendriyaḥ, karkaśendriyaḥ paruṣendriyaśca bhavatyatyarthaṃ pareṣāṃ viheṭhanajātīyo bhavati | yaduta kāyena, vācā | suvivenya(jya)śca bhavati | susaṃvejyaḥ | dhvāṅkṣo bhavati mukharaḥ | pragalbhaḥ anadhimuktibahulaḥ | na dṛḍhakarmānto, nasthirakarmāntaḥ | na dṛḍhavrato, na sthiravrataḥ | daurmanasyabahulaśca bhavatyupāyāsabahulaḥ | akṣamo bhavatyamahiṣṭhaḥ | vilomanajātīyaḥ | apradakṣiṇagrāhī duḥpratyāneya jātīya upanāhabahulaḥ | krūrāśaṃsaścaṇḍaśca bhavatyādā[yī] pratyakṣaravādī so 'lpamātramapyuktaḥ sannabhiṣajyate | kupyati | vyāpadyate | madgu[ḥ] pratitiṣṭhati | kopaṃ saṃja[na]yati | [vi]kṛtabhṛkuṭiśca bhavati | anuttānamukhavarṇa[ḥ] parasampattidveṣṭā, īrṣyābahula ityevaṃbhāgīyāni [dveṣa]caritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni veditavyāni ||
children.translated_text: To overpower objects worthy of hatred. He is of dry faculties, rough faculties, harsh faculties, and coarse faculties. He is excessively of a nature to harm others, whether by body or speech. He is easily disgusted and easily alarmed. He is like a crow: garrulous, bold, generally lacking in aspiration. He is not firm in undertakings, not steady in undertakings, not firm in vows, not steady in vows. He is generally of unpleasant temperament, generally distressed, intolerant, not possessive, of a contrary nature, unable to receive graciously, of a nature hard to bring back, generally harboring grudges, cruel and fierce. He is aggressive, retaliating word for word — when told even the slightest thing, he does not calm down; he becomes angry, hostile, and like a mongoose, stands firm [in resentment], generating fury. He is with a contorted frown, with an unopen countenance, hating the prosperity of others, generally envious — such and similar should be understood as the marks of a person of hateful conduct.

body.translated_text: What are the marks of a person of hateful conduct? Here, a person of hateful conduct, even with a small cause for aversion, produces a dense, abundant envelopment of aversion (<s>pratighaparyavasthāna</s>) in an object worthy of hatred — how much more with a middling or great [cause]. He sustains the continuity of that aversion-envelopment for a long time; he is pursued by the aversion-envelopment for a long duration. He is overpowered by objects worthy of hatred, yet is unable

body.text: tatra katamāni mohacaritasya pudgalasya liṅgāni | iha [moha]caritaḥ pudgalaḥ mohasthānīye vastuni parīttaṃ, ghanaṃ, prabhūtaṃ mohaparyavasthānamutpādayati | prāgeva madhyādhimātre, dṛḍhaṃ ca kālaṃ tasya mohaparyavasthānasya santatimavasthāpayati | tena cānubaddho bhavati | (

children.text: ) sa mohanīyairdharmairabhibhūyate | no tu mohanīyān dharmāṃcchaknotyabhibhavituṃ (dharmāñchaknotyabhibhavituṃ) | baddhe(dhandhe?)ndriyaśca bhavati | jaḍendriyaśca bhavati | mattendriyaśca, śithilakāyakaryānta(nto)duścintitacintī, durbhāṣitabhāṣī, duṣkṛtakarmakārī, alaso 'nutthānasampannaḥ | mandabhāgī, durmedho(dhaḥ) | muṣitasmṛtiḥ | asaṃprajānadvihārī | vāmagrāhī, durvivejyo, duḥsaṃvejyo, hīnādhimuktikaḥ | jāta eḍamūko hastasaṃbādhikaḥ | apratibalaḥ | subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāmarthamājñātuṃ pratyaya(pa?)hāyaśca bhavati | parahāyaḥ parapraṇeya ityevaṃ bhāgīyāni mohacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni veditavyāni ||
children.translated_text: He is overpowered by objects conducive to delusion, yet is unable to overpower objects conducive to delusion. He is of dull faculties, of stupid faculties, of bewildered faculties. He is lax in bodily activities, thinking poorly-considered thoughts, speaking poorly-spoken words, performing poorly-done deeds. He is lazy, endowed with non-exertion, of meager fortune, of poor intelligence, of lost mindfulness, dwelling without clear comprehension, grasping wrongly, hard to disgust, hard to alarm, of low aspiration. He is like a born mute, awkward with his hands, incapable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken words. He is one who abandons himself, who is abandoned by others, who is led by others — such and similar should be understood as the marks of a person of deluded conduct.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the marks of a person of deluded conduct? Here, a person of deluded conduct, even in a small object that is a basis for delusion, produces a dense, abundant envelopment of delusion (<s>mohaparyavasthāna</s>) — how much more in a middling or great one. He firmly sustains the continuity of that delusion-envelopment for a long time, and he is pursued by it.

body.text: tatra katamāni mānacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni | iha mānacaritaḥ pudgalo mānasthānīye vastuni parīttepi ghanaṃ mānaparyavasthānamutpādayati | kaḥ punarvādo madhyādhimātre [|] tasya ca mānaparyavasthānasya dīrghakālaṃ santatimavasthāpayati | tena cānubaddho bhavati | [katamāni mānacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni [|] iha mānacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ mānasthānīye vastuni parīttepighanaṃ mānaparyavasthānamutpādayati kaḥ punarvādo madhyādhimātre | tasya mānaparyavasthānasya dīrghakālaṃ santatimavasthāpayati | tena cānubaddho bhavati] sa mānasthānīyairdharmairabhibhūyate | (

children.text: ) no tu mānasthānīyāndharmāñchaknotyabhibhavituṃ | uddhatendriyaśca bhavatyunnatendriyaśco[nnatendriyaśca] kāyamaṇḍanānuyuktaśca bhavatyadhimātramunnatāñca vācaṃ bhāṣate, nāvanatāṃ, sātāpikagurusthānīyānāṃ ca na kālena kālaṃ yathārūpāmapacitiṃ kartā bhavati | stabdho bhavati | apraṇatakāyo nābhi vādanavandanapratyutthānānāṃ jālisāmīcīkarmaśīla, ātmapragrāhako bhavatyātmotkarṣo parapaṃsakaḥ | lābhakāmaḥ satkārakāmaḥ kīrtiśabdaślokakāmaḥ |utplāvanābhāṇḍonuvivedhyaśca(jyaśca) bhavati | duḥsaṃvejya udārādhimuktiśca bhavati | mandakāruṇyaḥ [|] adhimātraṃ cātmasattvajīvapo[ṣapu]ruṣapudgaladṛṣṭimanyubahalo bhavati | upanāhī cetyevaṃbhāgīyāni mānacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni veditavyāni ||
children.translated_text: but he is unable to overcome the <s>dharmas</s> that are occasions for pride. He has agitated faculties and elevated faculties, is devoted to adorning the body, speaks in an exceedingly haughty manner and not in a humble manner. He does not from time to time render appropriate respect to those who are in the position of elders and teachers. He is stiff, does not bend his body, and is not accustomed to greetings, salutations, rising to receive, and courteous behavior. He is self-aggrandizing, self-exalting, and disparaging of others. He desires gain, desires honor, desires fame and renown. He is one who jumps ahead and who intrudes upon others' possessions. He is hard to arouse [spiritually] and has lofty aspirations. He has little compassion, and he is greatly filled with views and resentment concerning self, being, soul, life-force, person, and individual. He bears grudges — such and similar are to be understood as the signs of a person of proud temperament.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the marks of a person of proud conduct? Here, a person of proud conduct, even in a small object that is a basis for pride, produces a dense envelopment of pride (<s>mānaparyavasthāna</s>) — how much more in a middling or great one. He sustains the continuity of that pride-envelopment for a long time, and he is pursued by it. [The passage is repeated in the manuscript.] He is overpowered by objects that are bases for pride.

body.text: tatra katamāni vitarkacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni | iha vitarkacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ vitarka sthānīye vastuni parīttepi ghanaparyavasthānamutpādayati | tacca paryavasthānaṃ dīrghakālamavasthāpayati | tena cānubaddho bhavati | sa vitarkasthānīyairdharmairabhibhūyate | no tu vitarkasthānīyān dharmāṃ (rmāñ) chaknotyabhibhavituṃ | asthirendriyaśca bhavati | capalendriyaḥ | (

children.text: ) traṃ (caṃ)calendriyaḥ | vyākulendriyaḥ | [asthira]kāyakarmāntaḥ [|] cha(du)ritavākkarmāntī, durvivejyo duḥsaṃvejyaḥ, prapaṃcārāmaḥ prapaṃcarataḥ | kāṃkṣābahulo, vicikitsābahulaḥ | chandikaśca bhavatyasthiravrataḥ | aniścitavrataḥ | asthirakarmāntaḥ [|] aniścitakarmāntaḥ [|] śaṃkābahulaḥ, pramuṣitasmṛtiḥ | vivekānabhirato, vikṣepabahulaḥ | lokacitreṣu chandarāgānusṛtaḥ [|] dakṣonalasa ityevaṃ bhāgīyāni vitarkacaritasya pudgalasya liṃgāni veditavyāni || idaṃ caritaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: wavering faculties, agitated faculties. [He has] unsteady bodily conduct, hasty verbal conduct, is hard to instruct and hard to arouse. He delights in and is attached to mental proliferation (<s>prapañca</s>). He is full of doubt and full of uncertainty. He is impulsive and of unsteady vows, of undetermined vows, of unsteady undertakings, of undetermined undertakings. He is full of suspicion, of lost mindfulness, not delighting in seclusion, full of distraction, following desire and attachment for the spectacles of the world, clever but not lazy — such and similar are to be understood as the signs of a person of discursive temperament. This is to be understood as the classification of persons according to the distinction of temperament.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of a person of discursive temperament (<s>vitarkacarita</s>)? Here, a person of discursive temperament, even with respect to a minor object that is an occasion for discursive thought, generates a thick mental affliction, and he maintains that affliction for a long time, and is pursued by it. He is overcome by <s>dharmas</s> that are occasions for discursive thought, but is unable to overcome the <s>dharmas</s> that are occasions for discursive thought. He has unsteady faculties, fickle faculties,

body.text: tatra praṇidhānaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ | asti pudgalaḥ śrāvakayāne kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ [|] asti pratyekabuddhayāne [|] asti mahāyāne [|] tatra yoyaṃ pudgalaḥ | śrāvakayāne kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ samyakchrāvakagotraḥ syātpratyekabuddhagotraḥ | syānmahāyānagotraḥ | tatrayoyaṃ pudgalaḥ pratyekāyāṃ bodhau kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ so 'pi syātpratyekabuddhagotraḥ, syācchāvakagotraḥ, syānmahāyānagotraḥ [|] tatra yoyaṃ pudgalo mahāyāne kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ so 'pi syāchrāvakagotraḥ, syātpratyekabuddhagotraḥ, syānmahāyānagotraḥ | tatra yoyaṃ śrāvakagotraḥ pudgalaḥ pratyekayāmbodhau, anuttarāyāmvā samyaksaṃbodhau kṛtapraṇidhānaḥ | sa śrāvakagotratvādavaśyamante kāle tatpraṇidhānaṃ (

children.text: ) vyāvartyaṃ śrāvakayānapraṇidhāna evāvatiṣṭhate | evaṃ pratyekabuddhayānagotro mahāyānagotro veditavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: he may turn away and settle in the aspiration for the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> alone. Likewise, one of the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> lineage and one of the <s>Mahāyāna</s> lineage should be understood.

body.translated_text: Therein, the classification of persons according to the distinction of aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): there is a person who has made an aspiration for the <s>Śrāvakayāna</s> (Hearers' Vehicle); there is one for the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> (Solitary Buddhas' Vehicle);

body.text: tatra bhavatyeṣāṃ pudgalānāṃ praṇidhānasaṃbhāraḥ praṇidhānavyatikaraḥ | no tu gotrasaṃbhāro, gotravyatikaraḥ | asmiṃstvarthe śrāvakayānapraṇidhānā[ḥ] śrāvakagotrāścaite pudgalā veditavyāḥ || evaṃ praṇidhānaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, for these persons there may be a mixing of aspirations and a crossing over of aspirations, but there is no mixing of lineages (<s>gotra</s>) and no crossing over of lineages. In this matter,

body.text: kathaṃ pratipatprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati | eṣāṃ yathoddiṣṭānāṃ yathāparikīrttitānāṃ pudgalānāṃ catasṛbhiḥ pratipadbhirniryāṇaṃ bhavati | katamābhiścatasṛbhiḥ [|] asti pratipad duḥkhā dhandhābhijñā | [asti pratipad duḥkhā kṣiprābhijñā] | asti pratipatsukhā dhandhābhijñā asti pratipatsukhā kṣiprābhijñā || tasya mṛdvindriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānalābhino yā pratipadiyamucyate duḥkhā dhandhābhijñā | tatra tīkṣṇendriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānalābhino yā pratipadiyamucyate duḥkhā kṣiprābhijñā | tatra mṛdvindriyasya pudgalasya mauladhyānalābhino yā pratipadiyamucyate sukhā dhandhābhijñā | tatra tīkṣṇendrisya pudgalasya mauladhyānalābhino yā pratipadiyamucyate sukhā kṣiprābhijñā | evaṃ pratipatprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ veditavyaṃ ||
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons according to the distinction of practice (<s>pratipatti</s>)? For these persons as enumerated and described, through four types of practice

body.text: tatra kathaṃ mārgaphalaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ (
