children.text: ) veditavyaṃ | tadyathā | caturṇāṃ pratipannakānāṃ strota āpattiphalapratipannakasya sakṛdāgāmiphalapratipannakasya anāgāmiphalapratipannakasya, arhatta(arhattva)phalapratipannakasya, caturṇāṃ phalasthānāṃ srota āpannasya, sakṛdāgāminaḥ | anāgāminorhataśca ye pratipannakamārgā vartante | te pratipannakāsteṣāṃ pratipannakamārgeṇa vyavasthānaṃ | ye 'rhatphalaśrāmaṇyaphalavyavasthitāsteṣāṃ [mārgapha]lavyavasthānamevaṃ mārgaphalaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: It is as follows: among the four practitioners — the one practicing for the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpatti</s>), the one practicing for the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>), the one practicing for the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>),

body.translated_text: therein, how is the classification of persons according to the distinction of path and fruit (<s>mārgaphala</s>) to be understood?

body.text: kathaṃ prayogaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati | tadyathā śraddhānusāridharmānusāriṇā [|] yaḥ pudgalaḥ śraddhānusāreṇa prayuktaḥ | sa śraddhānusārī, yo dharmeṣu parapratyayavinayānusāreṇa prayuktaḥ sa dharmānusārī | evaṃ prayogaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons according to the distinction of approach (<s>prayoga</s>)? It is as follows: the faith-follower (<s>śraddhānusārin</s>) and the <s>dharma</s>-follower (<s>dharmānusārin</s>). A person who is a faith-follower

body.text: tatra kathaṃ samāpattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati | tadyathā kāyasākṣiṇaḥ (sākṣī) aṣṭau vimokṣān kāyena sākṣātkṛtyopasampadya viharati | na ca sarveṇa sarvamāsravakṣayamanuprāpto bhavati | rūpī rūpāṇi paśyati | adhyātmamarūpasaṃjñāṃ bahirdhā rūpāṇi paśyati | śubhavimokṣaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtyopasampadya viharati | ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ, vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ, ākiñcanyāyatanaṃ, naiva saṃjñā nāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ, saṃjñāvedayitanirodhamanulomapratilomaṃ (

children.text: ) samāpadyate ca, vyuttiṣṭhate ca | evaṃ samāpattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: he enters and emerges [from them]. Thus is the classification of persons according to the distinction of attainment.

body.translated_text: Therein, how is the classification of persons according to the distinction of attainment (<s>samāpatti</s>)? It is as follows: the body-witness (<s>kāyasākṣin</s>) directly experiences the eight <s>vimokṣas</s> (liberations) with the body,

body.text: kathamupapattiprabhedena | pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati | tadyathā saptakṛdbhavaparamasya, kulaṃkulasya, ekavīcikasyāntarāparinirvāyiṇaḥ upapadyaparinirvāyiṇaḥ, ūrdhvaṃsrotasaśca | evamupapattiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons according to the distinction of rebirth (<s>upapatti</s>)? It is as follows: one who is reborn at most seven times (<s>saptakṛtbhavaparama</s>), one who passes from family to family (<s>kulaṃkula</s>), one who has one more interval (<s>ekavīcika</s>), one who attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the intermediate state (<s>antarāparinirvāyin</s>),

body.text: kathamaparihāṇiprabhedena | pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati | tadyathā samayavimuktasyārhataḥ yo bhavyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇāya, aparihāṇiprabhedena punarvyavasthānaṃ || akopyadharmakasyārhataḥ yo na bhavyo dṛṣṭadharmasukhavihārebhyaḥ parihāṇāya [|] eva maparihāṇiprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: How is the classification of persons according to the distinction of non-decline (<s>aparihāṇi</s>)? It is as follows: for the <s>Arhat</s> who is liberated by occasion (<s>samayavimukta</s>), who is capable of abiding in the pleasure of the present <s>dharma</s>,

body.text: tatra kathamāvaraṇaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavati | tadyathā prajñāvimuktasyobhayatobhāgavimuktasyārhataḥ | tatra prajñāvimuktorhan kleśāvaraṇavimukto, na samāpattyāvaraṇāt | ubhayatobhāgavimuktastu | arhan | kleśāvaraṇācca vimuktaḥ, samāpattyāvaraṇācca tasmādubhayatobhāgavimukta ityucyate | evamāvaraṇaprabhedena pudgalavyavasthānaṃ bhavatyebhistribhirbhedairyayoddiṣṭairyathoddiṣṭānāṃ pudgalānāṃ yathākramaṃ vyavasthānaṃ veditavyam ||
body.translated_text: Therein, how is the classification of persons according to the distinction of obstruction (<s>āvaraṇa</s>)? It is as follows: the <s>Arhat</s> liberated by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukta</s>) and the one liberated in both ways (<s>ubhayatobhāgavimukta</s>). Therein,

body.text: tatrālambanaṃ katamat | āha [|] catvāryāryālambanavastūni | (

children.text: ) katamāni catvāri | vyāpyālambanaṃ, caritaviśodhamālambanaṃ kauśalyālambanaṃ, kleśaviśodhanaṃ cālambanaṃ |
children.translated_text: What are the four? The pervading object (<s>vyāpyālambana</s>), the object for purification of temperament (<s>caritaviśodhanālambana</s>), the object of skill (<s>kauśalyālambana</s>), and the object for purification of defilements (<s>kleśaviśodhanālambana</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the object of meditation (<s>ālambana</s>)? He says: There are four noble objects of meditation.

body.text: tatra vyāpyālambanaṃ katamat | āha | tadapi caturvidhaṃ | tadyathā savikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ, nirvikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ, vastuparīttatā | kāryapariniṣpattiśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the pervading object? He says: It too is of four kinds — namely, the image with conceptual elaboration (<s>savikalpaṃ pratibimba</s>), the image without conceptual elaboration (<s>nirvikalpaṃ pratibimba</s>), the reality of the object (<s>vastutathatā</s>),

body.text: tatra savikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ katamat | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ saddharmaśravaṇaṃ vā avavādānuśāsanīmvā niśritya, dṛṣṭamvā, śrutamvā, parikalpitaṃ vopādāya jñeyavastusabhāgaṃ sa vikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ samāhitabhūmikai rvipaśyanākārairvipaśyati | vicinoti | pravicinoti | parivitarkayati | parimīmānsā (māṃsā)māpadyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the image with conceptual elaboration? Here, a certain person, relying on the hearing of the true <s>Dharma</s> or on instruction and admonition, with respect to what has been seen, heard,

body.text: tatra jñeyamvastu [|] tadyathā aśubhā vā, maitrī vā, (

children.text:
) idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādo vā, dhātuprabhedo vā, ānāpānasmṛtirvā | skandhakauśalyamvā, dhātukauśalyamāyatanakauśalyaṃ, pratītyasamutpādakauśalyaṃ, sthānāsthānakauśalyaṃ | adhobhūmīnāmaudārikatvaṃ | uparibhūmīnāṃ sātatyaṃ, samudayasatyaṃ, nirodhasatyaṃ, mārgasatyamidamucyate | jñeyamvastu |
tasyāsya jñeyavastunaḥ avavādānuśāsanīmvā āgamya, saddharmapra(śra)vaṇaṃ vā, tanniśrayeṇa samāhitabhūmikaṃ manaskāraṃ saṃmukhīkṛtya, tāneva dharmānadhimucyate | tadevaṃ jñeyamvastuni (stvadhi)mucyate | sa tasmin samaye pratyakṣānubhāvika iti vā[dhi]mokṣaḥ pravarttate | jñeyaṃvastuni (stviti) ca | tajjñeyamvastu pratyakṣībhūtaṃ bhavati | samavahitaṃ, saṃmukhībhūtaṃ, na punaranyattajjātīyaṃ dravyamapi tvadhimokṣānubhavaḥ | sa tādṛśā(śo) manaskārānubhavaḥ samāhitabhūmiko, yena tasya jñeyasya vastunaḥ anusadṛśaṃ tad bhavati (|) pratibhāsaṃ, yena taducyate | jñeyavastubhāvaṃ (-sabhāgaṃ) pratibimbimiti | yadayaṃ (dimaṃ) yoga[ṃ] santīrayaṃstasmin prakṛte, jñeye vastuni parīkṣya guṇadoṣāvadhāraṇaṃ karoti | idamucyate savikalpaṃ pratibimbaṃ [|]
children.translated_text: <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) as conditionality, or <s>dhātuprabheda</s> (analysis of elements), or <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing); or skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases),

body.translated_text: Therein, the knowable object is as follows: <s>aśubhā</s> (contemplation of the impure), or <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), or

body.text: nirvikalpaṃ (|) pratibimbaṃ katamat | ihāyaṃ yogī pratibimbānnimittamudgṛhya na punaḥ vicinoti | (

children.text: ) prativicinoti | parivitarkayati | parimīmānsā (māṃsā)māpadyate | api tu tadevālambanamasaktañcārthākāreṇa tannimittaṃ śamayati | api tu navākārayā cittasthityā adhyātmameva cittaṃ sthāpayati | saṃsthāpayati | avasthāpayatyupasthāpayati | damayati | śamayati | [vyupaśamayati] | ekotīkaroti | samādhatte [|] tasya tasminsamaye nirvikalpaṃ tatpratibimbaṃ ālambanaṃ bhavati | yatrāsāvekāṃśenaikāgrāṃ smṛtimavasthāpayati (|) tadālambanaṃ, no tu vicinoti | parivitarkayati | parisīmānsā (māṃsā)māpadyate | tacca pratibimbaṃ pratibimba mityucyate | itīmāni tasya jñeyavastusabhāgasya pratibimbasya paryāyanāmāni veditavyāni |
children.translated_text: ) he investigates, he deliberates, he engages in examination. But rather, that very object, without attachment and in the aspect of meaning, he calms its sign. Rather, by the ninefold mode of mental stability, he internally establishes the mind, makes it settle, makes it abide, makes it stand, tames it, calms it, thoroughly calms it, unifies it, and concentrates it. For him at that time, the non-conceptual <s>pratibimba</s> (reflected image) becomes the object, wherein he establishes one-pointed mindfulness in one aspect. That is the object — but he does not investigate it, does not deliberate upon it, does not engage in examination of it. And that <s>pratibimba</s> is called 'reflected image.' These should be understood as the synonymous names of that reflected image which is similar to the knowable object.

body.translated_text: What is the image without conceptual elaboration? Here, this <s>yogī</s>, having grasped the sign from the image, does not further investigate it.

body.text: vastupapannatā (vastuparyantatā) katamā | yadālambanasya yadbhāvikatā yathāvadbhāvikatā | yathāvadbhāvikatā ca |
body.translated_text: What is <s>vastuparyantatā</s> (the finality of the object)? It is the <s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s> (extent-reality) and <s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s> (mode-reality) of the object.

body.text: tatra yāvadbhāvikatā katamā | yasmātpareṇa rūpaskandho (

children.text: ) vā, vedanāskandho vā, saṃjñāskandho [vā], saṃskā[ra]skandho vā, vijñānaskandho vā, vijñānaskandho veti | sarvasaṃskṛtavastusaṃgrahaḥ paṃcabhirdharmaiḥ sarvadharmasaṃgraho dhātubhirāyatanaiśca sarvajñeyavastusaṃgrahaśca | āryasatyairiyamucyate yāvadbhāvikatā ||
children.translated_text: ) or the <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling), or the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of perception), or the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations), or the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness). The inclusion of all conditioned objects is through the five <s>dharmas</s>; the inclusion of all <s>dharmas</s> is through the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) and <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); and the inclusion of all knowable objects is through the Noble Truths. This is called <s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s> (extent-reality)? Beyond which, the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form),

body.text: tatra yathāvadbhāvikatā katamā | yā ālambanasya bhūtatā | tathatā ca tasṛbhiryuktibhiḥ | yuktyupetatā | yadutāpekṣā (|) yuktyā, kāryakāraṇayuktyā | upapattisādhanayuktyā | dharmatāyuktyā ca | iti yā cālambanasya yāvadbhāvikatā, yā ca yathāvadbhāvi[ka]tā tadekatyamabhisaṃkṣipya vastuparyantatetyucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s> (mode-reality)? It is the true nature of the object, its <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), and its being endowed with reasoning through three types of reasoning: reasoning by dependency, reasoning by causal relation, reasoning by evidential proof, and reasoning by the nature of things. The <s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s> and <s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s> of the object — these two, condensed into one, are called <s>vastuparyantatā</s>.

body.text: tatra kāryapariniṣpattiḥ katamā | yadasya [yogina]āsevanānvayā[d]bhāvanānvayād bahulīkārānvayācchamathavipaśyanāyā[ḥ] pratibimbālambano manaskāraḥ | sa paripūryate, tatparipūryā pratibimbālambano manaskāraḥ | sa paripūryate | tatparipūryā(ś)cāśrayaḥ parivarttate | sarvadauṣṭhulyāni ca pratipraśrabhyante | āśrayaparivṛtteśca pratibimbamatikramya tasminneva jñeye vastuni nirvikalpaṃ pratyakṣaṃ jñānadarśanamutpadyate | prathamadhyānasamāpattuḥ, (

children.text: ) prathamadhyānalābhinaḥ prathamadhyānagocare, dvitīyatṛtīyacaturthadhyānasamāpattuḥ | caturthadhyānalābhinaḥ | caturthadhyānagocare, ākāśānantyāyatanavijñānānantyāyatanākiṃcanyāyatananaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattustallābhinastadgocare [|] iyamucyate kārya pariniṣpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) — for one who has attained the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), within the domain of the first <s>dhyāna</s>; of the second, third, and fourth <s>dhyāna</s> attainments; for one who has attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, within the domain of the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the accomplishment of the result? That which, through the yogin's repeated practice, cultivation, and repeated engagement, the accomplishment of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight)

body.text: tānyetāni bhavati | catvāryālamba navastūni | sarvatragāni sarveṣvālambaneṣvanugatāni atītānāgapratyutpannaissamyaksaṃbuddhairdeśitāni | tenaitadbāhyālambanamityucyate | api caitadālambanaṃ śamathapakṣyaṃ, vipaśyanāpakṣyaṃ, sarvavastukaṃ, bhūtavastukaṃ, hetuphalavastukaṃ ca | tena tadvyāpītyucyate |
body.translated_text: These are the four object-matters. They are universal, pervading all objects, present in the past, future, and present, by all Perfectly Awakened Ones.

body.text: yattāvadāha | savikalpaṃ pratibimbamiti | idamatra vipaśyanāpakṣyasya [|] yatpunarāha | vastuparyantateti | idamatra sarvavastukatāyā bhūtavastukatāyāśca | yadāha | kāryapariniṣpattiriti | idamatra hetuphalasambandhasya |
body.translated_text: What he says as 'the reflected image with conceptualization' — this pertains to the side of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). What he then says as '<s>vastuparyantatā</s>' — this pertains to all

body.text: yathoktambhagavatā | āyuṣmantaṃ revatamārabhya [|] evamanuśrūyate | āyuṣmān revato bhagavantaṃ praśnamaprākṣīt | (

children.text: ) kiyatā, bhadanta, bhikṣuryogā, [(gī) yogā]cāra ālambane cittamupanibaddhaḥ, katamasminnālambane cittamupanibaghnātīti | kathaṃ punarālambanai(ne) cittamupanibaddhaṃ sūpanibaddhaṃ bhavati | sādhu, sādhu, revata, sādhu khalu tvaṃ revata | etamarthaṃ pṛcchati (si) | tena hi śrṛṇu ca, sādhu ca, manasi kuru, bhāṣiṣye [|] iha, revata bhikṣuryogī yogācāraḥ caritamvā viśodhayitukāmaḥ, kauśalyamvā kartukāmaḥ | āsravebhyo vā cittaṃ vimocayitukāmaḥ | anurūpe cālambane cittamupanibadhnāti | pratirūpe ca samyageva copanibaghnāti | tatra cānirākṛtadhyāyī bhavati |
children.translated_text: ) 'To what extent, Venerable Sir, does a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk), a practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, have his mind bound to the object, and in which object does he bind the mind?' [The Blessed One replied:]

body.translated_text: As stated by the Blessed One, with reference to the venerable <s>Revata</s>: 'Thus it is heard: the venerable <s>Revata</s> asked the Blessed One a question:' (

body.text: kathamanurūpe ālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | [sa ce]drevata, bhikṣuryogī yogācāraḥ (ro) rāgacarita eva, sa na śubhālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | evamanurūpe ālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | dveṣacarito vā punarmaitryāṃ, mohacarito vā idaṃ pratyayatāpratītyasamutpāde, mānacarito dhātuprabhede | sa cedrevata, sa bhikṣuryogī yogācārovitarkacarita eva ānāpānasmṛtau cittamupanibaghnāti | evaṃ so 'nurūpe ālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | sa cetsa, revata, bhikṣuḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ svalakṣaṇe saṃmūḍhaḥ, kintu kauśalye cittamupanibaghnāti | (

children.text: ) hetusaṃmūḍho dhātukauśalye, pratyayasaṃmūḍha āyatanakauśalye, kāmadhātorvāvairāgyaṃ karttukāmaḥ, kāmānāmaudārikatve, rūpāṇāṃ śāntatve, rūpebhyo vā vairāgyaṃ karttukāmaḥ | rūpāṇāmaudārikatve ārūpyaśāntatāyāṃ ca cittamupanibaghnāti | sarvatra vā satkāyānnirvekṣukāmo, vimoktukāmaḥ, duḥkhasatye(ṣu) samudayasatye, nirodhasatye, mārgasatye cittamupanibaghnāti | evaṃ hi, revata, bhikṣuryogī yogācāraḥ | anurūpe ālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | iha revata, bhikṣuryadyadeva jñeyaṃ vastu nicettukāmo bhavati, pracettukāmaḥ | parivitarkayitukāmaḥ | parimīmānsa (māṃsa)yitukāmaḥ | tacca tena pūrvameva dṛṣṭamvā bhavati | śrutamvā | matamvā | vijñātamvā [|] sa tadeva dṛṣṭamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā, śrutaṃ, mataṃ, vijñātamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā, samāhitabhūmikenamanaskāreṇa manasikaroti | vikalpayatyadhimucyate | sa na tadeva jñeyamvastu samāhitaṃ sammukhībhūtaṃ paśyatyapi tu tatpratirūpakamasyotpadyate | tatpratibhāsamvā, jñānamātramvā, darśanamātramvā, pratismṛtamātramvā yadālambanamayaṃ bhikṣuryogī yogācāraḥ samyagevālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | sa cedayaṃ, revata, bhikṣuryogī yogācāra ālambane cittamupanibaghnātyā (ti yā)vad(j) jñeyaṃ jñātavyaṃ bhavati | tacca yathābhūta[maviparītacittaṃ (ta)mevaṃ hi, revata, (
children.translated_text: ) confused about causes, [he should train in] skill regarding the <s>dhātus</s> (elements); confused about conditions, in skill regarding the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); wishing to produce dispassion toward the desire realm, [he should contemplate] the coarseness of sensual pleasures, the

children.text: ) bhikṣuryogī yogācā]raḥ | samyagevālambane cittamupanibaghnāti | kathaṃ ca, revata, bhikṣuryogī yogācāra[ḥ] anirākṛtadhyāsī (yī) bhavati | sa cetsa, revata, bhikṣurevamālambane samyakprayujyamāna[ḥ] sātatyaprayogī ca bhavati | satkṛtyaprayogī ca | kālena ca kālaṃ śamathanimittaṃ bhāvayati | pragrahanimittamupekṣāni mittamāsevanānvayād bhāvanānvayādvahulīkārānvayātsarvadauṣṭhulyānāṃ pratipraśrabdherāśrayapariśuddhimanuprāpnoti | sparśayati (spṛśati) | sākṣātkaroti | jñeyavastupratyavekṣatayā ca ālambanapariśuddhiṃ, rāgavirāgāccittapariśuddhimavidyā [vi]rāgāt (|) jñānapariśuddhimadhigacchati | sparśayati (spṛśati), sākṣātkaroti | evaṃ hi sa, revata, bhikṣuryogī yogācāraḥ anirākṛtadhyāyī bhavati | yataśca revata, bhikṣurasminnālambane cittamupanibadhnātyevaṃ cālambane cittamupanibadhnātyevamasya taccittamālambane sūpanibaddhaṃ bhavati |
children.translated_text: ) the <s>bhikṣu</s>, the practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, properly binds his mind to the object. And how, <s>Revata</s>, does a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, not reject the <s>Dharma</s>

body.translated_text: How does he bind the mind to an appropriate object? 'If, <s>Revata</s>, a <s>bhikṣu</s>, a practitioner of <s>yoga</s>, is of a passionate temperament, he does not take up the <s>śubha</s> (beauty) meditation as his object.

body.text: || tatra gāthā ||
body.translated_text: Herein is a verse:

children.translated_text: The <s>yogin</s> who moves among the signs, knowing the welfare of all beings,
the meditator on the reflected image, constant in practice, attains purity.

body.text: tatra yattāvadāha || nimitteṣu caranyogī anena tāvacchamathanimitte, pragrahanimitte, upekṣānimitte satatakāritā cākhyātā || yatpunarāha | sarvabhūtārthavedaka iti | anena vastuparyantatā ākhyātā || yatpunarāha | bimbadhyāyī sātatikaḥ | ityanena savikalpaṃ nirvikalpañca pratibimbamākhyātam | yatpunarāha | pāriśuddhiṃ vigacchatītyanena kārya[pari]niṣpattirākhyātā || punarapi coktaṃ bhagavatā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what he says — 'The <s>yogin</s> who moves among the signs' — by this, the constant application to the sign of calm (<s>śamatha</s>), the sign of exertion (<s>pragraha</s>), and the sign of equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) is declared.

body.text:
cittanimittasya kovidaḥ
pravivekasya (prāvivekyasya?) ca vidante rasaṃ |
dhyāyī nipakaḥ pratismṛto
bhuṃkte prītisukhaṃ nirāmiṣaṃ [||]
body.translated_text: Skilled in the sign of the mind, and understanding the flavor of seclusion — the meditator, wise, mindful, enjoys the bliss of <s>prīti</s> (joy) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness).

body.text: tatra yattāvadāha, cittanimittasya kovida ityanena savikalpaṃ nirvikalpaṃ ca pratibimba[ṃ] nimittaśabdenākhyātaṃ | vastupaparyantatā kovidaśabdena | yatpunarāha | prāvivekyasya ca vidante rasamityanenālambane samyakprayuktasya prahāṇārāmatā bhāvanārāmatā cākhyātā | yatpunarāha | dhyāyī nipaka[ḥ] pratismṛta ityanena śamathavipaśyanāyā bhāvanāsātatyamākhyātam || yatpunarāha | bhuṃkte prītisukhaṃ nirāmiṣamityanena kāyapariniṣpattirākhyātā || tadevaṃ satyetadvyāpyālambanamāptāgamaviśuddhaṃ (

children.translated_text: ) should be understood. And it accords with reasoning. This is called the pervading object.

body.translated_text: Therein, what he says — 'skilled in the sign of the mind' — by this, the reflected image both with conceptualization and without conceptualization is declared by the word 'sign.' The object-

body.text: tatra caritaviśodhanamālambanaṃ katamat || tadyathā aśubhā [|] maitrī | idaṃ pratyayatāpratītyasamutpādaḥ | dhātuprabhedaḥ | ānāpānasmṛtiśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the object for purifying one's temperament? Namely: <s>aśubhā</s> (the meditation on the unattractive), <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness), <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) as conditionality, analysis of the <s>dhātus</s> (elements),

body.text: tatrāśubhā katamā | āha [|] ṣaḍavidhā aśubhā | tadyathā pratyaśubhatā | duḥkhāśubhatā | avarāśubhatā | āpekṣikī aśubhatā | kleśāśubhatā | prabhaṃgurāśubhatā ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>aśubhā</s> (the unattractive)? He says: <s>aśubhā</s> is of six kinds, namely: <s>pratyaśubhatā</s> (direct unattractiveness), <s>duḥkhāśubhatā</s> (unattractiveness through suffering), <s>avarāśubhatā</s> (inferior unattractiveness), <s>āpekṣikī aśubhatā</s> (relative unattractiveness),

body.text: tatra pratyaśubhatā katamā | āha | pratyaśubhatā adhyātmaṃ copādāya, bahirdhā copādāya veditavyā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>pratyaśubhatā</s> (direct unattractiveness)? He says: Direct unattractiveness should be understood both with reference to what is internal and with reference to what is external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmamupādāya | tadyathā- keśā, romāṇi, nakhā, dantā, rajo, malaṃ, tvaṅmānsa(māṃsa)masthi, snāyu[ḥ], sirā, vṛkkā (kkaṃ), hṛdayaṃ, plīhakaṃ, klomaṃ, antrānyaṇtraguṇā, āmāśayaṃ (yaḥ), pakvāśayaṃ(yaḥ), mūtraṃ, purīṣamaśru, svedaḥ, kheṭā, śiṃghāṇakaṃ, vasā, lasīkā, majjāmedaḥ, pittaṃ, śleṣmā, pūyaḥ, śoṇitamastakaṃ, mastakaluṃgaṃ, prasrāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, with reference to what is internal — namely: head-hair, body-hair, nails, teeth, dust, filth, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, veins, kidneys,

body.text: tatra bahirdhā copādāya aśubhā (aśubhatā) katamā | tadyathā vinīlakambā, vipūyakamvā, vibhadrātmakamvā, vyādhmātma(ta)kamvā, vikhādita(ka)mvā | vilohitakamvā | vikṣiptakamvā | asthi vā | śaṃkalikāṃ (kā) vā | uccārakṛtamvā, prasrāvakṛtamvā, kheṭākṛtamvā, śiṃghāṇakakṛtamvā, rudhiramrakṣitamvā, pūyamrakṣitamvā, gūthakaṭhillamvā, syandanikā vā | ityevaṃ bhāgīyā bahirdhopādāya pratyaśubhatā veditavyā |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the unattractiveness based on what is external? Namely: the blue-discolored [corpse], or the festering, or the gnawed, or the bloated, or the cut-up, or the blood-smeared, or the scattered [corpse], or a bone, or a chain of bones, or what is made of excrement, or of urine, or of phlegm, or of nasal mucus, or smeared with blood, or smeared with pus, or a lump of feces, or [bodily] discharge. Such and similar [things] should be understood as the unattractiveness of counter-[contemplation] based on what is external.

body.text: yā cādhyātmamupādāya | yā ca bahirdhopādāyāśubhatā | iyamucyate | pratyaśubhatā |
body.translated_text: That which is based on what is internal, and that unattractiveness which is based on what is external — this is called 'counter-unattractiveness' (<s>pratyaśubhatā</s>).

body.text: tatra duḥkhāśubhatā katamā | yadduḥkhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate | kāyikacaitasikamasātaṃ vedayitaṃ vedanāgata miyamucyate | duḥkhāśubhatā |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the unattractiveness of suffering? That which arises dependent on a contact to be experienced as painful — the unpleasant physical and mental feeling that has entered the category of sensation — this is called the unattractiveness of suffering.

body.text: tatrāvarāśubhatā katamā | yatsarvanihīnamvastu, sarvanihīno dhātustadyathā kāmadhātuḥ, yasmātpunarhīnataraścāvarataraśca, pratikruṣṭataraścāsau dhāturnāsti | iyamucyate avarāśubhatā |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the unattractiveness of inferiority? Whatever entity is entirely low, whatever element is entirely low — namely, the <s>kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) — since there is no element lower, more inferior, or more despised than that one — this is called the unattractiveness of inferiority.

body.text: āpekṣikī aśubhatā katamā | tadyathā tadekatyamvastu śubhamapi sadanyacchubhataramapekṣyāśubhataḥ khyāti | tadyathā | ārūpyānapekṣya rūpadhāturaśubhataḥ khyāti | satkāyanirodhanirvāṇamapekṣya yāvadbhavāgramaśubhaśca (bha iti) saṃkhyāṃ gacchati | iyamevaṃ bhāgīyāpekṣikī aśubhatā [|]
body.translated_text: What is relative unattractiveness? Just as a certain entity, though attractive in itself, appears as unattractive in comparison with something more attractive. For example, the <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form realm) appears as unattractive in comparison with the formless realms; and everything up to the peak of existence is reckoned as unattractive in comparison with the <s>nirvāṇa</s> that is the cessation of the personal aggregate. Such and similar is relative unattractiveness.

body.text: traidhātukāvacarāṇi (|) sarvāṇi saṃyojanabandhanā[nya]nuśayopakleśāśubhatetyucyate (-śā aśubhatetyucyate) ||
body.translated_text: All fetters, bonds, latent tendencies, and defilements pertaining to the three realms are called 'the unattractiveness of defilements.'

body.text: tatra prabhaṃgurāśubhatā katamā | yā paṃcānāmupādānaskandhānāmanityatā, adhruvānāśvāsikatā, vipariṇāmadharmatā itīyamaśubhatā rāgacaritasya viśuddhaye | ālambanaṃ tatra rāgastadyathā | adhyātmaṃ kāmeṣu (

children.text: ) kāmachandaḥ (cchandaḥ), kāmarāgaḥ, bahirdhā kāmeṣu maithunachandaḥ (cchandaḥ), maithunarāgaḥ | viṣayachandaḥ (cchandaḥ) | viṣayarāgaḥ | rūpachando (cchando) rūparāgaḥ satkāyacha(ccha)ndaḥ satkāyarāgaśceti | ayaṃ pañcavidho rāgaḥ | tasya pañcavidhasya rāgasya prahāṇāya, prativinodanāya | asamudācārāya | ṣaḍvidhā aśubhatā ālambanaṃ | tatrādhyātmamupādāya | pratyaśubhatālambanena adhyātmaṃ kāmeṣu kāma[c]chandāt kāmarāgāccittamviśodhayati | bahirdhopādāya pratyaśubhatālambanena bahirdhā taiḥ rāgāccaturvidhā[d] rāgapratisaṃyuktādvarṇarāgasaṃsthānarāgasparśarāgopacārarāgapratisaṃyuktāccittaṃ viśodhayati |
children.translated_text: ) sensual desire (<s>kāmacchanda</s>), sensual attachment (<s>kāmarāga</s>); regarding external sensual objects: desire for sexual intercourse (<s>maithunacchanda</s>), attachment to sexual intercourse (<s>maithunarāga</s>); desire for sense objects (<s>viṣayacchanda</s>), attachment to sense objects (<s>viṣayarāga</s>); desire for form (<s>rūpacchanda</s>), attachment to form (<s>rūparāga</s>); desire for the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyacchanda</s>), and attachment to the personal aggregate (<s>satkāyarāga</s>). This is the fivefold passion. For the abandonment, dispelling, and non-recurrence of this fivefold passion —

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the unattractiveness of fragility? The impermanence, instability, unreliability, and nature of change belonging to the five aggregates of clinging — this unattractiveness [serves as] the object for the purification of one of passionate temperament. Therein, the passion [has as] its object — namely, internal sensual desires:

body.text: tatra yadā vinīlakamvā, vipūyakamvā, vimadrāmakamvā, vyādhmātmakamvā, vikhāditakaṃ vā manasi karoti | tadā varṇarāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | yadā punarvilohitakaṃ vā manasi karoti | tadā saṃsthānarāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | yadā punarasthi vā śaṃkalikāmvā manasi karoti | tadā sparśarāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | yadā vikṣiptakaṃ manasikaroti tadā upacārarāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | ataeva bhagavatā bahirdhopādāya pratyaśubhatā sā catasṛṣu śiva pathikā[su vya]vasthāpitā | (

children.text: ) yā yaivānena śivapathikā dṛṣṭā bhavati | ekāhamṛtā vā, saptāhamṛtā vā, kākaiḥ kuraraiḥ khādyamānā, gṛdhraiḥ, śvabhiḥ, śrṛgālaiḥ | tatra tatremameca (va) kāyamupasaṃharati | ayamapi me kāya evaṃ bhāvī, evaṃ bhūta, evaṃ dharmatāmanatīta iti | anena tāvadvinī lakamupādāya yāvadvikhāditakamākhyātaṃ |
children.translated_text: ) Whatever cemetery [corpse] has been seen by him — dead one day, or dead seven days — being eaten by crows, hawks, vultures, dogs, and jackals — therein, one applies [the contemplation] to just this body: 'This body of mine too is of such a nature, will become such, has not transcended this natural law.' By this, the [contemplation] from the blue-discolored up to the cut-up [corpse] is explained.

body.translated_text: Therein, when one contemplates the blue-discolored, or the festering, or the gnawed, or the bloated, or the cut-up [corpse] — then one purifies the mind from attachment to color. When one contemplates the blood-smeared [corpse] — then one purifies the mind from attachment to shape. When one contemplates a bone or a chain of bones — then one purifies the mind from attachment to touch.

body.text: yatpunarāha | yā anena śivapathikā dṛṣṭā bhavati | apagatatvaṅmānsa(māṃsa)śoṇitamvā sūpanibaddhetyanena vilohitakamākhyātaṃ |
body.translated_text: As for what is further said: 'Whatever cemetery [corpse] has been seen by him — with skin, flesh, and blood gone, well bound together [by sinews]' — by this, the blood-smeared [contemplation] is explained.

body.text: yatpunarāha | yānyeva śivapathikāsthānāni pṛṣṭhīvaṃśo, hanunakraṃ, dantamālā, śiraḥkapālaṃ tathā bhinnapratibhinnāni ekavārṣikāni dvivārṣikāni (rṣikāṇi) | yāvatsaptavāṣi(rṣi)kāni (ṇi) śvetāni śaṃkhanibhāni | kapotavarṇāni pānsu(pāṃsu)varṇavyatimiśrāṇi dṛṣṭāni bhavantītyanena vikṣiptakamākhyātaṃ |
body.translated_text: As for what is further said: 'Whatever cemetery bones — the vertebral column, the jaw, the row of teeth, the skull — broken and scattered in pieces — one year old, two years old, up to seven years old — white, resembling conch shells, dove-colored, mixed with the color of dust — have been seen' — by this, the scattered [contemplation] is explained.

body.text: evaṃ pratyaśubhatālaṃbanena bahirdhā pratisaṃyuktena maitrena (ṇa) rāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | tatra duḥkhatāśubhatālambanenāvarāśubhatālambanena ca | viṣayapratisaṃyuktātkāmarāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | tatrāpekṣāśubhatālambanena rūparāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | tatra kleśāśubhatālambanena prabhaṃgurāśubhatālambanena ca kā[ma]bhavāgramupādāya (

children.text: ) sarvasmātkāya(ma)rāgāccittaṃ viśodhayati | idaṃ tāvadrāgacaritasya caritaviśodhanena sālambanaṃ saṃbhavaṃ pratyetaducyate | sarvaṃ sarvākāramaśubhatālambanaṃ | saṃgṛhītaṃ bhavatyasmiṃstvarthe pratyaśubhatai vābhipretā | tadanyā tvaśubhatā tadanyasyāpi caritasya viśuddhaye | ālambanaṃ ||
children.translated_text: ) one purifies the mind from all attachment to the personal aggregate. This much is stated regarding the purification of one of passionate temperament — the object together with its basis and origin. All objects of unattractiveness in every aspect are included in this meaning. Herein, counter-unattractiveness alone is intended [as the primary]. But the other [types of] unattractiveness [serve as] objects for the purification of other temperaments as well.

body.translated_text: Thus, by the object of counter-unattractiveness connected with what is external, one purifies the mind from passion. Therein, by the object of the unattractiveness of suffering and by the object of the unattractiveness of inferiority, one purifies the mind from sensual attachment connected with objects. Therein, by the object of relative unattractiveness, one purifies the mind from attachment to form. Therein, by the object of the unattractiveness of defilements and of fragility,

body.text: tatra maitrī katamā | yo mitrapakṣe vā, amitrapakṣe vā | udāsīnapakṣe vā | hitā[dhyā]śayamupasthāpya mṛdumadhyādhimātrasya sukhasyopasaṃhārāyādhimokṣaḥ | (

children.text: ) samāhitabhūmikaḥ | tatra yoyaṃ mitrapakṣaḥ | amitrapakṣa udāsīnapakṣaśca [|] idamālambanaṃ | tatra yo hitādhyāśayaḥ, sukhopasaṃhārāya cādhimokṣaḥ samāhitabhūmikaḥ ayamālambaka iti (|) yaccālambanaṃ | yaścālambakastadekatyamabhisaṃkṣipya maitrītyucyate |
children.translated_text: ) belonging to the level of concentration (<s>samāhitabhūmika</s>). Therein, those in the category of friend, the category of enemy, and the category of the indifferent — this is the object. Therein, the benevolent intention and the determination for the application of happiness, belonging to the level of concentration — this is the one who takes the object. That which is the object and that which takes the object — when these are condensed into one, it is called <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)? That which, having established a benevolent intention toward those in the category of friend, the category of enemy, or the category of the indifferent, is the determination for the application of happiness — mild, middling, and intense —

body.text: tatra yattāvadāha maitrīsahagatena cittenetyanena triṣu pakṣeṣu mitrapakṣe, amitra pakṣe, udāsīnapakṣe hitadhyāśaya ākhyātaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, as for what was said — 'with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness' — by this, the benevolent intention toward the three categories — the category of friend, the category of enemy, and the category of the indifferent — is explained.

body.text: yatpunarāha | avaireṇāsampannenāvyābādhenetyanena tasyaiva hitādhyāśayasya trividhaṃ lakṣaṇamākhyātaṃ ||
body.translated_text: As for what was further said — 'without enmity, without conflict, without harm' — by this, the threefold characteristic of that very benevolent intention is explained.

body.text: tatrāvairatayā hitādhyāśayaḥ sā punaravairatā dvābhyāṃ padābhyāmākhyātā(ḥ) | asamarthatayā avyābādhata[yā ca] tatrāpratyanīkabhāvasthānārthenāsamarthatā | apakārāviṣaṣṭanārthena (
body.translated_text: Therein, the benevolent intention [is characterized] by non-enmity (<s>avairatā</s>). That non-enmity is explained by two terms: non-hostility (<s>asamartatā</s>) and non-harm (<s>avyābādhatā</s>). Therein, non-hostility has the meaning of the absence of an adversarial position; non-harm [has the meaning of]

body.text: yatpunarāha | vipulena mahadgatena pramāṇenetyanena mṛdumadhyādhimātrasya sukhasyopasaṃhāra ākhyātaḥ | kāmāvacarasya, prathamadvitīyadhyānabhūmikasya vā, tṛtīyadhyānabhūmikasya vā [|] yatpunarāha | adhimucyasyāni rvo( )pasampadya viharatītyanena sukhopasaṃhārādhimokṣaḥ | samāhitabhūmika ākhyātaḥ | sa punareṣa sukhopasaṃhāro hitādhyāśayaparigṛhītaḥ | ādhimokṣikaḥ | manaskārānugataḥ | aduḥkhāsukhite mitrapakṣe, amitrapakṣe, udāsīnapakṣe, sukhakāme veditavyaḥ | yastu duḥkhito vā, aduḥkhito vā punarmitrapakṣaḥ | amitrapakṣa udāsīnapakṣo vā [|] tatra yo duḥkhitaḥ sa karuṇāyā ālambanaṃ | yaḥ sukhitaḥ sa muditāyā ālambanamiyamucyate maitrī [|] tatra vyāpādacaritaḥ pudgalaḥ (

children.text: ) maitrī bhāvayan sattveṣu yo vyāpādastaṃ pratanu karoti | vyāpādāccittaṃ pariśodhayati ||
children.translated_text: ) one who cultivates <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward beings attenuates the ill-will toward them, and purifies the mind from ill-will.

body.translated_text: As for what was further said — 'vast, great, immeasurable' — by this, the application of happiness — mild, middling, and intense — is explained: [happiness] belonging to the <s>kāmāvacara</s> (desire realm), or belonging to the level of the first and second <s>dhyānas</s>, or belonging to the level of the third <s>dhyāna</s>. As for what was further said — 'having determined, one enters and abides' — by this, the determination for the application of happiness, belonging to the level of concentration, is explained.

body.text: tatredaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ | yattriṣvadhvasu saṃskāramātraṃ, dharmamātraṃ, vastumātraṃ, hetumātraṃ, phalamātraṃ, yuktipatitaṃ, yadutāpekṣā yuktyā, kāryakāraṇayuktyā | upapattisādhanayuktyā ca | dharmāṇāmeva dharmāhārakatvaṃ | niṣkārakavedakatvaṃ ca | idamucyate | idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpādālambanaṃ | yadālambanaṃ manasi kurvan mohādhikaḥ pudgalo mohacaritaḥ mohaṃ prajahāti | tanūkaroti | [moha]caritāccittaṃ viśodhayati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the conditionality of dependent origination (<s>idaṃpratyayatāpratītyasamutpāda</s>)? That which in the three periods of time is mere formations, mere phenomena, mere entities, mere causes, mere effects — [all] falling under the scope of reasoning: namely, the reasoning of dependence (<s>apekṣāyukti</s>), the reasoning of cause and effect (<s>kāryakāraṇayukti</s>), and the reasoning of proof by logical establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>) — the fact that phenomena are merely the nutriment of [other] phenomena, without an agent or experiencer — this is called the conditionality of dependent origination.

body.text: tatra dhātuprabhedaḥ katamaḥ | tadyathā ṣaḍdhātavaḥ | pṛthivīdhāturabdhātustejodhāturvāyudhāturākāśadhāturvijñānadhātuśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the analysis of elements (<s>dhātuprabhedha</s>)? Namely, the six elements: the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the wind element, the space element, and the consciousness element.

body.text: tatra pṛthivīdhāturdvividhaḥ | ādhyātmiko (

children.text: ) bāhyaśca | tatrādhyātmiko yadasminkāye adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ khakkhaṭaṃ kharataramupādattaṃ | bāhyaḥ punaḥ pṛthivīdhāturyadbāhyaṃ khakkhaṭaṃ kharagatamanu (mu?)pagatamanu (mu?)pādattaṃ |
children.translated_text: ) and external. Therein, the internal [earth element] is whatever is solid, hard, clung to, internal and personal within this body. The external earth element is whatever is solid, hard, external, not taken up [as personal].

body.translated_text: Therein, the earth element is twofold: internal

body.text: sa punaradhyātmikapṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ | tadyathā keśā, romāṇi, nakhā, dantā, rajo,malaṃ, tvaṅmānsamasthi, snāyu[ḥ], sirā, vṛkkā(kkaṃ), hṛdayaṃ, plīhakaṃ, klomamantrāṇyantraguṇāḥ | āmāśayaḥ | pakvāśayaḥ | yakṛtpurīṣamayamucyate ādhyātmikaḥ pṛthivīdhātuḥ |
body.translated_text: What then is the internal earth element? Namely: hair of the head, hair of the body, nails, teeth, dirt, impurity, skin, flesh, bones, sinews, veins, kidneys, heart, spleen, lungs, intestines, intestinal coils, stomach, lower bowels, liver, and feces — this is called the internal earth element.

body.text: sa punarbāhyaḥ pṛthivīdhātuḥ katamaḥ | kāṣṭhāni vā, loṣṭhāni vā, śarkarā vā, kaṭhillā vā, vṛkṣā vā, parvatāgrā vā, iti vā punaranyopyevaṃbhāgīyaḥ ayamucyate (
body.translated_text: What then is the external earth element? Logs, or clods of earth, or gravel, or stones, or trees, or mountain peaks, and whatever else is of this kind — this is called

body.text: abdhātuḥ katamaḥ | abdhāturdvividhaḥ | ādhyātmiko bāhyaśca |
body.translated_text: What is the water element? The water element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text:
tatrādhyātmika kopdhātuḥ(bdhātuḥ) katamaḥ | yadadhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ snehaḥ snehagataṃ | āpaḥ abdhātumupagatamupādātuṃ (abdhātugatamupagatamupādattaṃ) | tadyathā aśru, svedaḥ | kheṭaḥ śiṃghāṇakaḥ | basā, lasīkā, majjā, medaḥ, pittaṃ, śleṣmā, pūyaḥ, śoṇitaṃ, mastakaṃ, mastakaluṃgaṃ, praśrāvoya(srāvo 'ya)mucyate ādhyātmikobdhātuḥ |
bāhyobdhātuḥ katamaḥ | yadbāhyamāpaḥ apgataṃ (abgataṃ), snehaḥ snehagatamanu(tamu)pagatamanu(tamu)pādattaṃ | tatpunarutso vā, sarāṃsi vā, taḍāgā (

children.text: ) vā, nadyo vā,prasravaṇāni vā, iti yo vā punaranyopyevaṃbhāgīyoyamucyate bāhyobdhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) or rivers, or springs, and whatever else is of this kind — this is called the external water element.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the internal water element? Whatever is internal and personal — moisture, of the nature of moisture, water, pertaining to the water element, taken up [as personal] — namely: tears, sweat, phlegm, nasal mucus, fat, lymph, marrow, grease, bile, mucus, pus, blood, brain, brain-membrane, urine,

body.text: tejodhātuḥ katamaḥ | tejodhāturdvividhaḥ ādhyātmiko bāhyaśca ||
body.translated_text: What is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmikastejodhātuḥ katamaḥ | yadadhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ tejastejogatamūṣmā ūṣmāgatamupagatamupādattaṃ | tadyathā yadasminkāye tejo yenāyaṃ kāya ātapyate | saṃtapyate, paritapyate | yena cāśitapītakhāditāsvāditaṃ samyaksukhena paripākaṃ gacchati | yasya cotsadatvāt jārito jārita iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the internal fire element? Whatever is internal and personal — heat, of the nature of heat, warmth, pertaining to warmth, taken up [as personal] — namely: whatever heat in this body by which this body is heated, burned, scorched; by which what has been eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is properly digested; and by the increase of which one is reckoned as 'feverish' —

body.text: bāhyastejodhātuḥ katamaḥ | yadbāhyaṃ tejastejogatamūṣmā(ṣma)gatamanu(mu)pagatamanu(mu)pādattaṃ | (

children.text: ) tatpunaryanmanuṣyā araṇīsahagatakebhyo gomayacūrṇebhyaḥ samanveṣate (nte) | yattūtpannaṃ grāmamapi dahati | grāmapradeśamapi | nagaramvā, nagarapradeśamvā, janapadamvā, janapadapradeśamvā, dvīpamvā, kakṣamvā, dāvamvā, kāṣṭhamvā, tṛṇamvā, gomayamvādahan paraiti | iti yo vā punaranyopyevaṃbhāgīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) Furthermore, that which humans seek from cow-dung powder mixed with fire-sticks — yet once arisen, it burns a village, a part of a village, a town, a part of a town, a country, a part of a country, an island, a thicket, a forest, wood, grass, or cow-dung — burning, it moves on. And whatever else is of such a nature [belongs to the fire element].

body.translated_text: What is the external fire element? Whatever is external — heat, of the nature of heat, pertaining to warmth, not taken up [as personal].

body.text: tatra vāyudhātuḥ katamaḥ | vāyudhāturdvividhaḥ | ādhyātmiko bāhyaśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>vāyudhātu</s> (wind element)? The wind element is twofold: internal and external.

body.text: tatrādhyātmiko vāyudhātuḥ | yadapyadhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ vāyurvāyugataṃ | laghutvaṃ samudīraṇatvamupagatamupādattaṃ | sa punaḥ santyasmin kāye ūrdhvaṃgamā vāyavaḥ, adhogamā vāyavaḥ, pārśvaśayā vāyavaḥ | kukṣiśayā vāyavaḥ | pṛṣti(ṣṭhi)śayā vāyavaḥ | vāyvaṣṭhīlā(vātāṣṭhīlā) vāyavaḥ | kṣurakapippalakaśastrakā vāyavaḥ | āśvāsapraśvāsā vāyavaḥ | aṃgapratyaṃ[gānusāriṇovāyavaḥ]
body.translated_text: Therein, the internal wind element is whatever wind or wind-natured thing within oneself, personally — lightness and agitation that is appropriated and clung to. Furthermore, in this body there are upward-moving winds, downward-moving winds, winds dwelling in the sides, winds dwelling in the abdomen, winds dwelling in the spine, winds like hard lumps (<s>vātāṣṭhīlā</s>), winds like razors, peppercorns, and knives, inhalation and exhalation winds, and winds coursing through the major and minor limbs.

body.text: bāhyo vāyudhātuḥ katamaḥ | yadbāhyaṃ vāyurvāyugataṃ laghutvaṃ, samadīraṇatvaṃ | anu(u)pagatamanu(mu)pādattaṃ [|] santi bahirdhā pūrvā vāyavo, dakṣiṇā vāyavaḥ | uttarā vāyavaḥ paścimā vāyavaḥ | sarajaso vāyavaḥ, arajaso vāyavaḥ, [parīttā] mahadgatā vāyavaḥ, viśvā vāyavo, vairambhā vāyavaḥ vāyumaṇḍalakavāyavaḥ [|] bhavati ca samayaḥ yanmahān vāyuskandhaḥ samudāgataḥ vṛkṣāgrānapi pātayati | kuḍyāgrānapi pātayati | parvatāgrānapi pātayati | pātayitvā nirupādāno niga(nirga)cchati | ye sattvāścīvarakarṇikena vā paryeṣante, tālavṛntena vā, vidhamanakena vā | iti vāyuranyopyevaṃbhāgīya[ḥ ||]
body.translated_text: What is the external wind element? Whatever external wind or wind-natured thing — lightness and agitation — that is not appropriated and not clung to. Externally there are eastern winds, southern winds, northern winds, western winds, dusty winds, dustless winds, small and great winds, universal winds, whirlwind-winds, and circular wind-currents. And there comes a time when a great mass of wind arises that topples the tops of trees, topples the tops of walls, topples the tops of mountains — and having toppled them, it passes on without support. And those beings who seek [wind] with a corner of a robe, a palm-leaf fan, or a bellows — that wind too, and whatever else is of such a nature [belongs to the wind element].

body.text: ākāśadhātuḥ katamaḥ | yaccakṣuḥ sauṣiryamvā, (

children.text: ) śrotrasauṣiryamvā, ghrāṇasauṣiryamvā, mukhasauṣiryamvā, kaṇṭhasauṣiryamvā | iti yena cābhyavaharati | yatra vābhyavaharati | yena vābhyavahriyate | yadadhobhāgena pragharati | iti yo vā puranarapyopyevaṃbhāgīyaḥ [?] ayaṃ ucyate ākāśadhātuḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) the cavity of the ear, the cavity of the nose, the cavity of the mouth, the cavity of the throat — and that by which one swallows, that where one swallows, that by which [food] is carried down, and that through which it passes out below — and whatever else is of such a nature — this is called the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space element).

body.translated_text: What is the <s>ākāśadhātu</s> (space element)? Whatever is the cavity of the eye, (

body.text: vijñānadhātuḥ katamaḥ [|] yaccakṣurvijñānaṃ śrotraghrāṇajihvākāyamanovijñānaṃ | tat punaścittaṃ manovijñānaṃ ca | ayamucyate vijñānadhātuḥ ||
body.translated_text: What is the <s>vijñānadhātu</s> (consciousness element)? Whatever is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. That, furthermore, is <s>citta</s> (mind) and <s>manovijñāna</s> (mental consciousness). This is called the <s>vijñānadhātu</s> (consciousness element).

body.text: tatra mānacaritaḥ pudgala imaṃ dhātuprabhedaṃ manasi kurvan kāye piṇḍasaṃjñāṃ vibhāvayati | aśubhasaṃjñāṃ ca pratilabhate | na ca punastenonnatiṃ gacchati | mānaṃ pratanu karoti | tasmāccaritāccittaṃ viśodhayati | ayamucyate dhātuprabhedaḥ | mānacaritasya pudgalasya caritaviśodhanamālambanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, a person of proud temperament (<s>mānacarita</s>), by attending to this analysis of elements, dispels the perception of a compact [self] regarding the body, and obtains the perception of unattractiveness. And thereby he does not become conceited; he diminishes his pride. Thus his mind is turned away from that temperament.

body.text: tatrānāpānasmṛtiḥ katamā | āśvāsapraśvāsālambanā smṛtiriyamucyate ānāpānasmṛti[ḥ] |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing)? Mindfulness with inhalation and exhalation as its object — this is called <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing).

body.text:
tatra dvāvāśvāsau katamau |
dvavau āśvāso 'ntarāśvāsaśca |
dvau praśvāsau katamau |
dvau praśvāsontarapraśvāsaśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the two [types of] inhalations? The two are: inhalation and intermediate inhalation. What are the two [types of] exhalations? The two are: exhalation and intermediate exhalation.

body.text: tatra śvāsaḥ yaḥ praśvāsasamanantaraṃ antarmukho vāyuḥ pravarttate | yāvannābhīpradeśāt |
body.translated_text: Therein, the inhalation is the inward-moving wind that occurs immediately after the exhalation, extending down to the region of the navel.

body.text: tatrāntarāśvāso ya uparatesminnāśvāse na tāvatpraśvāsa utpadyate | yadantarālaviśrāmasthānasahagata itvarakālīnastadanusadṛśo vāyurutpadyate | ayamucyatentarāśvāsaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the intermediate inhalation is: when the inhalation has ceased, before the exhalation has yet arisen, that momentary and brief wind of a similar nature that arises in the interval of rest — this is called the intermediate inhalation.

body.text: yathāśvāso 'ntarāśvāsaścaivaṃ praśvāsontara(ntaḥ)praśvāsaśca veditavyaḥ | tatrāyaṃ, viśeṣaḥ | bahirmukho vāyuḥ pravartate bahi[ḥ] nābhīdeśamupādāya | yāvanmukhāgrānnāsikāgrā[t]tato vā punarbahiḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as the inhalation and intermediate inhalation, so too the exhalation and intermediate exhalation should be understood. Therein, the distinction is: the outward-moving wind proceeds from the region of the navel outward, up to the tip of the mouth and the tip of the nose, and from there further outward.

body.text: dvāvāśvāsapraśvāsanidānau [|] katamau dvau | tadākṣe pakaṃ ca karma, nābhīpradeśasauṣiryaṃ ca | tato vā (

children.text: ) puna[rutpannaṃ]yatkāyasauṣiryaṃ [|] dvāvāśvāsapraśvāsayoḥ saṃniśrayau katamau | dvau kāyaścittaṃ ca | tatkasya hetoḥ [|] kāyasaṃnni(sanni)śritāścittasaṃnni(sanni)śritāścāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ pravartante | te ca yathāyogaṃ sa cetkāyasaṃnniśritā [eva] pravarteran | asaṃjñisamāpannānāṃ, nirodhasamāpannānāṃ asaṃjñisattveṣu deveṣūpapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ pravarteran | sa ceccittasanniśritā eva pravartteran | tenārūpyasamāpannopapannānāṃ sattvānāṃ pravarteran | sa cetkāyasanniśritāścittasanniśritāḥ pravarteran | te ca na yathāyogaṃ tena caturthadhyānasamāpannopapannānāṃ, kalalagatānāñcārbudagatānāṃ, peśīgatānāṃ sattvānāṃ pravarteran | na ca pravarttate (tante) | tasmādāśvāsapraśvāsātkāyasanniśritāści (tasmādāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ kāyasanniśritāści)ttasanniśritāśva pravarttante tena yathāyogaṃ |
children.translated_text: ) that which arises as cavities within the body. What are the two supports of inhalation and exhalation? The two are: the body and the mind. Why? Because inhalations and exhalations proceed dependent on the body and dependent on the mind.

body.translated_text: What are the two causes of inhalation and exhalation? The two are: the action associated with that [body], and the cavity in the region of the navel. Or alternatively, (

body.text: dve āśvāsapraśvāsayorgatī [|] katame dve | āśvāsayoradhogatiḥ | praśvāsayorūrdhvagatiḥ |
body.translated_text: What are the two courses of inhalation and exhalation? The two are: the downward course of inhalations, and the upward course of exhalations.

body.text: dve āśvāsapraśvāsayorbhūmī | katame dve | audārikaṃ ca sauṣiryaṃ, sūkṣmaṃ ca (|) sauṣiryaṃ | tatraudārikaṃ sauṣiryaṃ nābhīpradeśamupādāya | yāvanmukhanāsikādvāraṃ | mukhanāsikādvāramupādāya (

children.translated_text: ) down to the cavity in the region of the navel. What is the subtle cavity? All the pores of the body throughout.

body.translated_text: What are the two grounds of inhalation and exhalation? The two are: the coarse cavity and the subtle cavity. Therein, the coarse cavity extends from the region of the navel up to the opening of the mouth and nose; and from the opening of the mouth and nose (

body.text: catvāryāśvāsapraśvāsānāṃ paryāyanāmāni [|] katamāni catvāri | vāyava[ḥ], ānāpānāḥ, āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ | kāyasaṃskārāśceti | tatrānyairvāyubhiḥ sādhāraṇaṃ paryāyanāmaikaṃ | yaduta vāyuriti | asādhāraṇāni tadanyāni trīṇi |
body.translated_text: What are the four synonyms for inhalation and exhalation? The four are: 'winds' (<s>vāyavaḥ</s>), 'breathings' (<s>ānāpānāḥ</s>), 'inhalation-exhalation' (<s>āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ</s>), and 'bodily formations' (<s>kāyasaṃskārāḥ</s>). Therein, one synonym is shared in common with other winds, namely 'wind.' The others are not shared.

body.text: dvāvapakṣālāvāśvāpraśvāsaprayuktasya [|] katamau dvau | aśithilaprayogatā ca, satyābhyavaṣṭabdhaprayogatāca | tatrāśithilaprayogatayā kausīdyaprāptasya styānamiddhamvā cittaṃ paryavanaha (hya)ti, bahirdhā vā vikṣipyate | tathābhyavaṣṭabdhaprayuktasya kāyavaiṣamyaṃ cotpadyate | cittavaiṣamyamvā | kathaṃ kāyavaiṣamyamutpadyate | balābhinigraheṇānāśvāsapraśvāsānabhiniṣpīḍayataḥ kāye viṣamā vāyavaḥ pravartante | yesya tatprathamatasteṣu teṣvaṃgapratyaṅgeṣu sphuranti | ye sphārakāya (sphurakā) ityucyante | te punaḥ sphurakā vāyavo vivarddhamānā rujakā bhavanti | yepyeteṣvaṃgapratyaṃgeṣu rujamutpādayanti | idamucyate kāyavaiṣamyaṃ || kathaṃ cittavaiṣamyamutpadyate | cittamvāsya vikśipyate | prāga[sau] na vā daurmanasyopāyāsenābhibhūyate | evaṃ cittavaiṣamyamutpadyate ||
body.translated_text: What are the two faults of one engaged in inhalation and exhalation [practice]? The two are: applying too loosely and applying too tightly and tensely. Therein, through loose application, due to being overcome by sloth, <s>styānamiddha</s> (sloth and torpor) overwhelms the mind, and the [attention wanders] outward.

body.text: asyā ānāpānasmṛteḥ pañcavidhaḥ pa[ricayo] veditavyaḥ | tadyathā gaṇanāparicayaḥ, skandhāvatāraparicayaḥ | pratītyasamutpādāvatāraparicayaḥ | satyāvatāraparicayaḥ | ṣoḍaśākāraparicayaśca |
body.translated_text: The familiarization with this <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing) should be understood as fivefold, namely: familiarization through counting (<s>gaṇanā</s>), familiarization through entry into the aggregates (<s>skandhāvatāra</s>), familiarization through entry into dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>), familiarization through entry into the truths (<s>satya</s>), and familiarization through the sixteen aspects (<s>ṣoḍaśākāra</s>).

body.text: tatra gaṇanāparicayaḥ katamaḥ | samāsataścaturvidho gaṇanāparicayaḥ | tadyathā ekaikagaṇanā [|] dvayaikagaṇanā [|] anulomagaṇanā | pratilomagaṇanā ca ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is familiarization through counting? In brief, there are four types of counting: counting one by one (<s>ekaikagaṇanā</s>), counting two as one (<s>dvayaikagaṇanā</s>), forward counting (<s>anulomagaṇanā</s>), and reverse counting (<s>pratilomagaṇanā</s>).

body.text: tatraikaikagaṇanā katamā |yadā āśvāsaḥ praviṣṭo bhavati | tadā āśvāsa praśvāsopanibaddhayā smṛtyā ekamiti gaṇayati | yadā āśvāse niruddhe praśvāsa utpadya nirgato bhavati | tadā dvitīyaṃ gaṇayatyevaṃ yāvaddaśa gaṇayati | eṣā hi gaṇanā saṃkhyā nātisaṃkṣiptā nātivistarā iyamucyate ekaikagaṇanā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is counting one by one? When the inhalation has entered, then with mindfulness bound to the inhalation and exhalation, one counts 'one.' When the inhalation has ceased and the exhalation has arisen and gone out, then one counts the second. Thus,

body.text: dvayaikagaṇanā katamā | yadā āśvāsaḥ praviṣṭo bhavati, niruddhaśca | praśvāsa utpanno bhavati | nirgataśca tadā ekamiti gaṇayati | anena gaṇanāyogena yāvaddaśa gaṇayati | iyamucyate | dvayaikagaṇanā | āśvāsaṃ ca praśvāsaṃ cedaṃ dvayamekatyamabhisaṃkṣipyaikamiti gaṇayati tenocyate dvayaikagaṇanā ||
body.translated_text: What is counting two as one? When the inhalation has entered and has ceased, and the exhalation has arisen and gone out, then one counts 'one.' By this method of counting, one counts up to ten. This is called 'counting two as one.'

body.text: anulomagaṇanā katamā | anayaivaikaikagaṇanayā, dvayaikagaṇanayā vā, anulomaṃ yāvaddaśa gaṇayati | (
body.translated_text: What is forward counting? By this same one-by-one counting, or by the two-as-one counting, one counts forward up to ten. (

body.text: pratilomagaṇanā katamā | pratilomaṃ daśa upādāya, navāṣṭau, sapta, ṣaṭ, paṃca, yāvadekaṃ gaṇayati | iyamucyate pratilomagaṇanā |
body.translated_text: What is reverse counting? Counting in reverse, starting from ten: nine, eight, seven, six, five, down to one. This is called 'reverse counting.'

body.text: yadā sa ekaikagaṇanāṃ niśritya, dvayaikagaṇanāmvā, anulomagaṇanāyāṃ, pratilomagaṇanāyāṃ ca kṛtaparicayo bhavati | na cāsyāntarāccittaṃ vikṣipyate [|] avikṣiptacittaśca gaṇayati | tadāsyottaragaṇanāviśeṣo vyapadiśyate |
body.translated_text: When one, relying on one-by-one counting or two-as-one counting, has become practiced in forward counting and reverse counting, and one's mind is not scattered in between, and one counts with an unscattered mind — then a further refinement of counting [is taught].

body.text: katamo gaṇanāviśeṣaḥ | ekaikagaṇanayā vā, dvayaikagaṇanayā vā, dvayamekaṃ kṛtvā gaṇayati | tatra dvayaikagaṇanayā catvāra āśvāsapraśvāsā ekaṃ bhavati | ekaikagaṇanayā punarāśvāsapraśvāsaścaikaṃ bhavatyevaṃ yāvaddaśa gaṇayati | evamuttarottara vṛddhyā yāvacchatamapyekaṃ kṛtvā gaṇayati | tadā śataikagaṇanayānupūrveṇa yāvaddaśa gaṇayati | evamasya gaṇanāprayuktasya yāvaddaśaikaṃ kṛtvā gaṇayati | yāvacca daśa paripūrayati | tayā daśaikagaṇanayā na cāsyottarāccittamvikṣipyate | iyatā tena gaṇanāparicayaḥ kṛto bhavati |
body.translated_text: What is the refinement of counting? By one-by-one counting or by two-as-one counting, one counts two as one. Therein, by two-as-one counting, four inhalations and exhalations become one [count]; by one-by-one counting, one inhalation and one exhalation become one [count].

body.text: tasya ca gaṇanāprayuktasya sa cedantarāccittaṃ vikṣipyate tadā punaḥ pratinivartyādito gaṇayitumārabhate | anulomamvā, pratilomamvā [|] yadā cāsya gadhayāccittaṃ svarasenaiva bāhimārga(svarasavāhimārgeṇaiva) (

children.text: ) samārūḍhamāśvāsapraśvāsālambanopanibaddhamavyavacchinnaṃ nirantaraṃ, pravarttamāse āśvāsa(se) pravṛttigrāhakaṃ, niruddhe āśvāse praśvāsaśūnyāvasthāgrāhakaṃ, pravṛtte praśvāse pravṛttigrāhakaṃ, nivṛtte punarnivṛttigrāhakaṃ, avikaṃpyamavicalamavikṣepākāraṃ, sābhirāmaṃ ca pravarttate | iyatā gaṇanābhūmisamatikramo bhavati |
children.translated_text: ) has ascended to being bound to the object of inhalation and exhalation, and proceeds uninterruptedly and continuously — grasping the occurrence when inhalation occurs, grasping the state of emptiness [between breaths] when inhalation has ceased, grasping the occurrence when exhalation occurs, and [grasping] when exhalation has ceased —

body.translated_text: If, while engaged in counting, one's mind becomes scattered in between, then one turns back again and begins counting from the beginning — whether forward or reverse. And when one's mind, through sustained effort and by its own momentum, following the external path,

body.text: punastadā gaṇayitavyaṃ bhavati | nānyatrāśvāsapraśvāsālambanaṃ cittamupanibadhyate | āśvāsapraśvāsā anugantavyāścā[bhilakṣa]yitavyāśca sāntarāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ sapravṛttinivṛttyavasthāḥ ayamucyate gaṇanāparicayaḥ |
body.translated_text: then there is no longer any need to count. The mind is not bound to any object other than inhalation and exhalation. The inhalations and exhalations should be followed and observed — together with the intermediate inhalations and exhalations, together with the states of occurrence and cessation. This is called the familiarization through counting.

body.text: sa khalveṣa gaṇanāparicayo mṛdvindriyāṇāṃ vyapadiśyate | teṣāmetad vyākṣepasthānaṃ bhavati | cittasthitaye cittanirataye [|] anyathā gaṇanāmantareṇa teṣāṃ styānamiddhamvā cittaṃ paryavahet, bahirdhā vā cittaṃ vikṣipyeta, gaṇanāprayuktena tu teṣāmetanna bhavati |
body.translated_text: This familiarization through counting is taught for those of soft faculties. For them, this is the basis of distraction; [counting serves] for the stability and engagement of the mind. Otherwise, without counting, <s>styānamiddha</s> (sloth and torpor) would overwhelm their minds, or [attention would wander] outward.

body.text: ye tu tīkṣṇendriyāḥ paṭubuddhayaḥ teṣāṃ punargaṇanāprayogeṇa priyārohatā bhavati | tatropadiṣṭā evaṃ gaṇanāprayogaṃ laghu laghveva pratividhyanti | na ca tenābhiramante [|] te punarāśvāsapraśvāsālambanāṃ smṛtimupanibadhya yatra ca pravarttante, yāvacca pravarttante | yathā ca pravarttante, (

children.text: ) yadā ca pravarttante | tatsarvamanupracchatyupalakṣayatyupasthitayā smṛtyā [|] ayamevaṃ rūpasteṣāṃ prayogaḥ |
children.translated_text: and when it operates. All of this one inquires into and observes with established mindfulness. This is the practice that is of such a nature for them.

body.translated_text: But those who are of sharp faculties and keen intelligence — for them, the practice of counting becomes tedious. Being thus instructed, they penetrate the counting practice lightly and swiftly, but do not delight in it. Rather, they bind their mindfulness to the object of inhalation and exhalation — where it operates, how long it operates, in what manner it operates,

body.text: tasya ca prayogasyāsevanānvayādbhāvanānvayād bahulīkārānvayātkāyapraśrabdhirutpadyate, cittapraśrabdhiśca | ekāgratāṃ ca spṛśatyālambanābhiratiṃ ca nirgacchati | ya evaṃ kṛtaparicayo grāhyagrāhakavastumanasikāreṇa skandhānavatarati | ye cāśvāsapraśvāsā yaścaiṣāmāśrayakāyastaṃ manasi kurvan rūpaskandhamavatarati | yā teṣāmāśvāsapraśvāsānāṃ tadgrāhikayā smṛtyā saṃprayuktā anubhāvanā sa vedanāskandha ityavatarati | yā saṃjānanā[sa]saṃjñāskandha ityavatarati | yā cāsau smṛtiryā ca cetanā, yā ca (|) tatra prajñā | ayaṃ saṃskāra ityuvatarati | yaccittaṃ, mano, vijñānamayaṃ vijñānaskandha ityavatarati | yā tadbahulavihāritā | evaṃ skandheṣvavatīrṇasyāyamucyate skandhāvatāraparicayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Through the cultivation, development, and repeated practice of this exercise, bodily tranquility (<s>kāyapraśrabdhi</s>) arises, and mental tranquility (<s>cittapraśrabdhi</s>) as well. One touches one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>) and attains delight in the object. One who has thus gained familiarity, through mental attention to the object that is grasped and the grasper, descends into the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates). Attending to the inhalations and exhalations and their supporting body, one descends into the <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form). The experience conjoined with the mindfulness that apprehends those inhalations and exhalations — one descends into that as the <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling). The act of perceiving — one descends into that as the <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of perception). The mindfulness itself, the volition, and the wisdom therein — one descends into these as the <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of formations). The consciousness, mind, and cognition — one descends into that as the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness). This is the frequent dwelling therein. For one who has thus descended into the aggregates, this is called 'familiarization with descent into the aggregates' (<s>skandhāvatāraparicaya</s>).

body.text: yadā cānena skandhamātraṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavati | parijñātaṃ sasaṃskāramātraṃ, vastumātraṃ, tadā sa eṣāmeva saṃskārāṇāṃ pratītyasamutpādamavatarati |
body.translated_text: When by this means one has seen merely the aggregates, has fully known merely the formations, merely the things — then one descends into the dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) of these very formations.

body.text: kathaṃ ca punaravatarati | sa evaṃ rūpamanveṣate, paryeṣate, (

children.text: ) itīye āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ kimāśritāḥ, kiṃpratyayāstasyaivaṃ bhavati | kāyāśritā ete āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ kāyapratyayācci (ści)ttāśritāścittapratyayāśca | kāyaḥ punaścittaṃ ca kiṃ pratyayaṃ ca [|] sa kāyaṃ (yaḥ) cittañca jīvitendriyapratyayamityavatarati | pūrvakaḥ saṃskāraḥ [|] sa pūrvakaṃ saṃskāramavidyāpratyayami (i)tyavatarati | iti hi avidyāpratyaya(ḥ) pūrvakaḥ saṃskāraḥ sarvasaṃskārapratyayaṃ jīvitendriyaṃ, jīvitendriyapratyayaḥ kāyo, vijñānaṃ ca, kāyacittapratyayā āśvāsapraśvāsāḥ | tatrāvidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ | saṃskāra nirodhājjīvitendriyanirodhaḥ | jīvitendriyanirodhātkāyacittanirodhaḥ [|] kāyacittanirodhādāśvāsapraśvāsanirodhaḥ | evamasau pratītyasamutpādamatavarati |
children.translated_text: 'What do these inhalations and exhalations depend upon? What is their condition?' Thus it occurs to one: 'These inhalations and exhalations depend on the body and are conditioned by the body; they depend on the mind and are conditioned by the mind.' And what is the condition of the body and mind? One descends into the understanding that the body and mind are conditioned by the life-faculty (<s>jīvitendriya</s>). The preceding formations — one descends into the understanding that the preceding formations are conditioned by ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). Thus: the preceding formations are conditioned by ignorance; the life-faculty is conditioned by all formations; the body and consciousness are conditioned by the life-faculty; and inhalations and exhalations are conditioned by body and mind. Therein, from the cessation of ignorance comes the cessation of formations; from the cessation of formations comes the cessation of the life-faculty; from the cessation of the life-faculty comes the cessation of body and mind; from the cessation of body and mind comes the cessation of inhalations and exhalations. In this way one descends into dependent origination.

body.translated_text: And how does one descend? One investigates and searches for form thus:

body.text: sa tadbahulavihārī pratītyasamutpā[dākā]re kṛtaparicaya ityucyate | ayamucyate pratītyasamutpādāvatāraparicayaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: One who dwells frequently in this manner is said to have gained familiarity with the mode of dependent origination. This is called 'familiarization with descent into dependent origination' (<s>pratītyasamutpādāvatāraparicaya</s>).

body.text: sa evaṃ pratītyasamutpāde kṛtaparicayo ya ete saṃskārāḥ pratītyasamutpannāḥ | anityā eta ityavatarati | anityatvādabhūtvā [ca prati]vigacchanti | punarete abhūtvā bhavanti | bhūtvā ca prativigacchanti | te jāti dharmāṇo, jarādharmāṇo, vyādhidharmāṇo, maraṇadharmāṇaḥ | ye jātijarāvyādhimaraṇadharmāṇaste duḥkhā, ye duḥkhāstenātmānaḥ, asvatantrāḥ, svāmivirahitāḥ [|] evaṃ so 'nityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmākārairduḥkhasatyamavatīrṇo bhavati | yā kācideṣā[ṃ] saṃskārāṇāmabhinirvṛttiḥ | duḥkhabhūtā, rogabhūtā, gaṇḍabhūtā, sarvāsau tṛṣṇāpratyayā(ḥ) | yatpunarasyā duḥkhajanikāyāstṛṣṇāyā aśeṣaprahāṇametacchāntametatpraṇītametattamevaṃ ca me jānata, evaṃ bahulavihāriṇastṛṣṇāyā aśeṣaprahāṇaṃ bhaviṣyatīti | evaṃ hi samudayasatyaṃ, nirodhasatyaṃ, mārgasatyamavatīrṇo bhavati | sa tadbahulavihārī yadā satyānyabhisamāgacchati | ayamucyate satyāvatāraparicayaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: Having thus gained familiarity with dependent origination, one descends into the understanding that these formations, which have arisen dependently, are impermanent. Because of being impermanent, they pass away having not [previously] existed; and again, not having existed, they come into being, and having come into being, they pass away. They are subject to birth, subject to aging, subject to disease, subject to death. Those that are subject to birth, aging, disease, and death are <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering); those that are suffering are without self, not autonomous, devoid of a master. Thus, through the aspects of impermanence, suffering, emptiness, and non-self, one descends into the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>). Whatever production of these formations there is — that is of the nature of suffering, of the nature of disease, of the nature of a boil — all of that is conditioned by craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>). The complete abandoning of this craving that gives rise to suffering — that is peaceful, that is sublime. 'Knowing thus, dwelling frequently thus, the complete abandoning of craving will come about for me' — in this way one descends into the truth of the origin (<s>samudayasatya</s>), the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>), and the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). One who dwells frequently in this manner, when one fully comprehends the truths — this is called 'familiarization with descent into the truths' (<s>satyāvatāraparicaya</s>).

body.text: tasyaivaṃ satyeṣu kṛtaparicayasya | darśanaprahātavyeṣu dharmeṣu prahīṇeṣu bhāvanāprahātavyā avaśiṣṭā bhavanti | yeṣāṃ prahāṇāya ṣoḍaśākāraparicayaṃ karoti |
body.translated_text: For one who has thus gained familiarity with the truths, when the qualities to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>) have been abandoned, there remain those to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>). For the abandoning of these, one undertakes the familiarization with the sixteen aspects.

children.translated_text: fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). Therefore the text says: 'Mindful, breathing in — mindful, I shall breathe in,' one trains. When one takes inhalation or exhalation as the object, then one trains: 'I shall breathe in long, I shall breathe out.' When one makes the interval between inhalation and exhalation the object, then one trains: 'I shall breathe in short, I shall breathe out.' For inhalations and exhalations operate as long; and the intervals between inhalations and exhalations operate as short — and so one likewise observes and knows them. When, with regard to the subtle inhalations and exhalations that have entered a refined and delicate state, one attends to them within the body — one makes them the object. And when the exhalation has ceased and the interval-exhalation [has ceased], and when the inhalation and interval-inhalation have not yet arisen, one makes the cool state devoid of exhalation and inhalation, free from them, interrupted by them, one's object.

body.translated_text: And if one further attains the basic first, second, and third <s>dhyānas</s> — and one necessarily attains the preliminary stage of the first <s>dhyāna</s> (the access concentration, <s>anāgamya</s>) — then relying on that, one examines one's own arisen mind: whether it is with passion or free from passion, with hatred or free from hatred, with delusion or free from delusion, contracted, sunken, excited, restless or not restless, calmed or not calmed, concentrated or not concentrated, well-cultivated or not well-cultivated, liberated or not liberated — one knows it as it truly is; one experiences it. Therefore the text says: 'Experiencing the mind.'

body.text: sa yadā styāna[middha]nivaraṇe cittaṃ niśritaṃ (|) bhavati | adhyātmaṃ saṃgamayataḥ yadānyatamānyatamena prasādanīyenālambanena saṃdarśayati | samādāpayati | samuttejayati | saṃpradīpayati | tenāha [|] abhipramodayaṃścittaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: When the mind has settled into the hindrance of sloth-and-torpor, one who is collecting it inwardly shows it, persuades it, inspires it, and illuminates it with one or another faith-inspiring object. Therefore the text says: 'Gladdening the mind.'

body.text: yadā [puna]rauddhatyanivaraṇena kaukṛtyanivaraṇena nivṛttaṃ paśyati | abhisaṃpragṛhṇata stadā anyatamamānyatamena prasādanīyenālambanena saṃdarśayatyadhyātmamavasthāpayati | śamayati, samādhatte | tenāha samadadhaccitaṃ (samādadhaṃścittaṃ) [|]
body.translated_text: When one sees that [the mind] has become distracted through the hindrance of restlessness or the hindrance of remorse, becoming overconfident — at that time, one shows it, steadies it inwardly, calms it, and concentrates it with one or another faith-inspiring object. Therefore the text says: 'Concentrating the mind.'

body.translated_text: When his mind is freed from the <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances), there remain <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies) that are obstructive to the cultivation of the path and must be abandoned. For their abandonment, he brings the path face to face — namely, he thoroughly, correctly, and methodically examines the impermanence of <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned formations). Therefore it is said: "contemplating impermanence." And whereas previously, through the support of the first, second, or third <s>dhyāna</s>, or through the support of <s>anāgamya</s> (the access concentration), he practiced <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), now he directly applies himself to <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) contemplating impermanence. Thus his mind, thoroughly cultivated by <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, is liberated in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements) — that is, from the <s>anuśayas</s> (latent tendencies).

children.translated_text: <s>virāgadhātu</s> (element of dispassion), and the <s>nirodhadhātu</s> (element of cessation). Among these, <s>prahāṇadhātu</s> is the abandonment of all <s>saṃskāras</s> that are to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>). <s>Virāgadhātu</s> is the abandonment of all <s>saṃskāras</s> that are to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>). <s>Nirodhadhātu</s> is the cessation of all <s>upadhis</s> (substrates of existence). Thus, mentally attending to these three <s>dhātus</s> as peaceful, as secure, and as healthy, he cultivates <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>. Through repeated practice, through the continuity of cultivation, and through the continuity of habituation, his mind is liberated from the remaining <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) to be abandoned by cultivation. Therefore it is said: "contemplating abandonment, contemplating dispassion, contemplating cessation — breathing in, he trains thinking 'I shall breathe in contemplating cessation.'" Thus, when the <s>kleśas</s> to be abandoned by seeing and cultivation are abandoned, he becomes an <s>Arhat</s> (worthy one), one whose <s>āsravas</s> (outflows) are destroyed; there is nothing further to be done by him, or it is the familiarization with what has been done. This is called his sixteen-aspect familiarization. And this fivefold familiarization — this is called his <s>ānāpānasmṛti</s> (mindfulness of breathing). Therein, a person of discursive temperament (<s>vitarkacarita</s>), when applying himself, applies himself with delight. This object of meditation involves active engagement; it involves casting attention inward, upon oneself,

body.translated_text: Now, what is the <s>kauśalyālambana</s> (skillfulness-object)? It is as follows: skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates), skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (elements), skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases), skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), and skill in <s>sthānāsthāna</s> (places and non-places). Therein, what are the <s>skandhas</s>, and what is skill in the <s>skandhas</s>? It is said: there are five <s>skandhas</s> — <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form), <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling), <s>saṃjñāskandha</s> (aggregate of perception), <s>saṃskāraskandha</s> (aggregate of volitional formations), and <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness).

body.translated_text: What is skill in the <s>skandhas</s> (<s>skandhakauśalya</s>)? children.translated_text: the <s>vedanāskandha</s> (aggregate of feeling) is another, and so on up to the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness) being yet another. This is the manifold nature (<s>nānātmakatā</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the manifold nature (<s>nānātmakatā</s>) of the <s>skandhas</s>? The <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form) is one thing,

body.text: tatra katamā bahvātmakatā | yo rūpaskandho nekavidho nānāprakāraḥ | bhūtalaukikabhedenānāgatapratyutpannādikena ca | prakārabhedena [|] iyamucyate anekātmakatā | rūpaskandhasyaivamavaśiṣṭānāṃ skandhānāṃ yathāyogaṃ veditavyam | kiṃ ca na tasmātparaṃ upalabhate, vikalpayati | skandhamātramupalabhate | vastumātraṃ no tu skandhavyatirekeṇāhvā(tmā)namupalabhate | nityadhruvamavipariṇāmadharmakaṃ, nāpyātmīyaṃ kiṃcididaṃ nopalabhate | no vikalpayati tasmātpareṇa |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the multiplicity (<s>bahvātmakatā</s>)? The <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form) is not of a single kind but of many varieties — by the distinction of <s>bhūtas</s> (elements) and worldly [types], and by the distinction of modes such as past, future, present, and so forth. This is called the multiplicity (<s>anekātmakatā</s>) of the <s>rūpaskandha</s>. The same should be understood for the remaining <s>skandhas</s> as appropriate. Furthermore, what does one not apprehend or conceptualize beyond that? One apprehends only the aggregate, only the entity — but one does not apprehend a self (<s>ātman</s>) apart from the <s>skandhas</s>, nor anything permanent, stable, or not subject to change, nor does one apprehend or conceptualize anything as belonging to a self (<s>ātmīya</s>) beyond that.

body.text: tatra katame dhātavaḥ | katamaddhātukauśalyaṃ | āha | (

children.text: ) aṣṭādaśa dhātavaḥ | cakṣurdhātū rūpadhātuścakṣurvijñānadhātuḥ | śrotradhātuḥ | śabdadhātuḥ | śrotravijñānadhātuḥ | ghrāṇadhātuḥ | gandhadhātuḥ | ghrāṇavijñānadhātuḥ | jihvadhātūrasadhātuḥ | jihvavijñānadhātuḥ | kāyadhātuḥ, spraṣṭavyadhātuḥ, kāyavijñānadhāturdharmadhāturmano vijñānadhāturimaucyante dhātavaḥ | yatpunaretānaṣṭādaśadharmānsvakasvakāddhātoḥ svakasvakādvījāt | svakasvakādgotrājjāyante nirvartante prādurbhavantīti | jānāti rocayatyupanidhyāti | idamucyate dhātukauśalyaṃ || yadaṣṭādaśānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ svarusvakāddhātoḥ pravṛttiṃ jānāti | tadevameti hetupratyakauśalyametadyaduta dhātukauśalyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: There are eighteen <s>dhātus</s> (elements): <s>cakṣurdhātu</s> (eye-element), <s>rūpadhātu</s> (form-element), <s>cakṣurvijñānadhātu</s> (eye-consciousness-element); <s>śrotradhātu</s> (ear-element), <s>śabdadhātu</s> (sound-element), <s>śrotravijñānadhātu</s> (ear-consciousness-element); <s>ghrāṇadhātu</s> (nose-element), <s>gandhadhātu</s> (smell-element), <s>ghrāṇavijñānadhātu</s> (nose-consciousness-element); <s>jihvādhātu</s> (tongue-element), <s>rasadhātu</s> (taste-element), <s>jihvāvijñānadhātu</s> (tongue-consciousness-element); <s>kāyadhātu</s> (body-element), <s>spraṣṭavyadhātu</s> (tangible-element), <s>kāyavijñānadhātu</s> (body-consciousness-element); <s>dharmadhātu</s> (mental-object-element), <s>manovijñānadhātu</s> (mind-consciousness-element). These are called the <s>dhātus</s>. Furthermore, knowing, approving, and reflecting that these eighteen <s>dharmas</s> arise, come into being, and manifest from their own respective <s>dhātu</s> (element), from their own respective seed (<s>bīja</s>), from their own respective lineage (<s>gotra</s>) — this is called skill in the <s>dhātus</s>. That one knows the arising of the eighteen <s>dharmas</s> from their own respective <s>dhātu</s> — this is skill in causes and conditions (<s>hetupratyayakauśalya</s>), which is precisely skill in the <s>dhātus</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the <s>dhātus</s> (elements)? What is skill in the <s>dhātus</s> (<s>dhātukauśalya</s>)? It is said:

body.text: tatra katamānyāyatanāni | katamadāyatanakauśalyamāha | dvādaśayatanāni | cakṣurāyatanaṃ, rūpāyatanaṃ | (

children.text: ) śrotrāyatanaṃ | śabdāyatanaṃ | ghrāṇāyatanaṃ | gandhāyatanaṃ | jihvāyatanaṃ | rasāyatanaṃ | kāyāyatanaṃ | spraṣṭavyāya tanaṃ, mana āyatanaṃ, dharmāyatanaṃ ca | imānyucyante āyatanāni | katamadāyatanakauśalyaṃ | tatra cakṣuradhipatiḥ rūpāṇyālambanaṃ cakṣurvijñānasya saṃprayogasyotpattaye [|] samanantaraniruddhaṃ ca manaḥ samanantarapratyayaḥ | (
children.translated_text: <s>śrotrāyatana</s> (ear-base), <s>śabdāyatana</s> (sound-base), <s>ghrāṇāyatana</s> (nose-base), <s>gandhāyatana</s> (smell-base), <s>jihvāyatana</s> (tongue-base), <s>rasāyatana</s> (taste-base), <s>kāyāyatana</s> (body-base), <s>spraṣṭavyāyatana</s> (tangible-base), <s>mana āyatana</s> (mind-base), and <s>dharmāyatana</s> (mental-object-base). These are called the <s>āyatanas</s>. What is skill in the <s>āyatanas</s>? Therein, the eye (<s>cakṣus</s>) is the dominant condition (<s>adhipati</s>), forms (<s>rūpa</s>) are the object-condition (<s>ālambana</s>) for the arising of eye-consciousness and its associated [mental factors]. And the mind (<s>manas</s>) that has ceased immediately prior is the immediately-antecedent condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>).

children.text: ) tatra śrotramadhipatiḥ | śabda ālambanaṃ | samana[ntara]niruddhaṃ ca manaḥ samanantarapratyayaḥ | śrotravijñānasya sa saṃprayogasyotpattaye [|] evaṃ yāvanmanaḥ samanantaraṃ tajjo manasikārodhipatipratyayo dharmālambanaṃ (dharma ālambanaṃ) manovijñānasya saṃprayogasyotpattaye iti | tribhiḥ pratyayaiḥ samanantarapratyayena, ālambanapratyayenādhipatipratyayena ca | ṣaṇṇāṃ vijñānakāyānāṃ pravṛttirbhavati | sasaṃprayogānā(ṇā)miti | yadevamādhyātmikabāhyeṣvāyataneṣu pratyayakauśalyamidamucyate āyatanakauśalyam ||
children.translated_text: Therein, the ear (<s>śrotra</s>) is the dominant condition, sound (<s>śabda</s>) is the object-condition, and the mind that has ceased immediately prior is the immediately-antecedent condition — for the arising of ear-consciousness and its associated [mental factors].
