Likewise, up to: the mind (<s>manas</s>) that has immediately preceded, the mental attention (<s>manasikāra</s>) born from it being the dominant condition, <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) being the object-condition — for the arising of mind-consciousness and its associated [mental factors]. Thus, through three conditions — the immediately-antecedent condition (<s>samanantarapratyaya</s>), the object-condition (<s>ālambanapratyaya</s>), and the dominant condition (<s>adhipatipratyaya</s>) — the six classes of consciousness together with their associated [mental factors] operate. This skill in conditions (<s>pratyayakauśalya</s>) regarding the internal and external <s>āyatanas</s> is called skill in the <s>āyatanas</s>.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases)? What is skill in the <s>āyatanas</s> (<s>āyatanakauśalya</s>)? It is said: there are twelve <s>āyatanas</s> — <s>cakṣurāyatana</s> (eye-base), <s>rūpāyatana</s> (form-base),

body.text: tatra katamaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ katamaḥ (mat) (

children.text: ) pratītyasamutpādakauśalyaṃ [|] āha | avidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ, saṃskārapratyayamvijñānaṃ, vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpaṃ | vistareṇa yāvadevamasya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavatyayamucyate pratītyasamutpādaḥ | yatpurardharmā eva dharmānabhiṣpandayati(nti) dharmā eva dharmān pariṣpandayanti | saṃskārā eva dharmāṇāmāhārakāḥ tena hetusamutpannatvāt pratītyasamutpannatvātvādabhūtvā bhavanti | bhūtvā ca prativigacchanti | tasmādanityā ete saṃskārā ye punaranityāste jātidharmāṇo, jarāṃdharmāṇo, vyādhidharmāṇo, maraṇadharmāṇaḥ, śokaparidevaduḥkhādaurmanasyopāyāsadharmāṇaḥ | te jarā dharmitvādyāvadupāyāsadharmitvāt | duḥkhā, ye vā punarduḥkhā, asvatantrā, durbalāste anātmāna iti | yadebhirākāraiḥ (
children.translated_text: skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (<s>pratītyasamutpādakauśalya</s>)? It is said: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) are <s>saṃskāras</s> (volitional formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> is <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> is <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); and so on in detail, up to: thus arises this entire great mass of <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). This is called <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>. Since <s>dharmas</s> alone impel <s>dharmas</s>, <s>dharmas</s> alone set <s>dharmas</s> in motion, <s>saṃskāras</s> alone are the sustenance of <s>dharmas</s> — therefore, because they arise from causes, because they arise dependently, they come into being having not existed before, and having existed, they pass away. Therefore these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent. And whatever is impermanent is subject to birth, subject to aging, subject to illness, subject to death, subject to sorrow, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and despair. Because they are subject to aging and so on up to subject to despair, they are <s>duḥkha</s> (suffering). And whatever is suffering, lacking self-mastery, and feeble — that is <s>anātman</s> (non-self). This knowledge of impermanence, knowledge of suffering, and knowledge of non-self regarding

children.text: ) pratītyasamutpanneṣu dharmeṣu anityajñānaṃ, duḥkhajñānaṃ, nairātmyajñānaṃ | idamucyate pratītatyasamutpādakauśalyam ||
children.translated_text: dependently arisen <s>dharmas</s> through these aspects — this is called skill in <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination)? What is

body.text: sthānāsthānakauśalyaṃ punaḥ pratītyasamutpāda eva veditavyaṃ || tatrāyaṃ viśeṣaḥ [|] sthānāsthānakauśalyenā viṣamahetukatāṃ jānāti | asti kuśalākuśalānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaḥ | akuśalānāmaniṣṭa iti || yadevaṃ jñānamidamucyate sthānāsthānakauśalyaṃ || taccaitatpañcasthānakauśalyaṃ samāsataḥ svalakṣaṇakauśalyaṃ bhavati | sāmānyalakṣaṇakauśalyaṃ ca | tatra skandhakauśalyena svalakṣaṇakauśalyamākhyātaṃ | avaśiṣṭaiḥ sāmānyalakṣaṇakauśalyamidamucyate kauśalyālambanaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Skill in <s>sthānāsthāna</s> (places and non-places) should be understood as pertaining to <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination) itself. The distinction here is this: through skill in <s>sthānāsthāna</s>, one knows the non-irregular causality — that there is fruition and ripening of <s>kuśala</s> (wholesome) and <s>akuśala</s> (unwholesome) <s>karmas</s> (actions), and that the [result] of unwholesome [actions] is undesirable. Such knowledge is called skill in <s>sthānāsthāna</s>. And this fivefold skill, in brief, constitutes skill in specific characteristics (<s>svalakṣaṇakauśalya</s>) and skill in general characteristics (<s>sāmānyalakṣaṇakauśalya</s>). Among these, through skill in the <s>skandhas</s>, skill in specific characteristics is indicated. Through the remaining [four skills], skill in general characteristics [is indicated]. This is called the <s>kauśalyālambana</s> (skillfulness-object).

body.text: tatra kleśaviśodhanamālambanaṃ katamat | āha | (

children.text: ) adhobhūmīnāmaudārikatvaṃ tadyathā kāmadhātau prathamadhyānasya evaṃ yāvannaiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasya |
children.translated_text: The coarseness of the lower realms — namely, of the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) relative to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, and so on up to [the coarseness of the base of nothing whatsoever] relative to <s>Naiva-saṃjñā-nāsaṃjñāyatana</s> (the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the <s>kleśaviśodhanālambana</s> (affliction-purification object)? It is said:

body.text: tatra katamā audārikatā | audārikatā dvividhā | svabhāvodārikatā (svabhāvaudārikatā) saṃkhyaudārikatā ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is coarseness (<s>audārikatā</s>)? Coarseness is twofold: coarseness by intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaudārikatā</s>) and coarseness by enumeration (<s>saṃkhyaudārikatā</s>).

body.text: tatra svabhāvaudārikatā kāmadhātāvapi pañca skandhāḥ saṃvidyante | prathame tu dhyāne ye kāmāvacarāste sādīnavatarāśca duḥkhavihārata[rāś]ca | alpakāvasthāyitarāśca | hīnatarāḥ pratikruṣṭatarāśca [|] iyameṣāṃ svabhāvaudārikatā prathame tu dhyāne [|] tathā tena te śāntatarāḥ praṇītatarā ityucyante |
body.translated_text: Therein, coarseness by intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvaudārikatā</s>): in the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> (desire realm) too the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) are found. But compared to the first <s>dhyāna</s>, those belonging to the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> are more disadvantageous, more afflicted in their mode of abiding, more short-lived, more inferior, and more debased. This is their coarseness by intrinsic nature relative to the first <s>dhyāna</s>. Correspondingly, those [of the first <s>dhyāna</s>] are said to be more peaceful and more excellent.

body.text: tatra saṃkhyaudārikatā katamā | kāmāvacaro rūpaskandhaḥ prabhūtataraḥ parijñeyaḥ | prahātavya evaṃ yāvadvijñānaskandha iyamucyate skandhaudārikatā || evamuparimābhūmiṣu svabhāvo (vau) dārikatā saṃkhyaudārikatā ca | yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ (:) |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is coarseness by enumeration (<s>saṃkhyaudārikatā</s>)? The <s>rūpaskandha</s> (aggregate of form) belonging to the <s>Kāmadhātu</s> is more abundant, is to be fully known, and is to be abandoned — and so on up to the <s>vijñānaskandha</s> (aggregate of consciousness). This is called coarseness of the <s>skandhas</s>. Likewise, coarseness by intrinsic nature and coarseness by enumeration in the successively higher realms should be understood as appropriate.

body.text: iyaṃ tūparimāsu bhūmiṣu yāvadākiṃcanyāyatanā[t]tadaudārikata[rā]śca veditavyāḥ sarvā adharimā bhūmayaḥ | duḥkhavihārata[rā]śca alpāyuṣkatarāśca, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanaṃ punaḥ śāntameva upari śreṣṭhatayā bhūmerabhāvāt | yatra samāsata ādīnavārthaḥ | audārikatārthaḥ | yasyāṃ yasyāṃ bhūmau prabhūtataramā(ā)dīnavaṃ(vo) (

children.text: ) bhavati | sā ādīnavataḥ | audāriketyucyate | yasyāṃ laukikānāṃ bhūmāvalpatara mā(ā)dīnavaṃ(vo) bhavati | sā ādīnavataḥ śāntetyucyate | idaṃ laukikānāṃ laukikena mārgeṇa kleśaviśodhanamālambanaṃ tathāpi tasyādharimāṃ bhūmimādīnavataḥ paśyataḥ | rogataḥ, ayogakṣemataḥ, uparimāṃca bhūmiṃ śāntataḥ [|] ye adhobhūmikāḥ kleśā yāvadākiṃcanyāyatanabhūmikāḥ, kāmadhātumupādāya te prahīyante | na tvatyantataḥ prahīyante | te punareva te pratisandhikā bhavanti |
children.translated_text: that ground is called 'coarse' from the standpoint of danger. And whatever worldly ground has less danger, that is called 'calm' from the standpoint of danger. This is the object for the purification of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) by worldly beings through the worldly path. Accordingly, one who sees the lower ground as dangerous — as a disease, as insecurity — and sees the higher ground as calm, abandons the afflictions of the lower grounds, from the desire realm up to those of the sphere of nothingness. But one does not abandon them ultimately. Those very [afflictions] become again the causes of rebirth (<s>pratisandhi</s>).

body.translated_text: This [meditation object], however, pertains to the higher grounds up to the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiṃcanyāyatana</s>). And all the lower grounds should be understood as coarser, involving more suffering, and shorter-lived. The sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), however, is calm, since there is no higher ground of superior status. Wherever, in summary, is the meaning of 'danger' — wherever, in a given ground, there is more abundant danger,

body.text: lokottareṇa vā punarmārgeṇa kleśaviśodhanamālambanaṃ caturvidhaṃ, tadyathā | duḥkhasatyaṃ, samudayasatyaṃ, nirodhasatyaṃ, mārgasatyañca ||
body.translated_text: Or again, the object for purification of afflictions by the supramundane path is of four kinds, namely: the truth of suffering (<s>duḥkhasatya</s>), the truth of the origin (<s>samudayasatya</s>), the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>), and the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>).

body.text: tatra duḥkhasatyaṃ katamat | tadyathā jātirduḥkhaṃ jarāpi [duḥkhaṃ] vyādhirmaraṇamapriyasaṃyogaḥ priyavinābhāva icchāvighātaśca | saṃkṣepataḥ pañcopādānaskandhā duḥkhaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the truth of suffering? Namely: birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness, death, association with the unpleasant, separation from the pleasant, and frustration of wishes [are suffering]. In brief, the five aggregates of clinging (<s>pañcopādānaskandhas</s>) are suffering.

body.text: tatra samudaya āryasatyaṃ tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā tatra tatrābhinandinī ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the noble truth of the origin is <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, finding delight here and there.

body.text: tatra niro[dha ā]ryasatyaṃ yadasyā eva tṛṣṇāyā aśeṣaprahāṇaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the noble truth of cessation is the complete abandonment of that very <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) without remainder.

body.text: mārgasatyaṃ āryāṣṭāṃgo mārgaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: The truth of the path is the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅgamārga</s>).

body.text: tatra kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ śuklapakṣaṃ copādāya hetuphalavyavasthānena catuḥsatyavyavasthānaṃ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, with reference to the dark side and the bright side, the establishment of the Four Truths is through the establishment of cause and effect.

body.text: tatra duḥkhasatyaṃ phalaṃ | samudayasatyaṃ hetuḥ | nirodhasatyaṃ phalaṃ | mārgasatyaṃ hetuḥ prāptaye, sparśanāyai | tatra duḥkhasatyaṃ vyādhisthānīyaṃ tatprathamataḥ parijñeyaṃ | samudayasatyaṃ vyādhinidānasthānīyaṃ | taccāntaramparivarjayitavyaṃ | nirodhasatyamārogyasthānīyaṃ | tacca sparśayitavyaṃ (spraṣṭavyam), sākṣātkartavyaṃ | mārgasatyaṃ bhaiṣajyasthānīyaṃ | taccāsevitavyaṃ, bhāvayitavyaṃ | bahulīkartavyaṃ | bhūtaṃ caitattathā avitathā (-thama)viparītamaviparyastaṃ (

children.text: ) duḥkhaṃ duḥkhārthena, yāvanmārgo mārgārthena tasmātsatyamityucyate | svalakṣaṇaṃ ca [na] visamvadati | taddarśanāccāviparītā buddhayaḥ pravarttante | tena satyamityucyate [|]
children.translated_text: suffering in the sense of suffering, and so on up to the path in the sense of the path — therefore it is called 'truth.' It does not contradict its own characteristic. And from seeing it, unerring cognitions arise. Therefore it is called 'truth.'

body.translated_text: Therein, the truth of suffering is the effect; the truth of the origin is the cause; the truth of cessation is the effect; the truth of the path is the cause — for attainment, for realization. Therein, the truth of suffering is analogous to a disease — it should be fully known first. The truth of the origin is analogous to the cause of the disease — it should be abandoned in the meantime. The truth of cessation is analogous to health — it should be realized, made directly known. The truth of the path is analogous to medicine — it should be practiced, cultivated, and made much of. And this is true, real, not false, not mistaken, not distorted:

body.text: kasmātpunaretānyāryāṇāmeva satyāni bhavanti | āryā etāni paśyantyeva samānāni, satyatā (to) jānanti paśyanti (|) yathābhūtaṃ, bālāstu na jānanti, na paśyanti | yathābhūtaṃ tasmādāryasatyānītyucyante | bālānāmetaddharmatayā satyaṃ nāvabodheta (budhyate) | āryāṇāṃ tūbhayathā tatra jānāti (jñāyate) |
body.translated_text: Why, moreover, are these truths only of the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>)? The noble ones see these as they truly are, know them as truths, and perceive them as they really are. But fools neither know nor see them as they really are. Therefore they are called 'noble truths.' For fools, the truth of this reality is not understood. But for the noble ones, it is known in both ways.

body.text: duḥkhamiti jāyamānasya duḥkhā vedanotpadyeta (|) kāyika caitasikī, na tu ja[ā]tireva duḥkhaṃ, duḥkhanidānaṃ sā, evaṃ yāvadicchāvighāto duḥkhamiti ||
body.translated_text: As for 'suffering' — when one is born, painful feeling arises, both bodily and mental. But birth itself is not suffering; it is the cause of suffering. Likewise, up to frustration of wishes is suffering.

body.text: icchāvighātanidānaṃ duḥkhamutpadyeta | kāyikacaitasikaṃ, na tvicchāvighāta eva (|) duḥkhaṃ, duḥkhanidānaṃ punaḥ sa iti peyālam | saṃkṣepataḥ paṃcopādānaskandhāḥ duḥkhamityebhirjātyādibhiḥ paryāyai[ḥ] | duḥkhaduḥkhataiva paridīpitā | tatra vipaṇāmaduḥkhatā saṃskāraduḥkhatā cāvaśiṣṭā | sā punaḥ pañcaskandhaduḥkhatayā paridīpitā bhavati | tathā hi paṃcopādānaskandhāstrivedanāparigatāste tathoktāyāḥ dukhaduḥkhatāyā bhājanabhūtā[ḥ |] yā ca noktā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā | saṃskāraduḥkhatā ca | sāpyeṣveva draṣṭavyā |
body.translated_text: From the cause of frustration of wishes, painful feeling arises, both bodily and mental. But frustration of wishes itself is not suffering; rather, it is the cause of suffering — and so on in abbreviation. 'In brief, the five aggregates of clinging are suffering' — by these synonyms beginning with birth, only the <s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of suffering) has been illuminated. Therein, the <s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of change) and <s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of conditioned existence) remain. These are illuminated by the suffering of the five aggregates. For the five aggregates of clinging, pervaded by three kinds of feeling, are the vessel for the stated suffering of suffering, and the unstated suffering of change and suffering of conditioned existence should also be seen within them.

body.text: kena punaḥ kāraṇena bhagavatā duḥkhaduḥkhataiva parikīrttitā | svaśabdena vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā, saṃskāraduḥkhatā punaḥ paryāyeṇa [|] tathā hi duḥkhaduḥkhatāyā (

children.text: ) māryāṇāṃ bālānāñca tulyā duḥkhatābuddhiḥ pravarttate | saṃvejikātyarthaṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatā pūrvamakṛtaprajñānāmevaṃ ca deśyamāne sukhamavatāro bhavati | satyeṣu vineyānāṃ [|]
children.translated_text: both the noble ones and fools have an equal cognition of suffering. The suffering of suffering [is stated first] for the sake of great urgency (<s>saṃvega</s>), for those who have not previously cultivated wisdom, and when taught in this way, there is an easy entry into the truths for those to be trained.

body.translated_text: For what reason, moreover, has the Blessed One proclaimed only the suffering of suffering by its own term, while the suffering of change and the suffering of conditioned existence [are proclaimed] by synonym? For with regard to the suffering of suffering,

body.text: tatra trividhāyā duḥkhatāyāḥ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati | yattāvadduḥkhaṃ jātirduḥkhaṃ yāvadicchāvighāto duḥkhamityanena sādhiṣṭhānā duḥkhā vedanā ākhyātā || sā ca duḥkhaduḥkhatā [|] idaṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatāyā vyavasthānaṃ | ye vā punaretadvipakṣā dharmāstathā yauvanaṃ jarāyā, vyādherārogyaṃ, jīvitaṃ maraṇasya, priyasaṃprayogo 'priyasaṃprayogasya | apriyavinābhāvaḥ priyavinābhāvasya, icchāsampattiricchāvighātasya, ye ca duḥkhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ pravṛttāḥ kleśāḥ sādhiṣṭhānā, ye cārogyādiṣu sukhasthānīyeṣu dharmeṣu tannirjātāyāṃ ca vedanāyāṃ ye pravṛttāḥ kleśā iyamucyate vipariṇāma duḥkhatā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, how is the establishment of the threefold suffering? First, as for 'birth is suffering,' up to 'frustration of wishes is suffering' — by this, painful feeling with its basis has been declared. And that is the <s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s> (suffering of suffering). This is the establishment of the suffering of suffering. Furthermore, the opposites of these states — youth as opposed to aging, health to sickness, life to death, association with the pleasant as opposed to association with the unpleasant, non-separation from the pleasant as opposed to separation from the pleasant, fulfillment of wishes as opposed to frustration of wishes — and whatever <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) with their basis that operate in painful feeling, and whatever <s>kleśas</s> that operate in states analogous to happiness such as health and the like, and in the feeling produced by them — this is called <s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s> (the suffering of change).

body.text: tatra sukhā vedanā sādhiṣṭhānā anityatayā pa[ri]ṇamantī | atyarthībhāvādhipateyaṃ duḥkhaṃ vidadhāti | kleśāḥ punaḥ sarvatra pravṛttāḥ paryavasthānaṣa(śa) eva duḥkhā bhavanti | vipariṇāmaśca sa cetasaḥ tasmādvipariṇāmaduḥkhatetyucyate || yathoktaṃ bhagavatā- avatīrṇavipariṇatena cittena mātṛgrāmasya hastigrahaṇaṃ ceti vistaraḥ || yathā coktaṃ- kāma[c]chandaparyavasthitaḥ | kāma[c]chandaparyavasthānapratyayaṃ tajjaṃ (

children.text: ) catasikaṃ duḥkhadaurmanasyaṃ pratisaṃvedayate | evaṃ vyāpādastyānamiddhāmauddha(middhauddha)tyakaukṛtyavicikitsāparyavasthitaḥ | tadanenāgamenāptena paramāptena kleśeṣu duḥkhārtopi lambate | vipariṇāmārtho(rtto)pi | tenocyate kleśavipariṇāma [duḥkhate ti [|] idaṃ vipariṇāma]duḥkhatāyā vyavasthānaṃ | saṃskāraduḥkhatā punaḥ | sarvatragā upādānaskandheṣu saṃkṣepata āryā ca dukhaduḥkhatā, yā ca kleśasaṃgṛhītā vipariṇāmadharmatā, ye (yā) ca sādhiṣṭhānā sukhā vedanā tāṃ sthāpayitvā, ye tadanye skandhāśca duḥkhāḥ(duḥkha)sahagatāstannirjātāstadutpattipratyayā stasya cotpannasya sthitibhājanā iyamucyate saṃskāraduḥkhatā || ye skandhā anityā udayavyayayuto(tāḥ) sopādānāstrivedanābhiranuṣaktā[ḥ] | dauṣṭhulyopagatā ayogakṣemapatitā avinirmuktāḥ | duḥkhaduḥkhatāyā vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāyā asvavaśavartinaśca [|] iyamucyate saṃskāraduḥkhatayā duḥkhatā [|] idaṃ saṃskāraduḥkhatāyā vyavasthānaṃ |
children.translated_text: likewise overcome by the envelopment of ill-will, sloth-and-torpor, restlessness-and-worry, and doubt.' By this scripture, reliable and supremely reliable, the meaning of suffering applies to the <s>kleśas</s>, and the meaning of change [also applies]. Therefore it is said: 'the suffering of affliction-and-change.' This is the establishment of the suffering of change. As for the <s>saṃskāraduḥkhatā</s> (suffering of conditioned existence), it is all-pervading in the aggregates of clinging. In summary: setting aside the noble suffering of suffering, the liability to change that is included among the <s>kleśas</s>, and the pleasant feeling with its basis — whatever other aggregates there are, those that are accompanied by suffering, produced by it, that are conditions for the arising of suffering, and that serve as the vessel for the persistence of suffering once arisen — this is called the suffering of conditioned existence. Whatever aggregates are impermanent, subject to arising and passing away, with clinging, pervaded by three kinds of feeling, beset by defilement (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), fallen into insecurity, not fully liberated, and not under one's own control with respect to the suffering of suffering and the suffering of change — this is called suffering in the sense of the suffering of conditioned existence. This is the establishment of the suffering of conditioned existence.

body.translated_text: Therein, pleasant feeling with its basis, by virtue of its impermanence, undergoes change and produces suffering through the preponderance of extreme [change]. And the <s>kleśas</s> operating everywhere are painful in the very form of their envelopment. And that transformation is [a transformation] of the mind — therefore it is called the suffering of change. As the Blessed One has said: 'With a mind into which transformation has descended, the catching of women [is like] the catching of elephants' — and so on in detail. And as it is said: 'Overcome by the envelopment of sensual desire, experiencing mental suffering and distress caused by the envelopment of sensual desire —

body.text: tabha(tra)tṛṣṇā prārthanābhilāṣobhinandaneti paryāyāḥ [|] sā punaḥ prārthanā tribhirmukhaiḥ pravṛttā(s)tadyathā punarbhavaprārthanā, viṣayaprārthanā ca | (

children.text: ) tatra yā punarbhavaprārthanā mā paunarbhavikī tṛṣṇā | viṣayaprārthanā punardvividhā [|] prāpteṣu viṣayeṣu saumanasyādhyavasānasahagatā, aprāpteṣu ca viṣayeṣu saṃyogābhilāṣasahagatā [|] tatra yā prāpteṣu viṣayeṣu saumanasyādhyavasānasahagatā nandīrāgasahagatetyucyate | yā punaraprāpteṣu viṣayeṣu saṃyogābhilāṣasahagatā tatra tatrābhinandinītyucyate |
children.translated_text: Therein, the longing for renewed existence is the craving that leads to renewed existence (<s>paunarbhavikī tṛṣṇā</s>). The longing for sense-objects is further of two kinds: that accompanied by the determination of satisfaction in attained objects, and that accompanied by the desire for union with unattained objects. Therein, that which is accompanied by the determination of satisfaction in attained objects is called 'accompanied by delight and passion' (<s>nandīrāgasahagatā</s>). And that which is accompanied by the desire for union with unattained objects is called 'finding delight here and there' (<s>tatra tatrābhinandinī</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), <s>prārthanā</s> (longing), <s>abhilāṣa</s> (desire), and <s>abhinandanā</s> (delight) are synonyms. That longing, moreover, operates through three modes, namely: longing for renewed existence (<s>punarbhavaprārthanā</s>) and longing for sense-objects (<s>viṣayaprārthanā</s>).

body.text: nirodhopidvividhaḥ | kleśanirodhaḥ, upakleśanirodhaśca |
body.translated_text: Cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) is also of two kinds: cessation of afflictions (<s>kleśanirodha</s>) and cessation of secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśanirodha</s>).

body.text: mārgopi dvividhaḥ | śaikṣaścāśaikṣaśca | idamālambanaṃ kleśaviśodhanaṃ lokottareṇa mārgeṇa veditavyaṃ | tenāha caturvidhamālambanaṃ | vyāpyālambanaṃ, caritaviśodhanaṃ, kauśalyālambanaṃ, kleśaviśodhanaṃ ceti ||
body.translated_text: The path (<s>mārga</s>) is also of two kinds: the training path (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and the path beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>). This should be understood as the object for purification of afflictions by the supramundane path. Therefore he says: 'The object is fourfold — the pervading object, the object for purifying temperament, the object of skill, and the object for purifying afflictions.'

body.text: tatrāvavādaḥ katamaḥ | caturvidho [a]vavādaḥ | (

children.translated_text: unerring instruction, sequential instruction, instruction based on scripture (<s>āgama</s>), and instruction based on realization (<s>adhigama</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, what is instruction (<s>avavāda</s>)? Instruction is of four kinds:

body.text: tatrāviparītāvavādaḥ katamaḥ | yadaviparītaṃ dharmasattvaṃ ca deśayati | grāhayati | bhūtaṃ yadasya niryāti | samyagduḥkhakṣayāya | duḥkhasyāntakriyāyai [|] ayamucyate 'viparītāvavādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is unerring instruction? That by which one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> and [the nature of] beings without error; causes them to grasp [the teaching]; what is real, what leads to liberation, to the correct destruction of suffering, to the making of an end of suffering — this is called unerring instruction.

body.text: anupūrvāvavādaḥ katamaḥ | yatkālena dharmaṃ deśayati | uttānottānāni [sthānāni] tatprathamato grāhayati | vācaya[ti] | tataḥ paścādgaṃbhīrāṇi prathamasya vā satyasyābhisamayāya tatprathamato 'vavadate | (

children.text: ) tataḥ paścātsamudayanirodhamārgasatyasya, prathamasya dhyānasya samāpattaye tatprathamatovavadate | tataḥ paścādanyāsāṃ dhyānasamāpattīnāmayamevaṃbhāgīyonupūrvāvavādo veditavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: and afterward for [the comprehension of] the truth of origin, cessation, and path; for the attainment of the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), one instructs in that first, and afterward for the other <s>dhyāna</s> attainments. This kind of instruction should be understood as sequential instruction.

body.translated_text: What is sequential instruction? That by which one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> at the appropriate time; causes them to grasp and recite the clear and straightforward topics first, and the profound ones afterward; for the comprehension of the first truth, one instructs in that first,

body.text: tatrāgamāvavādo yathā tena gurūṇāmantikādāgamitaṃ bhavati | gurusthānīyānāṃ, yogajñānāṃ, ācāryāṇāmupādhyāyasya vā, tathāgatasya vā, tathāgataśrāvakasya vā [|] tathaivānenānyūnamadhikaṃ kṛtvā parānavavadate | ayamucyate āgamāvavādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, instruction based on scripture (<s>āgama</s>) is that which one has learned from one's teachers, from those who stand in the place of teachers, from those who know <s>yoga</s>, from preceptors, from masters, from the <s>Tathāgata</s>, or from the disciples of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. One then instructs others in exactly that way, neither diminishing nor adding to it. This is called instruction based on scripture.

body.text: tatrādhigamāvavādaḥ [|] yathānena tedharmā adhigatā bhavanti | sparśitāḥ (spṛṣṭāḥ) sākṣātkṛtā, ekākinā vyavakṛṣṭavihāriṇā | tañcaiva pareṣāṃ prāptaye | sparśanāyai sākṣātkriyāyai | avavadate [|] ayamucyate adhigamāvavādaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, instruction based on realization (<s>adhigama</s>) is that which consists of <s>dharmas</s> that one has realized, contacted, and directly known while dwelling alone in solitude. And for the attainment, realization, and direct knowledge of that very [<s>Dharma</s>] by others, one instructs. This is called instruction based on realization.

body.text: asti punaḥ sarvākāraparipūrṇovavādaḥ | sa punaḥ katamaḥ [|] yastribhiḥ (yat tribhiḥ) prātihāraryaivavadati | ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa, ādeśanāprātihāryeṇa | anuśāstiprātihāryeṇa | ṛddhiprātihāryeṇa, (

children.text: ) anekavidhamṛddhiviṣayamupadarśayatyātmani ca bahumānaṃ ja[na]yati | pareṣāṃ yathā tena bahumānajātāḥ | śrotrāvadhānayoge manasikāre ādarajātā bhavanti | tatra [|] deśanā prātihāryeṇa cittacaritaṃ samanveṣya anuśāstiprātihāryeṇa yathendriyaṃ, yathācaritaṃ, yathāvatāraṃdharmadeśanāṃ deśayati | pratipakṣe samanuśāsti | tenāyaṃ prātihāryatrayasaṃgṛhītaḥ paripūrṇāvavādo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: one displays manifold supernatural abilities and generates in oneself great esteem, such that others, having generated esteem, become inclined with respect toward listening, mental engagement, and application. Therein, by the miracle of mind-reading, having searched out the mental disposition [of beings], by the miracle of teaching, one teaches the <s>Dharma</s> according to their faculties, according to their temperament, and according to their point of entry, and instructs them in the antidotes. Thus this instruction, encompassed by the three miracles, is complete instruction.

body.translated_text: There is, moreover, instruction that is complete in all aspects. What is that? It is instruction by means of three miracles (<s>prātihāryas</s>): the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>), the miracle of mind-reading (<s>ādeśanāprātihārya</s>), and the miracle of teaching (<s>anuśāstiprātihārya</s>). By the miracle of supernatural power,

body.text: tatra śikṣā katamā | āha | tisraḥ śikṣāḥ [|] adhiśīlaṃ śikṣā, adhicittamadhiprajñaṃ śikṣā ||
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the training (<s>śikṣā</s>)? He says: There are three trainings — the training in higher morality (<s>adhiśīlaśikṣā</s>), the training in higher mind (<s>adhicittaśikṣā</s>), and the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñāśikṣā</s>).

body.text: tatrādhiśīlaṃ śikṣā katamā | yathāpi tacchīlaṃ (

children.translated_text: one of moral conduct dwells [thus] — in detail as before.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the training in higher morality? Just as that moral conduct —

body.text: tatrādhiśīlaṃ (cittaṃ) śikṣā viviktaṃ kāmairviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ, savicāraṃ, vivekajaṃ, prītisukhaṃ, cittaikāgratā[ñ]ca, prathamaṃ dhyānaṃ yāvaccaturthaṃ dhyānamupasampadya viharati | iyamadhicittaṃ, śikṣā | api khalu sarve ārūpyāstadanyāśca samādhisamāpattayaḥ | adhicittaṃ śikṣetyucyate | api tu dhyānāni niśritya tatprathamataḥ satyābhisamayomā vakrāntirbhavati | na tu sarveṇa sarvaṃ vinā dhyānaiḥ tasmātpradhānāni dhyānāni kṛtvā adhicittaṃ śikṣetyuktāni |
body.translated_text: Therein, the training in higher mind: secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, with <s>vitarka</s> (initial thought), with <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), born of seclusion, accompanied by <s>prīti</s> (joy) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness), and one-pointedness of mind — one enters and dwells in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) up to the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>. This is the training in higher mind. Moreover, all the formless attainments and other meditative absorptions are also called the training in higher mind. However, it is in dependence on the <s>dhyānas</s> that the first realization of the truths, the entry [into the path], occurs — and not entirely without the <s>dhyānas</s>. Therefore, making the <s>dhyānas</s> primary, they are called the training in higher mind.

body.text: tatrādhiprajñaṃ śikṣā yā caturṣvāryasatyeṣu yathābhūtaṃ jñānaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, the training in higher wisdom is the knowledge of the Four Noble Truths as they truly are.

body.text: kena kāraṇena tisra eva śikṣā na tadūrdhvaṃ | āha | samādhipratiṣṭhārthena | jñānasaṃniśrayārthena | kṛtyakaraṇārthena ca [|] tatra samādhipratiṣṭhārthenādhiśīlaṃ | śikṣā | tathā hi śīlaṃ pratiṣṭhāya cittaikāgratāṃ spṛśati (||) cittasamādhiṃ [||] tatra jñānasanniśrayārthena adhicittaṃ śikṣā | tathā hi samāhitacittasyaikāgratā | smṛtyā jñeye vastuni yathābhūtaṃ jñānadarśanaṃ pravarttate | tatra kṛtyakaraṇārthena adhiprajñaṃ śikṣā | tathā hi suviśuddhena jñānadarśanena kleśaprahāṇaṃ sākṣātkaroti | eṣa hi svārtha e[tat] paramaṃ kṛtyaṃ yaduta kleśaprahāṇaṃ [|] tata uttarikaraṇīyaṃ punarnāsti | tena etāstisra eva śikṣāḥ |
body.translated_text: For what reason are there exactly three trainings and no more? He says: for the purpose of establishing <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), for the purpose of relying on knowledge, and for the purpose of accomplishing the task. Therein, for the purpose of establishing <s>samādhi</s>: the training in higher moral conduct. For indeed, having established moral conduct, one reaches one-pointedness of mind, the <s>samādhi</s> of the mind. Therein, for the purpose of relying on knowledge: the training in higher mind. For indeed, for one whose mind is concentrated and one-pointed, with mindfulness, knowledge and vision of the object as it truly is proceeds. Therein, for the purpose of accomplishing the task: the training in higher wisdom. For indeed, with well-purified knowledge and vision, one directly realizes the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). This indeed is one's own welfare, this is the supreme task — namely, the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s>. Beyond that, there is nothing further to be done. Therefore these are exactly three trainings.

body.text: kāḥ punarāsāṃ śikṣāṇāmānupūrvīṣu viśuddhaśīlasya vipratisāraḥ [|] avipratisāriṇaḥ prāmodyaṃ, prītiḥ, praśrabdhiḥ, sukhaṃ, sukhitasya cittasamādhiḥ [|] samāhitacitto yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | yathābhūtaṃ paśyati | yathābhūtaṃ jānanpaśyannirvidyate | nirviṇṇo (

children.text: ) virajyate | virakto vimucyate | vimukto [a]nupādāya parinirvāti | evamimāni śīlāni bhāvitāni agratāyāmupanayanti | yadutānupādāya parinirvāṇamiyamāsāṃ śikṣāṇāmānupūrvī |
children.translated_text: one becomes dispassionate. Being dispassionate, one is liberated. Being liberated, without further clinging, one attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Thus these moral precepts, when cultivated, lead to the highest — namely, <s>parinirvāṇa</s> without clinging. This is the sequential progression of these trainings.

body.translated_text: And what is the sequential progression of these trainings? For one whose moral conduct is purified, there is no remorse. For one without remorse, there is gladness, joy, tranquility, happiness; for one who is happy, there is <s>samādhi</s> (concentration of mind). One whose mind is concentrated knows things as they truly are, sees things as they truly are. Knowing and seeing as they truly are, one becomes disenchanted. Being disenchanted,

body.text: tatra kena kāraṇenādhiśīlaṃ śikṣā adhiśīlamityucyate | evamadhicittamadhiprajñamadhikārārthenā(dhikārārthena) ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, for what reason is the training in higher moral conduct called 'higher moral conduct'? And likewise 'higher mind' and 'higher wisdom'? It is in the sense of 'with reference to what is higher.'

body.text: tatra kathamadhikārārthenā (nā a)dhicittamadhikṛtya yacchīlaṃ sā adhiśīlaṃ śikṣā | adhiprajñamadhikṛtya yaścittasamādhiḥ | sā adhicittaṃ śikṣā |
body.translated_text: Therein, how in the sense of 'with reference to what is higher'? The moral conduct that has reference to higher mind — that is the training in higher moral conduct. The concentration of mind that has reference to higher wisdom — that is the training in higher mind.

body.text: kleśaprahāṇamadhikṛtya yajjñānaṃ darśanaṃ | sā adhiprajñaṃ śikṣā |
body.translated_text: The knowledge and vision that has reference to the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — that is the training in higher wisdom.

body.text: yā cādhicittaṃ | yā cādhiprajñaṃ śikṣā | etāḥ śikṣāḥ asminneva śāsane asādhāraṇā ito bāhyairevamadhikārthena [|]
body.translated_text: The training in higher mind and the training in higher wisdom — these trainings are uncommon to this teaching alone and not shared with those outside it. Thus in the sense of reference to what is higher.

body.text: asti punaradhicittaṃ śikṣā yā adhiprajñaṃ śikṣāyā āvāhikā, astyadhiprajñaṃ śikṣā yā adhicittaṃ śikṣāyā āvāhikā | tadyathā | āryaśrāvakaḥ | alābhī mauladhyānānāṃ, śaikṣo, dṛṣṭapadaḥ, tataḥ paścādbhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya prayujyamāna[ḥ] smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ bhāvayati | iyamadhiprajñaṃ śikṣā (|) adhicittaṃ (

children.text: ) śikṣāyā āvāhikā | adhicittaṃ punaḥ śikṣā adhiprajñāyā āvāhikā pūrvamevoktā || tatra astyadhiśīlaṃ śikṣā | nādhicittaṃ, nādhiprajñaṃ | astyadhiśīlamadhicittaṃ, nādhiprajñaṃ | na tvastyadhiprajñaṃ śikṣā yā vinādhiśīlenādhicittena ca | ato yatrādhiprajñaṃ | śikṣā | tatra tisraḥ śikṣā veditavyā[ḥ] || idaṃ tāvacchikṣāvyavasthānaṃ | tatra yoginā yogaprayuktena śikṣitavyaṃ |
children.translated_text: that leads to the training in higher mind. The training in higher mind that leads to the training in higher wisdom has already been stated above. Therein, there can be training in higher moral conduct without higher mind and without higher wisdom; there can be training in higher moral conduct together with higher mind, without higher wisdom; but there cannot be training in higher wisdom without higher moral conduct and higher mind. Therefore, wherever there is training in higher wisdom, all three trainings should be understood. This is the classification of the trainings. Therein, the practitioner engaged in yoga should train.

body.translated_text: Moreover, there is a training in higher mind that leads to the training in higher wisdom, and there is a training in higher wisdom that leads to the training in higher mind. For example, a noble disciple who has not attained the root <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), who is a learner and has seen the truth, thereafter, striving for the abandonment of the <s>kleśas</s> that are to be abandoned through cultivation, cultivates the <s>smṛti-saṃbodhyaṅga</s> (mindfulness factor of awakening). This is a training in higher wisdom

body.text: tatra trayaḥ pudgalāḥ satyānyabhisamāgacchanti | katame trayastadyathā | avītarāgaḥ yadbhūyo vītarāgaḥ, vītarāgaśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, three types of persons realize the truths. What are the three? Namely: one who is not free from passion, one who is mostly free from passion, and one who is free from passion.

body.text: tatra sarveṇasarvamavītarāgaḥ satyānyabhisamāgacchan saha satyābhisamayātsrota (-yena strota) āpanno bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therein, one who is entirely not free from passion, upon realizing the truths, simultaneously with the realization of the truths becomes a stream-enterer.

body.text: yadbhūyo vītarāgaḥ punaḥ sakṛdāgāmī bhavati |
body.translated_text: One who is mostly free from passion becomes a once-returner.

body.text: vītarāgaḥ saha satyābhisamayād (yenā) nāgāmī bhavati |
body.translated_text: One who is free from passion, simultaneously with the realization of the truths, becomes a non-returner.

body.text: trīṇīndriyāṇi | anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyaṃ | ājñendriyamājñātavata indriyaṃ |
body.translated_text: There are three faculties: the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown' (<s>anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriya</s>), the faculty of perfect knowledge (<s>ājñendriya</s>), and the faculty of one who has fully known (<s>ājñātāvīndriya</s>).

body.text: eṣāmindriyāṇāṃ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati | anabhisamitānāṃ (

children.text: ) satyānāṃ abhisamayāya prayuktasya anājñātamājñāsyāmīndriyavyavasthānaṃ | abhisamitavataḥ śaikṣasyājñendriyavyavasthānaṃ | kṛtakṛtyasyāśaikṣasyārhataḥ | ājñā[tāvīndriya]vyavasthānaṃ |
children.translated_text: the classification is the faculty of 'I shall come to know the unknown.' For one who has realized the truths and is a learner, the classification is the faculty of perfect knowledge. For one who has accomplished the task, who is beyond training, who is an <s>Arhat</s> — the classification is the faculty of one who has fully known.

body.translated_text: How is the classification of these faculties established? For one who is engaged in the realization of the truths not yet realized,

body.text: trīṇi vimokṣamukhāni | tadyathā śūnyatā [a]praṇihitamānimittemeṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ vimokṣamukhānāṃ kathaṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati | āha [|] dvayamidaṃ saṃskṛtamasaṃskṛtañca |
body.translated_text: There are three doors of liberation: <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness), and <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness). How is the classification of these three doors of liberation established? He says: there are two things — the conditioned and the unconditioned.

body.text: tatra saṃskṛtaṃ traidhātukapratisaṃyuktāḥ pañcaskandhāḥ, [a]saṃskṛtaṃ punaḥ nirvāṇaṃ | idamubhayaṃ yacca saṃskṛtaṃ, yaccā saṃskṛtamityucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the conditioned is the five <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) associated with the three realms. The unconditioned is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. These two together — that which is conditioned and that which is unconditioned — are so designated.

body.text: yatpunaridamucyate | ātmā vā, sattvo vā, jīvo vā, janturvā, idamasat | tatra saṃskṛte doṣadarśanādādīnavadarśanādapraṇidhānaṃ bhavati | apraṇidhānāccāpraṇihitaṃ vimokṣamukhaṃ vyavasthāpyate | nirvāṇe punaḥ tatra praṇidhānavataḥ praṇidhānaṃ bhavati | śāntadarśanaṃ | praṇītadarśanaṃ | niḥsaraṇadarśanaṃ ca | niḥsaraṇadarśanācca punarānimittaṃ vimokṣamukhaṃ vyavasthāpyate | tatrāsatyasamvidyamāne naiva praṇidhānaṃ bhavati | tadyathaivāsattathaivāsaditi | jānataḥ paśyataḥ śūnyatāvimokṣamukhaṃ vyavasthāpyate | evaṃ trayāṇāṃ vimokśamukhānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ bhavati ||
body.translated_text: But what is called 'self,' 'being,' 'soul,' or 'creature' — this is non-existent. Therein, through seeing the faults and disadvantages in the conditioned, there arises non-attachment. From non-attachment, the door of liberation called <s>apraṇihita</s> (wishlessness) is established. With respect to <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, for one who has aspiration, there arises the aspiration, the seeing of peace, the seeing of the sublime, and the seeing of escape. From seeing escape, the door of liberation called <s>ānimitta</s> (signlessness) is established. Therein, with respect to what is non-existent and not found, there is neither attachment nor aspiration — just as it is non-existent, so it is non-existent. For one who knows and sees thus, the door of liberation called <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) is established. Thus the classification of the three doors of liberation is established.

body.text: tatra katame śikṣānulomikā dharmāḥ | āha daśa śikṣāvilomā dharmāḥ | teṣāṃ pratipakṣeṇa daśa śikṣānulomikā [dharmā] veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what are the factors conforming to the training? He says: there are ten factors contrary to the training. By their antidotes, ten factors conforming to the training should be understood.

body.text: tatra katame śikṣāvilomādharmāstadyathā | mātṛgrāmaḥ | śiśurudāravarṇo raṃjanīyaḥ | śikṣāprayuktasya kulaputrasyādhimātramantarāyakaraḥ paripanthakaḥ, satkāyaparyāpanneṣu saṃskāreṣu niyantirālasyaṃ, kausīdyaṃ | satkāyadṛṣṭeḥ kabaḍaṃkārāhāramupādāya rasarāgaḥ | lokākhyānakathāsvanekavidhāsu bahunānāprakārāsu citreṣu (trāsu) cha(ccha)ndarāgānunayaḥ, dharmacintā, yogamanasikārāpakṣālaḥ | sa punaḥ katamastadyathā (

children.text: ) raseṣu vā, satyeṣu vā, skandheṣu vā [|] karmaphale vā prahāṇaprayuktasya ca kāyadauṣṭhulyaśaithilikasya śamathavipaśyanāpakṣālamanasikāraḥ | styānamiddhena vā cittābhibhavaḥ | cittābhisaṃkṣepaḥ | anvārabdhavīryasya vā kāyikaklamaḥ | caitasika upāyāsaḥ | atilīnavīryasya viśeṣāsaṃprāptiḥ kuśalapakṣaparyādānaṃ | lobhena vā, yaśasāvā, praśaṃsayā vā, anyatamānyatamena vā sukhalavamātratvena, nandīsaumanasyamauddhatyamavyupaśamaḥ | audvignya mutplāvitatvaṃ | satkāyanirodhe nirvāṇe uttrāsaśṭha(ḥsta)mbhitatvaṃ | amātrayā prayogaḥ | atyabhijalpaḥ | dharmyāmapi kathāṃ kathayatā vigṛhya kathāmārabhyānuyogaḥ | pūrvadṛṣṭaśrutānubhūteṣu viṣayeṣvanekavidheṣu bahunānāprakāreṣu cittavisāraḥ cittākṣepaḥ | anityeṣu ca saṃskā[reṣu] nidhyāyitatvaṃ, ime dharmāścintāyogamanasikārāpakṣālā veditavyāḥ |
children.translated_text: mental attention that departs from <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) regarding the elements of experience, or the truths, or the aggregates, or the results of <s>karma</s>, for one who is engaged in abandonment and whose body has become rigid and slack. Or mental overpowering by torpor and drowsiness, and mental contraction. Or for one who has applied energy, bodily fatigue and mental distress. Or for one whose energy is excessively lax, failure to attain distinction, and decline of wholesome qualities. Or through gain, fame, praise, or any small measure of ease, delight, mental pleasure, restlessness, and lack of tranquility; agitation and being swept away. Or terror and stupefaction regarding the cessation of personal existence, which is <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. Or immoderate application. Or excessive talking. Or even when discussing a Dharma-related topic, initiating contentious disputation and interrogation. Or mental scattering and mental distraction toward previously seen, heard, and experienced objects of various and manifold kinds. And brooding over impermanent formations. These factors should be understood as departures from reflection on the <s>Dharma</s> and from the mental attention of yoga practice.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the factors contrary to the training? Namely: women — a lovely young woman with a beautiful complexion who is attractive — constitutes a major obstacle and impediment for a son of good family engaged in the training. Sloth, laziness, and sluggishness with respect to the formations belonging to the <s>satkāya</s> (personal existence). Attachment to taste with regard to morsel-food, based on <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of a personal self). Desire, passion, and inclination toward various, manifold, and fascinating worldly stories and tales. Departure from reflection on the <s>Dharma</s> and from the mental attention of yoga practice. And what is that departure? Namely,

body.text: dhyāna[samāpatti]sukhāsvādanatā, ānimittaṃ samāpattukāmasya saṃskāranimittānusāritā | spṛṣṭasya śārīrikābhirvedanābhiḥ, duḥkhāmiryāvatprāṇahāriṇībhirjīvitaniyanti[ḥ] |, jīvitāśā tadāśānugatasya (

children.text:
) śocanā, klāmyanā, paridevanā iti | ime daśa śikṣāvilomā dharmāḥ [|]
katame daśa śikṣāpadānāṃ vilomānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ pratipakṣeṇa śikṣānulomikā bhavanti | tadyathā-aśubhasaṃjñā, anitye duḥkhasaṃjñā | duḥkhe anātmasaṃjñā | āhāre pratikūlasaṃjñā | sarvāloke anabhiratisaṃjñā | ālokasaṃjñā | virāgasaṃjñā | nirodhasaṃjñā | maraṇasaṃjñā | itīmā daśa saṃjñā[ḥ] | āsevitā bhāvitā bahulīkṛtā daśavidhasya śikṣāparipanthakasya daśānāṃ śikṣāvilomānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya samvartante |
children.translated_text: grieving, being fatigued, and lamenting. These are the ten factors contrary to the training. What are the ten factors conforming to the training that serve as antidotes to these ten contrary factors? Namely: the perception of the unattractive (<s>aśubhasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of suffering in what is impermanent, the perception of non-self in what is suffering, the perception of repulsiveness in food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of light, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation, and the perception of death. These ten perceptions, when cultivated, developed, and made much of, conduce to the abandonment of the tenfold obstacle to training, the ten factors contrary to the training.

body.translated_text: Relishing the pleasure of the <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) attainment; for one wishing to enter the <s>ānimitta</s> (signless) attainment, following after the signs of formations; for one who has been touched by bodily feelings of suffering, even life-threatening ones, attachment to life, and for one attached to such hope,

body.text: tatra dharmālokaḥ | arthālokaḥ | śamathāloko, vipaśyanālokaśca | etānālokānadhipatiṃ kṛtvā ālokasaṃjñā | asminnarthe abhipretā | dharmacintāyogamanasikāraḥ | paripanthasya prahāṇāya ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the light of the <s>Dharma</s>, the light of meaning, the light of <s>śamatha</s> (calm), and the light of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) — making these lights predominant, the perception of light is intended in this context, for the abandonment of the obstacle to reflection on the <s>Dharma</s> and the mental attention of yoga practice.

body.text: tatrāpare daśa śikṣānulomikā dharmā veditavyāḥ | katame daśa [|] tadyathā pūrvako hetuḥ | ānulomika upadeśaḥ | yoniśaḥ prayogaḥ | sātatyasatkṛtyakāritā tīvra[c]chandatā, yogabalādhānatā, kāyacittadauṣṭhulyapratipraśrabdha(bdhi)rabhīkṣṇapratyavekṣa[ṇa]tā | aparitamanā, nirabhimānatā ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, ten other factors conforming to the training should be understood. What are the ten? Namely: a prior cause, appropriate instruction, methodical application, continuous and earnest practice, intense aspiration, the laying down of the power of yoga practice, relief from bodily and mental rigidity, frequent self-examination, being not discontented, and freedom from conceit.

body.text: tatra pūrvako hetuḥ katamaḥ | yaḥ pūrvamindriyaparipākaḥ | (

children.translated_text: and the development of the faculties. Therein, what is appropriate instruction? Instruction that is correct and sequential.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the prior cause? The prior maturation of the faculties,

body.text: tatra yoniśaḥ prayogaḥ | yathaivā[va]vaditaḥ (voditaḥ) | tathaiva prayujyate | tathā prayujyamānaḥ samyagdṛṣṭimutpādayati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, methodical application: just as one has been instructed, so one applies oneself. Applying oneself thus, one generates right view.

body.text: tatra sātatyasatkṛtyakāritā [|] ṣaḍrūpeṇa prayogeṇa abandhyañca kālaṃ karoti | kuśalapakṣeṇa kṣiprameva kuśalapakṣaṃ samudānayati |
body.translated_text: Therein, continuous and earnest practice: through a sixfold mode of application, one does not waste time, and through wholesome qualities one quickly accumulates wholesome qualities.

body.text: tatra tīvra[c]chandatā [|] yathāpi taduttare vimokṣe spṛhāmutpādayati | kadā svidahaṃ tadāyatanamupasampadya vihariṣyāmi | yadāryā āyatanamupasaṃpadya viharantīti |
body.translated_text: Therein, intense aspiration: for example, one generates the aspiration for the higher liberations, thinking: 'When shall I enter and dwell in that domain in which the noble ones enter and dwell?'

body.text: tatra yogabalādhānatā [|] dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ yogabalādhānaprāpto bhavati | prakṛtyaiva ca tīkṣṇendriyatayā, dīrghakālābhyāsaparicayena ca | tatra kāyacittadauṣṭhu[lyaṃ, prītiḥ] praśrabdhiryathāpi tacchrāntakāyasya klāntakāyasyotpadyate | kāyadauṣṭhulyaṃ, cittadauṣṭhulyaṃ | tadīryāpathāntarakalpanayā pratiprasrambhayati | ativitarkitenātivicāritenotpadyate | kāyacittadauṣṭhulyaṃ tadā [cātma]cetaḥ śamathānuyogena pratipraśrambhayati | (

children.text: ) cittābhisaṃkṣepeṇa cittalayena styānamiddhaparyavasthānaṃ | cotpadyate | kāyacittadauṣṭhulyaṃ tadadhiprajñaṃ dharmavipaśyanayā, prasadanīyena ca manaskāreṇa praśrambhayati | prakṛtyaiva vā prahīṇakleśasya kleśapakṣaṃ kāyacittadauṣṭhulyaṃ avigataṃ bhavati | sadānuṣaktaṃ tatsamyaṅmārgabhāvanayā pratipraśrambhayati |
children.translated_text: Through the contraction of the mind, through mental sinking, the enveloping state of sloth and torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>) arises. The bodily and mental malleability (<s>kāyacittadauṣṭhulya</s>) [that is lost thereby] — having that as the governing [factor] — he calms it through the contemplation of <s>dharmas</s> with higher wisdom (<s>dharmavipaśyanā</s>) and through the attention that produces faith (<s>prasadanīya manaskāra</s>). Or, for one whose <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) are inherently abandoned, the bodily and mental malleability belonging to the affliction-side, though not yet departed, remains constantly attached — he gradually calms it through the cultivation of the right path.

body.translated_text: Therein, the laying down of the power of yoga practice: one attains the power of yoga practice through two causes — by being naturally of sharp faculties, and through long practice and familiarity. Therein, bodily and mental rigidity, joy, and tranquility: just as for one whose body is weary and fatigued, bodily rigidity and mental rigidity arise, one relieves them by changing one's posture. When rigidity arises from excessive initial thought and sustained thought, one relieves bodily and mental rigidity through the practice of mental calm.

body.text: tatrābhīkṣṇapratyavekṣā | abhīkṣṇaṃ śīlānyārabhya kukṛtaṃ pratyavekṣate | sukṛtañca | akṛtaṃ ca pratyavekṣate, kṛtaṃ ca | kukṛtāccākṛtād vyāvarttate | sukṛtācca kṛtānna pratyudāvarttate | tathā kleśānāṃ prahīṇāprahīṇānāṃ mīmānsā (māṃsā) manaskāramadhipatiṃ kṛtvā abhīkṣṇaṃ pratyavekṣate | tatra prahīṇatāṃ jñātvā punaḥ punastameva mārgaṃ bhāvayati |
body.translated_text: Therein, frequent examination (<s>abhīkṣṇapratyavekṣā</s>): one frequently examines, beginning with moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) — what is wrongly done and what is rightly done, what is left undone and what is done. One turns away from what is wrongly done and left undone, and does not turn back from what is rightly done and what is done. Likewise, with respect to <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that have been abandoned and those not yet abandoned, making investigative attention (<s>mīmāṃsā manaskāra</s>) the governing [factor], one frequently examines. Therein, having recognized the state of abandonment, one cultivates that very path again and again.

body.text: tatrāparitamanāya (nayā) tatkālāntareṇa jñātavyaṃ | draṣṭavyaṃ, prāptavyaṃ | tadajānato [a]paśyato, nādhigacchataḥ | paritamanā utpadyate, caitasikaḥ klamaḥ | caitasikovighātaḥ | tāmutpannānnādhivāsayati | prajahāti |
body.translated_text: Therein, regarding non-discouragement (<s>aparitamanāya</s>): in the intervening time, what is to be known, seen, and attained [has not yet been reached]. For one who does not know, does not see, and does not attain, discouragement arises, mental fatigue, mental distress. That which has arisen, one does not tolerate — one abandons it.

body.text: nirabhimānatā | adhigame prāptau | sparśanāyāṃ nirabhimāno bhavati | aviparītagrāhī, prāpte prāpta saṃjñī, adhigate adhigatasaṃjñī [|] itīme daśa dharmāḥ śikṣākāmasya yoginaḥ || ādimadhyaparyavasānamupādāya śikṣāmanulomayati (nti), na vilomayanti | tenocyante śikṣānulomikā iti |
body.translated_text: Absence of conceit (<s>nirabhimānatā</s>): regarding attainment, acquisition, and realization, one is free from conceit. One grasps without distortion — perceiving what has been attained as attained, perceiving what has been realized as realized. These ten <s>dharmas</s>, for a <s>yogī</s> (practitioner) who desires training, from beginning, middle, to end, are in conformity with the training; they do not run counter to it. Therefore they are called 'conforming to the training' (<s>śikṣānulomika</s>).

body.text: tatra katamo yograbhaṃśaḥ | āha | catvāro yogabhraṃśāḥ | katame catvāraḥ | asti yogabhraṃśa ātyantikaḥ | asti tāvatkālikaḥ | asti pārihāṇikaḥ | asti mithyāpratipattikṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text: What is yoga-failure (<s>yogabhraṃśa</s>)? He says: There are four yoga-failures. What are the four? There is absolute yoga-failure (<s>ātyantika</s>), there is temporary yoga-failure (<s>tāvatkālika</s>), there is yoga-failure through decline (<s>pārihāṇika</s>), and there is yoga-failure caused by wrong practice (<s>mithyāpratipattikṛta</s>).

body.text: tatrātyantiko yogabhraṃśaḥ | ayogasthānāṃ pudgalānāṃ veditavyaḥ | tasyāparinirvāṇadharmakatvādatyantaparibhraṣṭā eva yogādbhavanti |
body.translated_text: Therein, absolute yoga-failure should be understood as pertaining to persons who have no capacity for yoga (<s>ayogasthāna</s>). Since they are of a nature that cannot attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation), they are absolutely fallen from yoga.

body.text: tatra tāvatkālikaḥ | tadyathā gotrasthānāṃ parinirvāṇa dharmakāṇāṃ pratyayavikalānāṃ, te hi dūramapi, paramapi gatvā avaśyameva pratyayānāsādayiṣyanti | yogaṃ ca saṃmukhīkṛtya bhāvayitvā parinirvāsyanti | tenaiva teṣāṃ tāvatkālika eva bhraṃśo bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therein, temporary [yoga-failure]: it is like that of those in the <s>gotra</s>-stage who are of a nature capable of <s>parinirvāṇa</s> but lacking the right conditions. For they, even after going far, even after going to the uttermost, will necessarily encounter the [right] conditions. And having faced the yoga and cultivated it, they will attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>. Therefore their failure is only temporary.

body.text: tatra prāptiparihāṇiko yogabhraṃśaḥ | yathāpīhaikatye prāptādadhigatā[j]jñānadarśanasparśavihārātparihīyante |
body.translated_text: Therein, yoga-failure through decline of attainment: just as here, some persons fall from the attained, realized knowledge-and-vision, and the experience of [meditative] abiding.

body.text: tatra mithyāpratipattikṛto yogabhraṃśaḥ | yathāpīhaikatyeḥ | ayoniśaḥ prayujyamāno nārādhako bhavati (|) yogasya, nārādhayati (|) dhyāyyaṃ dharmaṃ kuśalaṃ [|] yathāpīhaikatyaḥ bahukleśo bhavati | prabhūtarajaskajātīyaḥ | mahāvijñānaśca bhavati | mahābuddhiḥ | mahatāyā (mahatyā) buddhayā samanvāgataḥ | sa śrutamudgṛhṇāti | śrutaṃ paryavāpnoti | alpamvā, prabhūtaṃ vā, araṇye vā punarviharati āgatāgatānāñca gṛhipravrajitānāṃ, rujakānāṃ, rujakajātīyānāṃ dharmadeśanayā (

children.text: ) cittamārādhayati | kuhanānucaritayā ca ceṣṭayā kāyavākyapratisaṃyuktayā, tasya tena hetubhāvena, tena pratyayenotpadyate | lābhasatkāraślokaḥ, sa jñāto bhavati | mahāsukho lābhī bhavati | cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsana[glānapratya]yabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ, satkṛtaśca bhavati, gurukṛto, rājñāṃ rājāmātrāṇāṃ, yāvatsārthavāhānāṃ, arhatsampata(da)ḥ | tasyāntā varttante śrāvakāḥ, gṛhiṇaḥ, pravrajitāḥ | api adhvādenteṣu gredhaṃ nigamayamvā varttate (apyadhvānteṣu grāmo nigamo vā vartate) vā [...]yatasyaivaṃ bhavati | santi ye śrāvakā, gṛhipravrajitā, ye mayi saṃbhāvanājātā yeṣāṃ mahatsaṃsa(ma)taḥ te cedyā(nmā)mupasaṃkramya yoge manasikāre śamathavipaśyanāyā[ṃ] praśnaṃ pṛccheyuḥ | teṣāṃ cāhaṃ pṛṣṭo vyākuryāṃ na jānāmītyevaṃ sati yā saṃbhāvanā sā ca hīyenna (hīyeta, na) ca syāmarhatsammataḥ, yannvahaṃ svayameva cintayitvā, tulayitvopaparīkṣya yogaṃ vyavasthāpayeyaṃ | sa etamevārthamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā lābhasatkārābhigṛddha ekākī rahogataḥ svayameva cintayitvā, tulayitvā, tulayitvopaparīkṣya yogaṃvyavasthāpayati | sa cāsya yogo na sūtre bhavati | na vinaye saṃdṛśyate | dharmatāṃ ca vilomayati | mayete(ya ete) bhikṣavaḥ | sūtradharā, vinayadharā, mātṛkādharāsteṣāṃ tadyogasthānaṃ (
children.translated_text: he gratifies his mind. And through deceptive behavior (<s>kuhanā</s>) connected with body and speech, by that cause and that condition, gain, honor, and fame arise for him. He becomes known and becomes one who obtains great ease — robes, almsfood, bedding and lodging, and medicines for the sick. He becomes respected and honored by kings, royal ministers, up to caravan-leaders, in the estimation of an <s>Arhat</s>. <s>Śrāvakas</s> (hearers) — both householders and renunciants — attend upon him. Even in places at the end of roads, or in villages and towns, there may be [devotees]. It occurs to him thus: 'There are <s>śrāvakas</s>, householders and renunciants, who have faith in me, to whom I am greatly esteemed. If they should approach me and ask questions about yoga, mental attention, and <s>śamatha-vipaśyanā</s> (calm and insight), and if I, when asked, were to declare "I do not know" — then that faith would diminish, and I would not be esteemed as an <s>Arhat</s>. Why should I not rather, by my own thinking, weighing, and examining, establish a yoga [practice]?' Making this very purpose the governing [factor], greedy for gain and honor, dwelling alone in seclusion, having thought it through, weighed it, and examined it by himself, he establishes a yoga. But that yoga of his is not found in the <s>sūtras</s>, is not seen in the <s>Vinaya</s>, and runs counter to the true nature of things (<s>dharmatā</s>). There are those monks who hold the <s>sūtras</s>, those who hold the <s>Vinaya</s>, those who hold the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Abhidharma) — from them he conceals that yoga-practice,

children.text: ) vinigūhati | na prakāśayati | yepyasya śrāvakā bhavanti | gṛhiṇaḥ, pravrajitāśca, tānapi yogapratiyuktaye ājñāpayati | tatkasya hetormā, maiva te sūtradharā, vinayadharā, mātṛkādharā, etadyogasthānaṃ śrutvā sūtrevatārayeyuḥ | tacca nāvatāraye(tare)dvinaye, saṃdarśayeyuḥ | tacca na saṃdṛśyate | dharmatayā upaparīkṣyeta | tacca dharmatāṃ virodhayet | te ca tato nidānam pratītā bhaveyurapratītavacanaiśca sāṃ codayeyuḥ | adhikaraṇāni cotpādayeyuḥ | evamahaṃ punarapi na satkṛtaḥ (|) syānna gurukṛto, rājñāṃ rājāmātrāṇāṃ yāvaddhanināṃ śreṣṭhināṃ sārthavāhānāṃ, na ca punarlābhī syāṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāmiti | sa tāmeva lābhasatkārakāmatāmadhipatiṃ kṛtvā adharme dharmasaṃjñī, vinidhāya saṃjñāṃ rūpi[ṇī]madharmaṃ dharmato dīpayati | saṃprakāśayati | tatra yesya dṛṣṭyanumatamāpadyante | tepyadharme | dharmasaṃjñino bhavanti | mandatvānmohatvātte adharme dharmasaṃjñino yathānuśiṣṭā api, pratipadyamānā mithyāpratipannā eva te veditavyāḥ | ayamevaṃ rūpo mithyāpratipattikṛto yogabhraṃśassaddharmapratirūpako hyasaddharmaḥ saddharmasyāntardhānāya [|] itīme catvāro yogabhraṃśā dhyāyinā bhikṣuṇā yogācāreṇa parijñeyā varjayitavyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and does not disclose it. And those who are his disciples — both householders and renunciants — he also instructs in the practice of this yoga. For what reason? Lest those who hold the <s>sūtras</s>, those who hold the <s>Vinaya</s>, those who hold the <s>Mātṛkā</s>, having heard this yoga-practice, should search for it in the <s>sūtras</s> — and it would not be found there; should look for it in the <s>Vinaya</s> — and it would not be seen there; should examine it by the true nature of things — and it would contradict the true nature; and they, on that account, would become dissatisfied and reproach him with words of disbelief, and create disputes. 'Thus I would once again not be respected, not be honored by kings, royal ministers, up to the wealthy, guild-leaders, and caravan-leaders, and I would no longer obtain robes, almsfood, bedding and lodging, and medicines for the sick.' Making that very desire for gain and honor the governing [factor], perceiving <s>Dharma</s> in what is not <s>Dharma</s>, deliberately suppressing [right] perception, he illuminates and proclaims that non-<s>Dharma</s>, which has form, as if it were <s>Dharma</s>. Those who come to share his views also perceive <s>Dharma</s> in what is not <s>Dharma</s>. Due to their dullness and confusion, perceiving <s>Dharma</s> in what is not <s>Dharma</s>, even when practicing as instructed, they should be understood as practicing wrongly. This type of yoga-failure caused by wrong practice is a counterfeit of the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>saddharmapratirūpaka</s>); this false <s>dharma</s> leads to the disappearance of the true <s>Dharma</s>. These are the four yoga-failures that should be fully understood and avoided by a meditating <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) who is a practitioner of yoga (<s>yogācāra</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, yoga-failure caused by wrong practice: just as here, some person, practicing improperly, does not succeed in the yoga and does not succeed in the wholesome <s>dharma</s> that is to be meditated upon. For example, here some person has many <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) and is of a type with abundant passion. Yet he has great understanding and great wisdom — endowed with great intelligence. He learns what he has heard, he masters what he has heard, whether little or much. He may dwell in the forest, and through teaching the <s>Dharma</s> to the householders and renunciants, the sick and the ailing, who come to visit him,

body.text: tatra yogaḥ katamaḥ | āha [|] caturvidho (

children.text: ) yogaḥ | tadyathā śraddhā, chando, vīryaṃ, upāyaśca ||
children.translated_text: It is as follows: faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), desire (<s>chanda</s>), effort (<s>vīrya</s>), and skillful means (<s>upāya</s>).

body.translated_text: What is yoga? He says: Yoga is fourfold.

body.text: tatra śraddhā dvividhādhiṣṭhānā-abhisaṃpratyayākārā prasādākārā ca || dharmayuktivicāraṇādhiṣṭhānā pudgalānubhāvādhimuktyadhiṣṭhānā ca ||
body.translated_text: Therein, faith (<s>śraddhā</s>) has a twofold basis — it has the aspect of conviction (<s>abhisaṃpratyaya</s>) and the aspect of clarity (<s>prasāda</s>). [It is also] based on the investigation of <s>Dharma</s>-reasoning (<s>dharmayuktivicāraṇā</s>) and based on conviction arising from the influence of a person (<s>pudgalānubhāvādhimukti</s>).

body.text: chandopi caturvidhaḥ | tadyathā prāptaye [|] yathāpīhaikatyaḥ uttare vimokṣaspṛhāmutpādayati | vistareṇa pūrvavat | paripṛcchāyai | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ spṛhāmutpādayati vistareṇa pūrvavatparipṛcchāyai | ārāmaṃ gamanāya, vijñānāṃ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ yogajñānāmantikamaśrutasya śravaṇāya, śrutasya ca paryavadānāya [|] saṃbhārasamudāgamācchandaḥ | yathāpīhaikatyaḥ śīlasamvarapāriśuddhaye, indriyaṃ saṃvarapāriśuddhaye, bhojane mātrajñatāyāṃ, jāgarikānuyoge, saṃprajānadvihāritāyāmuttarottarāṃ spṛhāmutpādayati | anuyogācchandaḥ | yā (yaḥ) sātatyaprayogatāyāṃ satkṛtyaprayo[gatā]yāṃ ca mārgabhāvanāyāṃ spṛhāmutpādayatyabhilāṣaṃ kartukāmatāmityayaṃ caturvidhaśchandaḥ | (ityayaṃ caturvidhaśchandaḥ) yaduta prāptaye | paripṛcchanāyai | saṃbhārasamudāgamāya | anuyogāya ca |
body.translated_text: Desire (<s>chanda</s>) is also fourfold: [1] For attainment: just as here some person generates an aspiration toward higher liberation — in detail as before. [2] For inquiry: just as here some person generates an aspiration — in detail as before — for inquiry, for going to the assembly, for hearing the unheard from wise fellow practitioners in the holy life who have yogic knowledge, and for the clarification of what has been heard. [3] Desire arising from the accumulation of provisions: just as here some person generates ever-higher aspiration for the purification of moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>), the purification of sense-faculty restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>), moderation in food, application to wakefulness, and dwelling in full awareness. [4] Desire for application: that which generates aspiration, longing, and eagerness for the continuous and earnest practice of path-cultivation. This is the fourfold desire — namely, for attainment, for inquiry, for accumulation of provisions, and for application.

body.text: tatra vīryamapi caturvidha[ṃ] tadyathā śra[vaṇā]ya, cintanāyai, bhāvanāyai | āvaraṇapariśuddhaye ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, effort (<s>vīrya</s>) is also fourfold — namely, for hearing, for reflection, for cultivation, and for the purification of obstructions.

body.text: tatra śravaṇāya vīryaṃ | yadaśrutaṃ śṛṇvataḥ | paryavadāpayataḥ | cetaso [a]bhyutsāhaḥ | avinyastaprayogatā, evaṃ yathāśrutānāṃ dharmāṇāmekākino rahogatasyārthaṃ | cintayatastulayata upaparīkṣamāṇasya | evaṃ pratisaṃlayanapraviṣṭasya kālena kālaṃ śamathavipaśyanāṃ bhāvayata evamahorātrānuyuktasya caṃkramaniṣadyābhyā[ṃ] nivaraṇebhyaścittaṃ viśodhayataḥ | yaścetasobhyutsāhaḥ | avinyastayāgatā(prayogatā) [|] evaṃ yathāśrutānāṃ dharmāṇāmekākino rahogatasyārthaṃ cintayata ālayadīrghatā tatra |
body.translated_text: Therein, effort for hearing: while hearing what has not been heard, while mastering [it], there is mental enthusiasm and unrelaxed application. Likewise, while reflecting on the meaning of the <s>dharmas</s> as heard, alone in seclusion, weighing and examining — likewise, while entering seclusion and cultivating <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) from time to time, thus engaged day and night in walking meditation and sitting meditation, purifying the mind of the hindrances — there is mental enthusiasm and unrelaxed application. Likewise, while reflecting on the meaning of the <s>dharmas</s> as heard, alone in seclusion, there is sustaining effort therein.

body.text: upāyopi caturvidhastadyathā śīlasamvaramindriyasaṃvaramadhipatiṃ kṛtvā sūpasthitasmṛtitā | tathā copasthitasmṛterapramādaścetasa ārakṣā | kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ niṣevaṇā | tathā vāpramattasyādhyātmaṃ cetaḥśamathayogaḥ | adhiprajñañca dharmavipaśyanā [|] sa cāyaṃ yogaścaturvidhaḥ | ṣoḍaśākāro bhavati | tatra śraddhayā prāptavyamarthamadhipatiṃ saṃprāpnoti | prāptimabhisaṃpratyayātkartukāmatāmutpādayati | kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu [|] sa evaṃ kartukāmaḥ | ahorātrānuyukto viharati | utsāhī | dṛḍhaparākramaḥ | tacca vīryamupādāya parigṛhītamaprāptasya prāptaye, anadhigatasyādhigamāya | asākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai | samvarttate | tasmādime catvāro dharmā yoga ityucyate |

children.text: tatra manasikāraḥ katamaḥ | catvāro manaskārāḥ katame catvāraḥ | (saṃsthāpayataśca dharmāḥ (dharmān) pravicinvataḥ | yāvanmanaskāraṃ na prāpnoti | tāvadasya balavāhano manaskāro bhavati | balādavaṣṭabhya taccittamekāgratāyāmavasthāpayati | tenocyate | balavāhana iti | sachidravāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ) tadyathā- balavāhanaḥ sa(c]chidravāhanaḥ, anābhogavāhanaśca |
children.translated_text: What is mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>)? There are four kinds of attention. What are the four? Namely: the forceful attention (<s>balavāhana</s>), the intermittent attention (<s>sacchidravāhana</s>), and the effortless attention (<s>anābhogavāhana</s>).

body.translated_text: Skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) is also fourfold: [1] Making moral restraint (<s>śīlasaṃvara</s>) and sense-faculty restraint (<s>indriyasaṃvara</s>) the governing [factor], well-established mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>). [2] Likewise, from well-established mindfulness, diligence (<s>apramāda</s>) and the guarding of the mind; the cultivation of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. [3] Likewise, for the diligent one, the internal practice of mental calm (<s>cetaḥśamatha</s>). [4] And the contemplation of <s>dharmas</s> with higher wisdom (<s>dharmavipaśyanā</s>). This yoga is fourfold and has sixteen aspects. Therein, through faith one attains the purpose to be attained as the governing [factor]. Through conviction, one generates the desire to act with regard to wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. Desiring thus to act, one dwells engaged day and night — enthusiastic, of firm exertion. Taking up that effort, it serves for the attainment of what has not been attained, for the realization of what has not been realized, and for the direct experience of what has not been directly experienced. Therefore these four <s>dharmas</s> are called yoga.

body.text: tatra balavāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ | tadyathā ādikarmikasyādhyātmameva cittaṃ sthāpayataḥ | saṃsthāpayataśca | (

children.text: ) dharmān pravicinvataḥ | yāvanmanaskāraṃ na prāpnoti | tāvadasya balavāhano manaskāro bhavati | balādavaṣṭabhya taccittamekāgratāyāmavasthāpayati | tenocyate balavāhana iti |
children.translated_text: examining the <s>dharmas</s>. As long as he has not attained [proper] attention, his attention is of the forceful kind. By force he holds that mind and establishes it in one-pointedness (<s>ekāgratā</s>). Therefore it is called 'forceful.'

body.translated_text: Therein, what is forceful attention (<s>balavāhana manaskāra</s>)? It is that of a beginner (<s>ādikarmika</s>) internally establishing the mind, making it settle,

body.text: sa[c]chidravāhano manaskāraḥ katamaḥ | yo labdhamanaskārasya ca laukikena mārgeṇa gacchato lokottareṇa vā (yo) lakṣaṇa pratisaṃvedī manaskāraḥ | tathā hi samādhistatra cintayā vyavathī(sthī)yate | naikāntena bhāvanākāreṇa pravarttate |
body.translated_text: What is intermittent attention (<s>sacchidravāhana manaskāra</s>)? That which is the characteristic-experiencing attention of one who has attained [proper] attention and who proceeds by the mundane path or the supramundane path. For in that [state], <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) is sustained by reflection (<s>cintā</s>); it does not proceed entirely in the mode of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: tatra ni[ś]chidravāhano manaskāraḥ | lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedino manaskārādūrdhvaṃ yāvat | prayoganiṣṭhānmanasikārāttathānābhogavāhano manaskāraḥ | yaḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphalo manaskāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>niśchidravāhana manaskāra</s> (uninterrupted-flow mental attention) is that which [extends] from the mental attention that discerns the characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedin</s>) up to the mental attention of the culmination of practice (<s>prayoganiṣṭhā</s>). And the <s>anābhogavāhana manaskāra</s> (effortless-flow mental attention) is the mental attention that is the fruit of the culmination of practice.

body.text: apare catvāro manaskārāḥ tadyathā ānulomikaḥ, prātipakṣikaḥ, prasadanīyaḥ, pratyavekṣaṇīyaśca [|]
body.translated_text: There are another four [types of] mental attention (<s>manaskāra</s>), namely: the concordant (<s>ānulomika</s>), the antidotal (<s>prātipakṣika</s>), the gladdening (<s>prasadanīya</s>), and the examining (<s>pratyavekṣaṇīya</s>).

body.text: tatrānulo[miko] manaskāraḥ | yenālambanaṃ vidūṣayati | samyakprayogaṃ cārabhate | no tu kleśaṃ prajahāti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the concordant mental attention is that by which one sees the faults of the object and undertakes the correct practice, but does not yet abandon the <s>kleśa</s> (defilement).

body.text: tatra prātipakṣiko yena kleśaṃ prajahāti |
body.translated_text: Therein, the antidotal [mental attention] is that by which one abandons the <s>kleśa</s>.

body.text: tatra prasadanīya yena līnaṃ cittaṃ pragrāhakairnimittairabhipramoca(da)yati | saṃ[praharṣa]yati | pragṛhṇāti | (

children.text: ) tatra pratyavekṣaṇīyo manaskāraḥ | tadyathā mimānsā(māṃsā)manaskāraḥ | yamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā prahīṇā prahīṇatāṃ kleśānāṃ pratyavekṣate |
children.translated_text: Therein, the examining mental attention (<s>pratyavekṣaṇīya manaskāra</s>) is, namely, the mental attention of investigation (<s>mīmāṃsā</s>), making which the governing factor, one examines the <s>kleśas</s> as abandoned, verifying their state of having been abandoned.

body.translated_text: Therein, the gladdening [mental attention] is that by which, when the mind has become sluggish, one enlivens it through uplifting signs, gladdens it, and uplifts it.

body.text: tatrālambanaṃ manasi kurvatā kati nimittāni manasi karttavyāni bhavanti | āha | catvāri | tadyathā | ālambananimittaṃ | parivartta(rja)nīyaṃ nimittaṃ [|] niṣevaṇīyaṃ ca nimittaṃ | tatrālambananimittaṃ yat | jñeyavastusabhāgaṃ pratibimbaṃ | pratibhāsaṃ (saḥ) ||
body.translated_text: Therein, how many signs (<s>nimitta</s>) should be attended to when one attends to the object? He says: Four — namely: the sign of the object (<s>ālambananimittam</s>), the sign to be avoided (<s>parivarjanīyam nimittam</s>), the sign to be cultivated (<s>niṣevaṇīyam nimittam</s>). Therein, the sign of the object is the reflected image (<s>pratibimba</s>) that is similar to the knowable object, the appearance.

body.text: tatra nidānanimittaṃ tadyathā samādhisaṃbhāropacayaḥ | anulomika upadeśaḥ | bhāvanāsahagataḥ | tīvra[c]chandaḥ, saṃvejanīyeṣu dharmeṣu saṃvegaḥ | vikṣepāvikṣepaparijñā | avadhānaṃ parataśca | saṃghahā manusya(ṣya) kṛto vā, ko (a)manuṣya kṛto vā, śabda kṛto vā, vyāpādakṛto vā | tathā vipaśyanāpūrvaṃgamaḥ | adhyātmaṃ cittābhisaṃkṣepaḥ | uttaptatarāyā vipaśyanāyāḥ uttaratra nidānanimittaṃ, tathā śamathapūrvaṃgamā vipaśyanā, uttaptatarasya śamathasyottaratra nidānanimittaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the causal sign (<s>nidānanimittam</s>) is as follows: the accumulation of the prerequisites of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration); concordant instruction; accompanied by cultivation; intense desire; disillusionment regarding things that cause disillusionment; the discernment of distraction and non-distraction; attentiveness directed toward others as well; interruption — whether caused by humans, non-humans, sounds, or ill-will. Likewise, <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) preceded [by <s>śamatha</s>] and the internal unification of the mind — this is the causal sign for the subsequent stage of more intensified <s>vipaśyanā</s>; and <s>vipaśyanā</s> preceded by <s>śamatha</s> is the causal sign for the subsequent stage of more intensified <s>śamatha</s>.

body.text: tatra parivarjanīyanimittaṃ caturvidhaṃ | tadyathā | layanimittaṃ, auddhatyanimittaṃ, saṃganimittaṃ, vikṣepanimittaṃ ca | tatra layanimittaṃ yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittaṃ līnatvāya paraiti | (

children.text: ) tatrauddhatyaṃ yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittamutpadyate | tatra saṃganimittaṃ yenālambananimittena | nidānanimittena cittamālambane rajyate || saṃrajyate | saṃkliśyate | tatra vikṣepanimittaṃ | yenālambananimittena nidānanimittena cittambahirdhā vikṣipyate | tāni punarnimittāni yathā samāhitāyāṃ bhūmau ebhirmanaskārairālambanamadhimucyate |
children.translated_text: Therein, the sign of excitement is that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind is stirred up. Therein, the sign of attachment is that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind becomes attached, strongly attached, and defiled with respect to the object. Therein, the sign of distraction is that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind is scattered outward. And these signs — on the level of concentration (<s>samāhita bhūmi</s>), through these mental attentions, one resolves upon the object.

body.translated_text: Therein, the sign to be avoided (<s>parivarjanīya nimitta</s>) is fourfold, namely: the sign of sinking (<s>layanimitta</s>), the sign of excitement (<s>auddhatyanimitta</s>), the sign of attachment (<s>saṅganimitta</s>), and the sign of distraction (<s>vikṣepanimitta</s>). Therein, the sign of sinking is that object-sign or causal sign by which the mind tends toward sluggishness.

body.text: katyadhimokṣā bhavanti | āha [|] navādhimokṣā stadyathā | prabhāsvaraścāprabhāsvaraśca | jaḍḥ, paṭuḥ, parītto, mahadgataḥ | apramāṇaḥ | pariśuddhaḥ | apariśuddhaśceti ||
body.translated_text: How many [types of] conviction (<s>adhimokṣa</s>) are there? He says: Nine convictions, namely: luminous and non-luminous; dull and sharp; limited and extensive; immeasurable; purified; and unpurified.

body.text: tatra prabhāsvarodhimokṣo ya ālokanimitte sūdgṛhīte ālokasahagataḥ |]
body.translated_text: Therein, the luminous conviction (<s>prabhāsvara adhimokṣa</s>) is that which, when the sign of light has been well-grasped, is accompanied by light.

body.text: tatrāprabhāsvarodhimokṣaḥ | tadyathā ālokanimitte sūdgṛhīte andhakārasahagataḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the non-luminous conviction is that which, even when the sign of light has been well-grasped, is accompanied by darkness.

body.text: tatra jaḍo 'dhimokṣaḥ | yo mṛdvindriyasantānapatitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the dull conviction is that which has fallen into the continuum of one with weak faculties.

body.text: tatra paṭuradhimokṣo yastīkṣṇendriyasantānapatitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the sharp conviction is that which has fallen into the continuum of one with keen faculties.

body.text: tatra parīttodhimokṣaḥ | yaḥ parīttaśraddhācha(ccha)ndasamādhiḥ parīttālambanaśca | iti manaskāraparīttatayā cālambanaparīttatayā ca parīttodhimokṣaḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the limited conviction is that which has limited faith, desire, and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), and has a limited object. Thus, through the limitedness of mental attention and the limitedness of the object, it is a limited conviction.

body.text: tatra mahadgatodhimokṣaḥ | tatra yo mahadgataḥ śraddhācchandasahagato mahadgatamvā ālambanamadhimucyate | yodhimokṣa iti | manaskāramahadgata[ta]yā cālambanamahadgatatayā mahadgatodhimokṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the extensive conviction is that which, being accompanied by extensive faith and desire, resolves upon an extensive object. Thus, through the extensiveness of mental attention and the extensiveness of the object, it is an extensive conviction.

body.text: tatrāpramāṇodhimokṣaḥ | apramāṇa[ḥ] śraddhācha(ccha)ndasahagataḥ | anantamvā aparyanta[mālamba]namadhimucyate | yo 'dhimokṣa iti | manaskārāpramāṇatayā cālambanapramāṇatayā cāpramāṇādhimokṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the immeasurable conviction is that which, accompanied by immeasurable faith and desire, resolves upon an infinite or boundless object. Thus, through the immeasurability of mental attention and the immeasurability of the object, it is an immeasurable conviction.

body.text: tatra pariśuddho 'dhimokṣaḥ yaḥ prabhāvitaḥ, pariniṣpannaḥ paryavasānagataḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the purified conviction is that which is well-developed, perfected, and brought to completion.
