body.text: apariśuddho vā punaryo na subhāvito, na (

children.translated_text: perfected, and not brought to completion.

body.translated_text: And the unpurified [conviction] is that which is not well-developed, not

body.text: tatra kati yogasya yogakaraṇīyāni | āha | catvāri | katamāni catvāri | tadyathā | āśrayanirodhaḥ | āśrayaparivarttaḥ | ālambanaparijñānaṃ | ālambanābhiratiśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, how many tasks of yoga (<s>yogakaraṇīya</s>) are there? He says: Four. Which four? Namely: cessation of the basis (<s>āśrayanirodha</s>), transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivartta</s>), full comprehension of the object (<s>ālambanaparijñāna</s>), and delight in the object (<s>ālambanābhirati</s>).

body.text: tatratrāśrayanirodhaḥ prayogamanasikārabhāvanānuyuktasya yo dauṣṭhulyasahagata āśrayaḥ | so 'nupūrveṇa nirudhyate | prasrabdhisahagataścāśrayaḥ parivarttate | ayamāśrayanirodhoyamāśraya parivartaḥ | yogakaraṇīyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the cessation of the basis: for one engaged in the cultivation of practice through mental attention, the basis accompanied by <s>dauṣṭhulya</s> (heaviness, unsuitability) gradually ceases, and the basis accompanied by <s>prasrabdhi</s> (pliancy, tranquility) undergoes transformation. This is the cessation of the basis and the transformation of the basis — a task of yoga.

body.text: tatrālambanaparijñānamālambanābhiratiśca | astyālambanaparijñānamālambanābhiratiḥ | āśrayanirodhaparivarttapūrvaṃgamaṃ | yadā cālambanaparijñānamālambanābhiratimadhipatiṃ kṛtvā āśrayo nirudhyate | parivarttate ca | astyālambanaparijñānamālambanābhiratiḥ | āśrayaviśuddhipūrvaṃgamaḥ | āśrayaviśuddhimadhipatiṃ (

children.text: ) kṛtvā suviśuddhamālambanajñānaṃ | kāryapariniṣpattikāle pravartate | abhiratiśca [|] tenocyate catvāri yogasya karaṇīyānīti ||
children.translated_text: well-purified knowledge of the object operates at the time of the accomplishment of the result, and delight as well. Therefore it is said that there are four tasks of yoga.

body.translated_text: Therein, full comprehension of the object and delight in the object: there is a full comprehension and delight in the object that is preceded by the cessation and transformation of the basis — when, taking the full comprehension and delight in the object as the governing factor, the basis ceases and transforms. And there is a full comprehension and delight in the object that is preceded by the purification of the basis — taking the purification of the basis as the governing factor,

body.text: tatra kati yogācārāḥ | āha trayastadyathā | ādikarmikaḥ, kṛtaparicayaḥ | atikrāntamanaskāraśca ||
body.translated_text: Therein, how many [types of] yogic practitioners (<s>yogācāra</s>) are there? He says: Three, namely: the beginner (<s>ādikarmikaḥ</s>), the one with established familiarity (<s>kṛtaparicayaḥ</s>), and the one who has transcended mental attention (<s>atikrāntamanaskāra</s>).

body.text: tatrādikarmiko yogācāraḥ | manaskārādikarmikaḥ | kleśaviśuddhyādikarmikaśca ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the beginner yogic practitioner is one who is a beginner in mental attention and a beginner in the purification from <s>kleśas</s> (defilements).

body.text: tatra manaskārādikarmikaḥ | tatra prathamakarmika ekāgratāyāṃ yāvanmanaskāraṃ na prāpnoti | cittaikāgratāṃ na spṛśati |
body.translated_text: Therein, the one who is a beginner in mental attention: the first-time practitioner, so long as he has not attained the [proper] mental attention and has not reached one-pointedness of mind.

body.text:
tatra kleśaviśuddhyādikarmikaḥ | adhigatepi manaskāre kleśasya cittaṃ vimocayitukāmasya yallakṣaṇapratisaṃvedino manaskārasyārambhaḥ pratigrahaścābhyāsaḥ | ayaṃ kleśaviśuddhyādikarmikaḥ |
tatra kṛtaparicayaḥ katamaḥ | lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedinaṃ manaskāraṃ sthāpayitvā tadanyeṣu ṣaṭsu manaskāreṣu prayoganiṣṭhāpanneṣu kṛtaparicayo bhavati |
body.translated_text:
Therein, the one who is a beginner in the purification from <s>kleśas</s>: even having attained the [proper] mental attention, when one wishes to liberate the mind from <s>kleśas</s>, the initial undertaking, grasp, and practice of the mental attention that discerns the characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedin</s>) — this is the beginner in the purification from <s>kleśas</s>.
Therein, who is the one with established familiarity (<s>kṛtaparicaya</s>)? Setting aside the mental attention that discerns the characteristics, one who has attained practice in the other six [types of] mental attention up to the culmination of practice — he has established familiarity.

body.text: tatrātikrāntamanaskārāḥ (raḥ) prayoganiṣṭhāphalamanaskāre veditavyaḥ | atikrānto 'sau bhavati | pramo(yo)gabhāvanāmanaskāraṃ | sthito bhavati | bhāvanāphale [|] tasmādatikrāntamanaskāra ityucyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, the one who has transcended mental attention (<s>atikrāntamanaskāra</s>) should be understood as being in the mental attention that is the fruit of the culmination of practice. He has transcended the mental attention of practical cultivation and abides in the fruit of cultivation. Therefore he is called one who has transcended mental attention.

body.text: api ca kuśalaṃ dharma[c]chandamupādāya | prayujyamāno (

children.text: ) yāvannirvedhabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlāni notpādayati | tāvadādikarmiko bhavati | yadā punarnirvedhabhāgīyānyutpādayati | tadyathā ūṣmagatāni | mūrdhānaḥ (mūrdhnaḥ), satyānulomāḥ | kṣāntayo(ntīḥ) laukikānagradharmān | tadā kṛtaparicayo bhavati | yadā punaḥ samyaktvaṃ nyāmamavatarati | satyānyabhisamāgacchati | aparapratyayo bhavatyananyaneyaḥ | śāstuḥ śāsane tadātikrāntamanaskāro bhavati | parapratyayaṃ manaskāramatikramyāparapratyaye sthitaḥ | tasmādatikrāntamanaskāra ityucyate |
children.translated_text: so long as he does not produce the wholesome roots pertaining to the decisive stages (<s>nirvedhabhāgīya kuśalamūla</s>), for that long he is a beginner. When, however, he produces the decisive stages — namely, heat (<s>ūṣmagata</s>), summit (<s>mūrdhan</s>), conformities with truth (<s>satyānuloma</s>), supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s> (<s>laukikāgradharma</s>) — then he has established familiarity. When, however, he enters the certainty of the right path (<s>samyaktvanyāma</s>), directly realizes the truths, becomes one who does not depend on another (<s>aparapratyaya</s>), not to be led by another in the teaching of the Master — then he has transcended mental attention, having gone beyond the mental attention dependent on others and being established in independence. Therefore he is called one who has transcended mental attention.

body.translated_text: Moreover, relying on the wholesome desire for <s>dharma</s>, one who applies himself —

body.text: tatra yogabhāvanā katamā | āha | dvividhā | saṃjñābhāvanā bodhipakṣyā bhāvanā ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the cultivation of yoga (<s>yogabhāvanā</s>)? He says: It is twofold — the cultivation of perceptions (<s>saṃjñābhāvanā</s>) and the cultivation of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyā bhāvanā</s>).

body.text: tatra saṃjñābhāvanā katamā | tadyathā laukikamārgaprayuktaḥ | (

Or again, when one is engaged in <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), one cultivates perceptions belonging to the <s>śamatha</s> side, above and below.

children.text: ) bhāvayati | vipaśyanāyāṃ prayuktaḥ | paścātpunaḥ saṃjñāṃ vipaśyanāpakṣyāṃ bhāvayati | vipaśyanāyāṃ prayuktaḥ | paścātpura imameva kāyaṃ yathāsthitaṃ yathāpraṇihitaṃ ūrdhvaṃ pādatalādadhaḥ keśamastakātpūrṇaṃ nānāvidhasyāśuceḥ pratyavekṣate | santyasminkāye keśā romāṇīti pūrvavat | tatra paścātpunaḥ | saṃjñī tathā tadekatyena pratyavekṣaṇānimittameva | sādhu ca, suṣṭhu ca, sūdgṛhītaṃ bhavati | sumanasīkṛtaṃ, sūtkṛṣṭaṃ | supratividdhaṃ | tadyathā sthito niṣaṇṇaṃ pratyavekṣate | niṣaṇṇo vā nipannaṃ | purato vā gacchantaṃ, pṛṣṭhato gacchanpratyavekṣate | sā khalveṣā traiyadhvikānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ pratītyasamutpannānāṃ vipaśyanākārā pratyavekṣāparidīpitā | tatra yattāvadāha- sthito niṣaṇṇaṃ (
children.translated_text: When engaged in <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), one subsequently cultivates perceptions belonging to the <s>vipaśyanā</s> side. When engaged in <s>vipaśyanā</s>, one subsequently examines this very body as it is situated, as it is disposed — from the soles of the feet upward, from the crown of the head downward — as full of various kinds of impurity, reflecting: "In this body there are head-hairs, body-hairs..." and so on as before. And subsequently, being thus perceptive, that contemplative sign, by one method or another, becomes well and truly grasped, well attended to, well drawn out, well penetrated. For instance, standing, one examines one who is seated; or seated, one examines one who is lying down; or from in front, one going behind examines one going [ahead]. This indeed is the contemplation in the mode of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) with respect to conditioned formations of the three times that are dependently arisen, illuminated by examination. Therein, what is stated — "standing, one examines one who is seated" —

children.text: ) pratyavekṣate | anena vartamānena manaskāreṇa anāgatajñeyaṃ pratyavekṣate | vartamānāpi manaskārāvasthā utpannā sthitetyucyate | anāgatā punaḥ jñeyāvasthā | anutpannatvādutpādābhimukhatvācca niṣaṇṇetyucyate | yatpunarāha | niṣaṇṇo vā nipannaṃ pratyavekṣata ityanena pratyutpannena manaskāreṇātītasya jñeyasya pratyavekṣaṇā paridīpitā | pratyutpannā hi manaskārāvasthā | nirodhābhimukhā niṣaṇṇetyucyate | atītā punaḥ niruddhatvājjñeyāvasthā nipannetyucyate | yatpunarāha | purato vā gacchantaṃ pratyavekṣata ityanena pratyutpannena manaskāreṇa | anantaraniruddhasya manaskārasya pratyavekṣā paridīpitā | tatra ya utpannotpanno manasikāro [a]nantaraniruddhaḥ sa purato yāyī [|] tatra anantarotpannaḥ | anantarotpanno manaskāraḥ | navanavo 'nantaraniruddhasyānantaraniruddhasya grāhakaḥ | sa pṛṣṭhato yāyī | tatra śamathaṃ ca vipaśyanāṃ ca bhāvayanstadubhayapakṣyāmālokasaṃjñāṃ bhāvayati | iyaṃ saṃjñābhāvanā |
children.translated_text: by this present mental attention, one examines the future knowable object. The present state of mental attention, being arisen, is called "standing"; the future state of the knowable object, being not yet arisen but facing arising, is called "seated." What is further stated — "seated, one examines one who is lying down" — by this, the examination of the past knowable object by the present mental attention is illuminated. For the present state of mental attention, facing cessation, is called "seated"; the past state of the knowable object, having ceased, is called "lying down." What is further stated — "from in front, one examines one going" — by this, the examination of the immediately ceased mental attention by the present mental attention is illuminated. Therein, whatever mental attention has arisen and immediately ceased, that is the one going ahead. And the mental attention that has immediately arisen, ever new, grasping the immediately ceased [attention] that has just ceased — that is the one going behind. Therein, cultivating both <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, one cultivates the perception of light (<s>ālokasaṃjñā</s>) belonging to the side of both. This is the cultivation of perceptions.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the cultivation of perceptions? Namely, when one is engaged in the worldly path,

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the cultivation of the factors of awakening (<s>bodhipakṣyabhāvanā</s>)? The practice

body.translated_text: Of the foundation of mindfulness regarding the body (<s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s>), of the foundation of mindfulness regarding feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>: for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one generates aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), strives, arouses vigor, takes hold of the mind, and applies it — [this pertains to] the right efforts (<s>samyakprahāṇa</s>). For the abandonment of arisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; and for the maintenance, non-loss, cultivation to completion, development, growth, and fullness of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s> — one generates aspiration, strives, arouses vigor, takes hold of the mind, and applies it — [this pertains to] the right effort, [specifically to] the base of supernormal power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>) endowed with the aspiration-concentration and the formative forces of effort,

body.text: tatra katamaḥ kāyaḥ | katamā kāye kāyānupaśyanā [|] katamā (|) smṛtiḥ [|] katamā[ni] (|) smṛterupasthānāni [|] āha | kāyaḥ pañcatriṃśadvidhaḥ | tadyathā ādhyātmiko, bāhyaśca | indriyasaṃgṛhītaḥ | (

children.text: ) anindriyasaṃgṛhītaśca | sattvasaṃkhyātā (to) 'sattvasaṃkhyātā (ta)śca | dauṣṭhulyasahagataḥ, praśrabdhisahagataśca | bhūtakāyaḥ, bhautikakāyaśca | nāmakāyo, rūpakāyaśca | nārakastairyagyonikaḥ | paitṛviṣayikaḥ | mānuṣyo, divyaśca | savijñānakaḥ | avijñānakaṃ (ko)vā | antaḥkāyo, bahiḥkāyaśca [|] vipariṇato [a]vipariṇataśca || strīkāyaḥ, puruṣakāyaḥ, ṣaṇḍa(ḍha)kakāyaśca | mitrakāyaḥ, amitrakāyaḥ | udāsīnakāyaśca | hīnakāyo, madhyakāyaḥ, praṇītakāyaśca, dahnakāyaḥ, yūna(yuva)kāyo, vṛddhakāyaśca | ayaṃ tāvatkāyaśca prabhedaḥ |
children.translated_text: and not included in the sense-faculties; counted as a sentient being and not counted as a sentient being; accompanied by rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) and accompanied by pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>); the body of great elements (<s>bhūtakāya</s>) and the body of derived matter (<s>bhautikakāya</s>); the name-body (<s>nāmakāya</s>) and the form-body (<s>rūpakāya</s>); the hell-being body, the animal body, the hungry-ghost body, the human body, and the divine body; with consciousness and without consciousness; the internal body and the external body; transformed and untransformed; the female body, the male body, and the eunuch body; the body of a friend, the body of an enemy, and the body of a neutral person; the inferior body, the middling body, and the superior body; the young body, the middle-aged body, and the old body. This, then, is the classification of the body.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the body (<s>kāya</s>)? What is the contemplation of the body in the body (<s>kāyānupaśyanā</s>)? What is <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness)? What are the establishments of mindfulness (<s>smṛterupasthāna</s>)? He says: The body is of thirty-five kinds, namely: internal and external; included in the sense-faculties,

body.text: tatrānupaśyanā trividhā | yā kāyamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā- śrutamayī vā prajñābhāvanāmayī vā [|] yayā prajñayā sarvaṃkāyaṃ sarvākāraṃ samyagevopaparīkṣate | saṃtīrayatyanupraviśati | anuvupyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, contemplation (<s>anupaśyanā</s>) is threefold: that wisdom which, taking the body as the governing principle, is born of learning (<s>śrutamayī</s>) or born of meditation (<s>bhāvanāmayī</s>), by which wisdom one properly examines, explores, penetrates, and investigates the entire body in all its aspects.

body.text: tatra smṛtipadasya kāyamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā (||) ye dharmā udgṛhītāsteṣāmeva ca dharmāṇāṃ yorthaḥ (|) cintito, ye (

children.text: ) ca bhāvanayā sākṣātkṛtā[ḥ] | tatra vyaṃjane, cārthe ca, sākṣākriyāyāṃ ca yaścetasaḥ asaṃmoṣaḥ sūdgṛhītā vā me te ete dharmā na veti || sūpalakṣitā vā tatra tatra prajñayā na veti | susaṃsparśitā[ḥ] (susaṃspṛṣṭāḥ) tatra tatra vimuktyā na veti rupasthitā bhavatīdaṃ smṛterupasthānaṃ | api ca smṛtyā rakṣāyai smṛterupasthānaṃ viṣayāsaṃkleśāyālambanopanibaddhāya (nibandhanāya) ca | tatra smṛtyā rakṣā yathoktaṃ pūrvamevārakṣitasmṛtirbhavati | nipakasmṛtiriti | tatra viṣayāsaṃkleśāya | yathoktaṃ smṛtyā rakṣitamānasaḥ | samāvasthācārako, na nimittagrāhī | nānuvyaṃjanagrāhī | yāvadvistareṇa rakṣati | mana indriyaṃ mana indriyeṇa samvaramāpadyate | tatrālambanopanibandhāya | yathoktaṃ caturvidhe ālambane smṛtimupanibadhnataḥ | tadyathā vyāpyālambane, caritaviśodhane, kauśalyālambane, kleśaviśodhane vā ebhistribhirākārairyā sūpasthitasmṛtitā idamucyate smṛterupasthānaṃ ||
children.translated_text: that have been directly realized through meditation — with respect to the expressions, the meanings, and the direct realization, the non-forgetfulness of the mind [is mindfulness]: 'Have these <s>dharmas</s> been well-learned by me or not?' 'Have they been well-observed there and there by wisdom or not?' 'Have they been well-contacted there and there by liberation or not?' — when thus well-established, this is the establishment of mindfulness (<s>smṛterupasthāna</s>). Moreover, the establishment of mindfulness is for the protection through mindfulness and for non-defilement regarding objects and for binding [the mind] to the object. Therein, protection through mindfulness is as stated earlier: 'one has guarded mindfulness, one has discerning mindfulness.' For non-defilement regarding objects, as stated: 'with the mind protected by mindfulness, established in [proper] conduct and comportment, not grasping at the sign, not grasping at secondary characteristics' — up to, in detail: 'one guards the mind-faculty, one undertakes restraint by means of the mind-faculty.' For binding to the object, as stated: 'one binds mindfulness to the fourfold object' — namely, the pervading object (<s>vyāpyālambana</s>), the object for purifying temperament (<s>caritaviśodhana</s>), the object of skill (<s>kauśalyālambana</s>), and the object for purifying defilements (<s>kleśaviśodhana</s>). By these three aspects, well-established mindfulness — this is called the establishment of mindfulness.

body.translated_text: Therein, regarding the word <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), taking the body as the governing principle: the <s>dharmas</s> that have been learned, and the meanings of those very <s>dharmas</s> that have been reflected upon, and those

body.text: tatra vedanā katamā [|] tadyathā sukhā, duḥkhā, (

children.text: ) aduḥkhāsukhā ca vedanā | tatra sukhāpi kāyikī | duḥkhāpyaduḥkhāsukhāpi [|] yathā kāyikī | evaṃ caitasikī | sukhāpi sāmiṣā, duḥkhāpyaduḥkhāsukhāpi | evaṃ nirāmiṣāpi, evaṃ gardha(vā) śrite (tā), naiṣkramyāśritā vedanā, sukhāpi duḥkhāpyaduḥkhāpyaduḥkhāsukhāpi | saiṣā ekaviṃśatividhā vedanā bhavati | navavidhā vā ||
children.translated_text: and neither-painful-nor-pleasant (<s>aduḥkhāsukhā</s>) feeling. Therein, pleasant feeling is also bodily; painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant are also [bodily]. As bodily, so also mental (<s>caitasikī</s>). Pleasant feeling is also carnal (<s>sāmiṣā</s>); painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant are also [carnal]. Likewise, non-carnal (<s>nirāmiṣā</s>). Likewise, worldly (<s>gardhāśritā</s>) and renunciation-based (<s>naiṣkramyāśritā</s>) feeling — pleasant, painful, and neither-painful-nor-pleasant. Thus, this feeling is of twenty-one kinds, or of nine kinds.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>vedanā</s> (feeling)? Namely: pleasant (<s>sukhā</s>), painful (<s>duḥkhā</s>),

body.text: tatra cittaṃ katamat | tadyathā- sarāgaṃ cittaṃ, sadveṣaṃ, vigatadveṣaṃ, samohaṃ, vigatamohaṃ, saṃkṣiptaṃ, vikṣiptaṃ, līnaṃ, pragṛhītaṃ | uddhatamanuddhataṃ, vyupaśāntamavyupaśāntaṃ | samāhitamasamāhitaṃ, subhāvitamasubhāvitaṃ | suvimuktaṃ cittamasuvimuktaṃ cittaṃ | tadetadabhisamasya viṃśatividhaṃ cittaṃ bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is <s>citta</s> (mind)? Namely: mind with passion (<s>sarāga</s>), mind with hatred (<s>sadveṣa</s>), mind free from hatred (<s>vigatadveṣa</s>), mind with delusion (<s>samoha</s>), mind free from delusion (<s>vigatamoha</s>), contracted (<s>saṃkṣipta</s>), distracted (<s>vikṣipta</s>), sunken (<s>līna</s>), uplifted (<s>pragṛhīta</s>), agitated (<s>uddhata</s>) and non-agitated (<s>anuddhata</s>), pacified (<s>vyupaśānta</s>) and non-pacified (<s>avyupaśānta</s>), concentrated (<s>samāhita</s>) and unconcentrated (<s>asamāhita</s>), well-cultivated (<s>subhāvita</s>) and not well-cultivated (<s>asubhāvita</s>), well-liberated (<s>suvimukta</s>) mind and not well-liberated (<s>asuvimukta</s>) mind. Altogether, this makes twenty kinds of mind.

body.text: tatra dharmāḥ katame [|] rāgo, rāgavinayaśca | (

children.text: ) dveṣo, dveṣavinayaśca | moho mohavinayaśca | saṃkṣepo, vikṣepaḥ | layaḥ, pragraha, auddhatyamanauddhatyaṃ | vyupaśamaḥ | avyupaśamassusamāhi[ta]tā, na susamāhitatā | subhāvitamārgatā, na subhāvitamārgatā | subhāvitamuktatā, na subhāvitamuktatā ca | itīme kṛṣṇaśukla[pakṣa]vyavasthitā viṃśatidharmā veditavyāḥ | saṃkleśavyavadānapakṣye (kṣyāḥ) |
children.translated_text: hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>) and the removal of hatred; delusion (<s>moha</s>) and the removal of delusion; contraction (<s>saṃkṣepa</s>) and distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>); sinking (<s>laya</s>) and uplift (<s>pragraha</s>); agitation (<s>auddhatya</s>) and non-agitation; pacification (<s>vyupaśama</s>) and non-pacification; good concentration (<s>susamāhitatā</s>) and poor concentration; well-cultivated path (<s>subhāvitamārgatā</s>) and not well-cultivated path; well-cultivated liberation (<s>subhāvitamuktatā</s>) and not well-cultivated liberation. These twenty <s>dharmas</s>, established in the dark and bright sides, should be known as [pertaining to] the sides of defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) and purification (<s>vyavadāna</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the <s>dharmas</s>? Passion (<s>rāga</s>) and the removal of passion (<s>rāgavinaya</s>);

body.text: tatra sukhāvedanā yatsukhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate [|] sātaṃ, veditaṃ, vedanāgataṃ | sā punaryā pañcavijñānasaṃprayuktā | sā kāyikī | yā manovijñānasaṃprayuktā sā caitasikī | yathā sukhavedanīyamevaṃ (

children.text: ) duḥkhavedanīyamaduḥkhāsukhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyotpadyate asātaṃ, naivasātaṃ nāsātaṃ veditaṃ [vigatarāgaṃ] | vedanāgatamidamucyate duḥkhā aduḥkhāsukhā vedanā | sā punaryā pañcavijñānakāyasaṃprayuktā | sā kāyikī | yā manovijñānasaṃprayuktā | sā caitasikī | yā nirvāṇānukūlā[sā]nairvedhikī | atyantaniṣṭhatāyai atyantavimalatāyai | atyantabrahmacaryaparyavasānāyai (ya?) | samvarttate | sā nirāmiṣā || yā punardhātupatitā, bhavapatitā sā sāmiṣā [|] yā puna(nā) rūpārūpya pratisaṃyuktā, vairāgyānukūlā vā, sā naiṣkramyāśritā | yā punaḥ kāyapratisaṃyuktā, na ca vairāgyānukūlā, sā gardhāśritā ||
children.translated_text: painful feeling arises dependent on contact that is to be experienced as painful; neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling arises dependent on contact that is to be experienced as neither-painful-nor-pleasant — what is disagreeable, or neither agreeable nor disagreeable, experienced, free from passion, belonging to feeling — this is called painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling. That which is associated with the five sense-consciousness-groups is bodily; that which is associated with mind-consciousness is mental. That which is conducive to <s>nirvāṇa</s>, which is penetrative (<s>nairvedhikī</s>), which conduces to ultimate finality, ultimate purity, and the ultimate consummation of the holy life — that is non-carnal (<s>nirāmiṣā</s>). That which falls within the [three] realms (<s>dhātu</s>) and within existence (<s>bhava</s>) is carnal (<s>sāmiṣā</s>). That which is connected with the form and formless [realms], or which is conducive to dispassion — that is renunciation-based (<s>naiṣkramyāśritā</s>). That which is connected with the desire-body and is not conducive to dispassion — that is worldly (<s>gardhāśritā</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, pleasant feeling (<s>sukhā vedanā</s>) arises dependent on contact (<s>sparśa</s>) that is to be experienced as pleasant — what is agreeable and experienced as belonging to feeling. Furthermore, that which is associated with the five sense-consciousnesses (<s>pañcavijñāna</s>) is bodily (<s>kāyikī</s>); that which is associated with mind-consciousness (<s>manovijñāna</s>) is mental (<s>caitasikī</s>). Just as with pleasant-to-be-experienced [contact], likewise

body.text: tatra sarāgaṃ cittaṃ | yadraṃjanīye vastuni rāgaparyavasthitaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, mind with passion (<s>sarāga citta</s>): that which is enveloped by passion toward an object that is capable of arousing passion.

body.text:
vigatarāṃgaṃ yadrāgaparyavasthānāpagataṃ [|]
sadveṣe(ṣaṃ) ya[d]dveṣaṇīye vastuni dveṣaparyavasthitaṃ |
vigatadveṣaṃ yaddveṣaparyavasthānāpagataṃ |
tatra sammo(mo)haṃ | yanmohanīye vastuni [....]
tānyetāni ṣaṭcittāni cārasahagatāni veditavyāni | tatra trīṇi saṃkleśapakṣyāṇi | trīṇi saṃkleśaprātipakṣikāṇi |
body.translated_text: Mind free from passion (<s>vigatarāga</s>): that from which the envelopment of passion has departed. Mind with hatred (<s>sadveṣa</s>): that which is enveloped by hatred toward an object that is capable of arousing hatred. Mind free from hatred (<s>vigatadveṣa</s>): that from which the envelopment of hatred has departed. Mind with delusion (<s>samoha</s>): that which [is enveloped by delusion] toward an object that is capable of arousing delusion. These six types of mind should be understood as accompanied by the four modes of conduct (<s>cāra</s>). Among them, three are on the side of defilement (<s>saṃkleśapakṣa</s>), three are the antidotes to defilement.

body.text: tatra saṃkṣiptacittaṃ yacchamathākāreṇādhyātmamātmanopanibaddhaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, contracted mind (<s>saṃkṣipta citta</s>): that which is internally bound to itself in the manner of calm abiding (<s>śamatha</s>).

body.text: vikṣiptaṃ | yadbahirdhā pañcasu kāmaguṇeṣvanuvisṛtaṃ |
body.translated_text: Distracted (<s>vikṣipta</s>): that which is dispersed outward among the five objects of sensual pleasure (<s>kāmaguṇa</s>).

body.text: tatra līnaṃ cittaṃ | yatstyānamiddhasahagataṃ, pragrahītaṃ yat prasadanīyenālambanena saṃpratiṣṭhitaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, sunken mind (<s>līna citta</s>): that which is accompanied by sloth and torpor (<s>styānamiddha</s>). Uplifted (<s>pragṛhīta</s>): that which is established in an object that is gladdening.

body.text:
uddhataṃ cittaṃ yadati saṃpragrahādauddhatyaparyavasthitamanubaddhacittaṃ yatpragrahakāle cābhisaṃkṣepakāle copekṣā prāptaṃ [|]
tatra praśāntaṃcittaṃ yannivaraṇebhyo vimuktamavyupaśāntaṃ punaryadavimuktaṃ |
body.translated_text: Agitated mind (<s>uddhata citta</s>): that which is enveloped by restlessness (<s>auddhatya</s>) due to excessive application. Settled mind (<s>anubaddha citta</s>): that which, at the time of application and at the time of restraint, has attained equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). Therein, pacified mind (<s>praśānta citta</s>): that which is freed from the hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>). Non-pacified: that which is not freed.

body.text: tatra samāhitaṃ cittaṃ yannivaraṇavimokṣānmauladhyānapraviṣṭaṃ, na susamāhitaṃ yadapraviṣṭaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, concentrated mind (<s>samāhita citta</s>): that which, freed from the hindrances, has entered the fundamental <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Not well-concentrated: that which has not entered.

body.text: tatra subhāvitaṃ cittaṃ yadasyaiva samādherdīrghakālaparicayānnikāmalābhī bhavatyakṛcchralābhī | āśusamāpattā |
body.translated_text: Therein, well-cultivated mind (<s>subhāvita citta</s>): that through which, by long familiarity with that very <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), one gains it easily, without difficulty, and attains it quickly.

body.text: tatra na subhāvitaṃ cittametadpiryayeṇa veditavyam |
body.translated_text: Therein, not well-cultivated mind should be understood as the opposite.

body.text: tatra suvimuktaṃ cittaṃ yatsarvataścātyantataśca vimuktaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, well-liberated mind (<s>suvimukta citta</s>): that which is liberated in every way and utterly.

body.text: na suvimuktaṃ | cittaṃ yanna sarvato nā(nā)pyatyantato vimuktamitīmāni caturdaśa cittāni (|) vihāragatāni veditavyāni |
body.translated_text: Not well-liberated mind: that which is not liberated in every way nor utterly. These fourteen types of mind should be understood as pertaining to the modes of dwelling (<s>vihāra</s>).

body.text: tatra nivaraṇabhūviśuddhā (ddhi)bhūmimārabhya vihāragatānyaṣṭau cittāni veditavyāni | vikṣiptaṃ saṃkṣiptaṃ yāvad vyupaśāntamavyupaśāntamiti | kleśaviśuddhiṃ punarārabhya vihāragatāni ṣaṭ cittāni yāvatsuvimuktaṃ cittaṃ na suvimuktamiti [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, beginning from the stage of purification from hindrances (<s>nīvaraṇabhūviśuddhi</s>), eight types of mind pertaining to modes of dwelling should be understood: distracted, contracted, up to pacified and non-pacified. Beginning from the purification of defilements (<s>kleśaviśuddhi</s>), six types of mind pertaining to modes of dwelling [should be understood]: up to well-liberated mind and not well-liberated mind.

body.text: yatpunaḥ satyadhyātmaṃ nivaraṇe asti me nivaraṇamiti jānāti | asati nivaraṇe nāsti me nivaraṇamiti jānāti | yathā cānutpannasya vivaraṇasyotpādo bhavati | tadapi yathā yotpannasya vigamo bhavati | tadapi prajānāti | yatra sati cakṣuḥsaṃyojane yāvatpunaḥ (nmana) (

children.text: ) saṃyojane asti me yāvatpunaḥ (manaḥ) saṃyojanamiti | asati yāvatpunaḥ (nmanaḥ) saṃyojane nāsti me manaḥ saṃyojanamiti prajānāti | yathā cānutpannasya yāvanmanaḥ saṃyojanasyotpādo bhavati | tadapi prajānāti | yathā cotpannasya nirodho bhavati | tadapi prajānāti | satyadhyātmaṃ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃge asti me [smṛti] saṃbodhyaṃgamiti prajānāti | asati nāsti me prajānāti | yathā cānutpannasya smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgasyotpādo bhavati | tadapi prajānāti | yathā cotpannasya sthitirbhavati | asaṃmoṣo bhāvanā (|) paripūrirbhūyo bhāvavṛddhirvipulatā tadapi prajānāti | satyadhyātmaṃ smṛtisaṃbodhyaṃgamevaṃ dharmavinayavīryapraśrabdhisamādhyupekṣāsaṃbodhyaṃgaṃ veditavyamiti yadevaṃ svabhāvādīnavapratipakṣākāraiḥ saṃkliṣṭadharmaparijñānamidaṃ śarīraṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānasya, yathā kāye kāyānupaśyanā smṛtyupasthānapakṣame (kṣae) vaṃ vedanā[yāṃ] yaccitte (yāvaccite) dharmeṣu yathāyogaṃ veditavyam |
children.translated_text: (<s>manaḥsaṃyojana</s>), one knows 'there is a mind-fetter in me.' When there is no mind-fetter, one knows 'there is no mind-fetter in me.' And one understands how the arising of an unarisen mind-fetter occurs. And one understands how the cessation of an arisen [fetter] occurs. When internally there is the mindfulness-factor of awakening (<s>smṛtisaṃbodhyaṅga</s>), one knows 'there is the mindfulness-factor of awakening in me.' When it is absent, one knows 'it is absent in me.' And one understands how the arising of the unarisen mindfulness-factor of awakening occurs. And one understands how the maintenance, non-loss, cultivation to completion, further development, growth, and fullness of the arisen [factor] occur. As with the mindfulness-factor of awakening, so too the factors of <s>dharma</s>-investigation, vigor, joy (<s>prīti</s>), pliancy (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) as awakening-factors should be understood. That which is thus the knowledge of defiled <s>dharmas</s> through their essential nature, danger, and antidote aspects — this is the domain of the <s>dharma</s>-foundation of mindfulness (<s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s>). Just as with the contemplation of the body in the body on the side of the foundations of mindfulness, so too with feelings, up to mind, and <s>dharmas</s> — it should be understood as appropriate.

body.translated_text: Now, when internally there is a hindrance (<s>nīvaraṇa</s>), one knows 'there is a hindrance in me.' When there is no hindrance, one knows 'there is no hindrance in me.' And one understands how the arising of an unarisen hindrance occurs. And one understands how the removal of an arisen [hindrance] occurs. When there is an eye-fetter (<s>cakṣuḥsaṃyojana</s>), up to a mind-fetter

body.text: tatra kathamadhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | kathaṃ bahirdhā kathamadhyātmabahirdhā [|] yadā adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ satva(ttva)saṃkhyāte kāye kāyānupaśyī (darśī) viharati | evamadhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | (

children.text: ) kathaṃ bahirdhā kathamadhyātmabahirdhā [|] yadā adhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ, yadā bahirdhā asattvasaṃkhyātaṃ rūpamālambanīkarotyevaṃ bahirdhākāye kāyānudarśī viharati | yadā bahirdhā (rdho)paraktaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ rūpamālambanīkarotyevamadhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati |
children.translated_text: How externally? How both internally and externally? When externally, one takes as one's object form that is not counted as a sentient being — thus one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. When externally, one takes as one's object form that is counted as a sentient being and that is affected [by defilements] — thus one dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally.

body.translated_text: Therein, how does one dwell contemplating the body in the body internally (<s>adhyātma</s>)? How externally (<s>bahirdhā</s>)? How both internally and externally? When one contemplates the body in the body that is internal, that is, one's own, counted as a sentient being — thus one dwells contemplating the body in the body internally.

body.text: tatrādhyātmaṃ rūpamupādāya | sūkṣmaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ | yā utpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, dharmāstānālambanīkurvan [|] adhyātmaṃ vedanā[yāṃ], citte, dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharati | bāhyamasattvasaṃkhyātaṃ rūpamupādāya | yā utpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, dharmāstānālambanīkurvan | bahirdhā vedanāyāṃ, citte, dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharati | bahirdhā bāhyaṃ rūpasattvamupādāya | yā utpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, dharmāstānālambanīkurvannadhyātmabahirdhā vedanāyāṃ, citte dharmeṣu dharmānudarśī viharati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, taking internal form — that which is subtle and classified as sentient — and making the object of the feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen [in dependence on it], one dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> internally. Taking external form that is not classified as sentient, and making the object of the feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen [in dependence on it], one dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> externally. Taking external form, both sentient [bodies], and making the object of the feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen [in dependence on it], one dwells contemplating <s>dharmas</s> in feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> both internally and externally.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | indriyasaṃgṛhītaṃ rūpamālambanīkurvan, adhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānupaśyī (darśī) viharati | anindriyasaṃgṛhītaṃ | rūpagatamanupādattamālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | anindriyasaṃgṛhītameva | rūpamadhyātmamupagatamupādattaṃ rūpamālambanīkurvannadhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānupaśyī (darśī) viharati | [anindriyasaṃgṛhītaṃ rūpagatamanupādattamālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī (

children.text: ) viharati | anindriyasaṃgṛhītameva rūpamadhyātmamupagatamupādattaṃ rūpamālambanīkurvannadhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati] [|] evaṃ pūrvaṃ [ṃ] trividhaṃ rūpamupādāya | yadu (yo)tpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, dharmāstānyathāyogamālambanīkurvan tathādarśī viharatīti veditavyaṃ |
children.translated_text: One dwells contemplating the body in the body externally [by taking] form not comprised in the sense-faculties, belonging to the category of form, that is not appropriated. [One dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally by taking] appropriated form that belongs internally, which is not comprised in the sense-faculties. Thus, with reference to the three kinds of form as before — the feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen [in dependence on them] — one should understand that, taking them as object as appropriate, one dwells contemplating accordingly.

body.translated_text: Another interpretation: Taking as object form that is comprised in the sense-faculties, one dwells contemplating the body in the body internally. Taking as object form that belongs to the category of form, that is not appropriated [by consciousness] and not comprised in the sense-faculties, one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. Taking as object appropriated form that belongs internally [to the body] yet is not comprised in the sense-faculties, one dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | yatsamāhitabhūmikaṃ praśrabdhisahagataṃ rūpamālambanīkarotyevamadhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | yatsūkṣmamevādhyātmaṃ samāhitabhūmikaṃ dauṣṭhulyasahagataṃ rūpamālambanīkaroti | evaṃ bahirdhā kāye kāyānupaśyī (darśī) viharati | paradauṣṭhulyasahagataṃ praśrabdhisahagataṃ ca rūpamālambanīkurvan adhyātmabahirdhā kāye | kāyānudarśī viharati | evaṃ tadupādāyotpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, dharmā yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Another interpretation: When one takes as object form that belongs to the level of concentration (<s>samāhitabhūmika</s>) and is accompanied by tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), one dwells contemplating the body in the body internally. When one takes as object the subtle, internal, concentration-level form that is accompanied by rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. Taking as object form accompanied by both another's rigidity and [one's own] tranquility, one dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally. The feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should be understood in the same way, as appropriate.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | adhyātmaṃ bhūtarūpamālambanīkurvannadhyātmaṃ kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | bāhyaṃ bhūtarūpamālambanī kurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | tacca bhūtarūpamupādāya | yadutpannamindriyaviṣayasaṃgṛhītamupādāya | rūpaṃ cālambanīkurvannadhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | evaṃ tadupādāya yā utpannā vedanā cittaṃ dharmāstepi yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ | aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | yadā savijñānakaṃ kāyamadhyātmamālambananīkaroti | evamadhyātmaṃ (

children.text: ) kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | avijñānakaṃ rūpaṃ sattvasaṃkhyātaṃ | vinīlakādiṣvavasthāsvālambanī kurvanbahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | a(sa)vijñānakasya ca rūpasyātīte kāle savijñānatāṃ [|] avijñāna[ka]sya ca rūpasyānāgate kāle avijñānatāṃ, tulyadharmatāṃ, samadharmatāṃ ālambanīkurvannadhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharatyevaṃ tadupādāya, yā utpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, dharmāstepi yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ | aparaḥ paryāyaḥ [|] ātmanaḥ anta[ḥ] kāyaṃ keśaromanakhādibhiḥ ākārairālambanīkurvannadhyātmabahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati || pareṣāmantaḥ kāyaṃ keśaromanakhādibhirākārairālambanīkurvanbahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharatyadhyātmaṃ cittaṃ ca bahiḥkāyavipariṇataṃ vinīlakādibhirākāraiḥ | bahirdhā ca bahiḥkāyaṃ vipariṇatamavipariṇataṃ ca | vinīlakādibhirākāraistulyadharmatayā ālambanīkurvan bahirdhā kāye kāyānudarśī viharati | tadupādāya yā utpannā vedanā, cittaṃ, (
children.translated_text: Taking as object form without consciousness, classified as sentient, in the stages of discoloration (<s>vinīlaka</s>) and the like, one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. Taking as object both the possession of consciousness of [what is now] form without consciousness in the past, and the lack of consciousness of [what is now] form without consciousness in the future, [seeing] the equality of their nature and the sameness of their nature — one dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally. The feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should also be understood in the same way, as appropriate. Another interpretation: Taking as object one's own internal body through the aspects of head-hair, body-hair, nails, and the like, one dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally. Taking as object the internal body of others through the aspects of head-hair, body-hair, nails, and the like, one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. [Taking as object] the internal mind together with the external body in its transformed [state] through the aspects of discoloration and the like, and the external body — both transformed and untransformed — through the aspects of discoloration and the like, [seeing] the equality of their nature, one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. The feelings, mind,

children.text: ) dharmāstepi yathāyogaṃ veditavyāḥ | ityevaṃbhāgīyā kāye vedanācittadharmaprabhedenabahavaḥ paryāyā veditavyāḥ | ime tu katipayāḥ (ye)paryāyāḥ | saṃprakāśitāḥ [|]
children.translated_text: and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should also be understood in the same way, as appropriate. Thus many interpretations of [contemplating] the body, distinguished by feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s>, and of the same kind, should be understood. But these are just a few of the interpretations that have been made clear.

body.translated_text: Another interpretation: Taking as object internal primary material form (<s>bhūtarūpa</s>), one dwells contemplating the body in the body internally. Taking as object external primary material form, one dwells contemplating the body in the body externally. Taking [both] that primary material form and the form comprised in the sense-faculties and their objects that has arisen in dependence on the appropriated [form] as object, one dwells contemplating the body in the body both internally and externally. The feelings, mind, and <s>dharmas</s> arisen in dependence on that should also be understood in the same way, as appropriate. Another interpretation: When one takes as object the living body with consciousness internally, one dwells thus contemplating the body in the body internally.

body.text: tatra caturṇāmviparyāsānāṃ pratipakṣeṇa bhagavatā catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni vyavasthāpitāni | tatrāśucau śucīti viparyāse pratipakṣeṇa kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | tathā hi bhagavatā kāyasmṛtyupasthānabhāvanāyāṃ | aśubhāpratisaṃyuktāścatasraḥ śivapathikā deśitāḥ | yā asya bahulaṃ kurvan manasikurvataḥ | aśucau śucīti viparyāsaḥ prahīyate | tatra sukhe sukhamiti | viparyāsapratipakṣeṇa vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | vedanānudarśī viharan | yatkiṃcidveditamidamatra duḥkhasyeti yathābhūtaṃ prajānātyevamasya yo duḥkhasukhe sukhamiti | viparyāsaḥ | sa prahāyate (

children.text: ) (prahīyate) | anitye nityamiti viparyāsaḥ | pratipakṣeṇa smṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | tasya sarāgādicittaprabhedena teṣāṃ teṣāṃ rātriṃdivasānāmatyayātkṣaṇalavamuhūrttānā (ṇā)manekavidhānāṃ bahunānāprakāratāṃ cittasyopalabhya yaḥ anitye nityamiti viparyāsaḥ [sa] prahīyate | yatrā[nā]tmanyātmeti viparyāsapratipakṣeṇa dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | tasya yeṣāṃ ātmadṛṣṭyādikā[nāṃ] saṃkleśānāṃ sadbhāvādyeṣāṃ nānātmadṛṣṭyādikānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmasadbhāvātskandheṣvātma darśanaṃ bhavati | nānyasya, svalakṣaṇataḥ | sāmānyalakṣaṇataśca dharmādharmānudarśino yathābhūtaṃ paśyataḥ | yonātmanyātmeti viparyāsaḥ | sa prahīyate |
children.translated_text: As the antidote to the perversion of [seeing] permanence in the impermanent, the <s>cittasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of mind) was established. For him, through the differentiation of the mind as with attachment and so forth, by observing the many diverse kinds and varieties of mind through the passing of days and nights, moments, instants, and hours — the perversion of [seeing] permanence in what is impermanent is abandoned. As the antidote to the perversion of [seeing] self in what is not-self, the <s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s>) was established. For him, because of the existence of afflictions such as the view of self and the like, and because of the non-existence of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> such as the view of non-self and the like, there is the seeing of self in the <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) — and of nothing else. For one who contemplates <s>dharmas</s> in their specific and general characteristics, seeing as it truly is, the perversion of [seeing] self in what is not-self is abandoned.

body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Bhagavān</s> established the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) as the antidote to the four <s>viparyāsas</s> (perversions). Therein, as the antidote to the perversion of [seeing] the pure in the impure, the <s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of the body) was established. For the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught four types of <s>śivapathikā</s> (cemetery meditations) connected with the unattractive (<s>aśubhā</s>) in the cultivation of mindfulness of the body. For one who frequently applies and attends to these, the perversion of [seeing] the pure in the impure is abandoned. Therein, as the antidote to the perversion of [seeing] happiness in suffering, the <s>vedanāsmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of feelings) was established. Dwelling contemplating feelings, one knows as it truly is: 'Whatever is felt, this is within the domain of suffering.' Thus the perversion of [seeing] happiness in what is suffering is abandoned.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | prāyeṇa hi loka evaṃ pravṛttaḥ | skandheṣu skandhamātraṃ, dharmamātraṃ, yathābhūtamaprajānan yathā kāye āśritaḥ | yadāśritaśca sukhaduḥkha ja dharmādharmābhyāṃ saṃkliśyate vyavadā(dī)yate ca | tatrātmana āśrayavastusaṃmohāpanayanārthaṃ | kāyasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | tasyaivātmanaḥ anubhavanavastusaṃmohāpanayanārthaṃ vedanāsmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | yatraiva ca te citte, manasi, vijñāne, ātmagrāheṇa saṃmūḍhā, ātmavastusammohāpanayanārthaṃ dharmasmṛtyupasthānaṃ vyavasthāpitam |
body.translated_text: Another interpretation: For the most part, beings in the world are disposed thus — not knowing the <s>skandhas</s> as merely <s>skandhas</s>, as merely <s>dharmas</s>, as they truly are — [the self] is based on the body. And based on what [the self is based], one is afflicted and purified through pleasant and unpleasant [experiences], through wholesome and unwholesome [actions]. Therein, for the purpose of removing the confusion regarding the basis-object of the self, <s>kāyasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of the body) was established. For the purpose of removing the confusion regarding the experience-object of that very self, <s>vedanāsmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of feelings) was established. And where, in the mind (<s>citta</s>), mental organ (<s>manas</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), they are confused through grasping at self — for the purpose of removing the confusion regarding the self-object, <s>dharmasmṛtyupasthāna</s> (mindfulness of <s>dharmas</s>) was established.

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | yatra ca karma karoti | yadarthaṃ ca karoti | yaśca karma karoti | (yadarthaṃ ca karoti | yaśca [karma] karoti |) (..) yena ca (

children.text: ) karoti | tatsarvamekatyamabhisaṃkṣipya catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni vyavasthāpitāni | tatra kāye karoti | vedanārthaṃ | cittena kuśalākuśalairdharmaiḥ |
children.translated_text: one performs it — combining all of that together, the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) were established. Therein, one acts in the body; for the purpose of feeling; by the mind; through wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.

body.translated_text: Another interpretation: Where one performs action, for what purpose one performs it, who performs it, [for what purpose one performs it, who performs it,] and by what means

body.text: aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | yatra ca saṃkliśyate | viśudhyate | yataśca yaśca yena kliśyate | viśudhyate yataśca yaśca yena saṃkliśyate viśudhyate ca | tadekatyamabhisaṃkṣipya catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni vyavasthāpitāni | tatra kāye saṃkliśyate, viśudhyate ca | vedanābhyaścittaṃ dharmaiḥ saṃkliśyate | viśudhyate ca |
body.translated_text: Another interpretation: Where one is afflicted and purified; from what, who, and by what one is afflicted; and from what, who, and by what one is afflicted and purified — combining all of that together, the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> were established. Therein, one is afflicted and purified in the body; through feelings and mind one is afflicted; through <s>dharmas</s> one is afflicted and purified.

body.text: tatra smṛtyupasthānamiti [ko] 'rtha āha | yatra ca smṛtimupasthāpayati | yena ca smṛtimupasthāpayati | taducyate smṛtyupasthānaṃ | yatra smṛtimupasthāpayati | tadālambanasmṛtyupasthānaṃ yena smṛtimupasthāpayati | tatra yā prajñā smṛtiśca samādhisaṃgrāhikā tatsvabhāvasmṛtyupasthānaṃ | tadanye tatsaṃprayuktāścittacaitasikā dharmāḥ | saṃsargasmṛtyupasthānaṃ | api [ca] kāyavedanādhipateyo (

children.text: ) mārgaḥ samutpannaḥ kuśalaḥ sāsravaḥ | anāsravaśca [|] tatsmṛtyupasthānaṃ | sa punaḥ śrutamayaścintāmayo bhāvanāmayaśca | tatra śrutacintāmayaḥ | sāsrava eva [|] bhāvanāmayaḥ syātsāsravaḥ syādanāsravaḥ ||
children.translated_text: that is the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>. And that [path] is of three kinds: born of learning (<s>śrutamaya</s>), born of reflection (<s>cintāmaya</s>), and born of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmaya</s>). Therein, that born of learning and reflection is with outflows only. That born of cultivation may be with outflows or without outflows.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the meaning of <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> (foundation of mindfulness)? He says: That wherein one establishes <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and that by means of which one establishes <s>smṛti</s> — that is called <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s>. That wherein one establishes <s>smṛti</s> — that is the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> in terms of its object (<s>ālambana</s>). That by means of which one establishes <s>smṛti</s> — therein, the <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and the <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) that comprises <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) — that is the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> in terms of its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>). The other mental and mental-factor <s>dharmas</s> associated with it — that is the <s>smṛtyupasthāna</s> in terms of association (<s>saṃsarga</s>). Moreover, the path that has arisen, wholesome, with or without outflows, governed by body and feelings,

body.text: sa evaṃ caturṣu smṛtyupasthāneṣu kṛtaparicaya audāriko(kau)dārikaṃ viparyāsamapīnaya kuśalākuśaladharmābhijñaḥ | tadanantaramanutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya | utpannānāṃ prahāṇāya | anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpādāya | utpannānāṃ sthitaya iti vistareṇa pūrvavadyāvaccittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | pradadhāti ||
body.translated_text: He, having thus become practiced in the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness), even the coarse perversion having been removed, being one who knows wholesome and unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, [proceeds] thereupon: for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>; for the abandonment of arisen [evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>]; for the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>; for the stability [of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>] — in detail as before, up to: he takes up and maintains the mind.

body.text: tatra katame pāpakā akuśalā dharmā[ḥ] [|] yatkāmāvacaraṃ kliṣṭaṃ kāyakarma, vākkarma, manaskarma, kāyavāṅmanoduścaritasaṃgṛhītaṃ | yena tatsamutthāpakāḥ kleśāste punarye asamavahitā, asaṃmukhībhūtāste utpannā, (

children.text: ) ye samavahitāḥ saṃmukhībhūtāste utpannāḥ [|] tatra kuśalā dharmā ye tatprātipakṣikā dharmāduścaritaprātipakṣikā, nivaraṇaprātipakṣikāḥ, saṃyojanaprātipakṣikā vā tepyanutpannāstathaiva veditavyāḥ | utpannāśca pāpakā akuśalā dharmāstatra yadā anutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya spṛhāmutpādayati | praṇidhatte, sarveṇa sarvaṃ sarvathā notpādayiṣyāmītyevaṃ chandaṃ janayati | utpannānvā punaḥ samavahitānsarveṇasarvaṃ nādhivāsayiṣyāmi prahāsyāmi | prativinodayiṣyāmi ya[da]nutpanneṣu pāpakeṣvakuśaleṣu pūrva mevotpāda(|)spṛhāmutpādayati | praṇidhatte [|] nādhivāsaya(yi)tukāmo bhavati | ayamutpannānāṃ prahāṇāya [c]chandaḥ [|]
children.translated_text: those that are directly present and brought face-to-face — they are arisen. Therein, the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are their antidotes — antidotes to misconduct, antidotes to the <s>nīvaraṇas</s> (hindrances), antidotes to the <s>saṃyojanas</s> (fetters) — they too, when unarisen, should be understood in the same way; and when arisen. [Regarding] evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that have arisen — therein, when one generates the aspiration for the non-arising of unarisen evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one resolves: 'I shall not produce them in any way whatsoever!' — thus one generates the desire. Or again, regarding those that have arisen and are directly present: 'I shall not tolerate them in any way whatsoever! I shall abandon them! I shall dispel them!' — when, regarding unarisen evil, unwholesome [<s>dharmas</s>], one generates the aspiration [for their non-arising] even before [their arising] — not wishing to tolerate [them] — this is the desire for the abandonment of the arisen.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>? The afflicted bodily action, verbal action, and mental action belonging to the desire realm, comprised in bodily, verbal, and mental misconduct. And the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) that give rise to those — those that are not directly present, not brought face-to-face — they are unarisen,

body.text: te punaḥ pāpakā akuśalā dharmā atītavastvālambanā vā, anāgatavastvālambanā vā, vartamānaviṣayālambanā vā utpadyante, bhavanti | yenoktaviṣayālambanā[ḥ], pratyakṣaviṣayālambanāśca ye atītānāgatāvasthālambanāste, ye coktaviṣayālambanā, ye vartamānaviṣayālambanāste pratyakṣaviṣayālambanā[ḥ |]
body.translated_text: Those evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> arise with reference to an object-thing that is past, future, or present. Those with reference to the stated object and with reference to a directly perceived object — those with reference to the past and future are [beyond direct perception]; those with reference to the stated object and those with reference to the present are [with reference to] a directly perceived object.

body.text: tatra parokṣālambanānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya | utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya | vyāyacchate [|] pratyakṣaviṣayālambananānāṃ punaḥ | (

children.text: ) anutpannānāmanutpādāyotpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vīryamārabhate | tathā hi teṣāṃ dṛḍhatareṇa vīryāraṃbheṇānutpattiḥ | prahāṇaṃ vā bhavati | api ca mṛdumadhyānāṃ samavasthānāmanutpannānāmanutpādāya | utpannānāṃ prahāṇāya vyāyacchate | adhimātrāṇāṃ samavasthānāṃ anutpannānāmanutpādāya | utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vīryamārabhate | sa cedatīte ālambane carati | tathā carati | yathāsya tenālambanena kleśo notpadyate | sa cetpunaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣādutpadyate nādhivāsayati | prajahāti | vyantīkaroti | yathā atīte ālambane evamanāgate [a]pi veditavyam | evamayamanutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāyotpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya vyāyacchata ityucyate | sa cedayamvarttamāne ālambane carati, tathā tathā carati | yathā tenālambanena kleśo notpadyate | sa cetpunaḥ smṛtisaṃpramoṣādutpadyate | utpannaṃ nādhivāsayati | prajahāti | vinodayati | vyantīkaroti | evamanutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya | utpannānāñca prahāṇāya vīryamārabhata ityucyate |
children.translated_text: ) he arouses vigor for the non-arising of unarisen [unwholesome states] and for the abandonment of arisen [unwholesome states]. For indeed, through their more resolute arousal of vigor, there is either non-arising or abandonment. Moreover, for the arising of soft and middling

body.translated_text: Therein, for the non-arising of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> whose object is beyond direct perception, and for the abandonment of those that have arisen, one makes effort. And for those whose object is directly perceived,

body.text: santi pāpakā akuśalā dharmā ye saṃkalpavaśe (bale)notpadyante | na viṣayabalena | santi ye saṃkalpabalena ca | viṣayabalena ca | tatra saṃkalpabalenotpadyante | tadyathā viharataḥ | atītānāgatālambanā ye utpadyante | (

children.text: ) tatra saṃkleśavaśe(le)na ca viṣayabalena cotpadyate (nte) | tadyathā carato vartamānenālambanenotpadyante | avaśyaṃ tatrāyoniśaḥ saṃkalpo bhavati | tatra ye saṃkalpabalenotpadyante teṣāmanutpannānāmanutpādāya | utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya | vyāyacchate | tatra ye viṣayaba[lena] saṃkalpaba[lena] cotpadyante | teṣāmanutpannānāmanutpādāya | utpannānāñca prahāṇāya vyāyaccha(te) tatra ye viṣayabalena saṃkalpabalena cotpadyante | teṣāmanutpannānāmamanutpādāya utpannānāñca prahāṇāya vīryamārabhate | tatrānutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanu(mu)tpādāya chandaṃ janayatīti | ye kuśalādharmā apratilabdhā [a]saṃmukhībhūtasya (tāḥ) teṣāṃ pratilambhāya saṃmukhībhāvāya ca smṛti mutpādayati [|] cittaṃ praṇidhatte [|] tīvrā pratilabdhukāmatā | saṃmukhīkartukāmatā cāsya pratyupasthitā bhavati | ayamanutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpattaye |
children.translated_text: ) therein, those that arise through both the power of defilement and the power of the object — for example, those that arise from encountering a present object while going about one's activities. In that case, there is inevitably improper mental attention.

body.translated_text: there are evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> (states) that arise through the power of intention alone, not through the power of the object. There are those that arise through the power of both intention and the object. Therein, those that arise through the power of intention

children.translated_text: ) With reference to the accomplishment and reaching of the final goal through the repeated practice of <s>dharmas</s> that have been obtained and become directly present, he says: 'for the fulfillment through cultivation.' Therein he generates aspiration, and the mind

body.translated_text: He generates desire for the stability, non-loss, and fulfillment through cultivation of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. The arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s> are those that have been obtained and have become directly present.

body.text: tatra vyāyacchate | utpannānāṃ sthitaye, asaṃmoṣāya, vīryamārabhate | bhāvanāparipūraye, api ca mṛdumadhyānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpannānāmutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca sthitaye | asaṃmoṣāya vyāyacchate | adhimātrāṇāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpannānāmutpādāya, utpannānāṃ ca yāvad bhāvanāparipūraye vīryamārabhate |
body.translated_text: therein he exerts himself. For the stability and non-loss of arisen [wholesome states], he arouses vigor. For the fulfillment through cultivation — moreover, for the arising of unarisen soft and middling wholesome <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text: tatra cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | yadā taccittaṃ śamathabhāvanāyāmekāgratāyāṃ prayuktaṃ bhavati | anutpannānāṃ pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpādāya | evaṃ vistareṇa yāvadutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpannānāmutpādāya | utpannānāñca yāvad bhāvanāparipūraye vīryamārabhate | tatra cittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | yadā taccittaṃ śamathabhāvanāyāmekāgratāyāṃ prayuktaṃ bhavati | anutpannānāṃ (

children.translated_text: ) for the non-arising of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> — thus in detail up to: for the stability, non-loss, and fulfillment through cultivation of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>. And that, in that manner,

body.translated_text: therein he uplifts the mind. When that mind is engaged in the one-pointedness of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) cultivation — for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and so on

body.text: kathaṃ pradadhāti | punaruddhatamauddhatyābhiśaṃki vā pragrahakāle paśyati | tadā punarapyadhyātmamabhisaṃkṣipati | śamathāya praṇidadhāti | tānyetāni bhavanti | catvāri samyakprahāṇāni | kṛṣṇapakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpannānāmanutpādāya | utpannānāṃ ca prahāṇāya [c]chando vyāyāmo vīryārambhaḥ | cittapragrahaḥ | pradadhanamime dve samyakprahāṇe śuklapakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmanutpannānāmutpādāya [|]
body.translated_text: How does he apply the mind? Again, when he sees that the mind is agitated or suspects agitation, at the time for exertion, then again he internally restrains it and directs it toward <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding). These

body.text: vistareṇa dve samyakprahāṇe veditavye | tadyathā kṛṣṇapakṣyāṇāṃ tatraikaṃ samvaraṇaprahāṇaṃ yadutpannānāmpāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya [c]chandaṃ janayatīti vistareṇa | dvitīyaṃ prahāṇaprahāṇaṃ yadanutpannānāmanutpādāya [c]chandaṃ janayatīti vistareṇa, utpannaṃ hi saṃvarayitavyaṃ | pāpakaṃ ca vastu | anutpannaṃ ca yattadasamudācārataḥ prahīṇamevaṃ tadasaṃmukhībhāvataḥ prahātavyamiti kṛtvā | prahīṇasya prahāṇaṃ prahāṇaprahāṇa[ṃ] |
body.translated_text: In detail, two <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts) should be understood. Namely: regarding the dark side, one is the effort of restraint — that is, for the abandonment of arisen evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, the desire

body.text: tatra bhāvanāprahāṇamekaṃ yadāha | anutpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmutpādāyeti vistareṇa yāvaccittaṃ pragṛhṇāti, pradadhātīti | tathā hi kuśalā dharmā āsevyamānā, bhāvyamānā, apratilabdhāśca pratilabhyante | pratilabdhāśca sammukhīkriyante |
body.translated_text: therein, one is the effort of cultivation — as stated: 'For the arising of unarisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — in detail up to: 'he uplifts the mind, he applies the mind.' For indeed, wholesome <s>dharmas</s>,

body.text: tatrānurakṣaṇāprahāṇamekaṃ | yadāha | utpannānāṃ kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye | vistareṇa yāvaccittaṃ pragṛhṇāti | pradadhāti | tathā hi pratilabdheṣu saṃmukhīkṛteṣu ca | kuśaleṣu dharmeṣu yāvatpramādavarjanā apramādaniṣevaṇā ca | sā kuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ sthitaye, asammoṣāya, bhāvanāparipūraye | evamanutpannāḥ kuśalā dharmā anurakṣitā bhavantyayaṃ tāvatsamyakprahāṇānāṃ vistaravibhāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: therein, one is the effort of guarding — as stated: 'For the stability of arisen wholesome <s>dharmas</s>' — in detail up to: 'he uplifts the mind, he applies the mind.' For indeed, regarding the obtained

body.text: samāsata(sārtha)ḥ punaḥ katamaḥ | āha | kṛṣṇaśuklapākṣikasya tyāgātpunarvastunaḥ | prāptaye pūrvameva spṛhāyuktena bhavitavyaṃ | paryavasthānaprahāṇāya ca | astyāśayasampatprayogasampacca | paridīpitā bhavati | tatrāsyā (styā)śayasampat | chandajananatayā, prayogasampatpunaḥ vyāyāmavīryārambhacittapragrahāpramādadhanaiḥ | etāvacca yoginā karaṇīyaṃ | yatprahātavyasya vustanaḥ prahāṇāya, prāptavyasya vastunaḥ prāptaye pūrvameva spṛhājātena bhavitavyaṃ, paryavasthānaprahāṇāya, vīryamārabdhavyamanuśayaprahāṇāya ca, kālena kālaṃ śamathapragrahopekṣānimittāni (

children.translated_text: ) [the antidotes] should be cultivated. And for the abandonment of manifest afflictions and the abandonment of latent tendencies, those wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that are their antidotes should be gathered together. All of this, in its entirety, is accomplished through the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right efforts).

body.translated_text: What then is the summary meaning? He says: With regard to abandoning what belongs to the dark and bright sides, and again with regard to attaining the [wholesome] object, one should first be endowed with aspiration. For the abandonment of the manifest afflictions,

body.text: tatra catvāraḥ samādhayaḥ, tadyathā chandasamādhiḥ | vīryasamādhiḥ, cittasamādhiḥ, mīmāṃsāsamādhiśca |
body.translated_text: Therein, the four <s>samādhis</s> (concentrations) are: <s>chandasamādhi</s> (concentration born of desire), <s>vīryasamādhi</s> (concentration born of vigor), <s>cittasamādhi</s> (concentration born of mind), and <s>mīmāṃsāsamādhi</s> (concentration born of investigation).

body.text: tatra chanda(samādhi)madhipatiṃ kṛtvā yaḥ pratilabhyate samādhirayaṃ chandasamādhiḥ | vīryaṃ, cittaṃ, mīmāṃsāmadhipati kṛtvā pratilabhyate (pratilabhyate) samādhirayaṃ [...........] mīmānsā (māṃsā) samādhiḥ | yadā (

children.text: ) tāvadayaṃ chandameva kevalaṃ janayati | chandajātaśca tānpāpakānakuśalāndharmān svabhāvato, nidānata, ādīnavataḥ, pratipakṣataśca | samyagevopanidadhyāti | ekāgrāṃ smṛtiṃ pravarttayati | evaṃ kuśalā[n]dharmāssva (dharmānsva)bhāvato nidānataśca | akuśalato niḥsaraṇataḥ samyagevopanidadhyā (dhā)ti | ekāgrāṃ smṛtimavasthāpayati | tadbahulākārāmekāgratāṃ spṛśati | samavasthānasamudācāradūrīkaraṇayogena | na tvasyāpyanuśayamutpādayati | pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmayamapyucyate | chandādhipateyaḥ | sa (sā) atītā (te) vā, anāgatapratyutpanne vā punarālambane pāpakākuśalādharmāsthānīye (ladharmasthānīye) mṛdumadhyādhimātrakleśasamavasthānīye, anutpannasya vā anutpādāya, utpannasya vā prahāṇāya, vyāyacchamāno vīryamāramamāṇaḥ | tatrālambane vicaratyantasya vālambanasya svabhāvato nidānataḥ pratipakṣataśca | samyagupanidhyāyataḥ | ekāgrāṃ smṛtimupasthāpayato yattadbahulavihāriṇaścittaikāgratā utpadyate | samavasthānadūrīkaraṇayogena tvasyāpyanuśayamudghātayati | pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāmayaṃ vīryādhipateyaḥ | samādhi[ḥ |] līnamvā punaścittaṃ pragṛhṇataḥ | pragṛhītaṃ cittaṃ samādadhataḥ | kālena ca kālamadhyupekṣitaḥ | yatpāpakānāmakuśalānāndharmāṇāṃ (
children.translated_text: ) first he merely generates desire. And having generated desire, those evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, by their own nature, by their cause, by their danger, and by their antidote — he properly contemplates them with careful reflection.

children.text: ) pāpakākuśalā(la) dharmasthānīyānvayāt kuśala[ta]ḥ | kuśalāndharmān kuśalākuśalasthānīyāṃśca dharmān svabhāvato, nidānata, ādīnavataḥ, anuśaṃsataḥ, pratipakṣato, niḥsaraṇataḥ, samyagupani (da)dhyāyataḥ | ekāgratāṃ smṛtimupasthāpayataḥ | tadbahulavihāriṇo yā utpadyante cittasyaikāgratāḥ vistareṇa yāvadayaṃ | cittādhipateyaḥ samādhiḥ |
children.translated_text: ) following from the status of evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, with regard to the wholesome; the wholesome <s>dharmas</s> and those <s>dharmas</s> that stand in the position of both wholesome and unwholesome — by their own nature, by their cause, by their danger, by their benefit, and by

body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>samādhi</s> that is obtained by making desire the predominant factor — this is <s>chandasamādhi</s>. That obtained by making vigor, mind, or investigation the predominant factor

body.text: tatra ye pāpakākuśalā (la)dharmasthānīyā dharmā bhavanti | ayoniśo manasikurvataḥ | ta eva kuśaladharmasthānīyā bhavanti | yoniśo manasikurvataḥ | tasyaivaṃ samavasthāneṣu dūrīkṛteṣu | samavasthānapratipakṣe ca | samādhipramukheṣu dharmeṣvanutpanneṣu te pāpakā akuśalā dharmā dharma mudā haranti | tasyaivaṃ bhavati | kiṃ sataḥ samvidyamānānpāpakānakuśalāndharmān na pratisaṃvedayāmyāhosvidasataḥ | asaṃvidyamānānyanva(nnva)haṃ parimīmānse (māṃsaye) yaṃ | sa mīmānsā(māṃsā)manaskāramadhipatiṃ kṛtvā prahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ mīmānsa(māṃsa)te samyagevopanidhyāpayati | tadbahulavihārī ca spṛśati] cittasyaikāgratāṃ yena ca nirabhimāno bhavati | paryavasthānamātrakācya(cca)cittaṃ vimuktaṃ, (

children.text: ) na tu sarveṇa sarvaṃmanuśayebhyaḥ | tatpratipakṣāśca me samādhipramukhāḥ kuśalā dharmā[ś]ca pratilabdhā, bhāvitā, na tvanuśayaprātipākṣikā iti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti | ayamasyocyate mīmānsā (māṃsā)samādhiḥ |
children.translated_text: But not completely from all the latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>). He knows as it truly is: 'The antidotes, headed by <s>samādhi</s>, the wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, have been obtained and cultivated by me, but not those that counteract the latent tendencies.' This is called his <s>mīmāṃsāsamādhi</s> (concentration born of investigation).

body.translated_text: Therein, those <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that are bases for evil, unwholesome states, when attended to with improper attention (<s>ayoniśo manasikāra</s>) — those very same become bases for wholesome states when attended to with proper attention (<s>yoniśo manasikāra</s>). When such mental states are removed and their antidotes, the <s>dharmas</s> headed by <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), have not yet arisen, those evil unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> steal away the [wholesome] states. It occurs to him thus: 'Am I not experiencing evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s> that exist and are present? Or am I merely examining those that do not exist and are not present?' Making this investigation-attention predominant, he investigates whether they are abandoned or not, and properly examines. Dwelling much in that, he touches one-pointedness of mind, whereby he becomes free from conceit. The mind is liberated merely from the envelopment (<s>paryavasthāna</s>),

body.text: sa taṃ caturvidhaṃ samādhimadhipatiṃ kṛtvā paryavasthāneṣu dūrīkṛteṣu | sarveṇa sarvamanuśayasamudghātāya pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ, tatprātipākṣikāṇāñca kuśalānāṃ (|) dharmāṇāṃ samudāgamāya [c]chandaṃ janayati | vyāyacchata iti vistareṇa caturbhiḥ samyakprahāṇaiḥ prayujyate | tathā prayujyamānasya tathabhūtasyāṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā bhavanti | ye [a]syānuśayasamudghātāya ca pravarttante | samādhiparipūraye ca tadyathā- chandaḥ (

children.translated_text: 'At some time I shall fulfill <s>samādhi</s> and I shall abandon the latent tendencies.' The effort for the abandonment of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, extending to the cultivation of the antidote, with an application of practice and with faith not yet firmly applied,
While dwelling [thus], there is confident trust (<s>abhisaṃpratyaya</s>) and faith (<s>śraddhānatā</s>) in the higher attainment.

body.translated_text: He, making this fourfold <s>samādhi</s> predominant, having removed the envelopments, for the complete uprooting of all latent tendencies, for the abandonment of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>, and for the arising of wholesome <s>dharmas</s> that counteract them, generates zeal (<s>chanda</s>), makes effort — and so in detail he engages in the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right abandonings). For one so engaged and so constituted, there are eight <s>prahāṇasaṃskāras</s> (formations of abandonment) that operate for the uprooting of the latent tendencies and for the fulfillment of <s>samādhi</s> — namely: zeal,

body.text: tatra praśrabdhiḥ | yacchraddhāpramādapūrvaṃgamaṃ prāmodyaṃ, prītiḥ, prītamanasaścānupūrvā pāpakākuśalā dharmapakṣasya dauṣṭhulyasya pratipraśrabdhiḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>praśrabdhi</s> (tranquility) is: the joy (<s>prāmodya</s>) preceded by faith and diligence, the rapture (<s>prīti</s>), and for one of joyful mind, the sequential calming of the dysfunction (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) of the evil, unwholesome <s>dharma</s>-side.

body.text: tatra smṛtiryā navākārā navākārāyāścittasthiteḥ śamathapakṣyāyāḥ saṃgrāhikā |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness) is that which, in its nine aspects, collects the nine aspects of the mental abiding that belongs to the <s>śamatha</s> (calm) side.

body.text: chaṃdasaṃprajanye | yā vipaśyanāpakṣyā prajñā | tatra cetanāyāścittābhisaṃskāraḥ | prahīṇāprahīṇato mīmānsa(māṃsa) mānasya yaścittābhisaṃskāraḥ śamathavipaśyanānukūlaḥ kāyakarma vākkarma samutthāpayati |
body.translated_text: As for zeal and clear comprehension (<s>saṃprajanya</s>): the wisdom that belongs to the <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) side. Therein, the mental formation of <s>cetanā</s> (volition): the mental formation that is favorable to <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>, that which investigates whether [defilements are] abandoned or not, and produces bodily and verbal action.

body.text: tatropekṣayā atītānāgatapratyutpanneṣu pāpakākuśalādharmāsthānīyeṣu carataḥ cittābhisaṃkleśaścittaṃgamatā | ābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ prahīṇatāmanuśayānāṃ paricchinatti jānāti | yaduta viṣayaviparokṣayā cetanayā viṣayaviparokṣayā cā(co)pekṣayā | ime [a]ṣṭau prahāṇasaṃskārā bhavanti | te caiteṣṭau (sa caiṣo 'ṣṭa) prahāṇasaṃskārayogo bhavatyanuśayasamudghātāya | tatra chanda(cchanda)śca, eta(ṣa) eva yo vyāyāmaḥ idaṃ vīryaṃ, yāśraddhā sā śuddhā, yā ca praśrabdhiryā ca smṛtiryacca saṃprajanyaṃ | yā ca cetanā, yā copekṣā | aya (idaṃ ?)mupādāya | tadidaṃ sarvamabhisamasya ye ca pūrvakāśchandasamādhayaḥ | ye ca ime prahāṇasaṃskārāḥ prahīṇeṣvanuśayeṣu, (

children.text: ) parikṣipte samādhau, chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipāda ityucyante(te) | vīryacittamīmānsā (māṃsā) samādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipāda ityucyate |
children.translated_text: And <s>samādhi</s> is fulfilled — [they] are called the <s>chandasamādhiprahāṇasaṃskārasamanvāgata ṛddhipāda</s> (base of spiritual power endowed with the concentration of zeal and formations of abandonment). [Similarly,] it is called the <s>ṛddhipāda</s> endowed with the concentration of energy, mind, and investigation together with the formations of abandonment.

body.translated_text: Therein, through <s>upekṣā</s> (equanimity), while moving among past, future, and present objects that are bases for evil, unwholesome states, [one recognizes] the mental defilement and the mental incapacity. By these two causes, he discerns and knows the state of abandonment of the latent tendencies — namely, through volition that is clear regarding the object and through equanimity that is clear regarding the object. These are the eight formations of abandonment. And this eightfold practice of the formations of abandonment is for the uprooting of the latent tendencies. Therein, zeal — and that very effort — this is <s>vīrya</s> (energy); that faith — it is pure; and that tranquility, that mindfulness, that clear comprehension, that volition, and that equanimity — taking all of this together, comprehending it all — the prior <s>chandasamādhis</s> (concentrations born of zeal) together with these formations of abandonment, when the latent tendencies are abandoned,

body.text: kena kāraṇena ṛddhipāda ityucte | āha | tadyathā | yasya pādaḥ samvidyate so [a]bhikramapratikrama(ma)parākramasamartho bhavati | evameva yasyaite dharmāḥ saṃvidyante | eṣa ca samādhiḥ saṃvidyayate | paripūrṇaḥ [|] sa evaṃ pariśuddhe citte, paryavadāte, anaṃgaṇe, vigatopakleśe, ṛjubhūte karmaṇyasthite, āniṃjyaprāpte, abhikramapratikramasamartho bhavati | lokottarāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prāptaye, sparśanāyai | eṣā hi parā ṛddhiḥ, parā samṛddhiḥ | yaduta lokottarā dharmāstenocyante (te?) ṛddhipāda iti ||
body.translated_text: For what reason are they called <s>ṛddhipāda</s> (bases of spiritual power)? He says: Just as one who possesses feet is capable of advancing, retreating, and exerting strength — in the same way, one in whom these <s>dharmas</s> are present and this <s>samādhi</s> is present in its fullness, when the mind is thus purified, cleansed, stainless, free from minor defilements, made straight, workable, stable, and having reached imperturbability — he becomes capable of advancing and retreating for the attainment and direct realization of supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>) <s>dharmas</s>. For this is the supreme <s>ṛddhi</s> (spiritual power), the supreme prosperity — namely, the supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. Therefore they are called <s>ṛddhipādas</s>.

body.text: sa evaṃ samādhipratiṣṭhitaḥ | samādhiṃ niśritya | (

children.text: ) [adhi]cittaṃ śikṣā[yā]madhiprajñaṃ śikṣāyāṃ yogaṃ karoti | tatrāsya yogaṃ kurvataḥ | pareṣāṃ cādhigame śāstuḥ śrāvakāṇāṃ ca yo [a]bhisaṃpratyayaḥ | prasādaḥ, śraddhānatā | samāpattyarthena śraddhendriyamityucyate | kutra punarasyādhipatyaṃ | āha | lokottaradharmotpattipramukhānāṃ vīryasmṛtisamādhiprajñānāmutpattaye ādhipatyaṃ | ye [a]pi te vīryādayaḥ teṣāmapi lokottaradharmotpattaye ādhipatyaṃ | yāvat pratipattaye ādhipatyaṃ | yāvat prajñayā lokottaradharmotpattaye | ādhiopatyaṃ | tainaitāni śraddhādīni paṃcendriyāṇi bhavanti |
children.translated_text: Applies himself to the training in higher mind (<s>adhicitta</s>) and to the training in higher wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>). While he applies himself thus, the confident trust, faith, and conviction in the attainment of others, of the Teacher, and of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> (disciples) — in the sense of attainment, this is called <s>śraddhendriya</s> (faculty of faith). And where does it hold sovereignty? He says: It holds sovereignty for the arising of energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, which are foremost in the arising of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>. And those [faculties] beginning with energy also hold sovereignty for the arising of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>, and sovereignty for practice, and sovereignty for the arising of supramundane <s>dharmas</s> through wisdom. Thus these are the five <s>indriyas</s> (faculties) beginning with faith.

body.translated_text: He, thus established in <s>samādhi</s>, relying on <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: ) śakyate | avamṛdituṃ | asaṃhāyā(ryā)sā śraddhā devena vā, māreṇa vā, brahmaṇā vā | kenacidvā punarloke, sahadharmeṇa kleśaparyavasthānena vā tena sā anavamṛdyetyucyate | tatpramukhāstatpūrvaṃgamā ye vīryādayastepibalānītyucyante | taiḥ sa balairbalavān sarvaṃ mārabalaṃ vijitya prayujyate | āsravāṇāṃ kṣayāya | tasmādbalānītyucyante |
children.translated_text: Not be crushed? This faith is unassailable — by a god, by <s>Māra</s>, by <s>Brahma</s>, or by anyone in the world, or by any affliction-envelopment together with its <s>dharma</s>-counterpart. Therefore it is called 'not to be crushed.' Those [powers] beginning with energy, which are preceded by and led by that [faith], are also called <s>balas</s> (powers). Empowered by those powers, being powerful, having conquered the entire force of <s>Māra</s>, he applies himself to the destruction of the <s>āsravas</s> (outflows). Therefore they are called powers.

body.translated_text: Furthermore, for one who, having previously [attained something], recognizes the higher attainment subsequent to the earlier, the confident trust, faith, and conviction in the attainment of those higher supramundane <s>dharmas</s> in accordance with that [prior experience] — in the sense of not being crushable, this is called <s>śraddhābala</s> (power of faith). By what then can it

body.text: tatra yaśca(yacca) śraddhendriyaṃ, yacca śraddhābalaṃ caturṣvetadavetya prasādeṣu draṣṭavyaṃ | tatkasya hetoḥ | yo 'sau samyaktvanyāmāvakrāntasyāvetya prasādaḥ | sa taddhetukastatpratyastannidānaḥ | tasmāddhetuphalasambandhena tasyāstadadhipatiphalamiti kṛtvā | tatra draṣṭavyamityuktaṃ bhagavatā | na tu taccharīratāṃ tallakṣaṇatāṃ [|] tatra vīryendriyaṃ caturṣu samyakprahāṇeṣu draṣṭavyaṃ | (tatkasya hetoḥ) yāni (tāni) katamāni | samyakprahāṇāni yāni darśanaprahātavyakleśaprahāṇāya prāyogikāṇi samyakprahāṇāni, tānyatra samyakprahāṇānyabhipretāni tāni hyatyantatāyai pāpakānāmakuśalānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ prahāṇāya samvarttante ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>śraddhendriya</s> (faith-faculty) and the <s>śraddhābala</s> (faith-power) should be seen in the four <s>āvetyaprasādas</s> (confirmed confidences). For what reason? The confirmed confidence of one who has entered the <s>samyaktvanyāma</s> (certainty of rightness) — that is caused by them, conditioned by them, originating from them. Therefore, by the connection of cause and result, and because they are its dominant result, it is said to be seen therein. But not as having the same identity or the same characteristic. Therein, the <s>vīryendriya</s> (energy-faculty) should be seen in the four <s>samyakprahāṇas</s> (right abandonings). (For what reason?) Which are those right abandonings? Those preliminary right abandonings that are for the abandonment of defilements to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>) — those are the right abandonings intended here, for they serve for the final abandonment of evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>.
