children.translated_text: Four establishments of mindfulness serve for the abandonment of the undiscriminated and the discriminated [types of] error (<s>viparyāsa</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>smṛtīndriya</s> (mindfulness-faculty) should be seen in the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (establishments of mindfulness). These

body.text: tatra samādhīndriyaṃ caturṣu (sthā) dhyāneṣu draṣṭavyaṃ | yāni dhyānānyagāmitāyāṃ prāyogikāni (ṇi) tatra prajñendriyaṃ caturdhvāryasatyeṣu draṣṭavyamiti | yatsatyajñānaṃ caturdhṇāmāryasatyānāmabhisamāya samvarttante (te) | śrāmaṇyaphalaprāptate, pa(ya)pendriyāṇi | evaṃ balāni veditavyāni | sa eṣāmindriyāṇāme teṣāṃ ca balānāmāsevanānvayādbhāvanānvayādabahulīkārānvayānnirvedhabhāgīyāni kuśalamūlānyutpādayati | mṛdumadhyādhimātrāṇi | tadyathā ūṣmagatāni | mūrdhagatāni | mūrdhānaḥ satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayaḥ laukikāna(da)gradharmāttadyathā | kaścideva puruṣaḥ agninā agnikāyaṃ karttukāmaḥ | agninārthī adharāraṇyāmuttarāraṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpyāsa [-]nnutsahate, ghaṭate, vyāyacchate | tathotsahato, ghaṭato, vyāyacchataśca | tatprathamato 'dharāraṇyāmūṣmā jāyate | saiva (

children.text: ) coṣmā | abhivardhamānā ūrdhvamāgacchati | bhūyasyā mātrayā abhivarddhamānā [|] nirarcciṣamagniṃ pātayatyagnipatanasamanantarameva cārcirjāyate | yathā arcciṣā utpannayā (nena) jātayā (tena) saṃjātayā (tena) agnikāyaṃ karoti | yathā abhimanthana vyāyāma evaṃ pañcānāmindriyāṇāmāsevanā draṣṭavyā | yathā adharaṇyā tatprathamata eva ūṣmagataṃ bhavati | evamūṣmagatāni draṃṣṭavyāni | pūrvaṃgamāni | nimittabhūtāni | agnisthānīyānāmanāsravāṇāṃ dharmāṇāṃ kleśaparidāhakānāmutpattaye | yathā tasyaivoṣmaṇa ūrdhva[mā]gamanamevaṃ mūrdhānodraṣṭavyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Warmth, as it increases, rises upward. Increasing further in greater measure, it produces fire without flame; and immediately upon the falling of the fire, a flame arises. Just as with the arisen flame, fire is produced — so too should the repeated practice of the five faculties be understood as like the rubbing-effort. Just as warmth first arises in the lower fire-stick — so should the <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat stage) be understood: as the precursor, the sign, for the arising of the outflow-free (<s>anāsrava</s>) <s>dharmas</s>, which are analogous to fire and which burn the defilements. Just as the rising upward of that very warmth — so should <s>mūrdhānas</s> (the summit stage) be understood.

body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>samādhīndriya</s> (concentration-faculty) should be seen in the four <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations). Those <s>dhyānas</s> that are preliminary to [the attainment of] the irreversible state (<s>agāmitā</s>). Therein, the <s>prajñendriya</s> (wisdom-faculty) should be seen in the four Noble Truths, as that truth-knowledge which serves for the full comprehension (<s>abhisamaya</s>) of the four Noble Truths, and for the attainment of the fruits of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>). Thus the [five] faculties. The [five] powers should be understood in the same way. Through the repeated practice, cultivation, and frequent engagement of these faculties and powers, he produces the <s>nirvedhabhāgīya kuśalamūlas</s> (wholesome roots of the penetrative class) — mild, middling, and intense — namely: <s>ūṣmagata</s> (the heat stage), <s>mūrdhagata</s> (the summit stage), <s>mūrdhānas</s> (summits), <s>satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayaḥ</s> (patient acceptances conforming to the truths), and <s>laukikāgradharma</s> (supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>). It is like this: a certain person, wishing to make fire with fire, desiring fire, having placed the upper fire-stick upon the lower fire-stick, makes effort, strives, and exerts himself. As he thus makes effort, strives, and exerts himself, first warmth arises in the lower fire-stick. That very

body.text: yathā dhūmaprādurbhāva evaṃ satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayo draṣṭavyāḥ || yathāgneḥ patanaṃ nirarcciṣa evaṃ laukikā agradharmā draṣṭavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Just as the appearance of smoke — so should <s>satyānulomāḥ kṣāntayaḥ</s> (patient acceptances conforming to the truths) be understood. Just as the falling of fire without flame — so should the <s>laukikāgradharma</s> (supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>) be understood.

children.translated_text: These are the limbs [of that realization]. For that realization as it truly is is encompassed by seven limbs: three belonging to the <s>śamatha</s> (calm) side, three belonging to the <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight) side, and one belonging to both sides. Therefore they are called <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening).

body.translated_text: Just as the arising of flame immediately after that — so should the supramundane, outflow-free <s>dharmas</s> be understood, which arise immediately after the five faculties comprised in the supreme worldly <s>dharma</s>. What then are those? He says: the seven <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening). That which is the realization as it truly is (<s>yathābhūtāvabodha</s>) — for a person who has entered the <s>samyaktvanyāma</s> (certainty of rightness),

body.text: tatra yaśca dharmavinayaḥ | yacca vīryaṃ, yā ca prītiritīmāni trīṇi vipaśyanāpakṣyāṇi | tatra yā ca praśrabdhiryaśca samārdhiyā copekṣā itīmāni trīṇi śamathapakṣyāṇi [|] smṛtirabhayapakṣyā(s) sarvatragetyucyate | sa tasmin samaye tatprathamato bodhyaṃgalābhācchaikṣo bhavati | prātipadaḥ [|] darśanaprahātavyāścāsya kleśāḥ prahīṇā bhavanti | bhāvanāprahātavyāścāvaśiṣṭāḥ [|] (

children.text: ) sa teṣāṃ prahāṇāya triskandhamāryāṣṭaṃgaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayati |
children.translated_text: For their abandonment, he cultivates the <s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s> (Noble Eightfold Path), which consists of three <s>skandhas</s> (groups).

body.translated_text: Therein, the investigation of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmavicaya</s>), energy (<s>vīrya</s>), and rapture (<s>prīti</s>) — these three belong to the <s>vipaśyanā</s> side. Therein, tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>) — these three belong to the <s>śamatha</s> side. Mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>) belongs to both sides and is called 'all-pervading.' At that time, from the first attainment of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s>, he becomes a <s>śaikṣa</s> (learner), one who has entered the path. The defilements to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>) are abandoned for him, and those to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>) remain.

body.text: tatra yā ca samyagdṛṣṭiryaśca samyaksaṃkalpaḥ, yaśca samyagvyāyāmaḥ | ayaṃ prajñāskandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right view), <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention), and <s>samyagvyāyāma</s> (right effort) — this is the <s>prajñāskandha</s> (wisdom group).

body.text: tatra ye samyakkarmāntājīvāḥ | ayaṃ śīlaskandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>samyakkarmānta</s> (right action) and <s>samyagājīva</s> (right livelihood) — this is the <s>śīlaskandha</s> (morality group).

body.text: tatra yā ca samyaksmṛtiḥ, yaśca samyaksamādhirayaṃ samādhiskandhaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>samyaksmṛti</s> (right mindfulness) and <s>samyaksamādhi</s> (right concentration) — this is the <s>samādhiskandha</s> (concentration group).

body.text: kena kāraṇenāryāṣṭāṃgo mārga ityucyate | āha | āryasya śaikṣasya dṛṣṭapadasyāyaṃ mārga iyaṃ pratipadaṣṭābhiraṃgaiḥ saṃgṛhītā(ḥ) || apariśeṣaḥ | sarvakleśaprahāṇāya vimuktisākṣātkriyāyai tenocyate āryāṣṭāṃgo mārgaḥ |
body.translated_text: For what reason is it called the <s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s> (Noble Eightfold Path)? He says: This is the path of the noble one, the trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>), who has seen the truth; this is the practice comprised of eight factors. It is without remainder — for the abandonment of all defilements and for the direct realization of liberation. Therefore it is called the Noble Eightfold Path.

body.text: tatra yaśca bodhyaṃgakāle tattvāvabodhaḥ (||) pratilabdhaḥ, pratilabhya ca yattasyaiva prajñayā vyavasthānaṃ karoti || yathāvigatasyāvabodhasya, tadubhayamekatyamabhisaṃkṣipya samyagdṛṣṭirityucyate | tāṃ samyagdṛṣṭimadhipatiṃ kṛtvā | yannaiṣkramyasaṃkalpaṃ saṃkalpayatyavyāpādasaṃkalpamavihinsā(hiṃsā)saṃkalpamayamucyate samyaksaṃkalpaḥ | sa cettāvadvitarkeṣu cittaṃ krāmati | sa evaṃ rūpādvitarkādvitarkayati [|] sa cetpunaḥ kathāyāṃ cittaṃ (

children.text: ) krāmati | samyagdṛṣṭimadhipatiṃ kṛtvā tene(na) kuśalātsaṃkalpāṃ (lasaṃkalpāṃ) dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayati | sāsya bhavati samyagvāk |
children.translated_text: making right view predominant, by that wholesome intention he speaks <s>Dharma</s>-talk. This is his <s>samyagvāc</s> (right speech).

body.translated_text: Therein, the realization of reality obtained at the time of the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening), and the determination made by that very wisdom after obtaining it — as to the nature of the realization that has occurred — condensing both of these into one, it is called <s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s> (right view). Making that right view predominant, when one forms the intention of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>), the intention of non-malice (<s>avyāpāda</s>), and the intention of non-harming (<s>avihiṃsā</s>) — this is called <s>samyaksaṃkalpa</s> (right intention). And if his mind inclines toward discursive thoughts, he thinks in such a way as to avoid [unwholesome] discursive thought. And if again his mind inclines toward speech,

body.text: sa ceccīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārairatīthī(rthī)bhavati | tatparyeṣaṇāmvāpadyate | so 'bhikramaḥ | pratikrame saṃprajānamvi(dvi)hārī bhavatyālokitavyavalokite [|] tasmiṃjita (saṃmiṃjita) prasārite | sāṃghaṭīcīvarapātradhāraṇe, aśitapītakhāditāsvādite | vihāragato vā punaḥ paryeṣiteṣu cīvarādiṣu gate, sthite, niṣaṇṇe | yāvannidrāklama[prati]vinodane saṃprajānadvihārī bhavati | ayamasyocyate samyakkarmāntaḥ | sa taccīvaraṃ yāvadbhaiṣajyapariṣkāraṃ dharmeṇa paryeṣate | yāvanmithyā [..........] dharmavivarjitaḥ so 'sya bhavati | samyagājīvaḥ |
body.translated_text: And if he needs robes, almsfood, bedding and lodging, and medicine and requisites for the sick, and he undertakes the search for them — in his going forth and returning, he dwells with clear comprehension; in looking forward and looking around, in bending and extending, in wearing the outer robe, upper robe, and carrying the bowl, in eating, drinking, chewing, and tasting, on entering the dwelling, and in the search for robes and other requisites, while standing, sitting, and up to dispelling drowsiness and fatigue, he dwells with clear comprehension. This is called his <s>samyakkarmānta</s> (right action). He seeks those robes through to medicine and requisites by <s>dharma</s>, avoiding what is wrong and devoid of <s>dharma</s>. This is his <s>samyagājīva</s> (right livelihood).

body.text: ye punarviratisaṃgṛhītāḥ | samyakkarmāntājīvāḥ | te anena pūrvameva manaskāralābhādbodhyaṃgaireva saha labdhā bhavanti | yopyāpakāntāni śīlānyucyante | kena kāraṇena dīrgha kālaṃ hyetadāryāṇāṃ satāṃ samyaggatānāmiṣṭaṃ kāntaṃ priyaṃ mana āpaṃ kaccidahaṃ tadvāgduścaritasya, kāyaduścaritasya, mithyājīvasyākaraṇaṃ | (

children.text: ) samvaraṃ pratilabheyaṃ | yadasya dīrgharātramiṣṭaṃ | kāntaṃ priyaṃ mana āpaṃ tadanena tasminsamaye pratilabdhaṃ bhavati | tasmādāpakāntamityucyate | tathā hi sa labdheṣvāpakānteṣu śīleṣu, na saṃprajā[nā]no mṛṣāṃ vācaṃ bhāṣate | na saṃvidhya prāṇinaṃ (|) jīvitād vyaparopayati | nādattamādatte [|] na (|) kāmeṣu mithyā carati | na cādharmeṇa cīvarādīni paryeṣate | iti tānyāpakāntāni śīlānyadhipatiṃ kṛtvā mārgabhāvanākāle yāvatpravartate | yacca kāyakarma yaścājīvaḥ tepi samyagvākkarmāntājīvā ityucyante |
children.translated_text: What he has long wished for, desired, loved, and found pleasing — that has been obtained by him at that time. Therefore they are called <s>āpakānta</s> (wished-for). For indeed, established in those wished-for moral precepts, he does not knowingly speak falsehood, does not intentionally deprive a living being of life, does not take what is not given, does not engage in sexual misconduct, and does not seek robes and other requisites by non-<s>dharma</s>. Thus, making those wished-for moral precepts predominant, during the time of path cultivation — whatever bodily conduct and whatever livelihood [he engages in] — these too are called right speech, right action, and right livelihood.

body.translated_text: Now, the right action and livelihood that are comprised of abstinence — those have already been obtained together with the <s>bodhyaṅgas</s> (factors of awakening) from the earlier attainment of mental attention. And what are called the <s>āpakānta</s> (wished-for) moral precepts? For what reason? For a long time indeed, this has been wished for, desired, loved, pleasing to the mind, by the noble and good ones who are rightly practiced: 'May I obtain restraint from verbal misconduct, bodily misconduct, and wrong livelihood.'

body.text: tasya samyagadṛṣṭisamyaksaṃkalpa (ḥ |) vākkarmāntājīvasanniśrayeṇa bhāvanāprayuktasya | yacchando (yaśchando), vīryaṃ, vyāyāmo, niṣkramaḥ, parākramasthāma āraṃbhaḥ | cetasaḥ saṃpragrahaḥ | sātatyamayamucyate | samyagvyāyāmaśamathaḥ | yaccatvāri smṛtyupasthānānyadhipatiṃ kṛtvā aviparyāyasaṃgṛhītā smṛtiḥ navākārā navākāracittasthitisaṃgrāhikā [|] iyamucyate samyaksmṛtiḥ | samyaksamādhiśca |
body.translated_text: For him, relying on right view, right intention, [right] speech, action, and livelihood, while engaged in cultivation — the desire, vigor, exertion, effort, striving, strength, and initiative; the restraint of the mind; and continuity — this is called <s>samyagvyāyāma</s> (right effort) and <s>śamatha</s> (calm). And making the four <s>smṛtyupasthānas</s> (foundations of mindfulness) predominant, the mindfulness that is comprised of non-error, the nine-aspected [mindfulness] that gathers the nine-aspected mental stability — this is called <s>samyaksmṛti</s> (right mindfulness) and <s>samyaksamādhi</s> (right concentration).

body.text: tadetatsarvamabhisamasya āryāṣṭāṃgo mārgaścārakaraṇīye ca vihārakaraṇīye cāvasthitaḥ |
body.translated_text: All of this, having been thoroughly comprehended, the <s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s> (Noble Eightfold Path) is established in both the domain of conduct (<s>cārakaraṇīya</s>) and the domain of meditation (<s>vihārakaraṇīya</s>).

body.text: tatra samyagvākkarmāntājīvāḥ cārakaraṇīye [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, right speech, right action, and right livelihood pertain to the domain of conduct.

body.text: vihārakaraṇīyaṃ punardvividhaṃ | śamatho vipaśyanā ca [|] tatra yā samyagdṛṣṭiḥ | yaśca samyaksaṃkalpaḥ | yaśca samyagvyāyāma iyaṃ vipaśyanā |
body.translated_text: The domain of meditation is of two kinds: <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight). Therein, right view, right intention, and right effort — this is <s>vipaśyanā</s>.

body.text: tatra yā ca samyaksamṛtiryaśca samyaksamādhisyaṃ śamathaḥ | evaṃ pariśuddhān samyagvākkarmāntājīvānniśritya śamathavipaśyanāṃ bhāvayati | kālena kālaṃ niravaśeṣasaṃyojanaprahāṇaṃ sākṣātkarotyagraphalamarhattvaṃ, prāpnoti | prākarṣikaśca (kañca) bhāvanāmārgaḥ (rgaṃ) [|] kālāntarābhyāsena kleśān prajahāti | jñānamātrapratibaddhavastudarśanamārgaḥ jñānotpattimātreṇa kleśān prajahātyanena kāraṇena vākkarmāntājīvā bhāvanāmārge vyavasthāpitāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, right mindfulness and right concentration — this is <s>śamatha</s>. Thus, relying on the purified right speech, action, and livelihood, one cultivates <s>śamatha</s> and <s>vipaśyanā</s>. From time to time one directly realizes the complete abandonment of all fetters, and attains the supreme fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>. And the culminating path of cultivation — by repeated practice over time one abandons the defilements. The path of seeing the object to which knowledge alone is bound — by the mere arising of knowledge one abandons the defilements. For this reason, speech, action, and livelihood are established in the path of cultivation.

body.text: iti ya evameṣāmanayā ānupūrvyā saptatriṃśatāṃ bodhapakṣyāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmabhyāsaḥ, paricayaḥ | iyamucyate bodhipakṣyā bhāvanā |
body.translated_text: Thus, the repeated practice and familiarization with the thirty-seven <s>bodhipakṣya dharmas</s> (factors conducive to awakening) in this sequence — this is called the cultivation of the factors conducive to awakening.

body.text: tatra bhāvanāphalaṃ katamat | āha | catvāri śrāmaṇyaphalāni | srota āpattiphalaṃ, sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ | anāgāmiphalamagraphalamarhattvaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the fruit of cultivation? He says: The four fruits of the ascetic life (<s>śrāmaṇyaphala</s>): the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotāpattiphala</s>), the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>), the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>), and the supreme fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>.

body.text: tatra katamacchrāmaṇyaṃ | katamatphalaṃ | āha | mārgaḥ, kleśaprahāṇaṃ phalaṃ | api ca pūrvotpannasya mārgasya paścādutpanno mārgaḥ | phalaṃ, madhyo, viśiṣṭo (

children.text: ) vā, punaḥ [|] tatra kena kāraṇena catvāri vyavasthāpitāni | āha | caturvidhakleśaprahāṇapratipakṣatayā | tadyathā nirvastukānāṃ kleśānāmapāyagamanahetubhūtānāṃ prahāṇātpratipakṣotpādācca srota āpattiphalaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ | trayāṇāṃ tu saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇādvyavasthāpitaṃ | bhagavatā triṣu pakṣeṣu, gṛhipakṣe, durākhyātadharmavinaya pakṣe ca, trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ mārgotpattaye vivṛddhākaratvāt | tatra gṛhipakṣe satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ | yayā yamādita eva na prayutyata ityādita u[t]trāsikā satkāyadṛṣṭiḥ | durākhyātedharmavinaye śīlavrataparāmarśaḥ | uccalitasyāpi mithyāpratipādayati | yenāryamārgo notpadyate | svākhyāte dharmavinaye vicikitsātaścoccalitaśca bhavati | na ca mithyāpratipannaḥ | api svābhyāsāttasya yāvad yathābhūtadarśanaṃ na bhavati | jñeyavastuni tāvatkāṃkṣā vimatayo vibandhakarā bhavanti | mārgasyotpattaye | anena tāvatkāraṇena srota āpattiphalavyavasthānaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Furthermore, for what reason are four [fruits] established? He says: Because they serve as antidotes to four types of defilement-abandonment. Namely, from the abandonment of defilements that are insubstantial [i.e., based on wrong views] and that are causes for rebirth in the lower realms, and from the arising of their antidote, the fruit of stream-entry is established. It is established through the abandonment of three fetters (<s>saṃyojana</s>). The <s>Bhagavān</s> has established it in [relation to] three groups: the householder group, the group of the wrongly-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, and [the properly proclaimed one]. [The three fetters] serve as the growth-factor for the arising of the path in these three. Therein, in the householder group: <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> (view of the perishable collection), by which one does not engage [in practice] from the very beginning — this is the terrifying <s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s> from the start. In the wrongly-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>: <s>śīlavrataparāmarśa</s> (clinging to rules and rituals), which leads even one who has moved forward astray. By which the noble path does not arise. In the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>: <s>vicikitsā</s> (doubt), whereby even one who has moved forward [may waver], though he is not wrongly practicing. But due to his habitual tendencies, until he has vision as it really is, there are doubts, hesitations, and hindrances regarding the knowable object that obstruct the arising of the path. For this reason, the establishment of the fruit of stream-entry.

body.translated_text: Therein, what is the ascetic life? What is the fruit? He says: The path [is the ascetic life]; the abandonment of defilements is the fruit. Moreover, the path that arises later, [in relation to] the previously arisen path, is the fruit — whether middling or superior.

body.text: tasyāsya srota āpannasya paraṃ sapta bhavā avaśiṣṭā bhavanti | sa cāsyajanma prabandhaḥ | yadā janmaprābandhikānkleśānprajahāti | devabhavasaṃgṛhītānmanuṣyasaṃgṛhītāṃśca [|] yeṣāṃ prahāṇātparamekaṃ devabhavamabhinirvarttayatyekaṃ manuṣyabhavaṃ [|] tasminsamaye sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate |
body.translated_text: For this stream-enterer, at most seven existences remain. And this succession of births — when he abandons the defilements pertaining to the succession of births, those included in divine existence and those included in human existence, by the abandonment of which he brings about at most one divine existence and one human existence — at that time, the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmiphala</s>) is established.

body.text: yadā tu devabhavameva kevalamabhinirvarttayati | iha pratyāgamajanmikaṃ kleśaṃ prahāya tadā anāgāmiphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate || sarvabhavopapattisaṃvarttanīyakleśaprahāṇādagraphalamarhattvaphalaṃ vyavasthāpyate |
body.translated_text: When, however, he brings about only divine existence alone, having abandoned the defilement pertaining to return to this [world], then the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmiphala</s>) is established. From the abandonment of all defilements that lead to rebirth in any existence, the supreme fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> is established.

body.text: tatpunaḥ sakṛdāgāmiphalaṃ trayāṇāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇādrāgadveṣamohānāṃ ca | tanutvād bhagavatā vyavasthāpitaṃ | paṃcānāmavarabhāgīyānāṃ saṃyojanānāṃ prahāṇādanāgāmiphalaṃ | paryādāya sarvakleśaprahāṇādarhattvaphala midamucyate bhāvanāphalaṃ |
body.translated_text: Furthermore, the fruit of once-returning is established by the <s>Bhagavān</s> through the abandonment of the three fetters and the attenuation of passion, hatred, and delusion. Through the abandonment of the five lower fetters (<s>avarabhāgīya saṃyojana</s>), the fruit of non-returning [is established]. Through the exhaustive abandonment of all defilements, the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s> — this is called the fruit of cultivation.

body.text: tatra ye rāgadveṣamohamānavitarkacariteṣu (tāḥ) pudgaleṣu (lāḥ) pūrvaṃ [taiḥ] tāvaccaritaviśodhane ālambane caritaṃ viśodhayitavyaṃ | tataḥ paścāccittasthitimadhigacchanti | teṣāṃ pratiniyatameva tadālambanamavaśyaṃ taistenālambanena prayoktavyaṃ | samabhāgacaritasya tu yatra priyārohitā | tatra tena prayoktavyaṃ kevalaṃ cittasthitaye | na tu caritaviśuddhaye | yathā samabhāgacarita evaṃ mandarajasko veditavyaḥ | ayaṃ tveṣāṃ viśeṣo rāgādicaritaḥ prayujyamānaścireṇādhigantā bhavati | samabhāgacarito nāticireṇa, mandarajaskastu āśu tvarita tvaritaṃ cittasthitamadhigacchati | tatroktāni pūrvaṃ rāgacaritānāṃ pudgalānāṃ liṃgāni |
body.translated_text: Therein, for persons of passionate, hateful, deluded, proud, and discursive temperaments, one must first purify the temperament through the object for temperament-purification. Thereafter they attain mental stability. For them, precisely that designated object must necessarily be employed. For one of balanced temperament, however, one should employ whatever [object] one finds agreeable — merely for mental stability, not for temperament-purification. As with one of balanced temperament, so too should one of little defilement (<s>mandarajaska</s>) be understood. But here is the distinction among them: one of passionate and other temperaments, when applying [to meditation], attains [stability] slowly; one of balanced temperament, not too slowly; but one of little defilement attains mental stability swiftly and rapidly. Therein, the signs of persons of passionate temperament have been stated earlier.

body.text: samabhāgacaritasya pudgalasya mandarajaskasya ca katamāni liṃgāni | āha | samabhāgacaritasya pudgalasya sarvāṇi tāni liṃgāni saṃvidyante | yāni rāgādicaritānāṃ, tāni rāgā[dī]ni tu nādhimātrāṇi, na pradhānāni | tathā rāgādicaritānāṃ samaprāptāni (

children.text: ) bhavanti pratyayeṣu satsu na prajñāyante | tatra mandarajaskasya pudgalasya liṃgāni | anāvṛto bhavatyādiśuddhasaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtaḥ | prasādabahulo medhāvī puṇyavān guṇānvitaśca bhavati |
children.translated_text: but in the presence of conditions they are not discerned. Therein, the signs of a person of little defilement: he is unobstructed, endowed with the accumulation of initial purity, full of faith, intelligent, meritorious, and endowed with virtues.

body.translated_text: What are the signs of a person of balanced temperament and of one with little defilement? He says: A person of balanced temperament possesses all those signs that belong to persons of passionate and other temperaments, but those [traits of] passion and so forth are neither predominant nor intense. Likewise, in persons of passionate and other temperaments, they are equally present

body.text: tatra trīṇyāvaraṇāni | karmāvaraṇaṃ | kleśāvaraṇaṃ | vipākāvaraṇaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the three obstructions are: the obstruction of <s>karma</s> (action), the obstruction of <s>kleśa</s> (defilements), and the obstruction of <s>vipāka</s> (karmic result).

body.text: tatra karmāvaraṇaṃ | pañcānantaryāṇi karmāṇi | yaccānyadapi kiṃcitkarmāṇi (karma) | sāṃcetanīyaṃ | gurukarma, vipakvavipākaṃ | mārgotpattaye | nibaddhakārakaṃ | tatra kleśāvaraṇaṃ | tīvrakleśatā | āyatakleśatā ca | yā dṛṣṭe dharme caritaviśodhanenālambanaviśodhanena na śakyate viśodhayituṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the obstruction of <s>karma</s> is: the five <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) actions, and also whatever other <s>karma</s> that is intentional, heavy, with ripened result, that functions as a hindrance to the arising of the path. Therein, the obstruction of defilements is: intense defilement and prolonged defilement, which cannot be purified in this present life through purification of temperament by means of [its appropriate] object.

body.text: tatra vipākāvaraṇaṃ yatrāryamārgasya apravṛttiraprasāda upapattyāyatane [|] tatra vā vipākamabhinirvarttayati | yatra vā āryamārgasya pravṛttiḥ | tatropapatro jāto bhavatyeḍamūko hastasaṃbādhikaḥ apratibalo bhavati | subhāvitadurbhāvitānāṃ dharmāṇāmarthamājñātuṃ | tatrādiśuddhiḥ, (

children.text: ) śīlaṃ ca suviśuddhaṃ dṛṣṭiśca ṛjvī [|] tatra śīlaṃ suviśuddhaṃ | daśabhiḥ kāraṇairveditavyam | tatra dṛṣṭi tṛptitā jātā śradadhāṃ(ddhā) saṃprayogāt | adhimuktisaṃprayogāddhi tamāryā [a]śāṭhyatayā sucintita dharmārthasya niḥkāṃkṣanirvicikitsāprayoganiryāṇatayā yā dṛṣṭiḥ śraddhayā saṃprayuktā | asmāddharma vinayādasaṃhāryādadhimuktyā ca saṃprayuktā buddhānāṃ buddhaśrāvakāṇāṃ ca | anityamanubhava[na]manityāni copapattyāyatanā ni | gaṃbhīrāṃ ca deśanāṃ, avyākṛtavastu cādhimucyate | no[t]trasati, na saṃtrāsamā padyate | vigatamāyāśāṭhyā ca yā dṛṣṭiḥ yayā ṛjuko bhavati | ṛjukajātīyaḥ | yathānuśiṣṭaśca pratipadyate | yathābhūtaṃ cātmānamāviṣkaroti | dharmāṇāṃ vānityatāmārabhyaṃ, duḥkhatāṃ, śūnyatāmanātmatāmarthaḥ suvicintitobhavati | sutulitaḥ sūpaparīkṣitaḥ | yaddhetorayaṃ niḥkāṅkṣo bhavati | nirvicikitsaḥ | dvedhā pathā gato viśeṣāya paraiti | itīyaṃ caturākārā dṛṣṭiryathoddiṣṭā | dṛṣṭiṛjutetyucyate | tatra saṃbhārasaṃbhṛtatāvistareṇa saṃbhāraḥ | pūrvameva nirdiṣṭaḥ samāsataḥ | punaścarvidho bhavati | puṇyasaṃbhāro, jñānasaṃbhāraḥ, pūrvako, dṛṣṭadhārmikaśca |
children.translated_text: ) and the moral discipline is well purified, and the view is straight. Therein, the well-purified moral discipline should be understood through ten reasons. Therein, the straightness of view: a satisfaction has arisen — through the conjunction with faith, through the conjunction with conviction. For the noble ones, through sincerity, through the non-doubting and unhesitating mode of progress toward liberation regarding a well-considered meaning of the <s>Dharma</s> — the view that is conjoined with faith, unshakable from this <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, conjoined with conviction regarding the <s>Buddhas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Buddhas</s>: [one understands that] experience is impermanent, the bases of rebirth are impermanent; one has conviction in the profound teaching and in the undetermined matters; one is not frightened, does not fall into terror; free from deceit and crookedness — this is the view by which one becomes straight, of straight nature; one practices as instructed, and reveals oneself as one truly is. Furthermore, regarding the impermanence of phenomena, their suffering-nature, emptiness, and non-self-nature, the meaning is well considered, well weighed, well investigated; on account of which one is free from doubt, free from hesitation; having gone by a twofold path, one progresses to distinction. Thus this fourfold view as outlined is called 'the straightness of view.' Therein, the endowment with the requisites [is stated] in detail; the requisites have already been indicated previously. In brief, furthermore, they are fourfold: the requisite of merit, the requisite of knowledge, the prior [requisite], and the [requisite] pertaining to the present life.

body.translated_text: Therein, the obstruction of karmic result is: being reborn in a realm where the noble path does not operate and there is no faith, or where one produces a karmic result, or [even] where the noble path does operate — if born there, one is mute, deaf-mute, or hand-impaired, and is incapable of understanding the meaning of well-cultivated and ill-cultivated <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, initial purity [means]

body.text: tatra puṇyasabhāro yenāpyetarhi ānulomikāḥ pariṣkārāḥ prādurābhavanti | pradakṣiṇāḥ | kalyāṇamitrāṇi ca pratilabhate | anantarāyaśca prayuktasya bhavati |
body.translated_text: Therein, the requisite of merit is that by which even now favorable provisions appear, which are auspicious, and one obtains good spiritual friends, and one who is engaged [in practice] encounters no obstacles.

body.text: tatra jñānasaṃbhāraḥ | yena medhāvī bhavati, pratibalaḥ | subhāṣitadurbhāṣitānāṃ dharmāṇāmarthamājñātuṃ [|] lābhī bhavati | ānulobhikāyā dharmadeśanāyāḥ, arthadeśanāyāḥ, avavādānuśāsanyāḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the requisite of knowledge is that by which one becomes intelligent, capable of understanding the meaning of well-spoken and ill-spoken teachings, and one obtains the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, the teaching of the meaning, and the instruction and admonition that are in conformity [with liberation].

body.text: tatra pūrvako yenaitahi (rhi) pa[ri]pakvānīndriyāṇi labhate | pūrvakuśalamūlopacayāt | tatra dṛṣṭadhārmikastadyathā | kuśalo dharmacha(ccha)ndaḥ | tathā paripakvendriyasya śīlasamvara, indriyasamvara iti vistareṇa pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: Therein, the prior [requisite] is that by which one now obtains ripened faculties — due to the accumulation of wholesome roots in previous [lives]. Therein, the one pertaining to the present life is, for example: a wholesome desire for the <s>Dharma</s>; likewise, for one whose faculties are ripened — the restraint of morality, the restraint of the senses, and so on in detail as before.

body.text: tatra prasādabahulatā [|] na śāstari kāṃkṣati | na vicikitsati | prasīdatyadhimucyate | yathāśāstaryevaṃ dharme, śikṣāyāmiti vistareṇa pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: Therein, the abundance of faith: one does not doubt or hesitate regarding the Teacher; one has faith in and is convinced [of the Teacher]. Just as regarding the Teacher, so regarding the <s>Dharma</s>, the training, and so on in detail as before.

body.text: tatra medhā yayā āśu dharmamudgṛhṇāti | cireṇa dharmamarthaṃ ca na vistārayati | āśu dharmamarthaṃ ca pratividhyati |
body.translated_text: Therein, <s>medhā</s> (intelligence) is that by which one quickly grasps the <s>Dharma</s>, does not long delay [in understanding] the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>, and quickly penetrates the <s>Dharma</s> and its meaning.

body.text: tatra kṛtapuṇyatā | yayā abhirūpo bhavati | darśanīyaḥ | prāsādiko dīrghāyurbhavatyādeyavākyo, maheśākhyo, jñāto bhavati | mahāpuṇyo, lābhī cīvarādīnāṃ | sa satkṛto, gurukṛtaśca | rājādīnāṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the condition of having accumulated merit: by which one becomes handsome, good-looking, inspiring trust; one is long-lived, one whose words are accepted; one becomes well-known, of great renown; one becomes of great merit, one who obtains robes and the like; one is honored and revered by kings and others.

body.text: tatra guṇānvita iti | guṇā alpecchatādayo veditavyāḥ | yathoktaṃ śramaṇālaṃkāre tairayaṃ prakṛtyaiva samanvāgato bhavati | itīmānyevaṃ bhāgīyāni mandarajaskasya pudgalasya liṃgāni veditavyāni ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'endowed with qualities' — the qualities should be understood as fewness of desires and the like. As stated in the <s>Śramaṇālaṅkāra</s> (Ornament of the Ascetic), one is endowed with these by one's very nature. These and similar are the signs to be understood of a person with little dust [on the eyes].

body.text: tatra ṣaṭ pudgalaparyāyāḥ | tadyathā śramaṇo, brāhmaṇo, brahmacārī, bhikṣuryati[ḥ], pravrajitaśceti |
body.translated_text: Therein, there are six synonyms for 'person': namely, <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priest), <s>brahmacārin</s> (celibate practitioner), <s>bhikṣu</s> (mendicant), <s>yati</s> (striver), and <s>pravrajita</s> (renunciant).

body.text: tatra catvāraḥ śramaṇāḥ | mārgajinaḥ | mārgadeśikaḥ | mārgajīvī | mārgadūṣī ca |
body.translated_text: Therein, there are four [types of] <s>śramaṇas</s>: the path-conqueror (<s>mārgajina</s>), the path-teacher (<s>mārgadeśika</s>), the path-liver (<s>mārgajīvin</s>), and the path-corrupter (<s>mārgadūṣin</s>).

body.text: tatra yaḥ sugataḥ sa mārgajinaḥ | yo dharmavādī sa mārgadeśikaḥ | tatra yaḥ pratipannaḥ | sa mārgajīvī | yo mithyāpratipannaḥ sa mārgadūṣī |
body.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) is the path-conqueror. The <s>Dharma</s>-teacher is the path-teacher. One who is [rightly] practicing is the path-liver. One who is wrongly practicing is the path-corrupter.

body.text: sugataścocyate | yośeṣaṃ rāgadveṣamohakṣayamanuprāptaḥ | dharmavādī | yo rāgadveṣamohavinayāya dharmaṃ deśayati | supratipanno yo rāgadveṣamohavinayāya (

children.translated_text: ) The immoral one, of evil nature, is the wrongly-practiced one.

body.translated_text: The <s>Sugata</s> is said to be one who has attained the complete destruction of passion, hatred, and delusion. The <s>Dharma</s>-teacher is one who teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the removal of passion, hatred, and delusion. The well-practiced one is one who practices for the removal of passion, hatred, and delusion.

body.text: api ca | śaikṣāśaikṣā mārgajinā ityucyante | darśanabhāvanāprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ vijayāttatra tathāgato bodhisattvaścāyatyāṃ bodhāya pratipannāḥ | śrāvakāśca sūtradharā, vinayadharā, mātṛkādharāśca | ye sāṃketikaṃ dharmavinayaṃ dhārayanti | dharmanetrīṃ pravarttayanti | ima ucyante mārgadeśikāḥ | tatra ye pṛthagjanakalyāṇakā ātmahitāya pratipannā śajjinaḥ (mārgadeśikāḥ) | kaukṛtikāḥ śikṣākāmāḥ | aprāptasya prāptaye anadhigatasyādhigamāya āsākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai prayuktā, bhavyāśca pratibalā, yāvadasākṣātkṛtasya sākṣātkriyāyai [|] ima ucyante mārga jīvinaḥ | apyeṣāmūṣmā yene[ya]masya āryasya prajñendriyasyotpattaye, na mṛtā jīvantītyucyate | tenocyante mārgajīvina iti | tatra yoyaṃ pudgalo duḥśīlaḥ pāpadharmā yāvadabrahamacārī [brahmacārī] (ri) pratijñaḥ | ayamucyate mārgadūṣī dūṣitonena mārgo bhavati mūlata āditaḥ | yenāyamabhavyo bhavatyapratiabalaḥ | abhājanabhūto mārgasyotpattaye | satyāṃ saṃvidyamānāyāṃ mārgadeśanāyāṃ sati saṃvidyamānedhigame [|] (
body.translated_text: Furthermore, learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>) and those beyond learning (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) are called 'path-conquerors' — because of their victory over the afflictions to be abandoned through seeing and meditation. Therein, the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have set out for future awakening, and the <s>śrāvakas</s> who bear the <s>sūtras</s>, bear the <s>Vinaya</s>, and bear the <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrices) — those who maintain the conventional <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, who set in motion the <s>Dharma</s>-leadership — these are called 'path-teachers.' Therein, those virtuous ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who have set out for their own benefit — the path-teachers; those who feel remorse, who desire training, who are engaged in attaining what has not been attained, realizing what has not been realized, directly witnessing what has not been witnessed, and who are capable and competent for directly witnessing what has not been witnessed — these are called 'path-livers.' Indeed, they have the warmth by which the noble wisdom-faculty will arise; they are not dead but alive — therefore they are called 'path-livers.' Therein, the person who is immoral, of evil nature, and even a non-celibate claiming to be celibate — this one is called a 'path-corrupter'; the path has been corrupted by him from the very root, from the beginning, whereby he becomes incapable, incompetent, an unfit vessel for the arising of the path — even though the path-teaching exists and the attainment exists.

body.text: idaṃ ca sandhāyoktaṃ bhagavatā | iha katamaḥ śramaṇaḥ | iha yāvaccaturthaḥ | śūnyāḥ parapravādāḥ | śramaṇaibrahmiṇaiśca | yatrāryāṣṭāṃgo mārgaḥ prajñāyate | tatra prathamaśramaṇastatra yāvaccaturtha iti ||
body.translated_text: And it is with this in mind that the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Here, who is a <s>śramaṇa</s>? Here, up to the fourth [type]. The doctrines of other teachers are empty — of <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Where the Noble Eightfold Path is discerned, there is the first <s>śramaṇa</s>, there up to the fourth.'

body.text: tatra (ya) trayo brāhmaṇāḥ | tadyathā jātibrāhmaṇaḥ | saṃjñābrāhmaṇaḥ | pratipattibrāhmaṇaśca | tatra jātibrāhmaṇaḥ | yoyaṃ jātibrāhmaṇaḥ kulajāto, yonijo, mātṛsambhūtaḥ | utpanno mātṛtaḥ, pitṛtaḥ | tatra saṃjñābrāhmaṇa iti loke nāma bhavati, saṃjñā, samājñā, prajñaptirvyavahāraḥ | pratipattibrāhmaṇaḥ | yotyantani(ntaṃ) bhavati kṛtārthaḥ | vāhitā bhavantyanena pāpakā akuśalā dharmāḥ | (

children.text: ) yathoktaṃ na kāryaṃ brāhmaṇasyāsti | kṛtārtho brāhmaṇaḥ smṛta iti |
children.translated_text: ) As it is said: 'A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> has nothing [more] to do; the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who has fulfilled his purpose is so called.'

body.translated_text: Therein, there are three [types of] <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: namely, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by birth (<s>jātibrāhmaṇa</s>), the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by designation (<s>saṃjñābrāhmaṇa</s>), and the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by practice (<s>pratipattibrāhmaṇa</s>). Therein, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by birth is one who is born in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> family, born from the womb, produced by the mother — born from the mother's side and the father's side. Therein, '<s>brāhmaṇa</s> by designation' is a name, a designation, a conventional term, a designation, a mode of speech in the world. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> by practice is one who has become completely fulfilled in his purpose; evil, unwholesome qualities have been expelled by him.

body.text: tatra trayo brahmacāriṇaḥ | tadyathā viratisamādāyī | tadantaraprahāyī, tadatyantaprahāyī ca | tatra viratisamādāyī | yo brahmacaryā[t]punardharmātprativirato bhavati | samādattaśikṣaḥ | tatra tadantaraprahāyī yo laukikena mārgeṇa kāmavītarāgaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ | tatra tadatyantaprahāyī | tadyathānāgāmī | arhatvātpunaḥ (arhanvā punaḥ) ||
body.translated_text: Therein, there are three [types of] <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibate practitioners): namely, one who undertakes abstention (<s>viratisamādāyin</s>), one who abandons [defilements] in the interim (<s>tadantaraprahāyin</s>), and one who abandons them ultimately (<s>tadatyantaprahāyin</s>). Therein, one who undertakes abstention is one who refrains from the <s>brahmacārya</s> (celibate practice) and from the <s>Dharma</s>, having undertaken the training. Therein, one who abandons in the interim is an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) who has become free from desire for the sense-realm through the mundane path. Therein, one who abandons ultimately is, for example, a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>), or an <s>arhat</s>.

body.text: tatra pañca bhikṣavaḥ | bhikṣatīti bhikṣuḥ | pratijñābhikṣuḥ | saṃjñābhikṣuḥ | bhinnakleśatvādbhikṣuḥ | jñapticaturthena karmaṇopasampādito bhikṣuḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, there are five [types of] <s>bhikṣus</s> (mendicants): one who begs (<s>bhikṣati</s>), hence a <s>bhikṣu</s>; a <s>bhikṣu</s> by profession; a <s>bhikṣu</s> by designation; a <s>bhikṣu</s> because of having destroyed the afflictions; and a <s>bhikṣu</s> ordained by the ceremony of the fourth motion (<s>jñapticaturtha karman</s>).

body.text: tatra trayo yatayaḥ | dauḥśīlyasaṃyamād yatiḥ | yokuśalād vākkāyakarmaṇaḥ prativirataḥ | viṣayasaṃyamādyatiḥ | ya indriye guptadvāraḥ | ārakṣitasmṛtiḥ | nipakasmṛti[ḥ |] vistareṇa pūrvavat | kleśasaṃyamādyatiḥ | yasya darśanaprahātavyāḥ kleśāḥ prahīṇā utpannotpannañca | vitarkaṃ vyāpādavihi[taṃ]vitarkamabhidhyāvyāpādadṛṣṭimithyādṛṣṭikrodhopanāhamrakṣapradāśādīnyāpāyikāni sthānāni nairayikāni(ṇi) | durgatigāmī[ni] (|) aśramaṇakārakāṇyutpannotpannāni nādhivāsayati | prajahāti | viśodhayati | vyantīkaroti | so 'yaṃ dvividhaḥ kleśasaṃyamo bhavati | (

children.translated_text: ) consists of the restraint of manifest afflictions (<s>paryavasthānasaṃyama</s>) and the combined restraint (<s>ubhayasaṃyama</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, there are three [types of] <s>yatis</s> (strivers): a <s>yati</s> through restraint from immorality — one who has refrained from evil physical and verbal actions; a <s>yati</s> through restraint of the senses — one who guards the doors of the senses, protects mindfulness, possesses vigilant mindfulness, as stated in detail before; a <s>yati</s> through restraint of the afflictions — one whose afflictions to be abandoned through seeing have been abandoned, and who, as they arise, does not tolerate arisen evil thoughts — thoughts of ill-will, of harm, thoughts of covetousness, ill-will, wrong view, false view, anger, resentment, concealment, malice, and other states leading to the lower realms, of hellish [nature], leading to bad destinies, productive of non-ascetic [behavior]; he abandons, purifies, and eliminates [them] as they arise. This twofold restraint of afflictions

body.text: tatra dvau pravrajitau | svāravyātadharmavinayo, durākhyātadharmavinayaśca | tatra svākhyātadharmavinayaḥ | bhikṣurbhikṣuṇī, śikṣamāṇā, śrāmaṇera[ḥ], śrāmaṇerī | api ca pravrājayatyātmanaḥ pāpakānakuśalān dharmān sa pravrajita ityucyate | paramārthataḥ | tatra durākhyātadharmavinayaḥ | tadyathā tīrthika[ḥ], parivrājo (vrāḍ), nirgrantho vā, parivrājakopāṇḍuroga iti | yo vā punarapyevaṃbhāgīyaḥ | tenāhaṃ (ha) śramaṇo, brāhmaṇo, brahmacārī, bhikṣuryatiḥ, pravra [........................................] ra-ca | kālaprabhedaḥ dīrghakālabhāvitamārgo, na dīrghakālabhāvitamārgaśca | itīme catvāraḥ prabhedāḥ kathaṃnidānāni bhavanti | yadvā saṃpra [.........................................] jña upāyajña[ḥ] kuśala ityarthaḥ | sātatyapakṣe prayogo (gaḥ) sātatiko nipakva ityucyate | dīrghakālabhāvitabhāvita [...........................................] trayeṇa bhedena | yogaprayogakālabhedenāptānāṃ pudgalānāṃ vyavasthānaṃ yastāvadpudgalaḥ aparipakvendriyaḥ | sa tāvadupāyajñopi sātatikopi kṛtaparicayopi nārādhako bhavati | (

children.text: ) dhyāyyasya dharmasya kuśalasya | tatra paripakvendriyaśca [...............................] jño bhavati | paripakvendriyo bhavati | upāyajño na kṣiprābhijño bhavati | tatra paripakvendriyo, bhavatyupāyajño, na sātatiko, na kṛtaparicayaḥ | na tāvatkṛtasvārtho bhavati | kṛtakṛtyaḥ | yaśca paripakvendriyo bhavatyupāyajñaḥ | sātatikaḥ, kṛtaparicayaśca bhavatyevaṃ sa ārādhako bhavati | kṣiprābhijñaśca | kṛtasvakāryaśca bhavati kṛtyakṛtyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) in the wholesome quality that is to be meditated upon. Therein, one whose faculties are ripened [...] becomes knowledgeable. One whose faculties are ripened but who is skillful in means [yet] is not one of swift direct knowledge. Therein, one whose faculties are ripened and who is skillful in means, [but] is not constant and not experienced — does not yet accomplish his own purpose, has not done what was to be done. But one whose faculties are ripened, who is skillful in means, who is constant and experienced — such a one succeeds, is of swift direct knowledge, accomplishes his own purpose, and has done what was to be done.

body.translated_text: Therein, there are two [types of] <s>pravrajitas</s> (renunciants): those in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, and those in the ill-proclaimed <s>dharma</s> and <s>vinaya</s>. Therein, [those] in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> are: <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>bhikṣuṇī</s>, <s>śikṣamāṇā</s> (probationary nun), <s>śrāmaṇera</s> (male novice), and <s>śrāmaṇerī</s> (female novice). Furthermore, one who drives out one's own evil, unwholesome qualities is called a <s>pravrajita</s> (renunciant) in the ultimate sense. Therein, [those] in the ill-proclaimed <s>dharma</s> and <s>vinaya</s> are, for example: <s>tīrthikas</s> (non-Buddhist ascetics), wanderers (<s>parivrājaka</s>), <s>Nirgranthas</s> (Jains), and <s>Parivrājakopāṇḍuroga</s>; and whoever else is of such a kind. Thus [it is said]: <s>śramaṇa</s>, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, <s>brahmacārin</s>, <s>bhikṣu</s>, <s>yati</s>, <s>pravrajita</s> [...] and [there is also] the distinction of time: one who has cultivated the path for a long time, and one who has not cultivated the path for a long time. Thus these four distinctions — how do they become the basis? Whoever is [skilled in proper methods is called] 'skillful in means'; the meaning is: one who is skilled. In the aspect of constancy, the practice is constant and steady — this is called 'ripened.' One who has cultivated [the path] for a long time [...] by this threefold distinction, through the distinction of the yoga-practice-time, the classification of accomplished persons [is made]. A person whose faculties are unripened — even though he is skillful in means, constant, and experienced — does not succeed

body.text: tatra catvāro mārāḥ saṃbahulāni mārakarmāṇi | (

children.text: ) veditavyāni yoginā | yogaprayuktena | te ca parijñāya parivarjayitavyāḥ | tatra catvāro mārāḥ | tadyathā- skandhamāraḥ, kleśamāraḥ, maraṇamāraḥ | devaputramāraśca | paṃcopādānaskandhāḥ skandhamāraḥ | traidhātukāvacarāḥ kleśāḥ | teṣāṃ teṣāṃ sattvānāṃ | tasmāttasmātsattvanikāyāḥ ya(yādya)nmaraṇaṃ kālakriyā (
children.translated_text: ) should be understood by the <s>yogin</s> (practitioner) who is engaged in yoga. And having fully understood them, they are to be avoided. Therein, the four <s>māras</s> are: the <s>skandhamāra</s> (the <s>Māra</s> of the aggregates), the <s>kleśamāra</s> (the <s>Māra</s> of the afflictions), the <s>maraṇamāra</s> (the <s>Māra</s> of death), and the <s>devaputramāra</s> (the <s>Māra</s> who is a son of the gods). The five aggregates of clinging are the <s>skandhamāra</s>. The afflictions pertaining to the three realms — the death, the passing away, of those respective beings and those respective classes of beings —

children.text: ) maraṇamāraḥ | yopyakuśalapakṣaprayuktasya skandhakleśamṛtyusamatikramāya kāmadhātūpapanno devaputraḥ | niścayaprāptaḥ antarāyamupasaṃharati | vyākṣepakaraṇe | ayamucyate devaputramāraḥ | tatra yatra ca mriyate | yaścāsau mṛtyuryena ca mṛtyuṃ namayati, krāmayatyantarāyikena vastunā [|] ityetadadhikṛtya catvāro mārā vyavasthāpitāḥ |
children.translated_text: ) is the <s>maraṇamāra</s> (the <s>Māra</s> of death). And that son of the gods (<s>devaputra</s>), born in the desire realm, who, when one is engaged in the wholesome side [of practice] for the transcendence of the aggregates, afflictions, and death, having reached certainty [in opposition], brings about obstacles and causes distraction — this is called the <s>devaputramāra</s>. Therein, [considering] where one dies, what that death is, and by what [cause] one brings about death, causing it to occur through an obstructive factor — with reference to this, the four <s>māras</s> have been established.

body.translated_text: Therein, there are four <s>māras</s> (evil ones), and numerous actions of <s>Māra</s>

body.text: tatra pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu jāteṣu varddhamāneṣu mriyate | kleśāṃ(śān)janayatyāyatyāṃ jātaśca mriyate | cyutiśca cyavanatā satvānāṃ jīvitendriyanirodhaḥ | kālakriyā svabhāva eva mṛtyuḥ | devaputramāraśca maraṇa samatikramāya prayuktasyāntarāyamupasaṃharati | yena naiva vā śaknoti maraṇadharmatāṃ samatikramitum || kālāntareṇa vā samatikrāmati | tatrāvaśagato mārasya bhavati laukikamārgavītarāgaḥ pṛthagjanaḥ || ihasthastatropapanno vā, [a]vaśagataḥ | punaryaḥ avītarāgaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, when the five <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) have arisen and are growing, one dies and generates <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) in the future; and having been born, one dies. Passing away and the state of passing away of beings is the cessation of the life-faculty, the making of time — death is its very nature. And <s>Devaputtamāra</s> (<s>Māra</s> the deity's son) creates obstacles for one who strives to overcome death. On account of this, one is either unable to transcend the nature of mortality, or transcends it only after a [long] interval of time. Therein, one who is worldly, a <s>pṛthagjana</s> (ordinary person), free from passion through the mundane path, is still under <s>Māra</s>'s power. Whether remaining here or reborn there, one is under his power. Furthermore, one who is not free from passion [is also under his power].

children.translated_text: ) — this should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activity. For one who dwells with sense-faculties well-guarded, when the mind runs toward attractive forms that are to be experienced in immediate contact, through grasping at signs and grasping at secondary features — this should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activity. Likewise, for one who dwells knowing moderation in food, when the mind runs toward exquisite flavors through desire, attachment, and compliance; and due to irregularity in eating — likewise, for one devoted to wakefulness in the first and last watches of the night, when the mind runs toward the pleasure of sleep, the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of turning on one's side — this should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activity. Likewise, for one dwelling with clear comprehension, while going forward and returning and so forth, upon seeing a woman — young, of fine complexion, attractive — the mind runs due to unwholesome grasping at signs; or upon seeing worldly spectacles, the mind runs; or the mind runs toward having many affairs and many duties; such as toward delight in association with householders and renunciants, toward being of one purpose with evil friends, toward approval of [wrong] views — this should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activity. Likewise, when doubts and uncertainties arise regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Saṃgha</s>, regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path, regarding this world and the next world — this should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activity. Or, when gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty house, one sees great fear and terror, hair-raising dread; or when someone approaches in the guise of a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a human, or a non-human, and inappropriately (

children.translated_text: ) cuts one off from the white [wholesome] side and urges one toward the dark [unwholesome] side — this should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activity. Thus, activities of this kind should be known as <s>Māra</s>'s activities, and they pertain to the four <s>Māras</s> as applicable.

body.translated_text: Therein, through four causes, even the exertion of one properly striving may be fruitless. Namely: through the development of the faculties, through [appropriate] instruction, and through the weakness of <s>samādhi</s> (concentration). If the faculties have not developed and the instruction is appropriate but the <s>samādhi</s> is merely bare — thus one's exertion is fruitless. If the faculties have not developed and the instruction is not appropriate but the <s>samādhi</s> is strong — thus the exertion is fruitless. If the faculties have developed and the instruction is appropriate but the <s>samādhi</s> is weak — thus the exertion is fruitless. If the faculties have developed and the instruction is appropriate but the <s>samādhi</s> is weak — thus the exertion is fruitless. [Only] if the faculties have developed and the instruction is appropriate and the <s>samādhi</s> is strong — then (

body.translated_text: III. The Third <s>Yogasthāna</s> (Station of Practice).

body.text: evaṃ kṛte pudgalavyavasthāne, ālambanavyavasthāne, yāvadbhāvanāphalavyavasthāne ātmakāmena pudgalena svārthamanuprāptukāmena ādikarmikena (ṇa) | tatprathamakarmikena(ṇa) yogajña, ācāryo vā, upādhyāyo vā, puruṣo, gurusthānīyo vā, caturṣu sthāneṣu smṛtimupasthāpya upasaṃkramitavyaḥ | abhijñābhiprāyeṇa, nopālambhacittatayā, sagauraveṇa, na samānastambhatayā | kiṃkuśalagaveṣiṇā | nātmodbhāvanārthaṃ | ātmānaṃ parāṃśca kuśalamūlena yojayiṣyāmīti | na lābhasatkārārthamevaṃ ca punarupasaṃkramya kālenāvakāśaṃ kṛtvā, ekāṃsamuttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā, dakṣiṇaṃ jānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya, nīcataramevāsane niṣadya, sapratīśena yoga āyācitavyaḥ | ahamasmiṃ (smi) yogenārthī, yogaṃ ādikṣvānukampāmupādāya |
body.translated_text: When the classification of persons, the classification of objects, and up to the classification of the fruits of cultivation has been established thus — a person who desires his own welfare, who wishes to attain his own goal, who is a beginner, a first-timer — having established mindfulness in four areas, should approach a <s>yoga</s>-knowing teacher, or preceptor, or person in the position of a spiritual guide, with the intention of gaining [higher] knowledge, not with a fault-finding mind, with respect, not with an attitude of equality, seeking what is wholesome, not for the purpose of self-aggrandizement, [thinking:] 'I shall connect myself and others with roots of wholesome <s>karma</s>' — not for the sake of gain and honor. And having thus approached, at the proper time making an opportunity, arranging the upper robe over one shoulder, placing the right knee on the ground, sitting on a lower seat, with deference, one should request <s>yoga</s> [instruction]: 'I am one who desires <s>yoga</s>; please grant me <s>yoga</s> [instruction] out of compassion from the beginning.'

children.translated_text: ) with very gentle, very smooth modes of speech, one should arouse [a sense of] urgency, one should inspire joy, and one should describe the benefit of abandonment: 'Well done, well done, O fortunate one! You who, among people who are heedless, inclined toward sense-objects, devoted to sense-objects, wish to strive for heedfulness; who, among those who have entered the stream leading to the lower realms, wish to emerge from the stream to the lower realms; who, among those devoid of the bonds of passion, hatred, and delusion, wish to cast off the bonds; who, among those who have entered the difficult path of the great forest of <s>saṃsāra</s>, wish to escape; who, among those who have arrived at the great famine of wholesome roots [caused by] the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), wish to attain the abundance of wholesome roots; who, among those beset by the great terror of the <s>kleśa</s>-bandits, wish to attain the safety of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; who, among those gripped by the great disease of the <s>kleśas</s>, wish to attain the supreme health of <s>nirvāṇa</s>; who, among those swept by the current of the four floods, wish to cross beyond the floods; who, among those who have entered the great darkness of ignorance, wish to attain the great light of knowledge. Otherwise, Venerable One, if you do not practice thus, you will consume the alms of the nation with confusion, [but if you do practice,] you will be one who carries out the Teacher's word — one who meditates without being rejected, endowed with <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), one who fills the empty dwellings, engaged in one's own practice, not censured by the wise, practicing for the equal welfare of one's fellow practitioners in the holy life, for the welfare of others, for the welfare of the many, out of compassion for the world, (

children.text: ) arthāya, hitāya, sukhāya devamanuṣyāṇāmityevaṃbhāgīyaiḥ ślakṣṇairvacanapathaiḥ | saṃharṣayitvā (saṃharṣya) prahāṇe cānuśaṃsaṃ darśayitvā, caturṣu paripṛcchāsthānīyeṣu dharmeṣu paripraṣṭavyaḥ | kaści(cci)dāyuṣmānekāntena buddhaśaraṇaṃ gato, dharmaṃ, saṃghaṃ, no cetobahirdhānyaṃ śāstāraṃ vā, dakṣiṇīyamvā saṃjānāti, kaccitte ādipariśodhitādbrahmacaryasya bhāvanāyai śīlaṃ ca te saviśuddhaṃ, dṛṣṭiśca ṛjvī kaccitte āryasatyānāmuddeśavibhaṃgamāramya dharmaḥ śrutaścodgṛhītaśca | alpo vā, prabhūto vā, kaccitte nirvāṇā dhimuktaṃ cittaṃ | nirvāṇābhiprāyaśca pravrajitaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) for the benefit, welfare, and happiness of gods and humans.' With such and similar gentle modes of speech, having inspired joy and having shown the benefit of abandonment, one should question [the student] on four topics that are fit for inquiry: 'Has the Venerable One exclusively taken refuge in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṃgha</s>, and does he not acknowledge any other teacher or object of veneration outside [these]? Is your morality purified from the foundation for the cultivation of the holy life? Is your view straight? Has the Venerable One heard and grasped the <s>Dharma</s>, whether a little or much, beginning with the exposition and analysis of the Noble Truths? Is your mind inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>? And have you gone forth with the intention of [attaining] <s>nirvāṇa</s>?'
