Therein, that by which one experiences the coarse characteristic with respect to discursive thoughts (<s>vitarka</s>), and the peaceful characteristic of the non-discursive second <s>dhyāna</s> — that is the characteristic-recognizing [attention].

body.translated_text: Just as the attainment of the first <s>dhyāna</s> [is accomplished] through seven [types of] mental attention, so too the attainments of the second, third, and fourth <s>dhyānas</s>, and the spheres of infinite space, infinite consciousness, and nothingness.

body.text: bāhyāyatanasaṃgṛhītāśca | sarva eva cātītā, anāgatapratyutpannā, hetusamutpannāḥ, pratītyasamutpannāḥ, ākāyikāstāvatkalikāḥ | itvarapratyupasthāyinaścittasaṃkṣobhakarā, iṃjakā apraśāntākāreṇa vartante | uparimāṃ bhūmimārabhya duḥkhavihārānugatatvātkuṣṇapakṣyā kāmavivekaprītisukhamevānuśaṃsānugatā bhūmiścaiṣā tādṛśī prakṛtyā yatra sthitasya nityaṃ nityakālaṃ, dhruvaṃ dhruvakālaṃ, savitarkaḥ, savicāraḥ, cittapracāraḥ pravartate | na śāntapraśānta ityevamādibhirākārairvitarkeṣvaudārikalakṣaṇaṃ pratisaṃvedayate |
body.translated_text: These are included in the external sense-bases (<s>bāhyāyatana</s>). And all of them are past, future, and present; arisen from causes, arisen from conditions; bodily [phenomena of a] temporary nature.

body.text: sarvaśo nāstyetadaudārikalakṣaṇamavitarkedvitīye dhyāne ityataḥ śāntaṃ dvitīyaṃ dhyānamasyaudārikatvasyāpagamāt | śeṣo(ṣe) manaskārā dvitīyadhyānasamāpattaye yathā(pi) yogaṃ pūrvavadveditavyaṃ | evaṃ bhūmau bhūmau yāvannaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasamāpattaye yathāyogaṃ sapta manaskārā veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: 'This coarseness does not exist at all, this non-discursive quality, in the second <s>dhyāna</s>' — therefore the second <s>dhyāna</s> is peaceful, due to the departure of this coarseness. The rest

body.text: audārikalakṣaṇaṃ punaḥ sarvāsvadharimāsu bhūmiṣu yāvadākiṃcanyāyatanāt samāsena dvividhaṃ veditavyaṃ | duḥkhataraṃ vihāvito(ritā) cādharmū(dhobhū)mīnāmapraśāntavihāritā ca | alpāyuṣkatarā ca | ityetad dvividhamaudārikalakṣaṇaṃ | ṣaḍbhirvastubhiryathāyogaṃ paryeṣate | yasyā yasyā bhūmervairāgyaṃ karttukāmo bhavatyupariṣṭācca yathāyogaṃ śāntalakṣaṇaṃ | yāvatprayoganiṣṭhāphalānmanaskārāttatra viviktaṃ kāmairiti |
body.translated_text: The coarse characteristic in all the lower stages up to the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>) should be understood in brief as twofold: more suffering, and more afflicted dwelling.

body.text: dvividhāḥ kāmāḥ kleśakāmā vastukāmāśca [|] (

children.text: ) kāmavitarko 'pi dvividhaḥ | saṃprayogaviveka ālambanavivekaśca [|] viviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmairiti | upakleśāḥ kāmahetukā akuśalā dharmāstadyathā kāyaduścaritaṃ, vāgduścaritaṃ, manoduścaritaṃ | daṇḍādānaṃ śastrādānaṃ | kalahabhaṇḍanavigrahavivādaśāṭhyavañcananikṛtimṛṣāvādāḥ sambhavanti | teṣāmprahāṇādviviktaṃ pāpakairakuśalairdharmairavitarkavicāreṣvadoṣadarśanātsvabhūmikairvitarkavicāraiḥ kāmaprātipakṣikaiḥ kuśalaiḥ [|] savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ prayoganiṣṭho manaskāraḥ kāmavivekaṃ (kaḥ) tasyānantaramutpannaṃ(nnaḥ) | taddhetukaṃ (kas) tatpratyayaṃ (yas) tenāha vivekajamīpsitābhilaṣitārthasaṃprāptaḥ, prītau vā doṣadarśanāt | sarvadauṣṭhulyāpagamācca vipulapraśrabdhi cittakāyakarmaṇyatayā prītisukhamanupūrveṇa gaṇayataḥ | tatprathamataśca kāmadhātūccalitāt prathamaṃ samyagālambanopanidhyānādekāgrasmṛtyupanibandhāddhyānaṃ prayoganiṣṭhāphalatvādupasampadya | uttaratra ca bhāvanābahulīkāraniṣpādanāt [|] (
children.translated_text: The thought of desire (<s>kāmavitarka</s>) is also twofold: seclusion from association (<s>saṃprayogaviveka</s>) and seclusion from the object (<s>ālambanaviveka</s>). 'Secluded from evil, unwholesome <s>dharmas</s>' means: the secondary afflictions (<s>upakleśa</s>).

children.text: ) nikāmalābhī, akṛcchralābhī, akisara(akṛtsna?)lābhī, tathā dhyānasamāpattyā rātrimatināmayati | divasamapi yāvadākāṃkṣamāṇaḥ saptarātriṃdivasāni tenāha viharatīti | savitarkasavicāraviviktebhyaścittamvyāvartayitvā (ttaṃ vyāvartya) avitarkāvicārasamādhinimitteṣūpanibadhnāti | vyagracāriṇa ālambanādvivecya avyagracāriṇyālambane ekadharmatayā śāntaṃ prasannaṃ cittaṃ pravarttate | vyavasthāpayati | tenāha vitarkavicārāṇāṃ vyupaśamādadhyātmasaṃprasādanātsabhāvanābhyāsāttasyaivāvitarkāvicārasya samādheḥ, vitarkavicārasya samādheḥ, sa[c]chidrasāntarāmavasthāmatikramya niśchidranirantarāmavasthāṃ prāpnoti | tenāha cetasa ekotībhāvāt sarveṇa sarvaṃ vitarkavicāraprahāṇādavitarkamavicāraṃ prayoganiṣṭho manaskāraḥ samādhistasyānantaraṃ taddhetukaṃ taṃtpra(kastatpra)tyayamutpa(yautpa)dyata iti | tenāha samādhijaṃ īpsitāninditārthaprāpteḥ prītau vā doṣadarśanāt | sa saṃpraharṣagataṃ daurmanasyagataṃ vitarkavicāraprathamadhyānakleśapakṣasarvadauṣṭhulyāpagamāttatprātipakṣikapraśrabdhicittakāyakarmaṇyatāsuravānugatvāt | prītisukhamanupūrveṇa gaṇayato dvitīyaṃ bhavatyevaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvavad veditavyam |
children.translated_text: one who obtains [the <s>dhyāna</s>] at will, without difficulty, and without impediment. Likewise, through the <s>dhyāna</s> attainment, one passes the night; and the day as well — as long as one desires, up to seven days and nights, one abides in it. Having turned away the mind from [the first <s>dhyāna</s>], which has both <s>vitarka</s> (applied thought) and <s>vicāra</s> (sustained thought), one binds [the mind] to the signs of the <s>samādhi</s> without <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>. Having separated [the mind] from the agitated object, one directs the mind, peaceful and serene, in a state of single-pointedness (<s>ekadharmatā</s>), to a non-agitated object. One establishes it. Therefore it is said: 'Through the pacification of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>, through internal serenity, through the cultivation and practice of that very <s>samādhi</s> without <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s>' — transcending the state of the <s>samādhi</s> with <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> that has gaps and intervals, one attains a state without gaps and intervals. Therefore it is said: 'Through the one-pointedness of mind — with the complete and total abandonment of <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> — without <s>vitarka</s>, without <s>vicāra</s>, the mental attention that is the culmination of effort, the <s>samādhi</s>, [arises]. Subsequently, the [<s>prīti</s> and <s>sukha</s>], caused by that and conditioned by that, arise.' Therefore it is said: 'Born of <s>samādhi</s>' — through the attainment of the desired, blameless goal [one has] <s>prīti</s> (joy), or through seeing the danger in [the first <s>dhyāna</s>'s defects]. At that time, for him, with the departure of all the rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) belonging to the affliction-side of <s>vitarka</s>, <s>vicāra</s>, and the first <s>dhyāna</s> — including the elation [aspect] and the dejection [aspect] — and being endowed with the tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>), mental and physical workability (<s>karmaṇyatā</s>), and [subtle] continuity that is their antidote — counting <s>prīti</s> (joy) and <s>sukha</s> (happiness) in sequence, the second [<s>dhyāna</s>] comes into being. All of this should be understood as before.

body.translated_text: Desires (<s>kāma</s>) are of two kinds: the desire that is defilement (<s>kleśakāma</s>) and the desire that is the object (<s>vastukāma</s>).

body.text: prītinimitteṣu doṣaṃ paśyati | tenāha prītervirāgāt [|] (

children.text: ) tasmiṃśca samaye dvividho 'sya cittakṣobhakaraḥ apakṣālo 'dhigato bhavati | niḥprītike tṛtīyadhyāne cittaṃ pradadhataḥ | dvitīye ca dhyāne vitarkavicārāḥ, etarhi ca prītiḥ, tenāha upekṣako viharati | etau hi dvau dharmau cittasaṃkṣobhakarau | nirantarāyā upekṣāyā vighnakārakau | tatra prathame dhyāne vitarkavicārā bhavanti | yena nirantaropekṣā na pravarttate | dvitīye dhyāne prītirbhavati | yenātrāpi nirantaropekṣā na pravarttate | tenāyaṃ dhyāyī prathamadvitīyeṣu(yayoḥ) dhyāneṣu(nayoḥ) nāsti, tena tṛtīye dhyāne upekṣako viharatītyucyate | sa upekṣakassanstathā(ssaṃstathā) tathopasthitasmṛtirviharati | yathā yathā te prītisahagatāḥ saṃjñāmanasikārāḥ samudācaranti | sa cetpunarabhāvitatvāt tṛtīyasya dhyānasya smṛtisaṃpramoṣātkadācitkarhicit citte prītisahagatāḥ saṃjñāmanasikārāḥ samudācaranti | tāṃ(tān) laghu laghveva (
children.translated_text: At that time, a twofold disturbance of mind — an impurity — has been overcome by him. While establishing the mind in the third <s>dhyāna</s>, which is without <s>prīti</s> — in the second <s>dhyāna</s> there were <s>vitarka</s> and <s>vicāra</s> [in the first], and now <s>prīti</s> [in the second]. Therefore it is said: 'One abides in equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>).' For these two <s>dharmas</s> are disturbances of the mind, obstructors of uninterrupted equanimity. In the first <s>dhyāna</s>,

children.text: ) prajñayā pratividhyati | samyageva prajānāti | utpannotpannāṃśca nādhivāsayati | prajahāti vinodayati | vyantīkaroti, cittamadhyupekṣate | tenāha smṛtaḥ saṃprajānā[na] iti | tasya tasminsamaye evamupekṣakasya viharatā smṛtasya saṃprajanya syāsevanānvayādbahulīkārānvayātprītisahagataṃ prahīyate | taccittauddhatyakaraṃ, niḥprītikaṃ, śāntaṃ, praśāntaṃ cetasi veditamutpadyate | prītiprātidvandvyena tasmin samaye rūpakāyena, manaḥkāyena vedita sukhaṃ ca praśrabdhisukhaṃ pratisamvedayate | tṛtīyācca dhyānāt | adhastadrūpaṃ sukhaṃ nāsti nāpi nirantarā upekṣā tṛtīyā[d]dhyānādūrdhvaṃ yadapyupekṣopalabhyate | na tu sukhaṃ | tatrādhaḥ sukhopekṣābhāvādūrdhvaṃ ca sukhābhāvāt | idaṃ tadāyatanaṃ yaduta tṛtīyaṃ dhyānaṃ yattadāryā ācakṣate | yatpratilambhavihāriṇaṃ pudgalamadhikṛtya smṛtimāṃ(mān) sukhavihārī tṛtīyaṃ dhyānamupasaṃpadya viharatīti āryāḥ punaḥ vṛddhāśca vṛddhaśrāvakāśca |
children.translated_text: one discerns with wisdom; one knows correctly. And those [disturbances] that have arisen, one does not tolerate — one abandons them, removes them, eliminates them; one regards the mind with equanimity. Therefore it is said: 'Mindful and clearly comprehending.' For him, at that time, abiding thus with equanimity, mindful and with clear comprehension — through repeated practice and cultivation, what is accompanied by <s>prīti</s> is abandoned. That

body.translated_text: One sees the danger in the signs of <s>prīti</s> (joy). Therefore it is said: 'Through dispassion from <s>prīti</s>.'

body.text: tatrātulyajātīyatvāt | pratipakṣasya sukhasya prahāṇapratipakṣānākhyātaḥ (kṣo 'nākhyātaḥ) | yadeva tatpratipakṣakṛtaṃ sukhaprahāṇaṃ tadevākhyātaṃ | kaḥ punarasau pratipakṣaḥ | yadutopekṣā smṛtisamprajanyañca | tasya ca niṣevaṇābhyāsāttṛtīyadhyānāccalito yatra (

children.text: ) tṛtīyadhyānabhūmisukhaṃ tatprajahāti | tenāha | sukhasya ca prahāṇātpūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayorasta(ṅ)gamāt | tatra caturthadhyānasamāpattikāle tasmin samaye sa dhyāyī sukhaduḥkhavyatikramamanuprāpnoti | tena yaś(c)ca pūrvaprahīṇaṃ, yaścai(ccai)tarhi prahīyate | tasya saṃkalanaṃ kurvannevamāha | sukhasya ca prahāṇāt(d), duḥkhasya ca prahāṇāt, pūrvameva ca saumanasyadaurmanasyayorasta[ṅ]gamāt | tanna caturthadhyānasamāpattikāle sukhasya ca prahāṇāaddvitīyadhyānasamāpattikāle duḥkhasya, tṛtīyadhyānasamāpattikāle saumanasyasyāstaṅgamāt, prathamadhyānasamāpattikāle daurmanasyasya, asti tāvatsukhaduḥkhasya(yoḥ) prahāṇādaduḥkhāsukhaivāsya vedanā, na viśiṣṭā bhavati | tenāha | aduḥkhāsukhā tasmin samaye prathamaṃ dhyānamupādāya sarve adhobhūmikāḥ apakṣālāḥ prahīṇā bhavanti | tadyathā vitarkavicārāḥ, prītirāśvāsapraśvāsāḥ | teṣāṃ ca prahāṇādyā tatropekṣā | smṛtiśca sā pariśuddhā bhavati | paryavadātā, yenāsya etaccittaṃ caturthadhyānasamāpannasyāniṃjyaṃ santiṣṭhate | sarveñjitāyatanaṃ | (
children.translated_text: abandons the happiness belonging to the ground of the third <s>dhyāna</s>. Therefore it is said: 'Through the abandonment of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure), and through the prior disappearance of <s>saumanasya</s> (mental pleasure) and <s>daurmanasya</s> (mental displeasure).' Therein, at the time of attaining the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, at that moment, the meditator reaches the transcendence of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) and <s>duḥkha</s> (pain). Adding together what was previously abandoned and what is now being abandoned,

children.text: ) tenāha | upekṣāsmṛtipariśuddhamiti [|] tatra caturthamiti pūrvavad veditavyam || yathāpramāṇādiṣu sthāneṣu ||
children.translated_text: therefore it is said: 'Purified by equanimity and mindfulness.' Therein, 'the fourth' should be understood as before — as in the sections on measure and the like.

body.translated_text: therein, because the antidote (<s>sukha</s>, happiness) is of a dissimilar kind [from <s>prīti</s>], the abandonment-antidote of <s>sukha</s> (pleasure) has not [yet] been declared. That very abandonment of <s>sukha</s> effected by its antidote is [subsequently] declared. And what is that antidote? Namely, equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>), <s>smṛti</s> (mindfulness), and <s>saṃprajanya</s> (clear comprehension). Through the practice and cultivation of these, one who has risen from the third <s>dhyāna</s>,

body.text: tatrākāśādhimokṣasya varṇasaṃjñā nīlapītalohitāvadātādipratisaṃyuktatāmasātāmasātayā nirvirāgatayā ca samatikrānto bhavati | tenāha | rūpasaṃjñānāṃ (

children.text: ) samatikramādanābhāsagamanahetoryā anekavidhā bahunānāprakārā varṇapracayahetukā āvaraṇasaṃjñā sā (yā) sā vigatā bhavati | tenāha | pratighasaṃjñānāmasta[ṅ]gamāt, tāsāmvā punarvigamahetoryā aupacayikīsaṃjñāsteṣvavaśiṣṭeṣu viśiṣṭeṣu saṃghāteṣu pravṛttāstadyathā bhojanapānavastrālaṃkāragṛhodyānavanasenāparvatādisaṃjñā[ḥ] | teṣu sarveṇa sarvamābhogo 'pyasya na pravartate | tenāha | nānātvasaṃjñānāmamanasikārāt | sa evaṃ rūpapratighanānātvasaṃjñā bhāvayitvā anantākāreṇākāśādhimukto bhavati | tenāha | anantamākāśama(śaṃsa)sāmantakamatikramya prayoganiṣṭhānmanasikārāduccaprayoganiṣṭhāphalaṃ maulaṃ samāpadyate | tenāha | ākāśānantyāyatanamupasampadya viharati | tasya yāvanmaulaṃ na samāpadyate | tasyākāśamālambanaṃ samāpannasya punastacca tadanye ca skandhāḥ svabhūmikāḥ sāmantake punaradhobhūmikā api skandhāḥ |
children.translated_text: through the non-attention to perceptions of diversity — the manifold, various resistance-perceptions (<s>pratighasaṃjñā</s>) that are causes of the accumulation of color, and the cause of obstruction — they have departed. Therefore it is said: 'Through the disappearance of resistance-perceptions.' And as the cause of their departure, the growth-perceptions (<s>aupacayikīsaṃjñā</s>) that operated in those remaining distinguished aggregates — such as food, drink, clothing, ornaments, houses, gardens, and forests —

body.translated_text: Therein, in the conviction of [infinite] space (<s>ākāśādhimokṣa</s>), one has transcended the color-perceptions (<s>varṇasaṃjñā</s>) — blue, yellow, red, white, and so forth — together with their agreeable and disagreeable [aspects] and their dispassion. Therefore it is said: 'Through the complete transcendence of form-perceptions (<s>rūpasaṃjñā</s>),'

body.text: samayena vijñānenānantamākāśamadhimucyate | tadeva vijñānamanantākārākāśādhimokṣikaṃ | vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ samāpattukāmaḥ | ākāśānantyāyatanasaṃjñāṃ vyāvartya | tadeva vijñānamanantākāreṇādhimucyate | sasāmantake maulamākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramyate | tenāha | sarvaśa ākāśānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramyānantaṃ vijñānamiti | sa vijñānānantyāyatanamiti sāmantakaṃ samatikramya yāvatprayoganiṣṭhānmanasikarānmaulaprayoganiṣṭhāphalaṃ samāpadyate | tenāha | vijñānānantyāyatanamupasampadya viharatīti |
body.translated_text: at that time, with consciousness one has the conviction of infinite space. That very consciousness, with the aspect of infinite space-conviction, [one takes as object for] the attainment of the <s>vijñānānantyāyatana</s> (sphere of infinite consciousness). Wishing to attain the sphere of infinite consciousness, having turned away the perception of the sphere of infinite space, one has the conviction of that very consciousness as infinite in aspect. Having transcended the sphere of infinite space, both its preliminary and fundamental [stages], therefore it is said: 'Having completely transcended the sphere of infinite space,'

body.text: sa vijñānānantyāyatanāduccalito vijñānāt pareṇālambanaṃ samanveṣamāṇo na punarlabhate (|) kiñcana pratisaṃyuktaṃ rūpi vā, arūpi vā [|] sa tadālambanamalabhamānaḥ sasāmāntakamaulaṃ vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ [sa]matikramya nāsti kiñcidanyadā lambanamadhimucyate | so [a]kiñcanasaṃjñādhimukta eva bhavati | sa tasya saṃjñādhimokṣasya bahulīkārānvayādākiṃcanyāyatanasāmantakaṃ samatikramya yāvatprayoganiṣṭhā(n) manasikārānmaulaṃ prayoganiṣṭhāphale samāpadyate | tenāha | sarvaśo vijñānānantyāyatanaṃ samatikramya nāsti kiñcidityākiñcanyāyatanamupasaṃspṛśya (-sampadya) viharatīti |
body.translated_text: risen from the sphere of infinite consciousness, searching for an object beyond consciousness, one no longer finds any [object] whatsoever connected [with it] — whether material or immaterial. Not finding that object, having transcended the sphere of infinite consciousness — both its preliminary and fundamental [stages] — one has the conviction: 'There is nothing whatever as an object.' One becomes one of the conviction of nothingness (<s>akiñcana</s>). One

body.text: tenāha | saṃjñī yadutākiñcanyāyatanāduccalitaḥ | ākiñcanyasaṃjñāyāmaudārikasaṃjñī ādīnavasaṃjñī ākiñcanyāyatanasaṃjñāṃ vyāvarttayati | tena pūrvamākiñcanyāyatanasamāpattikāle [a]kiñcanasaṃjñāsamatikrāntā, etarhyakiṃcanasaṃjñā samatikrāntā bhavati | tenāha saṃjñī yaduta kiñcanasaṃjñāyā vā, akiñcanasaṃjñāyā vā, akiñcanasaṃjñā vā, na ca punaḥ sarveṇa sarvaṃ sāsya saṃjñā niruddhā bhavati | tadyathā āsaṃjñi[ke]vā, nirodhasamāpattau vā, nānyatra sūkṣmā sā saṃjñā nimittālambane pravartate | naiva saṃjñā nāsaṃjñā [|] evaṃ tadāyatanādhimuktaḥ sasāmantakamaulamākiñcanyāyatanaṃ samatikramya naiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanasāmantakasya yā vatprayoganiṣṭhānmanasikārāt prayoganiṣṭhāphalaṃ maulaṃ samāpadyate | tenāha | sarvaśa ākiñcanyāyatana[ṃ] samatikramya naiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanamupasampadya viharatīti ||
body.translated_text: therefore it is said: 'Percipient' — namely, one risen from the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), perceiving the coarse perception in the perception of nothingness, perceiving the danger, turns away the perception of the sphere of nothingness. Thus, the perception of nothingness, which was previously transcended at the time of the attainment of nothingness, is now [again] transcended. Therefore it is said: 'Percipient, namely of the perception of something, or of the perception of nothingness,'

body.text: tatra dhyānasamāpattikāle adho rasātalapraveśavat | kāyasaṃprakhyānaliṃgaṃ | ārūpyasamāpattikāle ākāśātpatanavat | tatra śamathākālenādhyupekṣaṇātsamyakprayogaḥ | tatra dve acittike samāpattī asaṃjñā(jñi)samāpattirnirodhasamāpattiśca | (

children.text: ) tatrāsaṃjñāsamāpatti[ṃ] saṃjñāvimukhena manaskāreṇa pṛthagjana eva samāpadyate, nirodhasamāpattiṃ punarārya eva |
children.translated_text: Therein, the attainment of non-perception is entered only by an ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) through mental attention that turns away from perception. The attainment of cessation, however, is entered only by a noble one (<s>ārya</s>).

body.translated_text: therein, at the time of <s>dhyāna</s> attainment, [there is] the sign of the body-manifestation, like descending into the depths of the earth. At the time of formless (<s>ārūpya</s>) attainment, [it is] like falling from the sky. Therein, through the mode of equanimous observation (<s>adhyupekṣaṇa</s>) at the time of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), there is correct practice. Therein, the two mindless attainments are: the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) and the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>).

body.text: tatra dvābhyāṃ manaskārābhyāmanayoḥ samāpattyoḥ samāpattipraveśo bhavati | tadyathā saṃjñāvimukhena manaskāreṇāsaṃjñā(jñi)samāpatteḥ, naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñoccalitenālambanasanniruddhena ca manaskāreṇa nirodhasamāpatteḥ [|] (

children.text: ) tatra saṃjñārogaḥ, saṃjñāgaṇḍaḥ, saṃjñāśalyaḥ (maṃ), etacchāntametatpraṇītaṃ yadutāsaṃjñikamiti | saṃjñāvimukhaṃ manaskāraṃ parigṛhyotpannotpannāmasaṃjñāsmṛtyamanasikārānu (ramanu)careti (rati) [|] tasya bhāvanānvayātprayogamārge sacittikāvasthā bhavati | samanaskārasamāpannasya ca punaścittaṃ na pravartata iti | sa evaṃ niḥsaraṇasaṃjñā pūrvakeṇa manaskāreṇa śubhakṛtyavītarāgasya, bṛhatphalebhyo vītarāgasya, cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodha iyamucyate [a]saṃjña (jñi)samāpattiḥ | evaṃ ca punarasyāḥ prāptirbhavati ||
children.translated_text: Therein, perception is a disease, perception is a boil, perception is a thorn — "this is peaceful, this is sublime, namely the state without perception" — thus, having adopted a mental attention that turns away from perception, one follows along with the <s>asaṃjñā</s> (non-perception) mindfulness and mental engagement as they arise again and again. Through the continuation of that cultivation, on the path of practice (<s>prayogamārga</s>) there is a state with mind. But when one has entered the attainment with mental attention, the mind no longer operates. Thus, through the mental attention preceded by the perception of escape (<s>niḥsaraṇasaṃjñā</s>), for one who is free from passion toward the <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> (heaven of complete beauty), who is free from passion toward <s>Bṛhatphala</s> (heaven of great fruit), the cessation of mental (<s>citta</s>) and mental-concomitant (<s>caitasika</s>) dharmas — this is called the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>). And thus is the attainment of it.

body.translated_text: Therein, the entry into these two attainments occurs by means of two [types of] mental attention: namely, [entry into] the attainment of non-perception through mental attention that turns away from perception; and [entry into] the attainment of cessation through mental attention that has risen from [the sphere of] neither-perception-nor-non-perception and in which the object has ceased.

body.text: tatra naiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanalābhī āryaḥ pareṇa śāntena vihāreṇa viharttukāmaḥ naiva saṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanāccittamuccā layati | taccittamuccalitamālambanaṃ na labhate | alabhamānaṃ nirudhyate | na pravarttata iti | ya evamākiñcanyāyatanavītarāgasya śaikṣasyārhato vā vihārasaṃjñāpūrvakeṇa manaskāreṇa cittacaitasikānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ nirodha iyamucyate nirodhasamāpattirevaṃ ca punarasyāḥ prāptirbhavati ||
body.translated_text: Therein, a noble one (<s>ārya</s>) who has attained the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naiva-saṃjñā-nāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), wishing to abide in a peaceful abiding beyond that, lifts the mind up from the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. That uplifted mind does not find an object of support (<s>ālambana</s>). Not finding one, it ceases; it does not operate. Thus, for a trainee (<s>śaikṣa</s>) or an <s>Arhat</s> who is free from passion toward the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), the cessation of mental and mental-concomitant dharmas through mental attention preceded by the perception of peaceful abiding (<s>vihārasaṃjñā</s>) — this is called the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). And thus is the attainment of it.

body.text: tatra dhyānasanniśrayeṇa paṃcānāmabhijñānāmabhinirhāro bhavati | kathaṃ ca punarbhavati | yathāpi taddhyāyī lābhī bhavati | pariśuddhasya dhyānasya [|] sa tatpariśuddhaṃ dhyānaṃ niśritya yo [a]nenābhijñādhipataye(pateyo) dharma[ḥ] śruto bhavatyudgṛhītaḥ, paryavāptaḥ, (

children.text: ) yaduta ṛddhiviṣayamvārabhya, pūrvenivāsadivyaśrotracyutyupapādacetaḥ paryāyamvā tameva manasi kurvan samāhitabhūmikena manaskāreṇārthapratisaṃvedī ca bhavati | dharmapratisaṃvedī ca | tasyārthapratisaṃvedino dharma(ḥ) pratisaṃvedinastathāstathā (stathā tathā) cittānyabhisaṃskurvato bahulīkārānvayād bhavati | sa kālo bhavati samayo yadasya bhāja(va)nāphalāḥ (ḥ) paṃcābhijñā utpadyante ||
children.translated_text: namely concerning the domain of <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power), knowledge of former births (<s>pūrvenivāsa</s>), the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapāda</s>), or the knowledge of others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya</s>) — reflecting on that very thing with mental attention at the level of concentration (<s>samāhitabhūmika</s>), he becomes one who comprehends the meaning and one who comprehends the dharma. For him who comprehends the meaning and the dharma, as he fashions his mind in various ways, through the continuation of repeated practice, the time comes, the occasion arises, when the five <s>abhijñās</s> arise as the fruit of cultivation.

body.translated_text: Therein, based on <s>dhyāna</s> (meditative absorption), the accomplishment of the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) takes place. And how does it take place? The meditator becomes one who has attained a purified <s>dhyāna</s>. Relying on that purified <s>dhyāna</s>, whatever dharma conducive to the mastery of the <s>abhijñās</s> has been heard, grasped, and fully comprehended by him,

body.text: api ca tasyā(sa tathā)rtha pratisaṃvedī, dharmapratisaṃvedī sarvābhijñānirhārāya dvādaśasaṃjñā bhāvayati | tadyathā laghu saṃjñā[ṃ] | mṛdusaṃjñā[ṃ] | ākāśadhātusaṃjñāṃ | kāyacittasama[va]dhānasaṃjñāmadhimuktisaṃjñāṃ, pūrvānubhūtacaryānukramānusmṛtisaṃjñāṃ nānāprakāraśabdasannipātanirghoṣasaṃjñāmavadātarūpanimittasaṃjñāṃ, kleśakṛtarūpavikārasaṃjñā[ma]dhimokṣasaṃjñāmamibhvāyatanasaṃjñāṃ kṛtsnāyatanasaṃjñāñca |
body.translated_text: Moreover, that one who comprehends the meaning and comprehends the dharma cultivates twelve perceptions (<s>saṃjñā</s>) for the accomplishment of all the <s>abhijñās</s>. They are: the perception of lightness (<s>laghusaṃjñā</s>), the perception of softness (<s>mṛdusaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the space element (<s>ākāśadhātusaṃjñā</s>), the perception of mind-body coordination (<s>kāyacittasamavadhānasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of resolve (<s>adhimuktisaṃjñā</s>), the perception of recollecting the sequence of previously experienced conduct (<s>pūrvānubhūtacaryānukramānusmṛtisaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the sounds of various assemblages (<s>nānāprakāraśabdasannipātanirghoṣasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the sign of luminous form (<s>avadātarūpanimittasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of bodily changes caused by afflictions (<s>kleśakṛtarūpavikārasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of resolve (<s>adhimokṣasaṃjñā</s>), the perception of the spheres of liberation (<s>abhivyāyatanasaṃjñā</s>), and the perception of the spheres of totality (<s>kṛtsnāyatanasaṃjñā</s>).

body.text: tatra laghusaṃjñāyāṃ laghukamātmānamadhimucyate | tadyathā tūlapindhurvā, karpāsapindhurvā [|] vāyumaṇḍalake vā sa tathā [a]dhimucyamānaḥ tatra prerayatyādhimokṣikeṇaiva manaskāreṇa [|] tadyathā mañcātpīṭhānmañce | evaṃ mañcāt tṛṇasaṃstarakānmañce | tatra mṛdusaṃjñā | mṛdukaṃ kāyamadhimucyate | tadyathā kauśayamvā, kaccamvā, padgamvā, [|] itīyaṃ mṛdusaṃjñāyā laghusaṃjñāyā[ḥ] poṣikā, anugrāhikā [ya]yā anugṛhyamāṇā laghusaṃjñā pṛthuvṛddhivaikalyatāṃ (vipulatāṃ) gacchati | tatrākāśadhātusaṃjñā yayā saṃjñayā laghutāṃ ca mṛdutāṃ cātmano 'dhimucyate | sa cet kvacid gantukāmo bhavati | tatra yadantarālaṃ vivandhacaraṃ rūpigataṃ gamanāya tadākāśamadhimucyate [|] ādhimokṣikaṃ (kena) ca (

children.text: ) manaskāreṇa | tatra cittakāyasamavadhānasaṃjñā yayā cittamvā kāye samavadadhāti | kāyamvā citte, yenāsya kāyo laghutaraśca bhavati, mṛdutaraśca, karmaṇyataraśca, prabhāsvarataraśca [|] cittānvayaścitta pratibandhaścittaṃ niśritya varttate | tatrādhimokṣikasaṃjñā yayā saṃjñayā bhū(dū)ragamāsanne [a]dhimucyate, āsannaṃ dūre, aṇu sthūlaṃ, sthūlamaṇu, pṛthivī āpaḥ, āpaḥ pṛthivī evamekaikena mahābhūtenānyonyaṃ karaṇīyaṃ | vistareṇa tathānirmitaṃ cādhimucyate, rūpanirmitaṃ vā, śabdanirmitaṃ vā [|]
children.translated_text: mental attention. As for the perception of mind-body coordination: by it one either coordinates the mind with the body or the body with the mind, whereby one's body becomes lighter, softer, more workable, and more luminous — following the mind, bound to the mind, operating in dependence on the mind. As for the perception of resolve (<s>adhimokṣikasaṃjñā</s>): by that perception one resolves upon the far as near, the near as far, the small as large, the large as small, earth as water, water as earth — thus each great element is to be interchanged with every other. And in detail, one resolves upon emanations (<s>nirmita</s>) — either form-emanations or sound-emanations.

body.translated_text: Therein, in the perception of lightness, one resolves upon oneself as being light, like a ball of cotton or a ball of kapok, or upon a disc of wind. So resolving, one propels oneself there by that very resolve-based mental attention — for example, from a bench to a seat, from a bench; likewise from a bench to a grass mat, from a bench. As for the perception of softness: one resolves upon the body as soft, like silk, or leather, or fine cloth. This perception of softness is the nourisher and supporter of the perception of lightness, by which, when supported, the perception of lightness reaches fullness, growth, and abundance. As for the perception of the space element: by that perception one resolves upon oneself as being light and soft. And if one wishes to go somewhere, whatever material obstruction intervenes as a hindrance to passage, one resolves upon that as space, and by resolve-based

body.text: ityābhiḥ pañcasaṃjñābhiḥ bhāvanāyā pariniṣpannābhiranekavidhamṛddhiṣayaṃ pratyanubhavatyeko bhūtvā bahudhātmānamupadarśayati | yadutādhimokṣikayā nairmāṇikayā(kyā)saṃjñayā tatra bahudhā punarātmānamupadarśayancai(yaṃścai)kī bhavati | yaduta nirmāṇāntardhāyikayā [a]dhimuktisaṃjñayā tiraḥkuḍyaṃ, tiraḥprākāramasajjamānena (

children.text: ) kāyena gacchati | yena gacchati | (yena gacchati) | pṛthivyāmunmajjanimajjanaṃ karoti | tadyathodake, udake bhidyamānena srātasā gacchati | tadyathā pṛthivyāmākāśe paryaṅkenākrāmati | tadyathā pakṣī śakuni[ḥ], imau vā sūryācandramasāvevaṃ mahardhikau mahānubhāvau pāṇinā āmārṣṭi | parāmārṣṭi | yāvadbrahmalokātkāyena vaśe varttayati | laghumṛdvākāśadhātucittakāyasamavadhānasaṃjñayā parigṛhītayā adhimuktisaṃjñayā sarvametatkaroti | yathāyogamveditavyaṃ | tatra dvividhābrahmalokasya kāyena vaśe vartanā, gamanena ca (|) vaśe varttayati | yathaivādhimuktyā vā, brahmalokādadhaścartukāmatā bhūtānāṃ tadekatyasya copādāyarūpasya [|]
children.translated_text: one goes wherever one wishes. One dives in and out of the earth as if it were water. One moves through water with the current parting, as if through earth. One sits cross-legged in space, just as a bird, a winged creature. One touches and strokes with the hand even these sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. One exercises mastery over the body as far as the <s>Brahmaloka</s> (world of Brahmā). All this one does through the perception of resolve supported by the perceptions of lightness, softness, the space element, and mind-body coordination — this should be understood as appropriate. Therein, exercising mastery over the <s>Brahmaloka</s> with the body is of two kinds: by going, one exercises mastery; and likewise by resolve. And a certain being who wishes to descend from the <s>Brahmaloka</s>, that is due to a form derived from [the primary elements].

body.translated_text: Thus, through these five perceptions, when perfected through cultivation, one experiences manifold domains of <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power). Having been one, one displays oneself as many — namely through the perception of resolve and the perception of emanation (<s>nairmāṇikī saṃjñā</s>). Then, having displayed oneself as many, one becomes one again — namely through the perception of resolve that causes the disappearance of emanations. One passes with the body unobstructed through walls and ramparts,

body.text: tatra pūrvānubhūtacaritānukramānusmṛtisaṃjñā yayā kumārakabhāvamupādāya yatrāsya smṛtiḥ pravarttate | na vyāhanyate | yatrārya gato bhavati, sthito, niṣaṇṇuḥ(ṇṇaḥ), (

children.text: ) śayito vistareṇa sarvāṃ pūrvānubhūtāṃ caryāmaudāraudārikaudārikatayā anuparivāṭikayā avyutkramanti(nte) | kayā samanusmaransaṃjānāti | tasyā bhāvanānvayād bhāvanāphalamanekavidhaṃ pūrvenivāsaṃ samanusmarati yāvatsansā(saṃsā)raṃ soddeśaṃ vistareṇa [|] tatra nānāprakāraśabdasannipātanirghoṣasaṃjñā [|] yasmin grāme vā, nigame vā śreṇyāmvā, pūge vā, parṣadi vā, āyataviśāle vā gṛhe, avavarake vā, nānāprakārasya janakāyasya sanniṣaṇṇasya sannipatitasya yo vyatimiśro, vicitro, nirghoṣo niścarita | yaḥ kalakalaśabda ityucyate | mahatyā vā nadyā vaha[n]tyā nirghoṣaḥ, tatra nimittamudgṛhya yā saṃjñābhāvanā yayā samāhitabhūmikena manasikāreṇāryānāryeṣu śabdeṣu, divyamānuṣyakeṣu, dūrāntikeṣvābhogaṃ vārayati | tasyāsya bahulīkārānvayād bhāvanāphalaṃ divyaṃ śrotraṃ pratilabhate | yena divyamānuṣyakāṃ [kān] śabdāṃ (bdān) śṛṇoti | ye 'pi dūre, ye 'pyantike [|] tatrāvabhāsarūpanimittasaṃjñā [|] pūrvavadālokanimittamudgṛhya tadeva nimittaṃ manasi karoti | iyamavabhāsarūpa nimittasaṃjñā [|] tasyā bhāvanānvayād (
children.translated_text: lain down — in detail, one follows along the entire previously experienced conduct progressively, from the coarser to the coarser, in a connected sequence. By that perception one recollects and cognizes. Through the continuation of that cultivation, as the fruit of cultivation, one recollects many kinds of former births (<s>pūrvenivāsa</s>), up to the entire cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with specific details and in full. As for the perception of the sounds of various assemblages: in whatever village, town, guild, corporation, assembly, or in a large and spacious house, or in a small room, whatever mixed and diverse sound issues forth from a gathering of various kinds of people sitting together and assembled — what is called a commotion of noise — or the sound of a great flowing river; having grasped that sign, whatever cultivation of that perception is undertaken with concentrated mental attention directed toward noble and ignoble sounds, divine and human, far and near — through the continuation of that repeated practice, as the fruit of cultivation, one obtains the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotra</s>), by which one hears both divine and human sounds, whether far or near. As for the perception of the sign of luminous form: as before, having grasped the sign of light, one reflects on that very sign. This is the perception of the sign of luminous form. Through the continuation of its cultivation,

children.text: ) bhāvanāphalaṃ cyutyupapādajñānaṃ pratilabhate | yena divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhena vistareṇa yāvatkāyasya bhedātsvargatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante(te) | tatra kleśakṛtarūpavikārasaṃjñā | yayā raktadviṣṭamūḍhānāṃ krodhopanāhapra[yu]ktaparidāhāhrīkyānapatrāpyakleśopakleśaparyavanaddhacittānāṃ sattvānāṃ rūpāvasthāmupalakṣayati | pari[c]chinatti [|] evaṃ rūpāraktasya rūpāvasthā bhavati | rūpavikṛtiḥ | tadyathā uddhatendriyatā, smitamukhatā [|] evaṃ rūpā dviṣṭasya rūpāvasthā bhavati | rūpavikṛtiḥ | tadyathā mukhavivarṇatā sagadgadasvaratā | kṛtabhṛkuṭitā | evaṃrūpā mūḍhasya paryavasthā bhavati | rūpavikṛtiḥ | tadyathā mūkatā arthanidhyaptāvapratipadyanatā (danatā) prākṛtāprākṛtā vā vāgvyāhāratā [|] ityebhirākārairevaṃ bhāgīyairyāvadāhrīkyānapatrāpyaparyavasthitasya (
children.translated_text: as the fruit of cultivation, one obtains the knowledge of death and rebirth (<s>cyutyupapādajñāna</s>), by which, with the divine eye (<s>divyacakṣus</s>) that is purified — in detail, up to — after the breaking up of the body, they are reborn among the gods in the heavenly realm. As for the perception of bodily changes caused by afflictions: by it one observes and discerns the physical condition of beings who are lustful, hateful, or deluded, whose minds are enveloped by anger, enmity, burning torment, shamelessness, lack of moral dread, and various afflictions and secondary afflictions. Thus, the physical condition and bodily change of one who is lustful is like this: agitated sense-faculties, a smiling face. Thus, the physical condition and bodily change of one who is hateful is like this: discoloration of the face, a faltering voice, a furrowed brow. Thus, the mental state and bodily change of one who is deluded is like this: muteness, inability to respond when reflecting on the meaning, speech that is either natural or unnatural. By these and similar characteristics, up to one who is overcome by shamelessness and lack of moral dread —

children.text: ) yā rūpāvasthā bhavati | rūpavikṛtiḥ | tato nimittamudgṛhya manasi karoti | tadyathā bahulīkārānvayād bhāvanāphalaṃ cetaḥparyāyajñānamutpadyate | yena parasattvānāṃ parapudgalānāṃ vitarkitaṃ vicāritaṃ mano manasā yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti |
children.translated_text: whatever physical condition and bodily change there is — having grasped the sign from that, one reflects upon it. Through the continuation of that repeated practice, as the fruit of cultivation, the knowledge of others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāyajñāna</s>) arises, by which one knows as it truly is the thoughts and deliberations, the mind, of other beings and other persons.

body.translated_text: Therein, the perception of recollecting the sequence of previously experienced conduct: by it, starting from childhood, wherever one's memory operates without being impeded, wherever one has gone, stood, sat down,

body.text: tatra vimokṣābhibhvāyatana-kṛtsnāyatanasaṃjñābhāvanā pūrvavadveditavyā | tadyathā samāhitāyāṃ bhūmau | yayā bhāvanayā āryāmṛddhimabhinirharati | vastupariṇāminī[ṃ] nairmāṇikīmādhimokṣikīṃ | tadyathā araṇā praṇidhijñānaṃ | catasraḥ pratisamvidaḥ tadyathā dharmapratisaṃvidartha pratisaṃvinniruktipratisamvitpratibhānapratisamvit [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, the cultivation of the perceptions of the liberations (<s>vimokṣa</s>), the spheres of mastery (<s>abhibhvāyatana</s>), and the spheres of totality (<s>kṛtsnāyatana</s>) should be understood as before, namely at the level of concentration. By that cultivation one accomplishes the noble <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power): that which transforms objects (<s>vastupariṇāminī</s>), the emanatory (<s>nairmāṇikī</s>), and the resolve-based (<s>ādhimokṣikī</s>). Such as the <s>araṇā</s> (non-contentiousness), the resolution-knowledge (<s>praṇidhijñāna</s>), and the four analytical knowledges (<s>pratisamvid</s>): namely, analytical knowledge of dharma (<s>dharmapratisaṃvid</s>), analytical knowledge of meaning (<s>arthapratisaṃvid</s>), analytical knowledge of etymology (<s>niruktipratisaṃvid</s>), and analytical knowledge of eloquence (<s>pratibhānapratisaṃvid</s>).

body.text: tatrāryāyāścānāryāyā ṛddherayaṃ viśeṣaḥ | āryayā ṛddhyā yadyadeva vastu pariṇāmayati | yadyadeva nimittaṃ nirmiṇoti | tattathaiva bhavati | nānyathā | sarveṇa tena kāryaṃ śakyate kartum | anāryayā na punarna tathaiva bhavatyapi tu | māyākārakasyaiva saṃdarśana mātrakaṃ khyāti | evamābhirdvādaśabhiḥ saṃjñābhirbahulīkārānvayādyathāyogaṃ sa pañcānāmabhijñānāmāryāṇāṃ ca guṇānāmapṛthagjanasandhāraṇānāṃ yathāyogamabhinirhāro veditavyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, this is the distinction between noble and non-noble <s>ṛddhi</s> (magical power): with noble <s>ṛddhi</s>, whatever object one transforms, whatever sign one emanates, it becomes exactly so and not otherwise — one is able to accomplish every purpose with it. With non-noble <s>ṛddhi</s>, however, it does not become exactly so; rather, it appears merely as a display, like that of a magician. Thus, through the repeated practice of these twelve perceptions, as appropriate, one should understand the accomplishment of the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges) and the noble qualities that are not shared by ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), each as appropriate.

body.text: tatra prathame dhyāne mṛdumadhyādhimātraparibhāvitena yathāyogaṃ brahmakāyikānāṃ, brahmapurohitānāṃ, mahābrahmaṇāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupasampadyate [|] dvitīye dhyāne mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhāvite yathāyogaṃ parīttānāmābhāsvarāṇāṃ ca devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupasaṃpadyate | tṛtīye dhyāne mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhāvite yathāyogaṃ parīttaśubhānāṃ, sapramāṇaśubhānāṃ, śubhakṛtyānāṃ ca devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupasaṃpadyate | caturthe dhyāne mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhāvite yathāyogamanabhrakānāṃ, puṇyaprasavānāṃ, bṛhatphalānāṃ ca devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupasampadyate | sa cetpunaranāgāmī anāsraveṇa dhyānena caturthena sāsravaṃ, vyavakīrṇaṃ (

children.text: ) bhāvayati | tasmiṃ(smin) mṛdumadhyādhimātrādhimātratarādhimātratamabhāvite yathāyogaṃ pañcānāṃ śuddhāvāsānāṃ devānāṃ sa(ha)bhāgatāyāmupasampadyate | tadyathā adahe(hre)ṣvatāpeṣu, sudarśaneṣu, akaniṣṭheṣu [|] ākāśavijñānākiñcanyanaivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatane mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhāvite ākāśavijñānākiñcanyanavasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatanopagānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupasampadyate [|] arūpiṇaśca devāstasmātteṣāṃ sthānāntarakṛto bhedo nāsti, vihārakṛtastu viśeṣo bhavati | asaṃjñisamāpattyāṃ bhāvitāyāmasaṃjñisattvānāṃ devānāṃ sabhāgatāyāmupasampadyate |
children.translated_text: ) one cultivates. When that [meditation] has been cultivated to mild, middling, intense, more intense, and most intense degrees, one is reborn according to correspondence in the companionship of the gods of the five <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) — namely, among the <s>Avṛhas</s> (Undecreasing), the <s>Atapas</s> (Unafflicted), the <s>Sudarśanas</s> (Beautiful to See), and the <s>Akaniṣṭhas</s> (Highest). When the bases of infinite space, consciousness, nothingness, and neither-perception-nor-non-perception have been cultivated to mild, middling, and intense degrees, one is reborn in the companionship of the gods who have attained the bases of infinite space, consciousness, nothingness, and neither-perception-nor-non-perception. And the formless gods — therefore there is no distinction among them based on different stations, but there is a distinction based on their mode of dwelling. When the attainment of non-perception (<s>asaṃjñisamāpatti</s>) has been cultivated, one is reborn in the companionship of the gods among the non-percipient beings.

body.translated_text: Therein, in the first <s>dhyāna</s>, when cultivated to a mild, moderate, or superior degree, one is reborn as appropriate in the company of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s>, <s>Brahmapurohita</s>, or <s>Mahābrahmā</s> gods. In the second <s>dhyāna</s>, when cultivated to a mild, moderate, or superior degree, one is reborn as appropriate in the company of the <s>Parīttābha</s> or <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods. In the third <s>dhyāna</s>, when cultivated to a mild, moderate, or superior degree, one is reborn as appropriate in the company of the <s>Parīttaśubha</s>, <s>Sapramāṇaśubha</s>, or <s>Śubhakṛtsna</s> gods. In the fourth <s>dhyāna</s>, when cultivated to a mild, moderate, or superior degree, one is reborn as appropriate in the company of the <s>Anabhraka</s>, <s>Puṇyaprasava</s>, or <s>Bṛhatphala</s> gods. And if one is a non-returner (<s>Anāgāmin</s>), with the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> that is uncontaminated (<s>anāsrava</s>), mixed with the contaminated,

body.text: tatra katamāni vītarāgasya liṃgāni | āha | sthirakāyakarmānto bhavatyacalendriyaḥ [|] na cāsyeryāpatha āśu paryādīyate | ekenāpīryāpathena ciraṃ kālamatināmayatyaparitasyamānaḥ | na tāśu(su)īryāntaraṃ spṛhayati | mandabhāṇī ca bhavati, praśāntabhāṇī ca [|] na saṃgaṇikārāmo, na saṃsargārāmo, dhīrā cāsya vāg(k)pravartate | cakṣuṣā rūpāṇi dṛṣṭvā rūpapratisamvedī bhavati | na rūparāgapratisamvedī | evaṃ śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyapratisaṃvedī bhavati | no tu (

children.text: ) yāvatspraṣṭavyarāgapratisaṃvedī | viśāradaśca bhavati | gambhīrabuddhirvipulapraśrabdhicittakāyopagūḍhaḥ || anabhidhyāluravikṣobhyaḥ | kṣamāvānna cāsya kāmavitarkādayaḥ pāpakāścittaṃ kṣobhayanti | ityevaṃ bhāgīyāni vītarāgaliṃgāni veditavyānītyayaṃ tāvat laukikamārgagamanasya vibhāgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: ) up to attachment to tangible objects. One becomes confident, of profound intelligence, pervaded by vast tranquility (<s>praśrabdhi</s>) of mind and body; free from covetousness, unshakable, patient — and the evil thoughts beginning with sensual thought do not disturb one's mind. Such and similar are the signs of one free from passion to be understood. This is the classification of progress through the mundane path.

body.translated_text: Therein, what are the signs of one free from passion (<s>vītarāga</s>)? He says: One becomes steady in bodily actions, with unmoved faculties. One's posture does not quickly deteriorate; one passes a long time even in a single posture without becoming weary; one does not quickly crave a change of posture. One becomes one who speaks sparingly and speaks calmly; one does not delight in socializing, does not delight in association; one's speech proceeds with composure. Having seen forms with the eye, one experiences the form but does not experience attachment to the form. Likewise, one experiences sounds, smells, tastes, and tangible objects, but not

body.text: atha lokottareṇa mārgeṇa gantukāmo bhavati tasya catvāryāryasatyānyārabhya sapta manaskārā anupūrveṇotpadyante | lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī[di]manaskārādayaḥ prayoganiṣṭhāphalaparyavasānā yāvadarhattvaprāpteḥ | tatra caturṇāmāryasatyānāṃ soddeśavibhaṃgānāṃ śramaṇenodgṛhītayogācāraḥ | subhāvitamanaskāro vā, mauladhyānārūpyalābhī vā, caturbhirākārairduḥkhasatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratisaṃvedayate | tadyathānityākāreṇa, duḥkhākāreṇa, anātmākāreṇa ca | caturbhirākāraiḥ samudayasatyasya tadyathā hetutaḥ, samudayataḥ, prabhavataḥ, pratyayataśca [|] caturbhirākārairnirodhasatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratisamvedayate | tadyathā nirodhataḥ, śāntataḥ, praṇītato, niḥsaraṇataśca [|] caturbhirākārairmārgasatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratisamvedayate | tadyathā mārgato, nyāyataḥ pratipattito, nairyāṇikataśca | so 'sya bhavati lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī manaskāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Now, when one desires to proceed by the supramundane path, with reference to the Four Noble Truths, seven mental attentions (<s>manaskāra</s>) arise in succession — beginning with the mental attention that apprehends the characteristics, and culminating in the fruit of the practice leading to the final goal, up to the attainment of <s>arhatship</s>. Therein, the <s>śramaṇa</s> (ascetic), having grasped the <s>yogācāra</s> (practice of yoga) regarding the Four Noble Truths with their outline and detailed exposition — or being one whose mental attention has been well cultivated, or being one who has obtained the root <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments] — apprehends the characteristic of the truth of suffering through four aspects: namely, the aspect of impermanence,

body.text: tatra daśabhirākārairduḥkhasatyaṃ parīkṣamāṇaścatura ākārānanupraviśati | katamairdaśabhistadyathā | vipariṇāmākāreṇa, avināśākāreṇa, viyogākāreṇa, sannihitā [|] kāreṇa, dharmatākāreṇa | saṃyojanabandhanākāreṇa, aniṣṭākāreṇa, ayogakṣemākāreṇa, anupa(kāreṇa)lambhākāreṇa, asvātantrākāreṇa ca | etānpunardaśākārān upapattisādhanayuktyā upaparīkṣate |
body.translated_text: Therein, examining the truth of suffering through ten aspects, one enters into [each of] the four aspects. By which ten? Namely: through the aspect of change, through the aspect of destruction, through the aspect of separation, through the aspect of being [ever-]present, through the aspect of natural law, through the aspect of fetters and bonds, through the aspect of the undesirable, through the aspect of insecurity, through the aspect of unobtainability, and through the aspect of non-autonomy. These ten aspects, furthermore, one investigates by means of the reasoning of proof by logical establishment (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>).

body.text: tatrāgamastāvadyathoktaṃ bhagavatā sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ [|] te punaḥ saṃskārāḥ samāsataḥ sattvalokaśca bhājanalokaśca || uktañca bhagavatā sattvalokamadhikṛtya, paśyāmyahaṃ, bhikṣavo, divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa satvāṃścyavamānāṃścotpadyamānāṃśca (

children.text: ) vistareṇa yāvat kāsasya bhedātsugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante | ityanena tāvatparyāyeṇa ityanena tāvatparyāyeṇa bhagavatā cakṣuṣmatā pratyakṣadarśinā sattvalokasyānityatā vyākhyātā | uktaṃcabhagavatā, bhavati, bhikṣavaḥ, sa samayo yaddīrghasyādhvano 'tyayādanupūrveṇa yāvatsaptānāṃ sūryāṇāṃ loke prādurbhāvo bhavati | (
children.translated_text: ) in detail up to: 'upon the breaking up of the body, they are reborn among the gods in the good destiny, in the heavenly world.' By this manner, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the one with eyes, who sees directly, has explained the impermanence of the world of sentient beings. And the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Bhikṣus</s>, there comes a time when, after the passing of a long period, gradually up to seven suns appear in the world.'

children.text: ) tadyathā saptasūryopame sūgre(tre)yāvadasyāḥ khalu mahāpṛthivyāḥ sumerośca parvata rājasya | yāvacca brahmalokād bhājanalokasya dagdhasya dhmātasya maṣirapi na prajñāyate | chāyikāvaśiṣṭamapi na prajñāyate [|] anena paryāyeṇa bhagavatā bhājanalaukika(loka)sthānityatā ākhyātāyaṃ(temaṃ) tāvadāptāgamaṃ niśrityāyaṃ yogī śraddhādhipateyaṃ sarvasaṃskārānityatāyāṃ niścayaṃ pratilabhate ||
children.translated_text: ) Just as in the Discourse on the Seven Suns — up to: of this great earth and of <s>Sumeru</s>, the king of mountains, and of the receptacle-world up to the <s>Brahma</s> world — when it is burned and consumed, not even a trace of ash is discerned; not even a shadow-residue is discerned. By this manner, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has declared the impermanence of the stations of the receptacle-world. Relying on this authoritative tradition (<s>āptāgama</s>), this <s>yogin</s>, through the predominance of faith, obtains certainty regarding the impermanence of all conditioned things.

body.translated_text: Therein, first the scriptural authority (<s>āgama</s>): as the <s>Bhagavān</s> said — 'All conditioned things (<s>saṃskāra</s>) are impermanent.' Those conditioned things, in brief, are twofold: the world of sentient beings (<s>sattvaloka</s>) and the world as receptacle (<s>bhājanaloka</s>). And the <s>Bhagavān</s> said with reference to the world of sentient beings: 'I see, <s>bhikṣus</s>, with the divine eye, purified, surpassing the human — beings passing away and being reborn —'

body.text: sa evaṃ niścayaṃ pratilabhya, śraddhādhipatyena punaḥ punaḥ pratyakṣatāmapi, parokṣatāmaparapratyayāṃ (yatāṃ) cānityatā(yāṃ) samanveṣate | kathañca punaḥ samanveṣate | āha | dvividhaṃ vastu vyavasthāpayati | āha | ādhyātmikambāhyaṃ ca | tatrādhyātmikamvastu yatṣaḍāyatanaṃ, bāhyamvastu (sa evaṃ niścayaṃ pratilabhya śraddhādhipatyena punaḥ punaḥ pratyavekṣatāmaviparokṣatāmaparapratyayatā(ṃ) cānityatāṃ(yāṃ) samanveṣate | āha | dvividhaṃ vastu vyavasthāpayati | ādhyātmikambāhyañca | tatrādhyātmikamvastu yatṣaḍāyatanaṃ bāhyamvastu) ṣoḍaśavidhaṃ | tadyathā pṛthivīvastu [tadyathā] grāmanigamagṛhāpaṇādayaḥ | ārāmavastu tadyathā tṛṇauṣadhivanaspatayaḥ | parvatavastu tadyathā citrāḥ (

children.text: ) parvatasanniveśāḥ | utsasara(sa)staḍāganadīprasravaṇavastu [|] kṣetravastu kośasannidhivastrālaṃkāranṛttagītavāditagandhamālyavilepanamāṇḍopaskāralokāstrīpuruṣapāricaryāvastūni ca tānyetāni bhavanti | ṣoḍaśavastūni [|]
children.translated_text: ) mountain configurations, springs, ponds, rivers, and stream-sources; agricultural land; treasury and stored wealth; cloth, ornaments, dance, song, and music; scents, garlands, ointments; vessels, furnishings; worldly entities; and the services of men and women. These are the sixteen [external] entities.

body.translated_text: Having obtained this certainty, through the predominance of faith, one again and again seeks out the impermanence — in direct perception, in the imperceptible, and in what depends on another's testimony. And how does one seek? He says: One establishes the domain as twofold. He says: internal and external. Therein, the internal domain is the six sense-bases; the external domain is [the objects].

body.text: sa evamādhyātmika[ṃ] bāhyaṃ vastu vyavasthāpayitvā (vyāvasthāpya) [ā]dhyātmikasya tāvadvastunaḥ pratyakṣādhipateyena manaskāreṇa viparimāṇā(ṇāmā)kāreṇa vipariṇāmānityatāṃ samanveṣate | tatra [pañcada]śavidha ādhyātmikasya vastuno vipariṇāmaḥ | aṣṭau vipariṇāmakaraṇāni |
body.translated_text: Having thus established the internal and external domains, one first seeks out the impermanence of change (<s>vipariṇāmānityatā</s>) of the internal domain through the mental attention that has direct perception as its predominant [mode], by the aspect of change. Therein, the change of the internal domain is of fifteen kinds; the causes of change are eight.

body.text: tatra katamaḥ [pañcada]śavidho vipariṇāmaḥ | ādhyātmikasya vastunastadyathā-avasthākṛto, varṇakṛtaḥ, saṃsthānakṛtaḥ, sampattivipattikṛtaḥ | aṃgasākalyavaikalyakṛtaḥ, [pariśramakṛtaḥ], paropakramakṛtaḥ, [śītoṣṇakṛtaḥ] | īryāpathakṛtaḥ, [svayaṃkṛtaḥ], saṃkleśakṛto(taḥ), [kṛṣikṛtaḥ], maraṇakṛto, vinīlakādi kṛtaḥ, sarveṇa sarvamasaṃprakhyānaparikṣayakṛto vipariṇāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the fifteenfold change of the internal domain? Namely: change due to stage [of life], change due to complexion, change due to bodily configuration, change due to fortune and misfortune, change due to completeness and deficiency of limbs, [change due to fatigue], change due to another's assault, [change due to cold and heat], change due to posture, [change due to one's own action], change due to affliction, [change due to agricultural work], change due to death, change due to blue-discoloration and so on [of the corpse], and change due to the utter perishing and complete exhaustion of all.

body.text: tatrāṣṭau vipariṇāmakāraṇāni | katamāni [|] āha | tadyathā kālaparivāsaḥ, paropakrama upabhogaḥ, (

children.translated_text: ) change of season (<s>ṛtuvipariṇāma</s>), burning by fire (<s>agnidāha</s>), wetting by water (<s>udakakleda</s>), drying by wind (<s>vāyuśoṣa</s>), and the arising of a different condition (<s>pratyayāntarasamudgama</s>).

body.translated_text: Therein, the eight causes of change — what are they? He says: namely, the passage of time (<s>kālaparivāsa</s>), another's assault, consumption/use (<s>upabhoga</s>),

body.text: tatra kālaparivāso nāma yeṣāṃ bhāvānāṃ rūpiṇāṃ svasthāne 'pyupanyastakānāṃ kālāntareṇa jarjarato palabhyate | jīrṇatā rūpavikṛtiḥ ||
body.translated_text: Therein, the 'passage of time' means: those material things which, even when placed in their own location, are found to be decayed after the passage of time — decay, deterioration, and disfigurement of form.

body.text: tatra paropakramo nāma yathāpi tat paro vividhāni rūpāṇi vividhaiḥ praharaṇaiḥ vividhairupakramaviśeṣaiḥ vicitrāṃ vikṛtimāpādayati |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'another's assault' means: just as another, through various forms with various weapons and various modes of assault, brings about manifold disfigurement.

body.text: tatropabhogo nāma yathāpi tatpratisvāmino vividhaṃ rūpamupabhuṃjānā upabhogavidhipatitvā (gamadhipatiṃ kṛtvā vi)kṛtimāpādayanti |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'consumption' means: just as owners, while using various forms of material things, making the mode of use the predominant factor, bring about disfigurement.

body.text: tatra ṛtuvipariṇāmo nāma tadyathā hemante tṛṇauṣadhivanaspatīnāṃ pāṇḍutvaṃ, śīrṇatvaṃ prajāyate | grīṣmavarṣāsu punaḥ saṃpūrṇatvaṃ, haritatā ca | tathā phalasamṛddhiḥ, puṣpasamṛddhiḥ, patrasamṛddhiḥ, vipattiśca teṣāmeva [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, 'change of season' means: just as in winter, yellowing and shedding occur among grasses, herbs, and forest trees; but in summer and the rains, fullness and greenness [appear]; likewise, the abundance of fruit, abundance of flowers, abundance of leaves — and the decline of those same [trees].

body.text: tatrāgnidāho nāma yathāpi tadagnirmukto grāmanigamarāṣṭrarājadhānīrdahan paraiti |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'burning by fire' means: just as fire, once released, burns through villages, towns, kingdoms, and capital cities, and moves on.

body.text: tatrodakakledo nāma tathāpi tanmahān udakaskandhaḥ samudāgato (grāmanigamarājarāṣṭradhānīṃ dahan paraiti | tatrodakakledo nāma tathāpi tanmahānudakaskandhaḥ samudāgato) grāmanigamarājarāṣṭradhānī[ḥ] plāvayan paraiti ||
body.translated_text: Therein, 'wetting by water' means: just as a great mass of water, having arisen, inundates villages, towns, kingdoms, and capital cities, and moves on.

body.text: tatra vāyuśoṣo nāma tathāpi tanmahatā vāyuskandhenārdrāḥ pṛthivīpradeśā laghu laghveva śuṣyanti | tathārdrāṇi vastūnyārdrāḥ sasyajātayaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'drying by wind' means: just as through a great mass of wind, moist areas of earth dry up quickly — and likewise moist things and moist crops.

body.text: pratyayāntarasamudgamo nāma tadyathā sukhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītya sukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānasya sukhavedanīya(ḥ)sparśasamudgamaḥ | [evaṃ duḥkhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānasya su(duḥ)kha vedanīya(ḥ) sparśasamudgamaḥ] aduḥkhāsukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānasyāsukhavedanīyasya vāduḥkhavedanīyasya vā sparśasya samudgamaḥ | tathā raktasya pratighanimittasamudgamaḥ yasya samudgamādrāgaparyavasthānaṃ ca vigacchati | pratighaparyavasthānaṃ cotpadyate (|) evaṃ dviṣṭasya mūḍhasya visabhāgaḥ | kleśotpattinimittaḥ samudgamo veditavyaḥ | tadyathā cakṣurvijñāne saṃmukhī bhūte śabdaviṣayasamudgamaḥ | gandharasaspraṣṭavyāḥ | dharmanimitta samudgamo yena viṣayāntareṇa visabhāgānyutpadyante | itīmānyaṣṭau vipariṇāmakāraṇāni [|] yā kācidvipariṇatirbhavati | rūpiṇāmvā, arūpiṇāmvā, dharmāṇāṃ sarvo(rvā) sau ebhiraṣṭābhirnāta uttari nāto bhūyaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, 'the arising of a different condition' means: just as for one who, dependent on a contact to be experienced as pleasant, is experiencing a pleasant feeling — there arises a contact to be experienced as [painful]; [likewise for one experiencing a painful feeling, a contact to be experienced as painful arises;] for one experiencing a neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling, there arises a contact to be experienced as pleasant or as painful. Likewise, for one who is passionate, the sign of hostility arises — upon whose arising, the state of being overcome by passion subsides.

body.text: tatrādhyātmikasya vastunaḥ kathamavasthākṛtaṃ vipariṇāmamparyeṣate | ihānecā(nā)tmano [vā] pareṣāmvā dahrāvasthāmupādāya yāvajjīrṇāvasthā dṛṣṭā bhavati | tāṃ pūrveṇāparāṃ visadṛśāṃ (śīṃ), vyatibhinnāṃ, vipariṇatāṃ, saṃskārasantatiṃ dṛṣṭvāsyaivaṃ bhavati | anityā bata(te) me saṃskārā[s] tathāpyeṣāṃ pratyakṣata eveyaṃ pūrvaṇāparā vikṛtirupalabhyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one seek out the change due to stage of life of the internal domain? Here, whether in oneself or in others, from the stage of infancy up to the stage of old age — these are seen. Having seen that successive mental continuum of conditioned things as dissimilar, as distinct, as transformed from the earlier to the later, one thinks: 'Impermanent indeed are my conditioned things! For their transformation from earlier to later is perceived directly.'

body.text: tatra kathaṃ suvarṇakṛtā(nāṃ) vipariṇāmānityatāṃ paryeṣate | ihānenātmano (sa tathātmano) vā, pareṣām vā, yā pūrvaṃ(tāma) sva(su)varṇatā(tāṃ), succhavitā(tāṃ), tvagvarṇatā (tām) | paścācca durvarṇatāṃ duśchavitāṃ rukṣatāṃ rukṣavarṇatāṃ ca | paśyati [|] dṛṣṭvā ca punareva pratyudāvarttyāpareṇa samayena tāmeva suvarṇatāṃ paryavadātatvagvarṇatāṃ ca paśyati | tasyaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bata(te)me saṃskārāṇā(rāsteṣā)miyamevaṃ rūpā pratyakṣato varṇavikṛtirupalabhyate |
body.translated_text: Therein, how does one seek out the impermanence of change due to complexion? Here, whether in oneself or in others, the former good complexion, good appearance, and beautiful skin-color — and later, the poor complexion, poor appearance, roughness, and rough color — one sees. And having seen, turning back again, after some time, one sees that very same good complexion and clear skin-color. One then thinks: 'Impermanent indeed are my conditioned things!'

body.text: tatra kathaṃ [saṃ]sthānakṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ paryeṣate | yathā varṇa ukta evaṃ kṛśasthūlatayā saṃsthānaṃ veditavyaṃ sampattirvipattiśca | tadyathā jñātisampattirvā, bhogasampattirvā, śīladṛṣṭisampattirvā [|] etadviparyayeṇa vipattista (ttiḥ [|] ta)tkathamaṃgapratyaṃgavipariṇāmānityatāṃ (

children.text: ) paryeṣate | ihānenātmano vā, pareṣāmvā yā pūrvaṃ suvarṇatā, succhavitā, paryavadātatvagvarṇatā dṛṣṭā bhavati | pa(pra)tisampattirvā bhogasampattirvā śīladṛṣṭisampattirvā (|) etadviparyayeṇa vipatti s(ḥ) [|]
children.translated_text: Here, one has previously seen in oneself or in others a good complexion, a good skin-tone, and a clear and pure skin-color; or prosperity of relatives, prosperity of wealth, or prosperity of moral conduct and views. Decline is the opposite of these.

body.translated_text: How does one investigate the impermanence-through-change produced by configuration (<s>saṃsthāna</s>)? Just as was stated regarding complexion, so too configuration should be understood through thinness and stoutness, and [through] prosperity and decline. Namely, prosperity of relatives, prosperity of wealth, or prosperity of moral conduct and views. Decline is the opposite of these. How does one investigate the impermanence-through-change of limbs and subsidiary limbs?

body.text: tatkathamaṃgapratyaṃgavipariṇāmānityatāṃ paryeṣati(te) | ihānenātmano vā, parasya vā, pūrvamapi (vi)kalāṃgatā dṛṣṭā bhavati | sopareṇa samayena vikalatāmpaśyati rājato vā, corato vā, manuṣyato vā, amanuṣyato vā [|] dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavati | anityā bata(te)me saṃskārā iti pūrvavade(t [|]) |
body.translated_text: How does one investigate the impermanence-through-change of limbs and subsidiary limbs? Here, one has previously seen in oneself or in another a state of complete [bodily] integrity. At a later time, one sees mutilation — whether from a king, a thief, a human, or a non-human. Having seen [this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> (conditioned phenomena) are impermanent!' — as stated before.

body.text: (eva)mātmanaḥ pareṣāṃ ca śrāntakāyatāṃ, klāntakāyatāṃ dhāvato vā, plavato vā, laṃghayato vā, abhiru(ro)hatovā, vividhaṃ vākkarma drutaṃ kurvataḥ | sopareṇa samayena vigataklamaśramatāṃ paśyati | tasyaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bateme saṃskārā iti pūrvavat | evampariśramakṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāmparyeṣate ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, one sees in oneself or in others — while running, swimming, jumping, climbing, or quickly performing various activities — bodily weariness and exhaustion. At a later time, one sees [them] freed from fatigue and weariness. It then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' — as before. Thus one investigates the impermanence-through-change produced by exertion.

body.text: evamātmano vā pareṣāmvā paropakrameṇa kāyavikṛtiṃ paśyati | tadyathā latābhirvā tāḍitasya, kaśābhirvā, (

Having seen [this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' — as before. Thus one investigates the impermanence-through-change produced by the harm of others.

body.translated_text: Likewise, one sees in oneself or in others a bodily deformation caused by the action of another — as when struck by creepers, whips,

body.text: tathātmānaṃ vā, paramvā, śīla(ta)kāle pratyupasthite aviśadakāyaṃ, saṃkucitakāyaṃ, śītaparyavasthānaparyavasthitamuṣṇābhilāṣaparigataṃ paśyati | uṣṇakāle vā punaḥ pratyupasthite aviśadakāyaṃ, saṃkucitakāyaṃ śītaparyavasthānaparyavasthitaviśadagātraprasvinnagātraṃ santaptagātramucchraṣya vacanaṃ tṛṣāparigataṃ | śītasaṃsparśābhilāṣiṇaṃ paśyati | dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ pratyudāvarttya punaḥ śītakāle pūrvoktairevākāraiḥ paśyati | dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavati | anityā bata(te)me saṃskārā iti pūrvavadeva[ṃ] śītakṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ paryeṣate |
body.translated_text: Likewise, when the cold season arrives, one sees oneself or another with an uncomfortable body, a contracted body, enveloped by the state of cold, gripped by the desire for warmth. Or when the hot season arrives, one sees an uncomfortable body, a contracted body [from cold] with limbs clear [with sweat], perspiring, burning, with raised voice, gripped by thirst, longing for the touch of coolness. Having seen [this], then turning back, in the cold season one again sees [them] in the previously described conditions. Having seen [this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' — exactly as before. Thus one investigates the impermanence-through-change produced by cold and heat.
