body.translated_text: Furthermore, one sees oneself or another internally in one of the four postures — walking, standing, sitting, or lying down — with one or another posture. Then at another time, one sees [them] refreshed by a different [posture]. Having seen [this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas,

body.text: kathaṃ sparśakṛtāmvipariṇāmānityatāmparyeṣate | sukhavedanīyena sparśena spṛṣṭaḥ, sukhavedanīyaṃ sparśaṃ pratītyotpannāṃ sukhāṃ vedanāṃ vedayamānaḥ | sukhā[ṃ] vedanāvasthāmātmanaḥ pari[c]chinatti | yathā sukhadevanāvasthā[ṃ] evaṃ duḥkhāsukhāsu(duḥ)khavedanāvasthāṃ [|] tasya pūrvāṃ paryeṣaṇā āsāṃ vedanānāṃ navanavatāniḥpurāṇa purāṇatāmāpāyikatāṃ tāvatkālikatāmitvarapratyupāsthāyitamanyathībhāvaṃ dṛṣṭvā, dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavati | anityā bateme saṃskārā iti pūrvat ||
body.translated_text: How does one investigate the impermanence-through-change produced by contact (<s>sparśa</s>)? Having been touched by a pleasant contact, experiencing a pleasant feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) arisen dependent on that pleasant contact, one discerns in oneself the state of pleasant feeling. Just as [one discerns] the state of pleasant feeling, so too [one discerns] the states of painful and neither-painful-nor-pleasant feelings. Through the previous investigation of these feelings — seeing their newness and novelty, their becoming old, their perishable nature, their temporary nature, the swiftness of their passing, and their becoming otherwise — having seen [this], it occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' — as before.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ kleśakṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | sarāgaṃ cittamutpannaṃ parijānāti | vigatarāgaṃ sadveṣamvigatadveṣaṃ | samohaṃ vigatamohamanyatamānyatamena vā upakleśenopakliṣṭaṃ cittamupakliṣṭamiti parijānāti | anupakliṣṭamvā punaranupakliṣṭamiti parijānāti | tasya pū(pau)rvāparyeṇaibhiḥ kleśopakleśairavatīparṇavipariṇatāvipariṇatāṃcittasantatiṃ dṛṣṭvaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bateme saṃskārā iti | tathā hyeṣāṃ pratyakṣataḥ saṃkleśakṛto vipariṇāmaupalabhyate ||
body.translated_text: How does one practice the impermanence-through-change produced by <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions)? One fully knows a mind arisen with attachment (<s>sarāga</s>), free from attachment, with aversion, free from aversion, with delusion, free from delusion, or afflicted by one or another secondary defilement (<s>upakleśa</s>) as afflicted, or unafflicted as unafflicted. Having seen, through the previous and subsequent [observation], the continuum of mind — transformed and untransformed by these afflictions and secondary afflictions — it occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' For indeed, the change produced by defilement is directly perceived in them.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ vyādhikṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | ihānenaikadātmā ca pare ca dṛṣṭvā(ṣṭā) (

children.text: ) bhavantyarogiṇaḥ, sukhino, balavantaḥ | so 'pareṇa samayena paśyatyātmānamvā, paramvā, ābādhikaṃ, duḥkhitaṃ, bāḍhaglānaṃ, spṛṣṭaṃ śārīrikābhirvedanābhiḥ duḥkhābhistīvrābhiriti vistareṇa pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: to be healthy, happy, and strong. At a later time, one sees oneself or another as sick, suffering, severely ill, touched by painful, intense bodily feelings — in detail as before.

body.translated_text: How does one practice the impermanence-through-change produced by illness? Here, at one time, one has seen oneself and others

body.text: tatra kathaṃ kleśakṛtāṃ vipariṇā[mā]nityatāṃ vyavacārayati | ihānenaikadātmā ca pare ca dṛṣṭvā (dṛṣṭā) bhavantyarogiṇaḥ, sukhino, balavantaḥ | so 'pareṇa samayena paśyatyātmānamvā, paramvā, ābādhikaṃ, duḥkhitaṃ, bāḍhaglānaṃ, spṛṣṭaṃ śārīrikābhirvedanābhiḥ | sa punarapareṇa samayena paśyatyarogiṇaṃ, sukhitaṃ, balavantaṃ, dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bata(te)me saṃskārā iti pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: How does one practice the impermanence-through-change produced by [illness]? Here, at one time, one has seen oneself and others to be healthy, happy, and strong. At a later time, one sees oneself or another as sick, suffering, severely ill, touched by bodily feelings. Then again at a later time, one sees [them] healthy, happy, and strong. Having seen [this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' — as before.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ maraṇakṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | ihāyaṃ jīvitaṃ paśyati dhriyantaṃ, tiṣṭhantaṃ, yāpayantaṃ, so 'pareṇa samayena mṛtaṃ kālagataṃ paśyati | vijñānaśūnyaṃ kalevaraṃ dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavatīti vistareṇa pūrvavat ||
body.translated_text: How does one practice the impermanence-through-change produced by death? Here, one sees a living being sustaining, maintaining, and carrying on life. At a later time, one sees [that being] dead, passed away — a body empty of consciousness. Having seen [this], it then occurs to one — in detail as before.

body.text: tatra kathaṃ [vi]nīlakādikṛtāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | so 'pareṇa samayena tāma(tada)sthiśaṃkalikāvasthānaṃ paśyati | sa tadeva mṛtakalevaraṃ vinīlakāvasthamekadā paśyati | ekadā vipūyakāvasthamenaṃ vistareṇa yāvasthiśaṃkalikāvasthaṃ dṛṣṭvāsyaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bata(te)me saṃskārā iti vistareṇa (
body.translated_text: How does one practice the impermanence-through-change produced by the stages of bluish discoloration and so forth? At a later time, one sees that [body] in the state of a bone-chain. That very dead body — at one time one sees it in the state of bluish discoloration, at one time in the state of festering — in detail up to the state of a bone-chain. Having seen [this], it occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent!' — in detail

body.text: tatra kathamasaṃkhyā(ya) na parikṣayakṛtāmvipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati [|] so 'pareṇa [samayena] tāma(tada)pya[sthi]śaṃkalikāvasthānaṃ paśyati | sarveṇa sarvaṃ naṣṭā(ṣṭo) bhavati, vidhvastā(sto), viśīrṇaḥ | sarveṇa sarvaṃ cakṣuṣo [a]nābhāsagatā, dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bata(te)me saṃskārāstathā hyeṣāṃ paurvāparyeṇa pratyakṣata evāyamevaṃ rūpo vikāra upalabhyate | vipariṇāmaḥ |
body.translated_text: How does one practice the impermanence-through-change produced by the uncountable destruction? At a later time, one sees that [body] in the state of a bone-chain. [Then it is] entirely destroyed, disintegrated, crumbled. Entirely gone beyond the range of vision. Having seen [this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent! For indeed, this kind of transformation and change is directly perceived in them through the previous and subsequent [observation].'

body.text: evaṃ tāvatpratyakṣādhipateyena manaskāreṇādhyātmikasya vastunaḥ [paṃca] daśabhirākārairvipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | vyavacārayitvā(vyavacārya) ṣoḍaśavidhasya bāhyasya vastuno vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | ye 'nena pṛthivīpradeśā nābhisaṃskṛtāḥ pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭā bhavanti | gṛhavastvāpaṇavastupuṇyaśālādevakulavihāravastuprakāraiḥ paścāccābhisaṃskṛtānpaśyatyanabhisaṃskṛtānpaśyatyanandinavānsukṛtānsūpaliptān (|) so 'pareṇa samayena jīrṇān paśyati | jarjarānalūnavilūnāṃ (nān) cchīrṇān cha(kṣa)titapatitān khalu chidrānagninā vā dagdhānudakena vāpahratāṃ(hṛtān) | dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavati | anityā bata(te)me saṃskārāḥ [|] tathāpyeḥ(hye)ṣāṃ paurvāparyeṇāyamevaṃrūpaḥ pratyakṣo vikāro (

children.text: ) vipariṇāma upalabhyate | evaṃ pṛthivyāṃ vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | evaṃ tṛṇauṣadhivanaspataya ārāmodyānāni ca samṛddhapatrapuṣpaphalāni paśyati | harati tāni (haritāni) prāsādikānyabhiramyāṇi [|] apareṇa sa samayenocchuṣkāṇi paśyati | vigatapatrapuṣphalāni (|) agnidāhena vā dagdhāni (vā,) tathā parvatānyekadā samṛddhapāṣāṇāni paśyatyekadā nirluṭhitapāṣāṇāni patita śrṛṃgāṇi, patitakūṭāni, utkūlanikūlānyagninā dagdhāni, udakābhiṣyanditāni, tathā utsasarastaḍāka(ga)nadīprasravaṇakūpādīnyekadā, samṛddhodakāni paśyatyekadā parikṣīṇodakāni, sarveṇa vā sarvaṃ viśuṣkāṇi khilībhūtāni koṭarāṇi | tathā karmāntānekadā sampadyamānānpaśyatyekadā vipadyamānāṃ (nān) [paśyati |] tadyathākṛṣikarmāntānnaukarmāntānsamyagvyavahārakarmāntān vividhāṃchilpa (vidhāñchilpa)sthānakarmāntān, tathā kośasannidhīnāṃ vicitrāṇāṃ nānāprakārāṇāmekadā ācayaṃ paśyatyekadā apacayaṃ | tathā bhojanapānaṃ ca ekadā[na]bhisaṃskṛtā(nnā)vasthaṃ paśyatyekadābhisaṃskṛtāvasthamekadā lālāvisaraviklinnamekadā yāvaduccāraprasrāvāvasthaṃ [paśyati] | (
children.translated_text: 'is perceived in them.' Thus one practices the impermanence-through-change with respect to the earth. Likewise, one sees grasses, herbs, and trees, gardens and parks — abundant with leaves, flowers, and fruits, green, pleasing, and delightful. At a later time, one sees them dried up, devoid of leaves, flowers, and fruits, or burned by fire. Likewise, mountains — at one time one sees them rich in rocks, at another time with rocks dislodged, with peaks fallen, with summits fallen, with uneven slopes, burned by fire, eroded by water. Likewise, springs, lakes, pools, rivers, streams, wells, and the like — at one time one sees them rich in water, at another time depleted of water, or entirely dried up, become barren hollows. Likewise, agricultural enterprises — at one time one sees them succeeding, at another time failing. Such as farming, shipping, proper trade, and various craft-enterprises. Likewise, treasuries and storehouses of various kinds — at one time one sees them growing, at another time diminishing. Likewise, food and drink — at one time one sees them in an unprepared state, at another time in a prepared state, at one time softened by saliva and dissolving, at another time up to the state of excrement and urine.

children.text: ) tathā vividhāni yānānyekadā sumaṇḍitāni svalaṃkṛtānyabhinavāni paśyatyekadā vigatālaṃkārāṇi | vigatamaṇḍanāni, jarjarāṇi | tathā vastrāṇāmekadā abhinavatāṃ paśyatyekadā purāṇatāṃ | prakṣīṇatāmekadā śuddhatāmekadā malinatāṃ | tathālaṃkārāṇāmekadānabhisaṃskṛtatāmekadābhisaṃskṛtatāmekadā sāratāmekadābhinna-prabhinnatāmvikṣīṇatāṃ paśyati | tathā nṛttagītavāditānāṃ pratyutpannaprayogavicitrabhūya[s]samudgatā[ṃ] bhavabhaṃgatāmpaśyati | tathā gandhamālyavilepanānāṃ pratyagrasugandhāmlānatāṃ paśyati | apareṇa samayena nātisugandhadurgandhamlānaviśuṣkatāṃ paśyati | tathā bhāṇḍopaskārāṇāmanabhisaṃskārābhisaṃskārasārabhagnatāṃ paśyati | tathā ālokānukārayoḥ saṃbhavavibhavatāmpaśyati | tathā strīpuruṣacaryāsambhavavibhavatāṃ paśyati | asthiratāṃ [|] dṛṣṭvā ca punarasyaivaṃ bhavatyanityā bata(te)me saṃskārāstathā hyeṣāṃ bāhyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ, ṣaṇṇāṃ ca parigrahavastūnāṃ, daśānāñca kāyaparivārāṇāṃ pratyakṣatā, vikāro, viparimāṇo 'yamīdṛśa upalabhyate | sarvatracaitat peyālaṃ veditavyaṃ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise, various vehicles — at one time one sees them well-adorned, well-decorated, and new; at another time, stripped of decoration, stripped of adornment, and worn out. Likewise, garments — at one time one sees their newness, at another time their age, their worn-out state; at one time their cleanliness, at another time their dirtiness. Likewise, ornaments — at one time their unworked state, at another time their worked state; at one time their solidity, at another time their broken, shattered, and diminished state. Likewise, dancing, singing, and music — one sees them in their momentary nature of arising and ceasing, with their varied display produced in the present moment. Likewise, perfumes, garlands, and ointments — one sees their fresh fragrance and their fading. At a later time, one sees them no longer fragrant, malodorous, faded, and dried up. Likewise, household goods and furnishings — one sees their unworked state, worked state, solidity, and broken state. Likewise, light and shadow — one sees their arising and disappearing. Likewise, the conduct of men and women — one sees its arising and disappearing, its instability. Having seen [all this], it then occurs to one: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent! For indeed, with respect to these external <s>saṃskāras</s>, the six categories of possessions, and the ten types of personal retinue — such a directly perceptible transformation and change is perceived.' The full elaboration should be understood throughout.

body.translated_text: Thus, with mental attention governed by direct perception, one practices the impermanence-through-change of the internal object through fifteen aspects. Having so practiced, one then practices the impermanence-through-change of the sixteen kinds of external objects. Those plots of land that were previously seen by him as uncultivated — [later] he sees them cultivated as dwelling-grounds, shop-grounds, merit-halls, temple-grounds, monastery-grounds, with enclosures; and afterwards he sees [them] cultivated or uncultivated, new, well-made, well-plastered. At a later time, he sees them worn out, dilapidated, peeled, crumbled, chipped, fallen, decayed, full of holes, or burnt by fire or carried away by water. Having seen [this], it then occurs to him: 'Alas, these <s>saṃskāras</s> are impermanent! For indeed, this kind of directly perceptible transformation and change',

body.text: ebhiraṣṭābhirvipariṇāmakāraṇaiḥ pūrvanirdiṣṭairasyādhyātmikabāhyasya vastuno yathāyogaṃ pratyakṣādhipateyena manaskāreṇaivaṃ vipariṇāmākāreṇānityatāṃ vyavacārayati | (

children.text: ) yathānena sā vipariṇāmānityatā pratyakṣaṃ dṛṣṭā bhavatyanubhūtā, aparapratyayaśca tasyāṃ bhavatyananyaneyaḥ | tathaivānusmaran vyavacārayati | niścitaśca bhavati | tenocyate pratyakṣādhipateyo manaskāra iti |
children.translated_text: Just as that impermanence through transformation has been directly seen and experienced by him, and he has gained a conviction regarding it that cannot be led astray by another — remembering in just that way, he analyzes. And he becomes certain. Therefore it is called mental attention governed by direct perception (<s>pratyakṣādhipateya manaskāra</s>).

body.translated_text: Through these eight causes of change, as previously indicated, for the internal and external objects as appropriate, with mental attention governed by direct perception, one practices impermanence in the mode of change.

body.text: sa evaṃ pratyakṣādhipateyena manaskāreṇa vipariṇāmānityatāṃ vyavahā(cā)rayitvā(vyavacārya) yeṣāṃ rūpiṇāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ satī samvidyamānā kṣaṇotpannabhagnā vinīlatā(vilīnatā) nopalabhyate | tatra pratyakṣādhipateyaṃ manaskāraṃ niśrityānumānaṃ karotyevañca punaranumānaṃ karoti | kṣaṇotpannabhagnavilīnānāmeṣāṃ saṃskārāṇāmiyaṃ pūrveṇāparā vikṛtiryujyate | na tu tathaivāvasthitānāṃ, iti hi kṣaṇikāḥ saṃskārāsteṣu teṣu pratyayeṣu satsu tathā tathotpadyante | utpannāścānapekṣya vināśakāraṇaṃ svarasena vipa(na)śyanti |
body.translated_text: He, having thus analyzed impermanence through transformation by means of mental attention governed by direct perception — regarding those material formations whose moment-by-moment arising and destruction, and their dissolution (<s>vinīlatā</s>), though existing, is not perceived — relying on mental attention governed by direct perception, he makes an inference: thus

body.text: yāni punaretāni vipariṇāmakāraṇāni tānyanyathotpattaye satya(mva)rttante vikṛtāyā utpatteḥ kāraṇībhavanti | na tu vināśasya [|] tatkasya hetoḥ [|] sahaiva tena vināśakāraṇena vinaṣṭānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ yasmādvisadṛśā (śī) pravṛttirupalabhyate | na tu sarveṇa sarvamapravṛttireva [|] yeṣāmvā punaḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ sarveṇa sarvamapravṛttirupalabhyate | tadyathā kvāthyamānāmasāmante sarveṇa sarvamparikṣayo bhavati agninirdagdhānāṃ ca lokabhājanānāṃ masirapi na [pra]jñāyate | chāyikā ca | śiṣṭamapi na prajñāyate teṣāmapyuttarottarakaraṇaparyādānādante sarveṇa sarvamabhāvo bhavati | na tvagninaiva kriyate [|] tasmādvipariṇāmakāraṇānyetānyaṣṭau yathoktāni svarasenaiva tu vināśo bhavati | sa evamānumānikamanaskāreṇa saṃskāreṇākṣaṇotpannabhagnavilīnatāyāṃ niścayaṃ pratilabhya punarapyapratyakṣaparalokāsaṃskārapravṛttāvanumānaṃ karoti ||
body.translated_text: those causes of transformation operate for a different kind of arising — they become causes of a modified arising, but not of destruction. Why? Because, for formations that have been destroyed simultaneously with that cause of destruction, a dissimilar operation is observed — but not entirely

body.text: evaṃ ca punaranumānaṃ karoti | santi satvā (ttvā) ye avarṇā api, durvarṇā apyupalabhyante, uccakulīnā api, ādyakulīnā api, daridrakulīnā api, alpeśākhyā api, dīrghāyuṣo (ṣa) ādeyavākyā api, anādeyavākyā api, tīkṣṇendriyā api [|] (

children.text: ) tadetat satva(ttva)vaicitryaṃ sati karmavaicitrye yujyate [|] nāsati | yadrūpaiḥ sattvairyadrūpaṃ pūrvameva bhūtaṃ (kṛtaṃ?) kuśalākuśalaṃ citrakarma kṛtamupacitaṃ, tena hetunā, tena pratyayena teṣāmidamātmabhāvavaicitryamabhinirvṛttaṃ ||
children.translated_text: This diversity of beings is fitting when there is diversity of <s>karma</s> (action), but not otherwise. Whatever beings have formerly created and accumulated such-and-such variegated wholesome and unwholesome <s>karma</s> — by that cause, by that condition, this diversity of their personal existence has been produced.

body.translated_text: And he further makes this inference: 'There are beings who are found to be ugly, ill-colored, of high birth, of eminent families, of impoverished families, of little renown, of long life, whose words are authoritative, whose words are not authoritative, whose faculties are sharp,'

body.text: na caitadīśvaranirmāṇahetukaṃ yujyate | sa cedīśvaranirmāṇahetukaṃ syāttadīśvarapratyayameva vā syādanyena vopādāneneśvaro nirmimīta | sa cedīśvara pratyayameva syāt teneśvarasyaiṣāñca saṃskārāṇāṃ yaugapadyaṃ syāt | atha pūrvamīśvaraḥ paścāt saṃskārā, neśvarapratyayāḥ saṃskārā bhavanti | atheśvarasya praṇidhānaṃ nirmāṇakāraṇaṃ, neśvara eva | tena samīcchā sahetukā (kī) vā syānnirhetu kā (kīṃ) vā [|] yadi sahetukā īśvarahetukaiva ca tena pūrvakeṇa doṣeṇa tulyatayā na yujyate | athānyahetukā (kī) tenecchā prayatnaḥ | (

children.text: ) praṇidhānamīśvaravinirmuktānyadharmahetukā tathā sarve 'pi saṃskārā dharmahetukā eva bhaviṣyanti | kimīśvareṇa vṛthā kalpitenetyevamādinā ānumānikena manaskāreṇaivaṃbhāgīyena, paralokena saṃskārapravṛttau niścayaṃ pratilabhate |
children.translated_text: the aspiration (<s>praṇidhāna</s>) of the <s>Īśvara</s>, being free from the <s>Īśvara</s>, would be caused by another <s>dharma</s>; similarly, all formations would be caused by <s>dharmas</s> alone — what need then for an <s>Īśvara</s>, needlessly posited? By such inferential mental attention and other [arguments] of this kind, one gains certainty regarding the operation of formations in the next world.

body.translated_text: And it is not fitting that this is caused by the creation of an <s>Īśvara</s> (Lord). If it were caused by the creation of an <s>Īśvara</s>, then either [the creation] would have the <s>Īśvara</s> alone as its condition, or the <s>Īśvara</s> would create with some other material cause (<s>upādāna</s>). If the <s>Īśvara</s> alone were the condition, then the <s>Īśvara</s> and these formations would be simultaneous. Or if the <s>Īśvara</s> is prior and the formations subsequent,

body.text: sa evaṃ triḥprakāramanaskārādhipatyena śraddhādhipateyena pratyakṣādhipateyenānumānādhipateyānāṃ(yām) nityatāṃ vyavacārayati | tatra yā pūrva pañca [vidhā]nityatā pañcākārabhāvanānugatā uddiṣṭā, tatra vipariṇāmākāranirdiṣṭā, vināśākārā ca |
body.translated_text: He thus, by the governance of three kinds of mental attention — governed by faith, governed by direct perception, and governed by inference — analyzes impermanence. Therein, the previous five kinds of impermanence, which were enumerated as conjoined with the cultivation of five aspects — therein, the aspect of transformation and the aspect of destruction have been indicated.

body.text: visaṃyogākārā anityākārā (anityatā) katamā | āha | adhyātmamupādāya bahirdhā ca veditavyā || tatrādhyātmamupādāya yathāpi tadekatyaḥ pūrvampareṣāṃ stā(svā)mī bhavatyadāsaḥ apreṣyaḥ | aparakarmakaraḥ | so 'pareṇa samayena svāmibhāvamadāsabhāvaṃ vihāya pareṣāṃ dāsabhāvamupagacchati | svāmibhāvādvisaṃyujyate | tathā santaḥ samvidyamānā bhogā avipariṇatā, avinaṣṭā rājñā(ḥ) apahriyante | corairvā, apriyairvā, dāyādai[ritya]nityatā veditavyā | tatra dharmatākārānityatā (

children.text: ) yathāpi tasyā eva vipariṇāmānityatāyāḥ vināśānityatāyāḥ | vartamāne 'pyadhvanyasamavahitāyāḥ anābhoge (gate) 'dhvani bhāvinyā dharmatāṃ pratividhyatyevaṃ dharmāṇa ete saṃskārā anāgate 'dhvani evaṃbhāgīyā iti | eṣu sannihitākārāya (rayā?) ita eva vipariṇāmānityatāṃ, vināśānityatāṃ, visaṃyogānityatāṃ samavahitāṃ saṃbhuravībhūtāmākārayati |
children.translated_text: just as, regarding that very impermanence through transformation and impermanence through destruction — even in the present time-period, when it is not directly present, when it is in the future time-period — one discerns its nature as <s>dharmatā</s>: 'These formations, these <s>dharmas</s>, in the future, will be of this same kind.' Regarding these, by the aspect of their being imminent, from this very [point],

body.translated_text: What is the impermanence of the aspect of separation (<s>visaṃyoga</s>)? He says: It should be understood with reference to what is internal and what is external. Therein, with reference to what is internal: just as a certain person was formerly the master of others, not a slave, not a servant, not another's laborer — but at a later time, having lost the status of master and non-slave,

body.text: sa evamādhyātmikabāhyānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ pañcavidhāyāmanityatāyāmebhiḥ pañcabhirākārairyathāyogaṃ manasikārabāhulyādupapattisādhanabhāvanādhipatyācca niye(rme)yaṃ pratilabhya tada[na]ntaraṃ duḥkhākāramavatarati | tasyaivaṃ bhavati | ya ete saṃskārā anityāsteṣāmanityatāṃ (tā) jātidharmato yujyate | iti hyeta eva saṃskārā jātidharmāṇaḥ jātiśca duḥkhā, yadā(yā) jātireva[ṃ] jarā vyādhirmaraṇa[ṃ], vipriyasaṃprayogaḥ, priyavinābhāva, icchāvighātaśca veditavyaḥ | evaṃ tāvadaniṣṭā(tyā)kāreṇa duḥkhākāramavatarati |
body.translated_text: he, having thus cultivated the five kinds of impermanence of internal and external formations through these five aspects, as appropriate, through abundance of mental attention and through the governance of the cultivation of logical proof (<s>upapattisādhana</s>), having gained certainty, thereupon descends into the aspect of suffering (<s>duḥkhākāra</s>). He thinks thus: 'These formations being impermanent —'

body.text: sa ye sukhavedanīyāḥ skandhāḥ, sāsravāḥ, sopādānāsteṣu saṃyojanabandhanākāreṇa duḥkhākāramavatarati | (

children.text: ) tathā hi te (tasya) tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanasyākāre 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ, tṛṣṇāsaṃyojanaṃ ca jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsabandhanasya, rāgadveṣamohabandhanasya cādhiṣṭhānaṃ |
children.translated_text: For those [aggregates] are the basis for the mode of the fetter of craving (<s>tṛṣṇāsaṃyojana</s>); and the fetter of craving is the basis for the bondage of birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental displeasure, and distress, and the bondage of attachment, aversion, and delusion.

body.translated_text: regarding the aggregates that are to be experienced as pleasant — those that are with outflows (<s>sāsrava</s>) and with clinging (<s>sopādāna</s>) — he descends into the aspect of suffering through the aspect of the fetter-bond (<s>saṃyojanabandhanākāra</s>).

body.text: tatrāyogakṣemāmāreṇa aduḥkhāsukhasthānīyeṣu skandheṣu duḥkhākāramavatarati | tathā hyaduḥkhāsukhāsthānīyāḥ skandhāḥ sopādānā dauṣṭhulyasahagatā abījānugatā avinirmuktā duḥkhaduḥkhatayā, vipariṇāmaduḥkhatayā ca | anityā, nirodhadharmāṇaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, through the aspect of insecurity (<s>ayogakṣema</s>), regarding the aggregates that occupy the position of neither-painful-nor-pleasant, he descends into the aspect of suffering. For the aggregates occupying the position of neither-painful-nor-pleasant, being with clinging, accompanied by rigidity (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>), following upon seeds, not yet freed — are [involved in] the suffering of suffering (<s>duḥkhaduḥkhatā</s>) and the suffering of change (<s>vipariṇāmaduḥkhatā</s>); they are impermanent, subject to cessation.

body.text: evamayaṃ yogī sukhasthānīyeṣu saṃskāreṣu, sukhāyāñca vedanāyāṃ vipariṇāmaduḥkhatāmavatīrṇo bhavati | yaduta saṃyojanabandhanākāreṇa duḥkhavedanāsthānīyeṣu saṃskāreṣuduḥkhāyāṃ vedanāyāṃ duḥkhaduḥkhatāmavatīrṇo bhavati | yadutāniṣṭākāreṇa aduḥkhāsukhasthānīyeṣu saṃskāreṣu(ṣva) duḥkhāsukhāyāñca vedanāyāṃ saṃskāraduḥkhatāmavatīrṇo bhavati | yadutāyogakṣemākāreṇa [|]
body.translated_text: Thus this <s>yogī</s>, regarding formations occupying the position of happiness and regarding pleasant feeling, has descended into the suffering of change — namely through the aspect of the fetter-bond. Regarding formations occupying the position of suffering and regarding painful feeling, he has descended into the suffering of suffering — namely through the aspect of the undesirable. Regarding [formations occupying the position of] neither-painful-nor-pleasant,

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavati | saṃyojanabandhanākāramaniṣṭākāraṃ yogakṣemākāraṃ cādhipatiṃ kṛtvā tisṛṣu vedanāsu yatkiñcidvedayitamidamatra duḥkhasyetyevamayamanityākārapūrvakeṇa manaskāreṇa duḥkhākāramavatīrṇo bhavati | tasyaivaṃ bhavatīndriyamātra(traṃ)saha(saḥ) upalabhate, viṣayamātraṃ | tajjamanubhavamātraṃ | cittamātra hatā ātmeti (hatātmeti) | nāmamātraṃ | darśanamātramupacāramātraṃ | (
body.translated_text: he thinks thus: 'Making predominant the aspect of the fetter-bond, the aspect of the undesirable, and the aspect of insecurity — regarding the three feelings: whatever is felt, this is within the domain of suffering.' Thus, through mental attention preceded by the aspect of impermanence, he has descended into the aspect of suffering. He thinks thus: 'This is merely sense-faculties, together with',

body.text: tadevaṃ sati skandhamātrametannāstyeṣu skandheṣu nityo, dhruvaḥ, śāśvataḥ svābhūtaḥ | kaścidātmā vā, satvo(ttvo) vā, yo 'sau jāyeta vā, hīyeta vā, mriyate (yeta) vā, tatra vā (tatra vā) tatra kṛtakṛtānāṃ karmaṇāṃ phalavipākaṃ pratisamvedayeta | iti hi (

children.text: ) śūnyā ete saṃskārāḥ, ātmavirahitā ityevamanupalambhākāreṇa śūnyākāramavatarati | tasyaivaṃ bhavati | ye punarete saṃskārāḥ svalakṣaṇenānityalakṣaṇena, duḥkhalakṣaṇena yuktāste 'pi pratītyasamutpannatayā asvatantrā, ye 'svatantrāste 'nātmāna ityevamasvatantrākāreṇānātmākāramavatarati | evaṃ punaryoginā daśākāraṃ gṛhītaiścaturbhirākārairduḥkhasatyalakṣaṇaṃ pratisaṃveditaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: these formations are empty, devoid of self — thus through the aspect of non-apprehension (<s>anupalambhākāra</s>), he descends into the aspect of emptiness (<s>śūnyākāra</s>). He thinks thus: 'These formations, which are marked by impermanence according to their own characteristics and by the mark of suffering — they too, being dependently arisen, are not under their own control (<s>asvatantra</s>); being not under their own control, they are not-self (<s>anātman</s>).' Thus

body.translated_text: This being so, this is merely aggregates. In these aggregates there is no [entity that is] permanent, stable, eternal, inherently existent — no self or being whatsoever who is born, decays, or dies, or who experiences the fruit and ripening of actions previously performed. Thus

body.text: tatrānityākāraḥ pañcabhirākāraiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ | tadyathā vipariṇāmākāreṇa, visaṃyojanākāreṇa, sannihitākāreṇa, dharmatākāreṇa [|]
body.translated_text: therein, the aspect of impermanence (<s>anityākāra</s>) is comprised in five aspects: namely, the aspect of transformation, the aspect of separation, the aspect of imminence, and the aspect of natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>).

body.text: duḥkhākārastribhirākāraiḥ saṃgṛhītaḥ | saṃyojanabandhanākāreṇa aniṣṭākāreṇa ayogakṣemākāreṇa ca [|]
body.translated_text: The aspect of suffering (<s>duḥkhākāra</s>) is comprised in three aspects: the aspect of the fetter-bond, the aspect of the undesirable, and the aspect of insecurity.

body.text: śūnyākāra ekenākāreṇa saṃgṛhīto yadutānupalaṃbhākāreṇa [|]
body.translated_text: The aspect of emptiness (<s>śūnyākāra</s>) is comprised in one aspect: namely, the aspect of non-apprehension.

body.text: anātmākāra ekenākāreṇa saṃgṛhīto yadutāsvatantrākāreṇa |
body.translated_text: The aspect of not-self (<s>anātmākāra</s>) is comprised in one aspect: namely, the aspect of being not under one's own control (<s>asvatantrākāra</s>).

body.text: sa evaṃ daśabhirākāraiścaturākārānupraviṣṭo (

children.text: ) duḥkhalakṣaṇāṃ pratisaṃvedya, asya duḥkhasya ko hetuḥ, kaḥ samudayaḥ, prabhavaḥ, pratyayaḥ iti | yasya prahāṇādasya duḥkhasya prahāṇaṃ syādityebhiścaturbhirākāraissamudayasatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratisaṃvedayati | tṛṣṇāyā duḥkhakṣemakatvāddhetutaḥ, ākṣipyābhinirvartakatvātsamudayānayanātsamudā[na]yataḥ | abhinirvṛttirduḥkhitatvāt prabhavatvāt prabhavataḥ | punarāyatyāṃ duḥkhabījaparigrahatvādanukrameṇa ca | duḥkhasamudayānayanātpratyayataḥ | aparaḥ paryāyaḥ | upādānahetukasya ca bhavasya samudāgamādbhavapūrvikāyā jāteḥ prabhavatvāt, jātipratyayatāṃ, jāti ca (teśca) jarāvyādhimaraṇaśokādīnāmabhinirvṛtteḥ | hetutaḥ samudayataḥ, prabhavataḥ, pratyayataḥ | yathāyogaṃ veditavyaṃ | aparaḥ paryāyaḥ [|] yaḥ kleśānuśaya āśraya[ḥ] punarbhavāmabhinirvṛttaye hetustajjasya ca paryavasthānasya yathāyogaṃ veditavyaṃ [|] aparaḥ paryāyaḥ [|] yaḥ kleśānuśaya āśrayastṛṣṇānuśayādikaḥ | sa āyatyāṃ punarbhavābhinirvṛttaye hetustajjasya ca paryavasthānasya yathāyogaṃ samudayaḥ, prabhavaḥ, pratyayaśca [|]
children.translated_text: having directly experienced the mark of suffering, [he contemplates:] 'What is the cause of this suffering? What is its origination, source, and condition? Through the abandonment of what would this suffering be abandoned?' — through these four aspects he directly experiences the mark of the truth of origination (<s>samudayasatya</s>). [He contemplates:] 'Because <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) is the factor of establishing suffering — from the standpoint of being its cause; because it projects [future existence],'

body.translated_text: He, having thus entered into the four aspects through [these] ten aspects,

body.text: tatra paunarbhavikyāstṛṣṇāyāḥ samudānanātsamudayataḥ | sāpuna[ḥ] paunarbhavikī tṛṣṇā nandīrāgasahagatāyāstṛṣṇāyāḥ (

children.text: ) prabhavo bhavati sā punarnandīrāgasahagatā tṛṣṇā prabhūtā, tatra tatrābhinandinyāstṛṣṇāyāḥ pratyayo bhavatyevamasyānuśayagatāṃ trividhaparyavasthāgatāṃ ca tṛṣṇāmāgamyāyati[ḥ] | punarbhavasyābhinirvṛttirbhavati prādurbhāvaḥ | tenāha hetu[taḥ], samudayataḥ, prabhavataḥ, pratyayataśca | evamayaṃ yogī ebhiścaturbhirākāraissamudayasatyalakṣaṇaṃ pratisamvedayate |
children.translated_text: it becomes the source. And that <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving), accompanied by delight and attachment, is abundant; it becomes the condition for that craving that delights here and there. Thus, tracing back his craving in its latent state and in its threefold envelopment state, in the future there is the production, the manifestation, of further existence (<s>punarbhava</s>). Therefore he said: from the standpoint of cause, from the standpoint of origin, from the standpoint of source, and from the standpoint of condition. Thus this <s>yogī</s>, by these four aspects, discerns the characteristic of the truth of the origin of suffering.

body.translated_text: therein, because of the gathering together of craving for renewed existence — from the standpoint of origination (<s>samudaya</s>). And that craving for renewed existence, of the craving accompanied by delight and attachment (<s>nandīrāgasahagatā tṛṣṇā</s>),

body.text: samudayasatyalakṣaṇaṃ pratisaṃvedya asya samudayasatyasyāśeṣoparamannirodhaṃ nirodhata ākārayati | duḥkhasatyasyāśeṣoparamecchātaḥ, agratvācchreṣṭhatvāttadantaratvāt praṇītataḥ, nityatvānnissaraṇataḥ | evamayaṃ caturbhirākāraiḥ nirodhasatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratisaṃvedayati | pratisamvedya jñeyaparimārgaṇārthena, bhūtaparimārgaṇārthena caturbhirduḥkhairanupravartanārthena | nirvāṇagamanāyaikāyanārthena mārgaṃ mārga[to], nyāyataḥ, pratipattito, nairyāṇikataśca ākārayati | sa evaṃ caturbhirākārairmārgatyasya lakṣaṇaṃ pratisamvedayate | ayamasyocyate caturṣvāryasatyeṣvadhyātmaṃ pratyātmaṃ lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī (yate | ayamasyocyate | caturṣvāryasatye[ṣu]) manaskāraḥ ||
body.translated_text: Having discerned the characteristic of the truth of origin, he contemplates the complete cessation of this truth of origin as cessation, from the standpoint of cessation; from the desire for the complete cessation of the truth of suffering, from its being supreme and most excellent, from its inner transcendence, as sublime; from its permanence, as escape. Thus, by four aspects, he discerns the characteristic of the truth of cessation. Having discerned it, for the purpose of seeking out the knowable, for the purpose of seeking out reality, for the purpose of pursuing the four [types of] suffering, for the purpose of proceeding to <s>nirvāṇa</s> as the sole path — he contemplates the path from the standpoint of path, from the standpoint of method, from the standpoint of practice, and from the standpoint of leading out. Thus, by four aspects, he discerns the characteristic of the truth of the path. This is called his mental attention that internally, personally, discerns the characteristics with respect to the Four Noble Truths.

body.text: sa evaṃ pratyātmikān skandhān pratyayenopaparīkṣya (

children.text: ) vyavacārayitvā (vyavacārya) viparokṣakān visabhāgadhātukān | skandhānanumānataḥ parāhanti | tepyevaṃ dharmāṇaḥ te 'pyevaṃnayapatitā iti | yatkiñcitsaṃskṛtaṃ sarvatra sarvaśaḥ [evaṃ tadevaṃ pratisaṃvedī manaskāraḥ | pratyayenopaparīkṣyavyavacārayitvā(cārya) viparokṣān visabhāgadhātukān skandhānanumānataḥ parāhanti | te 'pyevaṃ dharmāṇaste 'pyevaṃ nayapatitā iti yatkiñcitsaṃskṛtaṃ sarvatra sarvaśa] evaṃ tadevaṃprakṛtikaṃ, tasya ca nirodhaḥ | śāntaḥ, mārgo, nairyāṇiko yastatprahāṇāya tasya yadā vipakṣokteṣu pratyātmikeṣu skandheṣu satyajñānaṃ | yacca viparokṣeṣu visabhāgadhātukeṣvanumānajñānaṃ | taddharmajñānānvayajñānayorutpattaye bījasthānīyaṃ bhavati | sa cāyaṃ lakṣaṇapratisaṃvedī manaskāraḥ śrutacintāvyavakīrṇo veditavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: having investigated, he extends [this understanding] by inference to the imperceptible <s>skandhas</s> belonging to dissimilar realms: "They too are of such a nature, they too fall under this same principle." Whatever is conditioned, everywhere and in every way — [this is] the mental attention that thus discerns. Having examined by means of reasoning and having investigated, one extends by inference to the imperceptible <s>skandhas</s> belonging to dissimilar realms: "They too are of such a nature, they too fall under this same principle." Whatever is conditioned, everywhere and in every way, is of such a nature, such is its constitution; and its cessation is peaceful; and the path that leads to its cessation is liberating. When there is truth-knowledge (<s>satyajñāna</s>) regarding the personally experienced <s>skandhas</s> as stated in the antidote-section, and inferential knowledge (<s>anumānajñāna</s>) regarding the imperceptible [<s>skandhas</s>] belonging to dissimilar realms — this becomes the seed for the arising of <s>dharmajñāna</s> (knowledge of dharmas) and <s>anvayajñāna</s> (subsequent knowledge). And this mental attention that discerns characteristics should be understood as intermixed with hearing and reflection.

body.translated_text: Having thus examined the personal <s>skandhas</s> (aggregates) by means of reasoning,

body.text: yadā teṣu satyeṣvayaṃ yogī evaṃ samyak(g)vyavacāraṇānvayādibhiḥ ṣoḍaśabhirākāraiścaturṣvāryasatyeṣu niścayaḥ [-yaṃ] pratilabdho bhavati | yadutopapattisādhanayuktyā, yaduta yāvadbhāvikatāṃ vā, tadā śrutacintāmayaṃ manaskāraṃ samatikramya vyavatīrṇavarttinamekāntena bhāvanākāreṇādhimucyate | so [a]sya bhavatyādhimokṣiko manaskāraḥ | satyālambanaścaikāntasamāhitaśca [|] sa tasyānvayā[d]dve satye adhikṛtya duḥkhasatyañca (

children.translated_text: the truth of origin — one obtains boundless knowledge, by which one resolves boundlessly: "impermanent, impermanent, impermanent."

body.translated_text: When, with respect to those truths, this <s>yogī</s>, through proper investigation and by means of the sixteen aspects regarding the Four Noble Truths, has obtained certainty — whether through the reasoning of proof by evidence (<s>upapattisādhanayukti</s>), or through the extent-reality (<s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>) — then, having transcended the mental attention born of hearing and reflection, one who has descended [into practice] resolves exclusively in the mode of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>). That becomes his resolving mental attention (<s>ādhimokṣika manaskāra</s>), which has the truths as its object and is exclusively concentrated. And in accordance with that, with respect to the two truths — the truth of suffering and

body.text: evaṃ duḥkhāparyantatāṃ śūnyākāyā[rā]paryantatāṃ, saṃkleśāparyantāmapāyagamanāparyantatāṃ sampatti(ttya) [paryanta]nāṃ(tāṃ), vipati[ttya]paryantatāṃ, sa vyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā paryantatāṃ [|] tatrāparyanteti nāsti saṃsāraṃ(raḥ) sansa(saṃsa)rata, eṣāṃ dharmāṇāmanto nāsti paryantaḥ | yāvatsansā(saṃsā)rabhāvina ete dharmāḥ, sansā(saṃsā)rasya vāśeṣoparamādeṣāmuparamo, nāsti anyathoparama ityevaṃ sarvabhavagaticyutyupapādebhyaḥ apraṇihā(hitā)kāreṇāsanniśrayākāreṇa, prātikūlyāthi(dhi)kāreṇāsanniśrayākāreṇa [|] prātikūlyādhikāreṇādhimucyamāna ādhimokṣikamanaskāraṃ bhāvayati | sa evaṃ sarvabhāvopapattibhyaḥ | cittamudvejayitvā (-mudvejya) | uttrāsya | u(t)trāsayitvā (sya) [a]dhyāśayena nirvāṇe 'pyanyatamānyatamenākāreṇa praṇidadhāti | tasya dīrgharātraṃ taccitraṃ(ttaṃ)rūparataṃ śabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyarataṃ ā(tamā)citamupacitaṃ (rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyaratamā(tamā)citamupacitaṃ |) rūpaśabdagandharasaspraṣṭavyaiḥ | yenādhyāśayenāpi nirvāṇaṃ pradadhate | (

children.text: ) na praskandati, na prasīdati | na saṃtiṣṭhate | na vimucyate, na pratyudāvarttate (|) mānasaṃ, śāntadhātvanabhilakṣitatayā | paritamanāmupādāya, sa punaḥ punastaccittamudvejayatyu[t]trāsayati | duḥkhasatyātsamudayasatyādudvejyo[j]trāsya punaḥ punaradhyāśayato nirvāṇe praṇidadhāti | tathāpyasya na praskandati | tatkasya hetostathā hyasau [au]dāriko [a]smi māno 'bhisamayāya vibandhakaraḥ | sa manaskārānupraviṣṭaḥ sāntaravyantaro vartate | ahamasmi saṃskṛ(sṛ)tavānahamasmi saṃsariṣyāmi | ahamasmi parinirvāsyāmi, ahamasmi(n) parinirvāṇāya kuśalāndharmān bhāvayāmi | ahamasmiduḥkhaṃ duḥkhataḥ (|) paśyāmi, samudayaṃ samudayato, nirodhaṃ nirodhataḥ | ahamasmi mārgaṃ mārgataḥ paśyāmi | ahamasmi śūnyaṃ śūnyato 'praṇihitamapraṇihitataḥ | ānimittamānimittataḥ paśyāmi mamaite dharmāstaddhetostatpratyayasya taccittaṃ na praskandatyā(tya)dhyāśayamvādhyāśayato [a]pi nirvāṇama(ta)smimānaṃ nirba(viba)ndhakā(ka)raṃ vibandhakāra iti laghu laghveva prajñayā pratividhya, svarasānupravṛttau manaskāramutsṛjya, bahirdhā jñeyālambanād vyāvartya, mā(ma)naskārapraviṣṭāṃ, (
children.translated_text: it does not leap forward, does not become serene, does not settle, does not become liberated, does not turn back — the mental [activity], due to not being directed toward the peaceful element. Owing to distress, one again and again alarms and frightens that mind. Having alarmed and frightened it through the truth of suffering and the truth of origin, one again and again by deep intention sets [the mind] upon <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Yet still it does not leap forward. For what reason? For that coarse "I am" conceit (<s>asmimāna</s>) is obstructive to realization. It operates within the mental attention as an interval and interspace. "I have transmitted, I shall transmigrate, I shall attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I cultivate wholesome <s>dharmas</s> for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, I see suffering as suffering, origin as origin, cessation as cessation, I see the path as path, I see the empty as empty, the wishless as wishless, the signless as signless — these are my <s>dharmas</s>, for that cause and condition" — that mind does not leap forward. Even through deep intention toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, quickly and readily, through wisdom, having penetrated this "I am" conceit as obstructive, having let go of the mental attention in its natural flow, having turned away from the external knowable object,

children.text: ) manaskārānugatāṃ, satyavyavacārā(ra)ṇāmārabhate | sa utpannotpannaṃ cittaṃ nirudhyamānamanantarotpannena cittena bhajyamānaṃ paśyati | pravāhānuprabandhayogena | sa tathācittena cittamālambanīkarotyavaṣṭabhate | yathāsya yo 'sau manaskārānupraviṣṭo 'smimāno vipakṣa(bandha)karaḥ sa tasyāvakāśaḥ | punarbhavavyutpattaye ||
children.translated_text: one undertakes the investigation of truth that has entered into mental attention and follows mental attention. One sees each arisen mind ceasing and being broken by the immediately subsequent mind, through the continuity of the stream. One thus makes mind the object of mind, and steadies it, such that the "I am" conceit that has entered into mental attention and is obstructive — that finds no occasion for the production of further existence.

body.translated_text: Thus [one resolves upon] the boundlessness of suffering, the boundlessness of emptiness, the boundlessness of defilement, the boundlessness of going to lower rebirths, the boundlessness of prosperity, the boundlessness of adversity, and the boundlessness of disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, displeasure, and distress. Therein, "boundless" means: for one transmigrating in <s>saṃsāra</s>, there is no end, no limit to these <s>dharmas</s>. As long as these <s>dharmas</s> belong to <s>saṃsāra</s>, their cessation comes only through the complete cessation of <s>saṃsāra</s>; there is no cessation otherwise. Thus, with respect to all existences, destinies, deaths, and rebirths, through the aspect of non-aspiration (<s>apraṇihita</s>), through the aspect of non-reliance, and through the aspect of aversion, while resolving, one cultivates the resolving mental attention. Having thus alarmed and frightened the mind away from all modes of existence and rebirth, one also, through one's deep intention, sets one's mind upon <s>nirvāṇa</s> through one aspect or another. But for him, the mind that has long been delighted in form, sound, smell, taste, and touch — accumulated and stored up with [attachment to] form, sound, smell, taste, and touch — even though by deep intention one sets [the mind] upon <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

body.text: tathā prayukto 'yaṃ yogī yattasyāścittasantateḥ anyonyatāṃ navanavatāmāpāyikatāṃ tāvatkālikatāmitvarapratyupasthāyitāñca paurvāparyeṇa paśyatīdamasyā [a]nityatāyā yattasyāścittasantateḥ upādānaskandhānupraviṣṭatāṃ paśyatīdamasya duḥkhatāyāstatra yaccittaṃ dharmaṃ nopalabhate | idamatra śūnyatāyāstatra yasyā eva cittasantateḥ pratītyasamutpannatāmasvatantrāmpaśyatīdamasyānātmatāyā[ḥ |] evaṃ tāvad duḥkhasatyamavatīrṇo bhavati |
body.translated_text: Thus engaged, this <s>yogī</s>, seeing in sequence the mutual otherness, the ever-newness, the perishability, the temporariness, and the swift presence of that mind-continuum — this is the impermanence thereof; seeing the entry of that mind-continuum into the <s>upādānaskandhas</s> (aggregates of clinging) — this is the suffering thereof; therein, not finding any <s>dharma</s> as a [permanent] mind — this is the emptiness therein; therein, seeing the dependent origination of that very mind-continuum as non-autonomous — this is the selflessness thereof. Thus, one has first descended into the truth of suffering.

body.text: tasyaivaṃ bhavatīyamapi me cittasantatiḥ | tṛṣṇāhaitukī, tṛṣṇāsamudayā, tṛṣṇāprabhavā, tṛṣṇāpratyayā [|] asyā api cittasanteteryo nirodhaḥ so 'pi śāntaḥ | asyā api yo nirodhagāmī mārgaḥ | sa nairyāṇika ityevamaparīkṣitamanaskāraparīkṣāyogena sūkṣmayā prajñayā na tānyāryasatyānyavatīrṇo bhavati | tasyaivamāsevanānvayādbhāvanānvayāttasyāḥ samasamālambyālambakājñānamutpadyate | yenāsyaudārikatvāsmimāno nirvāṇābhirataye vibandhakaraḥ samudācarataḥ | prahīyate | nirvāṇe cādhyāyataścittaṃ pradadhataḥ praskandati | napratyudāvartate(yati) (|) mānasaṃ | paritamanāmupādāya | adhyāśayataścābhiratiṃ gṛhṇāti | tathābhūtasyāsya mṛdukṣāntisahagataṃ samasamālambyālambakajñānaṃ tadūṣmagatamityucyate | yanmadhyakṣāntiparigṛhītaṃ tanmūḍhe(ḍhami)tyucyate | yadadhimātrakṣāntisaṃgṛhītaṃ tanmadhyānulomā kṣāntirityucyate ||
body.translated_text: The following occurs to him: "This mind-continuum of mine too has <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving) as its cause, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> as its origin, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> as its source, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> as its condition. The cessation of this mind-continuum too is peaceful. The path leading to the cessation of this too is liberating." Thus, through the yoga of examination with unexamined mental attention, by means of subtle wisdom, one descends into those Noble Truths. Through the continuity of cultivation and practice, there arises in him knowledge that equally grasps its equal object, by which his coarse "I am" conceit — obstructive to delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — when manifesting, is abandoned. And for one whose mind is inclined toward <s>nirvāṇa</s> and directed [toward it], the mind leaps forward, does not turn back — the mental [activity], owing to distress; and through deep intention, one grasps delight. For one in such a state, the knowledge that equally grasps its equal object, accompanied by mild patience (<s>kṣānti</s>) — that is called <s>ūṣmagata</s> (heat). That which is grasped by middling patience is called <s>mūrdhan</s> (summit). That which is encompassed by intense patience is called <s>madhyānulomā kṣānti</s> (middling conforming patience).

body.text: sa evambibandhakaramasmimānaṃ prahāya nirvāṇe cādhyāśayaratiṃ parigṛhyayo 'sāvuttarottaraścittaparikṣayābhisaṃskāraḥ | tamabhisaṃskāraṃ samutsṛjya anabhisaṃskāratāyāṃ nirvikalpacittamupanikṣipati | tasya taccittaṃ tasmin samaye niruddhamiva khyāti | na ca taṃ (tan) niruddhaṃ bhavatyanālambanamiva khyāti | na ca tadālambanaṃ bhavati | tasya taccittaṃ praśāntaṃ vigatamiva (

children.translated_text: yet it has not departed. Nor again at that time, even though seized like a bee stunned [by smoke], does that mind appear as if ceased — yet it has not ceased. For some dull and confused persons, this becomes the basis for the conceit of realization, [thinking:] "Now this mind is indeed for realization; soon now, the entry into the certainty of the right path (<s>samyaktvanyāmāvakrānti</s>) will occur." If the mind reaches such a state, that final non-conceptual mind of his — immediately after which he makes effort toward the truths previously investigated internally — those are the <s>laukikāgradharmas</s> (supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s>).

body.translated_text: Having thus abandoned the obstructive "I am" conceit and having grasped delight in <s>nirvāṇa</s> through deep intention, that ever-higher mental conditioning of the examination of the mind — abandoning that conditioning, one deposits the non-conceptual mind into the state of non-conditioning. At that time, his mind appears as if ceased — yet it has not ceased; appears as if without an object — yet it is not without an object. His mind appears as peaceful, as departed,

body.text: tasmātpareṇāsya lokottarameva cittamutpadyate | na laukikaṃ [|] sīmā eṣā laukikānāṃ saṃskārāṇāṃ, paryanta eṣastenocyante laukikā agradharmā iti | teṣāṃ samanantarapūrvāvicāritāni satyā[nyā]bhra(vra)jati | ābhogasamanantaraṃ yathāpūrvānukramaḥ [|]
body.translated_text: After that, only a supramundane mind arises in him — not a worldly one. This is the boundary of worldly conditioned things, this is their limit; therefore they are called supreme worldly <s>dharmas</s>. Immediately after them, the truths that were not previously investigated are approached; immediately after the effort, the sequence follows as before.

body.text: vicāriteṣu satyeṣu anupūrveṇaiva nirvikalpapratyakṣaparokṣeṣu || niścayajñānaṃ pratyakṣajñānamutpadyate | tasyotpādāt traidhātukāvacarāṇāṃ darśanaprahātavyānāṃ kleśānāṃ pakṣyaṃ dauṣṭhulyasanniśrayasanniviṣṭaṃ tatprahīyate | tasya prahāṇāt sacetpūrvameva kāmebhyo vītarāgo bhavati | saha sa(ga?)tyābhisamayāt | tasminsamaye (

children.text: ) 'nāgāmītyucyate | tasya tānyeva liṃgāni veditavyāni | yāni pūrvamuktāni vītarāgasyāyantu viśeṣaḥ | ayamaupapāduko bhavati | tatra parinirvāyī | anāgantā punarimaṃ lokaṃ [|]
children.translated_text: one is called a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>). The signs of such a one should be understood as those previously stated for one free from passion, but with this distinction: this one is of spontaneous birth (<s>aupapāduka</s>), attaining <s>parinirvāṇa</s> there, not returning again to this world.

body.translated_text: When the truths have been investigated, in sequence, through the non-conceptual — whether directly perceived or imperceptible — the knowledge of certainty, the knowledge of direct perception, arises. From its arising, the group of defilements to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>), belonging to the three realms, lodged in the basis of the unsuitability (<s>dauṣṭhulya</s>) that is their support — that is abandoned. From its abandonment, if one has previously become free from passion toward sense-desires, then, simultaneously with the realization of the truths, at that time

body.text: sa cet punaryadbhūyo vītarāgo bhavati | saha gatyā abhisamayāt sakṛdāgāmī bhavati |
body.translated_text: But if one has become free from passion to a greater degree, then simultaneously with the realization of the truths, one becomes a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>).

body.text: sacetpunaravītarāgo bhavati | sa bhūyassa tasya dauṣṭhulyasya pratipraśrabdheḥ srota āpanno bhavati | jñeyena jñānaṃ samāgataṃ bhavati | pratyakṣatayā | tenocyate [a]bhisamayataḥ | tadyathā kṣatriyaḥ kṣatriyeṇa | sārdhaṃ sammukhībhāvaṃ tadanvabhisamayāgata ityucyate | evaṃ brāhmaṇādayo veditavyāḥ |
body.translated_text: If, however, he is not yet free from passion, then through the further subsiding of that coarseness, he becomes a stream-enterer (<s>srotaāpanna</s>). Knowledge has come together with the knowable in direct perception. Therefore it is said 'by direct realization' (<s>abhisamaya</s>). Just as a <s>kṣatriya</s> who has come face-to-face with [another] <s>kṣatriya</s> is said to have 'arrived at direct encounter' — so too should <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and others be understood.

body.text: tasyemāni liṃgāni catvāri jñānānyanena pratilabdhāni bhavanti | sattvacāravihāramanasikāreṣu tīrayato dharmamātrajñānamanucchedajñānamaśāśvatajñānaṃ | pratītyasamutpannasaṃskāramāyopamajñānaviṣayo 'pi cāsya carataḥ, sutīvramapi kleśaparyavasthānaṃ | yadyapi smṛtisaṃpramoṣādutpadyate | tadapyasyābhogamātrāllaghu laghveva vigacchati | tathā agantā bhavatyapāyāṃ (yān) na saṃcidhyaṇikṣāṃ (vidhya[ti] śikṣāṃ) vyatikrāmati | ca tiryagyoni(kṛtaṃ) gataṃ prāṇinaṃ jīvitād vyaparopayati | (

children.text: ) na śikṣāṃ pratyākhyāya hānāyārvattate | abhavyo bhavati pañcānāmānantaryāṇāṃ karmaṇāṃ karaṇatāyai | na svayaṃkṛtasukhaduḥkhaṃ paryeti, na parakṛtaṃ, na svayaṃkṛtaṃ ca parakṛtaṃ ca, na svayaṃkārāparakārāhetusamutpannaṃ | na ito bahirdhānyaṃ śāstāraṃ paryeṣate | na dakṣiṇīyaṃ | na pareṣāṃ śramaṇabrāhmaṇānāṃ sukhāvalokako bhavati | sukhaparīkṣakaḥ | nānyatra dṛṣṭadharmāḥ, prāptadharmā, paryavagāḍhadharmā, tīrṇakāṃkṣastīrṇavicikitsaḥ, aparapratyayo 'nanyaneyaḥ, śāstuḥ śāsane dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāptaḥ | sa na kautūhalamaṃgalābhyāṃ śuddhiṃ pratyeti | nāpyaṣṭamaṃ bhavamabhinirvarttayati | caturbhiravetyaprasādaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati | tasya yāvallaukikebhyo 'gradharmebhya adhimokṣiko manaskāraḥ satyānyabhisamitavataḥ darśanaprahātavyeṣu kleśeṣu prahīṇeṣu prāvivekyo manaskāraḥ, prahāṇāya ca |
children.translated_text: ) He does not, having rejected the training, turn back to decline. He is incapable of committing any of the five heinous deeds (<s>ānantarya</s>). He does not pursue [the view that] happiness and suffering are self-made, nor other-made, nor both self-made and other-made, nor arisen without the cause of self-making or other-making. He does not seek another teacher outside [the <s>Dharma</s>]; he does not seek another worthy recipient [of offerings]. He does not become one who looks with approval upon or investigates the happiness of other <s>śramaṇas</s> and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Rather, he is one who has seen the <s>Dharma</s> in this very life, who has attained the <s>Dharma</s>, who has penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, who has crossed beyond doubt, crossed beyond hesitation, not dependent on another, not to be led by another, who has attained confidence in the <s>Dharmas</s> of the Teacher's teaching. He does not resort to purification through superstitious omens and auspicious signs. Nor does he bring about an eighth existence. He is endowed with the four irreversible clarities of faith. For him, up to the time when the mundane supreme qualities [are transcended] — the mental attention of conviction, having directly realized the truths, the afflictions to be abandoned by seeing having been abandoned — there arises the mental attention of inclination toward seclusion, and [the mental attention] for abandonment.

body.translated_text: These are his signs: four knowledges have been obtained by him — regarding the behavior, dwelling, and mental attention of beings: the knowledge of mere phenomena, the knowledge of non-annihilation, the knowledge of non-eternalism, and his domain of knowledge is the dependently originated conditioned things that are like illusions. And furthermore, even while he is living [in the world], even an extremely intense afflictive state — even if it arises through loss of mindfulness — subsides for him quickly and easily by mere application of attention. Likewise, he does not go to the lower realms (<s>apāya</s>); he does not transgress the training; he does not deprive any living being, even one born as an animal, of life.

body.text: ata ūrdhvaṃ yathāpratilabdhaṃ mārgaṃ bhāvayato 'bhyasyataḥ kāmāvacarāṇāmadhimātramadhyānāṃ kleśānāṃ prahāṇāt sakṛdāgāmī bhavati | tasyāpi yāni srota āpannasya liṃgāni | sarvāṇi veditavyāni | ayañca viśeṣo yadviṣaye 'dharakleśasthānīyeṣu adhimātraparyavasthānīye 'pi baddhaṃ kleśaparyavasthānamutpādayatyāśu cāpanayati | sakṛccemaṃ lokamāgamya duḥkhasyāntaṃ karoti | anāgāmī | anāgāmiliṃgāni ca pūrvoktānītyeva tatra sarvo bhāvanāmārgaḥ pratyavekṣya pratyavekṣya mīmānsā(māṃsa) manaskāreṇa prahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ yathāpratilabdhamārgābhyāmaprabhāvitaḥ |
body.translated_text: Henceforth, cultivating and practicing the path as obtained — through the abandonment of the intense and middling afflictions belonging to the desire realm — he becomes a once-returner (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>). For him too, all the signs of a stream-enterer should be understood. And this is the distinction: even in the domain of the lower affliction-stations — even though aroused with intense afflictive states — [his] bound afflictive state arises [only weakly] and he quickly dispels it. Having come to this world only once more, he makes an end of suffering. [Then he becomes] a non-returner (<s>anāgāmin</s>). The signs of a non-returner are as stated previously. Therein, the entire path of cultivation (<s>bhāvanāmārga</s>) — reviewing again and again through the mental attention of investigation — [examining] what has been abandoned and what has not been abandoned — is not made manifest by the two paths as obtained.

body.text: tatra bhāvanāyāḥ katamaḥ svabhāvaḥ [|] katamatkarma | katamaḥ prakārabhedaḥ | yaḥ samāhitabhūmikena manaskāreṇa laukikalokottareṇaiṣāṃ kuśalānāṃ saṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāmabhyāsaḥ | paricayaḥ, sātatyasatkṛtya kriyā | cittasantatestanmayatā copanaya[na]mayamucyate bhāvanā svabhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: Therein, what is the intrinsic nature of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>)? What is its function? What is its classification by mode? That which is the repeated practice, the familiarization, the constant and reverential performance — through mental attention belonging to the concentrated level, whether mundane or supramundane — of these wholesome, conditioned <s>dharmas</s>; and the saturation and application of the mental continuum with them — this is called the intrinsic nature of cultivation.

body.text: tatra bhāvanāyā aṣṭavidhaṃ karma | ekatyāndharmānbhāvayan pratilabhate | ekatyāndharmānbhāvanayā niṣevate | ekatyāndharmānviśodhayatyekatyāndharmānprativinodayatyekatyāndharmān parijānāti | ekatyāndharmānprajahātyekatyān (

children.text: ) dharmān prajahātyekatyān dharmān sākṣātkarotyekatyāndharmāndūrīkaroti | tatra ye tāvadapratilabdhā dharmāḥ kuśalā vaiśeṣikāstān pratilabhate | ekatyā(tye) dharmābhāvanayā labdhāḥ, saṃmukhībhūtāśca vartta[n]te | tānniṣevate | tatra ye pratilabdhā, na ca saṃmukhībhūtāste tajjātīyairdharmairniṣevyamāṇau(ṇai)rāyatyāṃ saṃmukhīkriyamāṇā[ḥ], pariśuddhatarā[ḥ], paryavadātatarāścotpadyante tatra ye smṛtisaṃpramoṣā(t) kliṣṭā(n)dharmānsamudācaranti | tānkuśaladharmābhyāsabalenādhivāsayati | prajahāti | vinodayati | vyantīkarotyanutpannāneva vā prahātavyāndharmānrogataḥ parijānāti | vidūṣayati | śalyato, gaṇḍataḥ, aghataḥ, anityato, duḥkhataḥ, śūnyato, [a]nātmataśca parijānāti | vidūṣayati | tasya parijñānābhyāsādānantaryamārga utpadyate | kleśānāṃ prahāṇāya, yena prajahāti | prahīṇe ca punarvimuktiṃ sākṣātkaroti | yathā ca yathoparimāṃ bhūmimākramate | tathā tathā adhobhūmikāḥ prahāṇādharmā dūrī bhavanti | yāvanniṣṭhāgamanādidaṃ bhāvanīyamaṣṭavidhaṃ karma veditavyam ||
children.translated_text: ) one abandons certain <s>dharmas</s>; one directly realizes certain <s>dharmas</s>; one distances certain <s>dharmas</s>. Therein, first, those wholesome and distinguished <s>dharmas</s> that have not been obtained — one obtains them. Certain <s>dharmas</s>, once obtained through cultivation and having become present — one resorts to them. Therein, those that have been obtained but have not become present — when they are resorted to with <s>dharmas</s> of a similar kind, they arise in the future as more purified and more cleansed when brought into presence. Therein, those defiled <s>dharmas</s> that arise through loss of mindfulness — by the power of the repeated practice of wholesome <s>dharmas</s>, one tolerates them not, abandons them, removes them, eliminates them; or one fully knows the <s>dharmas</s> to be abandoned — even before they arise — as a disease, corrupts them, as a thorn, as a calamity, as impermanent, as suffering, as empty, as non-self — one fully knows and corrupts them. Through the repeated practice of full knowledge, the uninterrupted path (<s>ānantaryamārga</s>) arises — for the abandonment of afflictions — by which one abandons them. And when [they are] abandoned, one directly realizes liberation. And as one ascends to a higher level, so the <s>dharmas</s> to be abandoned on the lower levels become more distant — up to the final attainment. This eightfold function of what is to be cultivated should be understood.

body.translated_text: Therein, the function of cultivation is eightfold: by cultivating certain <s>dharmas</s>, one obtains them; by cultivation, one resorts to certain <s>dharmas</s>; one purifies certain <s>dharmas</s>; one dispels certain <s>dharmas</s>; one fully knows certain <s>dharmas</s>; one abandons certain <s>dharmas</s>;

body.text: tatra bhāvanāyāme (yā e)kādaśavidhaḥ prakārabhedo (

children.text: ) veditavyaḥ tadyathā śamathabhāvanā, vipaśyanābhāvanā, [pūrvavadeva tatra] laukikamārgabhāvanā, lokottaramārgabhāvanā, mṛdumadhyādhimātrabhāvanā, prayogamārgabhāvanā, ānantaryavimuktiviśeṣamārgabhāvanā [|]
children.translated_text: ) to be understood as follows: cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> (calm abiding), cultivation of <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), [as before;] cultivation of the mundane path, cultivation of the supramundane path; cultivation of mild, middling, and intense [degrees]; cultivation of the preparatory path; cultivation of the uninterrupted path, the liberation path, and the path of distinction.

body.translated_text: Therein, the classification by mode of cultivation is elevenfold,

body.text: tatra śamathabhāvanā navākārāyāścittasthityā[ṃ](ñcittasthityāṃ) pūrvavat |
body.translated_text: Therein, the cultivation of <s>śamatha</s> is the ninefold mental settling, as before.

body.text: vipaśyanābhāvanā pūrvavadeva | tatra laukikamārgabhāvanā[ya]dadhobhūmikānāmaudārikadarśanatayā uparibhūmīnāṃ ca śāntadarśanatayā, yāvadākiñcanyāyatanavairāgyagamanaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: The cultivation of <s>vipaśyanā</s> is as stated before. Therein, the cultivation of the mundane path is: through seeing the lower levels as coarse and the higher levels as peaceful — up to the attainment of dispassion from the <s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s> (sphere of nothingness).

body.text: tatra lokottaramārgabhāvanā duḥkhaṃ vā duḥkhato manasikurvataḥ, yāvanmārgamvā mārgato manasikurvataḥ | yadanāsraveṇa mārgeṇa samyagdṛṣṭyādikena yāvannaivasaṃjñā nāsaṃjñāyatanavairāgyagamanaṃ [|]
body.translated_text: Therein, the cultivation of the supramundane path is: attending to suffering as suffering, up to attending to the path as the path — by which, through the undefiled path beginning with right view, one reaches dispassion up to the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.

body.text: tatra mṛdumārgabhāvanā yayaudārikānadhimātrān kleśānprajahāti | tatra madhyamārgabhāvanā yayā madhyān kleśān prajahāti | tatrādhi[mātra]mārgabhāvanā yayā mṛduṃ kleśaprakāraṃ prajahāti | sarvampaścātpraheyaṃ |
body.translated_text: Therein, the cultivation of the mild path is that by which one abandons the coarse, intense afflictions. Therein, the cultivation of the middling path is that by which one abandons the middling afflictions. Therein, the cultivation of the intense path is that by which one abandons the mild [i.e., most subtle] variety of afflictions — all that which is to be abandoned last.

body.text: tatra prayogamārgabhāvanā yayā prayogamārabhate kleśa prahāṇāya | tatrānantaryamārgabhāvanā yayā prajahāti | (

children.text: ) tatra vimuktimārgabhāvanā yayā samanantaraprahīṇe kleśavimuktiṃ sākṣātkaroti | tatra viśeṣamārgabhāvanā yayāsta (yayā ta)ta ūrdhvaṃ yāvadanyabhūmikasya kleśaprayogamārabdhavyaṃ nārabhate | niṣṭhāgato vā nārabhate | ityayamekādaśavidho bhāvanāyāḥ prakārabhedo veditavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: ) Therein, the cultivation of the liberation path is that by which, immediately upon the abandonment of afflictions, one directly realizes liberation. Therein, the cultivation of the path of distinction is that by which, from that point onward, until one should commence the preparatory [path] for the afflictions of another level — one does not commence it; or, having reached the final goal, one does not commence it. This elevenfold classification by mode of cultivation should be understood.

body.translated_text: Therein, the cultivation of the preparatory path is that by which one commences the practice for the abandonment of afflictions. Therein, the cultivation of the uninterrupted path is that by which one abandons [them].

body.text:
tasyaivaṃ bhāvanāprayuktasya kālena ca kālaṃ kleśānāṃ prahīṇāprahīṇatāṃ mīmānsa(māṃsa)taḥ (mānasya?) kālena kālaṃ saṃvejanīyeṣu dharmeṣu cittaṃ samvejayataḥ, kālenakālamabhipramodanīyeṣvabhipramodayataḥ so 'sya bhavati [rati]saṃgrāha[ko] manaskāraḥ | tasyāsya ratisaṃgrāhakasya manaskārasyāsevanānvayād bhāvanānvayādbahulīkārānvayānniravaśeṣabhāvanāprahātavyā[ḥ] kleśaprahāṇāya sarvapaścimaḥ śaikṣo vajropamaḥ samādhirutpadyate | tasyotpādātsarve bhāvanāprahātavyāḥ kleśāḥ prahīyante |
kena kāraṇena vajropama ityucyate | tadyathā (

children.text: ) vajra[ṃ] sarveṣāṃ tadanyeṣāṃ maṇimuktāvaiḍūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravāḍā(lā)dīnāṃ maṇīnāṃ sarvasāraṃ sarvadṛḍhaṃ tadanyānvilikhati | na tvanyairmaṇibhirvilikhyate | evamevāyaṃ samādhiḥ sarvaśaikṣasamādhīnāmagryaḥ, śreṣṭhaḥ sarvasāraḥ sarvakleśānabhibhavati | na ca punarutpattikleśairabhibhūyate | tasmādvajropama ityucyate |
children.translated_text: ) Just as a diamond (<s>vajra</s>) is the essence of all, the most solid of all, among all other jewels — pearls, lapis lazuli, conch shells, crystals, coral, and other gems — it scratches all others, but is not scratched by other gems. Even so, this <s>samādhi</s> is the foremost, the supreme, the very essence among all concentrations of a learner; it overpowers all afflictions, but is not overpowered by arising afflictions. Therefore it is called 'diamond-like.'

body.translated_text:
For one thus engaged in cultivation — from time to time investigating the abandoned and unabandonded state of afflictions, from time to time arousing the mind regarding things that arouse urgency, from time to time gladdening it regarding things that bring gladness — this is his mental attention that gathers delight (<s>ratisaṃgrāhaka manaskāra</s>). Through the repeated practice, the cultivation, and the abundant engagement of this mental attention that gathers delight — for the abandonment of the very last afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation — the final <s>vajropama samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration) of a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>) arises. Upon its arising, all afflictions to be abandoned by cultivation are abandoned.
For what reason is it called 'diamond-like' (<s>vajropama</s>)?

body.text: tasya vajropamasya samādheḥ samanantaraṃ sarvakleśapakṣyaṃ dauṣṭhulyabījasamuddhātādatyantatāyai cittamadhimucyate | (

children.text: ) gotrapariśuddhiṃ cānuprāpnoti [|] sarva dauṣṭhulya kleśondhakṣayāya jñānamutpadyate | hetukṣayāccāyatyāṃ duḥkhasya sarveṇa sarvamaprādurbhāvāyānutpāda jñānamutpadyate | sa tasmin samaye 'rhan bhavati | kṣīṇāsravaḥ, kṛtakṛtyaḥ, kṛtakaraṇīyo 'nuprāptasvakāryaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaḥ | daśabhiraśaikṣairdharmaiḥ samanvāgataḥ | aśaikṣayā samyagdṛṣṭyā samyaksaṃkalpena yāvadaśaikṣayā samyagvimuktyā samyagjñānena [|] svacittavaśavartī ca bhavati | vihāre ca manasikāre ca | samayena yena kāṃkṣate | vihāreṇāryeṇa vā, divyena vā, brāhmeṇa vā, tena tena viharati | yaṃ yamevākāṃkṣate dharmaṃ manasi karttuṃ kuśalamarthopasaṃhitaṃ | laukikaṃ vā lokottaramvā, taṃ tameva manasi karoti |
children.translated_text: ) And one attains the purification of the <s>gotra</s> (spiritual lineage). Knowledge arises for the destruction of the entire darkness of coarseness and afflictions. And through the destruction of causes, knowledge of non-arising arises — [the knowledge that] in the future, suffering will in no way whatsoever come into being. At that time, one becomes an <s>arhat</s>: one whose <s>āśravas</s> (defilements) are destroyed, who has done what was to be done, who has accomplished what was to be accomplished, who has attained one's own purpose, whose bonds of existence are exhausted, whose mind is well-liberated through right knowledge. One is endowed with the ten qualities of one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>): right view beyond training, right intention, right speech, up to right liberation beyond training and right knowledge. And one becomes master of one's own mind — in dwelling and in mental attention. At whatever time one wishes — to dwell in a noble dwelling, or a divine dwelling, or a <s>Brahma</s> dwelling — one dwells in that very [dwelling]. Whatever <s>dharma</s> one wishes to attend to — wholesome, connected with purpose, whether mundane or supramundane — one attends to that very [dharma].

body.translated_text: Immediately following that <s>vajropama samādhi</s>, the mind is resolved upon the ultimate [goal] — for the complete uprooting of the seed of the coarseness belonging to the entire class of afflictions.

body.translated_text: Therein, the noble dwelling is: the dwelling in emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>), the dwelling in the signless (<s>ānimitta</s>), the dwelling in the wishless (<s>apraṇihita</s>), and the dwelling in the attainment of cessation (<s>nirodhasamāpatti</s>). The divine dwelling is the dwelling in the <s>dhyānas</s> and formless [attainments]. The <s>Brahma</s> dwelling is the dwelling in loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>), sympathetic joy (<s>muditā</s>), and equanimity (<s>upekṣā</s>). One becomes utterly free from greed, utterly free from stain, one whose holy life has reached its culmination. One has gone forth, as it were; risen above [the world]............................................. and endowed with the five factors abandoned and the six factors possessed,

body.text: bhavati suṣṭhumanāḥ upekṣako bhavati smṛtaḥ samprajā[nā]naḥ | evaṃ śrotreṇa śabdān, ghrāṇena gandhān, jihvayā rasān, kāyena spraṣṭavyān, manasā dharmān vijñāya | me va........tadūrdhva | upekṣako viharati smṛtaḥ saṃprajā[nā]naḥ | sa tasmin samaye apariśeṣarāgakṣayaṃ pratisaṃvedayati | sa kṣayādrāgadveṣamohānāṃ yattyāgaṃ (yastyāgaḥ), tanna karoti...........
body.translated_text: of well-settled mind, one becomes equanimous, mindful, clearly comprehending. Likewise, having cognized sounds with the ear, scents with the nose, tastes with the tongue, tangible objects with the body, and <s>dharmas</s> (mental objects) with the mind — beyond that [initial contact]......... one dwells equanimous, mindful, clearly comprehending. At that time, one experiences the exhaustion of passion without remainder. Through the destruction of passion, hatred, and delusion — whatever renunciation there is — one does not [reverse it]..........

One is called 'one who has crossed over, gone to the far shore, the bearer of the final body.' Of the five aggregates that were struck by former <s>karma</s> and afflictions — through their own momentum..........without fuel, [one enters] the <s>nirupadhiśeṣanirvāṇadhātu</s> (element of <s>nirvāṇa</s> without remainder).

body.text: ......parinirvṛto bhavati | yathā na saṃsṛto (tau) nānyatra yad duḥkhaṃ tanniruddhaṃ tavyupaśāntaṃ tacchītībhūtaṃ bhava iṃ gataṃ | śāntaṃ śāntamidaṃ padaṃ | yaduta sarvopadhipratiniḥsarvasaṃjñākṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇaṃ tasyemāni liṃgānyevaṃ bhāgīyāni veditavyāni | (

children.text: ) pañca sthānānyu..........bhikṣuḥ kṣīṇāsravaḥ prati | vi vine | kta manyamasaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: [Fragmentary:] ...five grounds... a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) whose outflows are destroyed... who knows... free from conceit...

body.translated_text: ...he attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final liberation). Just as he is not bound in <s>saṃsāra</s> — whatever suffering there was, that has ceased, is pacified, has become cool, has gone beyond existence. 'Peaceful, peaceful is this state' — namely, the relinquishment of all substrata, the exhaustion of all conceptualization, the cessation of desire, cessation, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. These are to be understood as the signs and characteristics pertaining to that.

body.text: prāpayituṃ mandadā tra ma brahmacaryaṃ maithunaṃ dharmaṃ pratiṣevituṃ | saṃprajānā(no) mṛṣāpabhāṣitumabhavyaḥ mandavikāreṇa kāmānparibhoktuṃ | tathā bhavyaḥ svayaṃ kṛtaṃ sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ pratyetuṃ | pūrvavadyāvatsvayaṃkāyakāro 'hetusamutpannamugraduḥkhaṃ praṇītamamavyāya kṛtastubhiḥ(tiḥ) | satrāsaṃ māṃsaṃ bhakṣya(vya).........
body.translated_text: [Fragmentary:] ...to bring about... the practice of <s>brahmacarya</s> (holy life)... [one is] incapable of engaging in sexual conduct; knowingly speaking falsehood; indulging in sensual pleasures through minor disturbance; and thus [one is] capable of experiencing for oneself the happiness and suffering created [by oneself]. As before, in detail: the action produced by one's own body, arising without cause, whether great suffering or subtle... not to be consumed... flesh...

body.text: 'anyatāmānyatamvā bhayabhairavaṃ........saṃtrāsamāpattu rayamasau vajropamaḥ samādhirayaṃ prayoganiṣṭho manaskāraḥ yaḥ punaragraphalārhattvasaṃgṛhītamanaskāro 'yaṃ prayoganiṣṭhāphalo manaskāraḥ | ebhiḥ saptabhirmanaskārairlokottareṇa mārgeṇātyantaniṣṭhāt ā/prā pā taḥ-ta
body.translated_text: [Fragmentary:] '...any fear or terror... alarm... this is the <s>vajropama-samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration); this is the <s>manaskāra</s> (mental attention) of the consummation of practice. That <s>manaskāra</s> which is comprised in the highest fruit — namely <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an arhat) — this is the <s>manaskāra</s> whose fruit is the consummation of practice. By these seven <s>manaskāras</s> (mental attentions), through the supramundane path, one attains the ultimate consummation.'

body.text: ityayamucyate sā/mo dha ka sarveṣāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāṃ saśrāvakasaṃyuktānāṃ nirdeśasthānīyānāṃ sākṣātkā[ra]sthānīyānāṃ tadyathā sarvanāmakāyapadakāyavyaṃjanakāyakāvyamanu śāstrāṇi || mātṛkā ||
body.translated_text: This is called the foundation. Of all the perfectly awakened <s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>, in conjunction with their <s>śrāvakas</s> (hearers), in the positions of exposition and the positions of direct realization — namely, all the collections of names, collections of words, collections of syllables, and the treatises of poetry — [this is] the <s>mātṛkā</s> (matrix, summary).

body.text: || uddānam ||
body.translated_text: Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):

children.translated_text: One who perceives the characteristics, and likewise one of conviction (<s>adhimokṣika</s>);
one who delights in seclusion, and one who investigates that;

body.text: punaḥ prayoganiṣṭhā kṛtyuttaratatphalaḥ paścimo bhavet |

children.translated_text: and the <s>manaskāra</s> (mental attention), and the classification of the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditative absorptions) and the formless attainments (<s>ārūpya</s>);

body.translated_text: further, the consummation of practice, the function, and its fruit — the last;

children.translated_text: the attainments, the superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>), the modes of rebirth, and the characteristics;
the determination of the truths (<s>satya</s>) and likewise their penetration (<s>prativedha</s>);

body.text: bhāvanāyā vibhaṅgaśca niṣṭhā bhavati paścimā ||
body.translated_text: the analysis of the stages of cultivation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) — the last is the consummation.

body.text: || śrāvakabhūmau caturthaṃ yogasthānam ||
body.translated_text: The fourth <s>yogasthāna</s> (stage of yoga) in the <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s>.

body.text: || samāptā śrāvakabhūmiḥ ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Śrāvakabhūmi</s> is completed.
